starts.name: Human iPSC
starts.blurb: Reprogrammed from a donor's own cells. The usual choice for disease modelling and patient-specific work.

starts.name: Human ESC
starts.blurb: Lines such as H1 and H9, on which many of these protocols were first worked out.
starts.note: Human ESC and iPSC share the same protocols. Many were developed on ESC lines such as H1 or H9 and later confirmed on iPSC. Efficiency still varies from line to line, so plan a small pilot before scaling up.

starts.name: Mouse ESC / iPSC
starts.blurb: Dome-shaped naive colonies kept in LIF or 2i. Faster timelines and the classic embryoid-body methods.

cell_types.name: Epiblast-like cells (EpiLC)
cell_types.summary: EpiLCs are the short-lived in vitro counterpart of the pre-gastrulation (E5.5-E6.5) mouse epiblast, made by pushing ground-state ESCs with activin A and bFGF for about two days. They are mainly used as the obligatory launch pad for primordial germ cell-like cells and for other post-implantation lineages, because this is the state in which cells are competent to respond to BMP4 with a germline fate.
cell_types.maturation_note: Competence is transient: it peaks around 44-48 h of induction and is lost by about day 3, so EpiLCs are used immediately rather than expanded.

morphology.endpoint: A flat, sub-confluent sheet of small, tightly packed cells with much less three-dimensional doming than naive ESC colonies. Colony borders blur as the sheet spreads, and the culture looks uniform rather than patchy.

stages.label: Naive ESC colonies
stages.look: Round, compact, upwardly convex domes on ornithine/laminin or gelatin in 2i+LIF, with smooth refractile edges.

stages.label: Flattening on fibronectin
stages.look: Cells spread out on the fibronectin coat; the domed colony shape gives way to a flatter, more continuous layer.

stages.label: Sub-confluent epiblast-like sheet
stages.look: An even, sub-confluent monolayer of small uniform cells; this is the point at which germline competence is highest.

markers.name: Pou5f1
markers.note: Core pluripotency factor that stays on through the naive-to-formative transition. (Marks: Epiblast-like cell.)

markers.name: Sox2
markers.note: Also maintained; reported as highly expressed in epiblast-like aggregates. (Marks: Epiblast-like cell.)

markers.name: Zfp42
markers.note: Naive marker; should fall as cells leave the ground state. (Marks: Naive ESC.)

markers.name: Klf4
markers.note: Naive network member, downregulated in epiblast-like cells. (Marks: Naive ESC.)

markers.name: Prdm14
markers.note: Naive/germline factor; low in the epiblast-like state before germline induction. (Marks: Naive ESC.)

markers.name: Dppa3
markers.note: Naive marker, low in EpiLCs; comes back later in germline cells. (Marks: Naive ESC.)

markers.name: Fgf5
markers.note: Classic post-implantation epiblast marker; its rise is the simplest sign the transition happened. (Marks: Epiblast-like cell.)

markers.name: Pou3f1
markers.note: Primed/formative epiblast transcription factor, upregulated. (Marks: Epiblast-like cell.)

markers.name: Otx2
markers.note: Upregulated during the naive-to-formative transition. (Marks: Epiblast-like cell.)

markers.name: Nodal
markers.note: Expressed at high levels in epiblast-like aggregates, matching the post-implantation epiblast. (Marks: Epiblast-like cell.)

markers.name: T
markers.note: Should still be absent: its appearance means the culture has run on into mesoderm. (Marks: Primitive streak.)

markers.name: Sox1
markers.note: Should be absent; premature neural differentiation indicates the window was overshot. (Marks: Neuroectoderm.)

markers.name: Sox17
markers.note: Should be absent in a properly timed EpiLC culture. (Marks: Definitive endoderm.)

functional_assays: Competence test: aggregate the cells in BMP4-containing medium and score germline reporter induction
Growth-curve timing (cells per well) to locate the competence window
qc: Harvest window set by counting: ~0.8-1 x 10^5 ESCs per 12-well should reach about 1 x 10^6 cells per well at 44-48 h (Ishikura 2022)
Naive markers (Zfp42, Klf4, Prdm14, Dppa3) down and Fgf5/Pou3f1/Otx2 up by qPCR
No T, Sox1, Sox17, Gata6 or Eomes expression yet

protocols.name: Two-day EpiLC induction from 2i+LIF ESCs (activin A + bFGF + 1% KSR)
protocols.principle: Ground-state ESCs are moved onto fibronectin in N2B27 with activin A and bFGF, which drives them through a formative, post-implantation epiblast-like state within about two days; the state is transient, so the window matters more than the end point.
protocols.start_requirements: ESCs maintained feeder-free in N2B27 with 2i (CHIR99021, PD0325901) and LIF; dissociate to a clean single-cell suspension and count accurately before plating onto fibronectin-coated wells.
materials: N2B27 (DMEM/F12 plus Neurobasal with N2 and B27)
tips: Treat EpiLCs as a window, not a cell line: competence is transient and the right harvest time has to be found for each ESC line.
Keep KSR low; the Saitou-lab protocols are explicit that above 1% the downstream germline induction suffers.
pitfalls: Letting the culture overgrow past the competence window.
Starting from ESCs that are not cleanly in a 2i+LIF ground state, which makes the transition uneven.
unverified: Concentrations (activin A 20 ng/ml, bFGF 12 ng/ml, 1% KSR), fibronectin coating and the 2-day window are taken from open-access papers restating Hayashi 2011 (Ishikura 2022 STAR Protoc; Sugawa 2015 EMBO J; Severino 2022 EMBO J); the Cell 2011 full text was not accessible in this session.
Seeding density and plate format as stated in the original paper not verified.
No efficiency figure for the EpiLC conversion itself was found in an accessible source.

source.authors: Hayashi K, Ohta H, Kurimoto K, Aramaki S, Saitou M
source.title: Reconstitution of the mouse germ cell specification pathway in culture by pluripotent stem cells

stages.name: Plating on fibronectin

factors.name: Activin A
factors.role: Nodal/activin signalling; drives the epiblast-like transition

factors.name: bFGF
factors.role: FGF signalling; exit from naive pluripotency

factors.name: KnockOut Serum Replacement
factors.role: Low serum-replacement supplement; higher levels reduce later PGCLC competence

stages.feeding: Single plating; medium not changed during the first 24 h
actions: Coat wells with human plasma fibronectin and equilibrate at 37 C
Dissociate 2i+LIF ESCs to single cells and count
Seed into EpiLC induction medium on the fibronectin-coated surface
stages.checkpoint: Cells attached as a flat, evenly spread layer rather than domed naive colonies

stages.name: Second day of induction
stages.feeding: Full medium change at 24 h, then culture to ~44-48 h
actions: Replace the medium with fresh EpiLC induction medium at 24 h
Harvest or pass on to the next step at around 44-48 h, before the culture overgrows
stages.checkpoint: A sub-confluent, flattened monolayer at ~44-48 h; PGC competence is highest in this window and falls away after about 3 days

protocols.name: EpiLC induction with defined cell numbers (STAR Protocols version)
protocols.principle: Same activin A / bFGF / 1% KSR route, but with the starting cell number and the harvest time pinned to a growth criterion so that the competence window can be found reproducibly for a new line.
protocols.start_requirements: ESCs grown feeder-free on poly-L-ornithine (0.01%) plus laminin (line-dependent, e.g. 10-300 ng/ml) in 2i+LIF (N2B27 with 3 uM CHIR99021, 0.4 uM PD0325901, 1,000 U/ml LIF); use cells in log growth, typically two or three passages after thawing.
materials: N2B27 (DMEM/F12 + N2 solution A; Neurobasal minus phenol red + B27 minus vitamin A solution B)
Poly-L-ornithine and laminin for the ESC stock
tips: Calibrate the harvest time per line by counting: find when 0.8-1 x 10^5 seeded cells reach ~1 x 10^6 per 12-well.
Culturing shorter than 44 h is explicitly not recommended in this protocol.
pitfalls: Overgrown EpiLCs: the downstream germline step then fails even though the monolayer looks healthy.
KSR lot variation; the protocol advises testing lots separately.
High ESC passage number, which brings karyotype drift and erratic induction.
unverified: This protocol states no percentage readout for the EpiLC state itself (its quantified endpoints are downstream germline cells).

source.authors: Ishikura Y, Ohta H, Nagano M, Saitou M
source.title: Optimized protocol to derive germline stem-cell-like cells from mouse pluripotent stem cells

stages.name: Seed on fibronectin

factors.name: KnockOut Serum Replacement
factors.role: Critical: above 1% the later germline induction drops

stages.feeding: 1 ml per well of a 12-well plate; no change for 24 h
actions: Coat 12-well plates with 610 ul/well of fibronectin solution (16.7 ug/ml stock in PBS) for at least 1 h at 37 C
Dissociate ESCs with TrypLE Express, wash and count
Seed 1.0 x 10^5 ESCs per well in 1 ml of EpiLC induction medium
Incubate 24 h at 37 C
stages.checkpoint: Even attachment across the well, no large naive-looking domes

stages.name: Medium change and competence window
stages.feeding: Replace with 1 ml fresh EpiLC induction medium at 24 h, then culture a further ~20 h
actions: Aspirate and add 1 ml fresh pre-warmed EpiLC induction medium
Incubate ~20 h more (44 h total for the reference line)
Check that the well has reached a sub-confluent state before using the cells
stages.checkpoint: Starting from 0.8-1 x 10^5 cells per 12-well, the culture should reach about 1 x 10^6 cells per well (sub-confluent) at 44-48 h; that time point is the one to use

protocols.name: 3D epiblast-like (EPI) aggregates in hydrogel microwells
protocols.principle: Instead of a monolayer, small ESC aggregates are formed in PEG microwells directly in activin A / bFGF / 1% KSR medium, giving post-implantation epiblast-like aggregates that later break symmetry on their own.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ESCs in s2iL (DMEM+GlutaMAX, 10% ESC-qualified FBS, pyruvate, NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol, pen/strep with 3 uM CHIR99021, 1 uM PD0325901 and LIF), passaged every 2-3 days at 8,000-9,000 cells/cm2; dissociate with Accutase and wash twice in PBS.
materials: Low-adherence U-bottom 96-well plates for the transfer
tips: Bulk RNA-seq in this paper shows naive markers (Zfp42, Klf2/Klf4, Esrrb, Prdm14, Dppa3) low and primed markers (Fgf4/Fgf5, Otx2, Sox2, Pou5f1/Pou3f1, Nodal) high, with no mesoderm, endoderm or neural markers yet.
Aggregates at the edge of the array grow slightly larger than central ones; size-select when picking.
pitfalls: Swirling the plate during seeding ruins the even split of cells between microwells.
Dispensing medium straight onto the array lifts the cells out of the wells.
unverified: No single percentage efficiency is given for the EPI aggregate state itself.

source.authors: Girgin MU, Broguiere N, Mattolini L, Lutolf MP
source.title: Gastruloids generated without exogenous Wnt activation develop anterior neural tissues

stages.name: Seeding into microwells
stages.base_medium: N2B27 (DMEM/F12 + Neurobasal, 0.5x N2, 0.5x B27, 0.5x GlutaMAX, pyruvate, NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol)

factors.name: XAV939
factors.role: Tankyrase/Wnt inhibitor; added when anterior neural tissue is wanted later

stages.feeding: 35 ul of a 484,000 cells/ml suspension onto the array, then 1 mL medium added gently from the side
actions: Equilibrate PEG microwell arrays (400 um wells, 121 wells per array) with 50 ul EPI differentiation medium for at least 30 min at 37 C
Add 35 ul of cell suspension to give 100-150 cells per microwell
Let cells sediment undisturbed for 20-30 min at 37 C
Add 1 ml medium slowly from the notch so the cells are not lifted out
stages.checkpoint: Cells settled into the wells and clumped within about an hour of seeding

stages.name: Aggregate formation
stages.feeding: No change during the 72 h on the array
actions: Leave the array undisturbed at 37 C, 5% CO2, 21% O2 for at least 72 h
At ~72-80 h flush the aggregates off the array with N2B27 and collect them in a non-treated 10 cm dish
stages.checkpoint: Smooth round aggregates; for 100 cells/well, pick those closest to but no more than about 220 um across

cell_types.notes: EpiLCs are a state, not a stable line - do not try to passage them. The exact competence window differs between ESC lines and even between KSR lots, so the first thing to do with a new line is a time course. KSR above 1% is repeatedly flagged as the single most common reason downstream germline induction fails.

cell_types.name: Neural progenitors and neurons (N2B27 monolayer)
cell_types.summary: Sox1+ neuroepithelial progenitors and the neurons they produce, made from mouse ES cells either as an adherent monolayer in serum-free N2B27 or through retinoic-acid-treated aggregates. They are used to study exit from pluripotency and neural commitment, to derive neural stem cell lines, and as a source of defined glutamatergic or cortical neurons.
cell_types.maturation_note: Sox1+ progenitors by day 4-6 and the first Tubb3+ neurons around day 6 in monolayer; aggregate and cortical protocols give plated neurons from day 8-14, with synaptic activity about 10 days after plating.

morphology.endpoint: A carpet of small neural progenitors, often arranged in rosette-like rings, with phase-bright neuronal cell bodies on top sending out long thin neurites that join into a network. Flat glial cells appear underneath in older cultures.

stages.label: ES cells at plating
stages.look: Single cells and small tight clumps at low density shortly after replating from compact, sharp-edged ES colonies.

stages.label: Flattening monolayer
stages.look: Cells spread out and lose the domed colony shape; some floating dead cells are normal in the first days.

stages.label: Neural progenitors
stages.look: Dense fields of small elongated Sox1+ cells that pack into ridges and rosette-like rings as the dish fills.

stages.label: First neurons
stages.look: Small phase-bright cell bodies with fine processes appear on top of the progenitor layer.

stages.label: Neuronal network
stages.look: After replating on laminin, well-separated neurons with long branching neurites form a network.

markers.name: Pou5f1
markers.note: Should disappear as Sox1 comes on; by day 3 a cell is either Oct4+ or Sox1+, not both (Mulas 2019). Persisting Oct4+ clusters mean density was too high or feeding was skipped.

markers.name: Nanog
markers.note: Lost early after LIF/2i withdrawal.

markers.name: Sox1
markers.note: Earliest specific neuroectoderm marker and the standard readout; 30-50% GFP+ on day 3 and 80-90% on day 4-5 in a good run (Mulas 2019).

markers.name: Sox2
markers.note: Also present in ES cells, so score Sox2+ Oct4- cells as committed progenitors (Lowell 2006).

markers.name: Nes
markers.note: Comes on roughly 12-24 h after the first Sox1-GFP+ cells; not exclusive to neural cells, so pair it with Sox1 or Sox2.

markers.name: Pax6
markers.note: Marks the radial-glia-like progenitors made by the aggregate + retinoic acid method and the dorsal forebrain progenitors of the cyclopamine method.

markers.name: Fabp7
markers.note: Radial glia marker scored alongside nestin and Pax6 in monolayer cultures (Lowell 2006).

markers.name: Foxg1
markers.note: Telencephalic identity; expected in the DDM/cyclopamine cortical protocol, not after retinoic acid.

markers.name: Tubb3
markers.note: First neurons appear around day 6 of monolayer differentiation.

markers.name: Map2
markers.note: Dendritic marker of maturing neurons.

markers.name: Slc17a7
markers.note: Glutamatergic identity; most neurons from the cyclopamine/DDM and aggregate/retinoic acid methods are glutamatergic.

markers.name: Slc17a6
markers.note: Second vesicular glutamate transporter used with VGLUT1 to score glutamatergic neurons.

markers.name: Slc32a1
markers.note: GABAergic neurons; a large VGAT+ fraction in a cortical run means ventral identity (cyclopamine missing or inactive).

markers.name: Gfap
markers.note: Astroglia follow neurons in time; many GFAP+ cells early usually means serum exposure.

functional_assays: Sox1-GFP flow cytometry (46C line)
Patch-clamp recording of action potentials and synaptic currents
Derivation of expandable NS cell lines in EGF + FGF-2
qc: Sox1-GFP+ 80-90% on day 4-5 from 2i-grown cells on laminin (Mulas 2019)
Little cell death on days 1-3; death on day 2-3 indicates a poor N2B27 batch (Mulas 2019)
No beating cells and no Oct4+ islands at day 5 (signs of too high a density or skipped medium changes)

protocols.name: N2B27 adherent monoculture on gelatin (Sox1-GFP 46C method)
protocols.principle: Mouse ES cells plated sparsely on gelatin in serum-free N2B27, with no LIF, serum or BMP, turn into Sox1+ neural progenitors on their own. Conversion depends on the FGF the cells make themselves, so density matters.
protocols.efficiency: The abstract states that the bulk of ES cells convert to neural precursors, and that they can be purified by FACS or drug selection; the exact percentage was not read from the paper.
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free mouse ES cells, subconfluent and undifferentiated (for example GMEM + 10% serum + LIF on gelatin; the 46C Sox1-GFP line makes scoring easy). Cells must be dissociated and replated into N2B27, not just switched to it. Plate about 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2 (10,500 cells/cm2 = 1 x 10^5 cells per well of a 6-well plate) on 0.1% gelatin.
materials: Modified N2 (insulin, apo-transferrin, progesterone, putrescine, sodium selenite, BSA)
tips: Titrate the plating density for every line and every batch of N2B27; 96-well plates needed roughly ten times the density per cm2 of 6-well plates in the JoVE write-up.
The Smith lab's later papers call 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2 the normal density for this method (Lowell 2006).
Another lab replated day 4 cells at 2 x 10^4 cells/cm2 on laminin with 5 ng/ml bFGF to carry cultures on to day 20 (Abranches 2009).
Progenitors from this method can be expanded as NS cell lines with EGF + FGF-2 (Conti 2005).
pitfalls: Too sparse and the cells die within 3 days; too dense (above roughly 36,500 cells/cm2 in 6-well plates) and far fewer cells turn on Sox1.
Some cell death in the first days is normal, but changing only the medium (without replating) always lowers efficiency.
Commercial N2 differs from the modified N2 used here; a poor N2B27 batch is the commonest cause of failure.
unverified: The full text of Ying 2003 (Nat Biotechnol) could not be opened; the plating density, coating, feeding schedule and timing given here come from the step-by-step JoVE protocol by Wongpaiboonwattana & Stavridis 2015 (PMID 26066640, doi 10.3791/52823; Stavridis is a co-author of Ying 2003), with the 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2 figure also stated in Lowell 2006 (PMID 16594731) and Abranches 2009 (PMID 19621087).
Ying 2003's own stated seeding density, medium-change interval and percentage of Sox1-GFP+ cells were not confirmed.
The JoVE recipe gives the final L-glutamine concentration as 0.2 mM as printed; not cross-checked against the original paper.
Stage 2 end day (7) is a convenient readout point, not a limit stated by the source.

source.authors: Ying QL, Stavridis M, Griffiths D, Li M, Smith A.
source.title: Conversion of embryonic stem cells into neuroectodermal precursors in adherent monoculture.

stages.name: Plating and neural commitment
stages.base_medium: N2B27: 1:1 mix of DMEM/F12 + modified N2 and Neurobasal + B27, with L-glutamine and 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol

factors.name: No added growth factors
factors.role: Neural conversion relies on autocrine FGF; LIF, serum and BMP are left out

stages.feeding: Replace all medium with fresh N2B27 every 1-2 days
actions: Coat wells with 0.1% gelatin for at least 30 min
Dissociate ES cells to single cells with a gentle dissociation reagent, spin, resuspend in warm N2B27 and count
Plate at about 10,500 cells/cm2; do not swirl the plate, which piles cells in the centre
Change medium gently; flushing cells off changes the density and lowers efficiency
If survival after plating is poor, plate in a 1:3 mix of the N2 and B27 halves for the first two days
stages.checkpoint: Sox1-GFP (46C) becomes visible within 4-6 days; Oct4 is lost as Sox1 comes on

stages.name: Neurogenesis in the same medium

factors.name: No added growth factors
factors.role: Progenitors begin to leave the cell cycle and make neurons

stages.feeding: Fresh N2B27 every 1-2 days
actions: Keep feeding without replating if you only need a readout; replating at this stage costs viability
Fix and stain for beta-III-tubulin around day 6
stages.checkpoint: Sox1-GFP+ progenitors with beta-III-tubulin+ neurons among them by about day 6

protocols.name: N2B27 monolayer on laminin from 2i-cultured ES cells (Smith lab standard protocol)
protocols.principle: The same default neural conversion in N2B27, updated for ES cells kept in 2i: cells go straight from 2i (with or without LIF) onto laminin at low density, which gives a synchronous and efficient exit from pluripotency.
protocols.efficiency: Good conditions typically give about 90% Sox1+ cells on day 5 (80-90% Sox1-GFP+ on day 4-5), with little non-neural differentiation.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ES cells kept in 2i or 2i/LIF in N2B27, passaged on time so colonies are not overgrown. Plates coated with about 10 ug/ml laminin in PBS overnight (minimum 2 h at 37 C). Plate 1.0 x 10^4 cells/cm2 (1.2 x 10^4 for flow-sorted cells). The lab uses 7% CO2.
tips: Test three densities side by side (for example 0.75, 1.0 and 1.5 x 10^4 cells/cm2).
Cells coming from 2i + LIF run about one day behind cells from 2i alone; the density can be dropped to 0.8 x 10^4 cells/cm2 for them.
Batch-test N2B27 for neural differentiation specifically; some mouse strains do better in a high-insulin N2B27.
A correction to this paper was published (Development 146(7):dev178970, PMID 30975648); check it before copying media recipes.
pitfalls: Skipping medium changes, or plating above 1.2 x 10^4 cells/cm2, gives mixed differentiation (beating cells are the obvious sign) and leaves undifferentiated ES cells behind.
Cell death on day 2-3 points to a poor N2B27 batch; good batches show little death until the culture is confluent.
unverified: The N2B27 formulation is in supplementary Table S1, which was not opened; no component concentrations are given here.
Stage boundaries (0-2, 2-5, 5-6) are drawn from the feeding schedule and the marker timeline in the text; the paper does not name stages.

source.authors: Mulas C, Kalkan T, von Meyenn F, Leitch HG, Nichols J, Smith A.
source.title: Defined conditions for propagation and manipulation of mouse embryonic stem cells.

stages.name: Plating into N2B27
stages.base_medium: N2B27 (recipe in the paper's Table S1)
stages.feeding: No medium change until day 2
actions: Aspirate the laminin coating without washing and add N2B27 to pre-equilibrate
Dissociate ES cells with Accutase, resuspend in N2B27 and count
Plate 1.0 x 10^4 cells/cm2 directly in N2B27
For lines that attach poorly: plate late in the day in 2i (or 2i/LIF) on laminin, then wash with PBS and switch to N2B27 early the next morning
stages.checkpoint: Day 1: cells mostly Oct4+, Sox2+, Sox1-; little cell death

stages.name: Neural commitment
stages.feeding: Fresh N2B27 on day 2 and every day after
actions: Change medium daily without fail
Watch for cell death on days 3-4 and score Sox1 on days 4-5
stages.checkpoint: Day 3: 30-50% Sox1-GFP+, with Oct4 and Sox1 mutually exclusive; day 4-5: 80-90% Sox1-GFP+

stages.name: First neurons

factors.name: No added growth factors
factors.role: Progenitors start to make post-mitotic neurons

stages.feeding: Fresh N2B27 daily
actions: Stain for Sox1 and Tuj1 to confirm progenitors and the first neurons
stages.checkpoint: Tuj1 (Tubb3)+ cells appear on about day 6

protocols.name: Cellular aggregates + retinoic acid (4-/4+) to Pax6+ radial glia and glutamatergic neurons
protocols.principle: ES cells are first cleared of feeders and kept strictly undifferentiated, then grown as floating aggregates for 8 days with retinoic acid during the second 4 days. This yields a near-uniform population of Pax6+ radial-glia-like progenitors that become glutamatergic neurons after plating.
protocols.efficiency: The abstract describes essentially pure populations of glutamatergic neurons; no percentage was read from the paper.
protocols.start_requirements: ES cells kept undifferentiated by repeated splitting (the abstract allows at least 2 weeks from starting the ES culture to plating progenitors). No reporter or selection line is needed. Start aggregates from 4 x 10^6 cells per non-adherent bacteriological dish.
materials: N2 components (insulin, transferrin, progesterone, putrescine, sodium selenite)
tips: The quality of the starting ES cells decides the outcome: remove feeders and split the cells repeatedly so that they are uniformly undifferentiated before making aggregates.
Because no reporter or drug selection is used, the method can be applied to any wild-type or mutant line.
pitfalls: Retinoic acid at this dose caudalises and removes most regional choice; do not expect forebrain identity as in the cyclopamine/DDM method.
Aggregates that attach to the dish, or ES cultures that had begun to differentiate, give mixed cultures.
unverified: The full text of Bibel 2007 (Nat Protoc) could not be opened. Cell number (4 x 10^6 per dish), CA medium, 5 µM retinoic acid from day 4 to day 8, plating density (2 x 10^5 cells/cm2), poly-DL-ornithine/laminin, N2 medium for 48 h then B27 complete medium are taken from two papers that restate the protocol: Sánchez-Martín 2013 PLoS One (PMID 24260418) and Manzo 2017 EMBO J (PMID 29074627).
Medium-change schedule during the 8 days of aggregate culture: not confirmed.
Number and timing of feeder-free passages before aggregation: not confirmed (abstract only says repeated splitting, at least 2 weeks overall).
Exact N2 and complete-medium recipes and the purity percentage in the original protocol: not confirmed.
Stage 4 end day (18) reflects the abstract's statement that synapses form within about 10 days of plating; it is not a fixed endpoint.

source.authors: Bibel M, Richter J, Lacroix E, Barde YA.
source.title: Generation of a defined and uniform population of CNS progenitors and neurons from mouse embryonic stem cells.

stages.name: Aggregate formation (4-)
stages.base_medium: CA medium: DMEM + 10% FBS, L-glutamine, non-essential amino acids, 2-mercaptoethanol (no LIF)

factors.name: No retinoic acid
factors.role: Cells aggregate and leave the pluripotent state

actions: Plate 4 x 10^6 ES cells in a non-adherent bacteriological dish in CA medium
Let floating cellular aggregates form for 4 days
stages.checkpoint: Smooth floating aggregates; nothing attached to the dish

stages.name: Retinoic acid (4+)

factors.name: All-trans retinoic acid
factors.role: Drives the aggregates to Pax6+ radial-glia-like neural progenitors

actions: Add retinoic acid to the CA medium on day 4 and keep it on until day 8
Protect retinoic acid from light
stages.checkpoint: Aggregates made up largely of Pax6+ progenitors on day 8

stages.name: Dissociation and plating
stages.base_medium: N2 medium: 1:1 DMEM and DMEM/F12 with insulin, transferrin, progesterone, putrescine, sodium selenite and BSA

factors.name: Poly-DL-ornithine + laminin coating
factors.role: Substrate for the progenitors and neurons

stages.feeding: N2 medium for the first 48 h
actions: Dissociate the aggregates with trypsin to single cells
Plate about 2 x 10^5 cells/cm2 on poly-DL-ornithine/laminin-coated plates in N2 medium
stages.checkpoint: Cells attach and start to extend processes within a day or two

stages.name: Neuronal maturation
stages.base_medium: Complete medium: DMEM-based with B27, insulin, transferrin, sodium selenite and BSA
actions: Switch from N2 to the B27-containing complete medium 48 h after plating
Keep for as long as the experiment needs; the neurons survive for long periods
stages.checkpoint: Network of neurons; synaptic transmission is established about 10 days after plating

protocols.name: DDM + cyclopamine: cortical progenitors and pyramidal neurons (protocol paper: Gaspard 2009 Nat Protoc)
protocols.principle: ES cells at low density in a defined, morphogen-free medium (DDM) take on forebrain identity by default. Blocking the Sonic hedgehog they make themselves with cyclopamine from day 2 to day 10 shifts them from ventral to dorsal (cortical) identity, and the progenitors then produce glutamatergic pyramidal neurons.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ES cells grown by standard procedures (E14- and J1-derived lines were used). Trypsinise to single cells and plate 5 x 10^3 cells/cm2 on gelatin-coated plastic in ES cell medium; switch to DDM once the cells have attached (day 0).
tips: The step-by-step version of this method is Gaspard N, et al. Nat Protoc 2009;4(10):1454-63 (PMID 19798080, doi 10.1038/nprot.2009.157); its abstract says millions of cortical neurons can be made in 2-3 weeks from one frozen vial of ES cells.
A later paper from the same lab gives cyclopamine as 400 ng/ml from day 2, refreshed every 2 days, with a return to plain DDM after day 10 (Bonnefont 2019, PMID 31353074).
Neurons with different cortical-layer identities appear in sequence, so the day of analysis changes which layer markers you see.
pitfalls: Without cyclopamine the same cultures are mostly ventral forebrain progenitors and give many more GABAergic neurons.
Any serum or added morphogen in the medium breaks the default forebrain programme.
unverified: Concentrations and days were read from the authors' accepted manuscript of Gaspard 2008 (Nature) in the ORBi repository, not from the journal's typeset version.

The Gaspard 2009 Nat Protoc full text could not be opened, so its exact seeding numbers, coating details and feeding schedule are not confirmed; a later paper from the lab quotes plating at 20 x 10^3 cells per ml rather than a per-cm2 figure.
Feeding interval during days 0-2 and days 10-21: not stated in the text read.
Percentage of cortical progenitors or glutamatergic neurons: not extracted (shown in figures).

cell_types.notes: All four methods depend on a clean, undifferentiated starting culture and on density. The monolayer methods give progenitors with a mainly anterior, unpatterned character; retinoic acid in the aggregate method imposes a more caudal one; cyclopamine in DDM gives cortex. N2B27 quality varies between batches and suppliers, so batch-test it. For three of the four sources the original full text was behind a paywall and numbers come from restating papers; see each protocol's unverified list.

cell_types.name: Spinal motor neurons
cell_types.summary: Cholinergic neurons of the ventral spinal cord that drive skeletal muscle, made from mouse ES cells in about a week by treating embryoid bodies with retinoic acid and a Hedgehog pathway agonist. They are used to study motor neuron specification and subtype identity, to build neuromuscular co-cultures, and to model motor neuron diseases such as ALS and SMA.
cell_types.maturation_note: Hb9+ motor neurons are present in embryoid bodies from day 5-7; after dissociation they extend long neurites within 2 days, and electrical maturation continues over weeks in co-culture with muscle or glia.

morphology.endpoint: Floating embryoid bodies 150-200 µm across that glow with the Hb9-GFP reporter; once dissociated and plated on ornithine/laminin, phase-bright neuronal cell bodies, often in small clusters, send out long neurites.

stages.label: ES colonies on feeders
stages.look: Round, compact, sharp-edged colonies about 50-100 µm across that do not touch one another.

stages.label: Early embryoid bodies
stages.look: Small floating aggregates just visible under the microscope; any carried-over feeder cells stick to the dish.

stages.label: Patterned embryoid bodies
stages.look: Larger smooth spheres, visible by eye from day 3-4, with Hb9-GFP coming on.

stages.label: Plated motor neurons
stages.look: Two days after plating, GFP+ cell bodies in small groups extend long neurites across the coverslip.

markers.name: Pou5f1

markers.name: Nkx6-1

markers.name: Lhx3

markers.note: V2a interneurons from the neighbouring ventral domain; general developmental biology, not quantified in the sources read here.

protocols.name: Embryoid bodies + retinoic acid + Hedgehog agonist (HB9::GFP original)
protocols.principle: Two-day-old embryoid bodies are neuralised and caudalised with retinoic acid and ventralised with a Hedgehog pathway agonist, copying the signals that specify motor neurons in the embryonic spinal cord.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ES cells (the HBG3 line carries an Hb9-eGFP transgene that lights up motor neurons). ES cells are taken off feeders and aggregated in suspension to form embryoid bodies.
materials: HBG3 (Hb9-eGFP) ES cells or another line
tips: Hh-Ag1.3 is not sold commercially; later protocols replace it with SAG or purmorphamine.
For electrophysiology, Miles 2004 plated the embryoid bodies on feeder fibroblasts or myotubes and added GDNF (20 ng/ml) and CNTF (10 ng/ml) 24 h after plating.
Motor neurons made this way are described by the same lab as rostral cervical in character (Peljto 2010).
pitfalls: Without the Hedgehog agonist, retinoic acid alone gives mostly spinal interneurons rather than motor neurons.
unverified: The full text of Wichterle 2002 (Cell) could not be opened (publisher blocks automated access). Medium, retinoic acid 1 µM, Hh-Ag1.3 1 µM and the 2 + 5 day timing are taken from Miles 2004 J Neurosci (PMID 15356197), co-authored by Wichterle and Jessell, which restates the method.
ES cell number or density used to start the embryoid bodies: not confirmed.
Medium-change schedule: not confirmed.
L-glutamine and heparin amounts are printed in Miles 2004 as '200 mM' and '1 u/µl', which look like stock concentrations; final concentrations not confirmed.
Miles 2004 also says embryoid bodies were plated 'on day 5'; whether that counts from aggregation or from retinoic acid addition is unclear, so the end day (7) is an interpretation.
Percentage of HB9+ motor neurons reported in the original paper: not confirmed.
The pitfall about interneurons without Hedgehog agonist reflects the paper's known conclusion but was not re-read in the text.

protocols.name: ADFNK embryoid bodies + retinoic acid + smoothened agonist (Wichterle lab standard)
protocols.principle: The refined Wichterle-lab version: ES cells are separated from feeders and aggregated in ADFNK medium; after 2 days without growth factors the embryoid bodies respond to retinoic acid, and a smoothened agonist supplies the ventral Hedgehog signal.
protocols.efficiency: About 40% of cells become motor neurons under retinoic acid/Hedgehog conditions, as stated by the same lab in Peljto 2010.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ES cells grown on feeder fibroblasts (Hb9-GFP HBG3 line for a live readout). Trypsinise, remove the feeders and seed the ES cells in suspension in ADFNK to form embryoid bodies (day 0).
tips: SAG dose differs between papers from this lab: 0.5 µM (Mazzoni 2013) and 0.25 µM (Rhee 2016); titrate for your lot.

To plate motor neurons, the lab dissociates day 6 embryoid bodies with Accumax plus DNase I for 10 min at 37 C, triturates, filters through a 40 µm strainer and plates on astrocytes (Patel 2022); many cells do not survive plating.
Leaving out retinoic acid and using low density in the same ADFNK medium gives fewer motor neurons (about 8%) but of brachial, limb-innervating (FoxP1+) type (Peljto 2010).
pitfalls: Feeder fibroblasts carried into the embryoid bodies lower efficiency; remove them before aggregation.
Retinoic acid added before or after the day 2 window is less effective, as the embryoid bodies are only briefly competent.
unverified: The Current Protocols unit itself could not be opened (paywalled). ADFNK composition, seeding at 5 x 10^5 cells/ml, medium changes on days 1, 2 and 5, retinoic acid 1 µM and SAG 0.5 µM on day 2 are taken from Mazzoni 2013 Nat Neurosci (PMID 23955559), a Wichterle-lab paper that cites this unit.
The seeding density printed in the unit itself is not confirmed; another paper from the lab used about 20,000 cells/ml for its retinoid-free variant.
Whether retinoic acid and SAG are included again in the day 5 medium: not stated in the restating paper.
Feeder-removal step details and the unit's own stated efficiency: not confirmed.
The pitfall about the timing window paraphrases the unit's abstract (embryoid bodies become responsive two days after growth-factor withdrawal); no tested alternative days were read.

protocols.name: Neural induction (Noggin + FGFs) then retinoic acid + SAG, with plating for axon outgrowth (JoVE)
protocols.principle: A two-day neural-induction step with Noggin, bFGF and FGF-8 is placed before the retinoic acid + SAG step of the Wichterle method; the authors report that this doubles the yield of Hb9::GFP+ motor neurons. Embryoid bodies are then dissociated and plated with neurotrophic factors.
protocols.efficiency: 51% ± 0.8% GFP+ cells by flow cytometry of dissociated day 7 embryoid bodies (HBG3 line); about 25% without the neural-induction step.
protocols.start_requirements: HBG3 (Hb9-eGFP) mouse ES cells grown for 3 days on mitomycin-C-treated mouse embryonic fibroblasts in ES medium with 10 ng/ml LIF, fed daily. Colonies should be round, compact and about 100 µm across; overgrown, flattened colonies differentiate poorly.
tips: The authors found SAG more effective than purmorphamine: 1-2.5 µM purmorphamine with 1 µM retinoic acid never gave more than 20% GFP+ cells.
Feed ES cells daily; they divide every 12-15 h and exhaust the medium quickly.
pitfalls: ES cells kept 4 days on feeders become overgrown and flat and are a poor starting point.
Feeder cells carried into suspension culture must be removed by moving the embryoid bodies to fresh dishes.

Monothioglycerol is listed as '1mM' as printed; not cross-checked.
Whether serum-containing Neural Differentiation Medium is otherwise supplemented (glutamine, antibiotics) is not stated in the rows read.

factors.name: Noggin

Collect the floating ES cells, spin, and resuspend in Neural Differentiation Medium

The cultures are mixed: the non-motor-neuron cells are mainly spinal interneurons and glia, so sort on GFP if purity matters. Neither Wichterle source could be opened in full, so their numbers come from restating papers by the same lab; the JoVE variant was read directly.

cell_types.name: Brain microvascular endothelial-like cells (blood-brain barrier model)
cell_types.summary: Cells that reproduce the defining functions of the blood-brain barrier: continuous tight junctions with very high transendothelial electrical resistance, BBB nutrient transporters, and polarised efflux pumps. They are used for CNS drug permeability screening and for neurovascular unit models - with the caveat that their endothelial identity is contested.
route: Primitive streak / mesoderm (or co-differentiating neural environment)
cell_types.maturation_note: Barrier phenotype appears within 8-10 days. TEER peaks about 2 days after replating onto a collagen IV/fibronectin or Matrigel-coated insert and then plateaus for about a week; astrocyte, pericyte or neuron co-culture adds a further increment within 24-48 h and keeps it elevated for up to 8 days.

morphology.endpoint: A confluent, contact-inhibited cobblestone sheet of polygonal cells with crisp, continuous junctions. Gaps, overlapping cells or ragged junctions predict low TEER whatever the staining says.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Singularised hPSCs at a precisely controlled 35,000 cells/cm2 (defined protocol) expanded three days.

stages.label: Primitive streak
stages.look: A uniform dense monolayer after 24 h of CHIR99021; nearly every cell is brachyury+.

stages.label: Endothelial progenitors
stages.look: Still a dense sheet; VEGFR2 is nearly universal and the morphology has not yet diverged.

stages.label: Emerging endothelial islands
stages.look: Patches of clearly endothelial, polygonal cells with bright junctions, surrounded in the undefined protocol by neural progenitors and neurons.

stages.label: Purified barrier monolayer
stages.look: After replating, a uniform cobblestone sheet with continuous junctions; this is the stage for TEER and permeability assays.

markers.name: PECAM1
markers.note: Nearly 100% at day 10 in the defined protocol; expressed before VE-cadherin, as in other stem-cell-derived endothelium.

markers.name: CDH5
markers.note: Appears later than PECAM1 and is strongly induced by retinoic acid - a useful maturation readout.

markers.name: VWF
markers.note: Absent during early induction and acquired on subculture; part of the evidence the cells are vascular.

markers.name: SLC2A1
markers.note: Elevated (not merely present) GLUT-1 is the discriminator from peripheral endothelium, and it tracks with nuclear beta-catenin. Used with PECAM1 to define the BMEC population by flow.

markers.name: CLDN5
markers.note: The most informative tight-junction marker: in the defined protocol only about 60% of cells express it without retinoic acid, and non-optimal seeding density gives patchy or discontinuous junctions even when the percentage looks acceptable.

markers.name: OCLN
markers.note: Expressed by nearly all cells regardless of retinoic acid, so on its own it will not warn you about a leaky monolayer - judge distribution, not percentage.

markers.name: TJP1
markers.note: Same caveat as occludin; look for continuous junctional staining.

markers.name: ABCB1
markers.note: Nearly 100% of cells; activity and basolateral-to-apical polarisation confirmed with cyclosporin A.

markers.name: ABCG2
markers.note: Activity confirmed with Ko143; substrate accumulation rises 150-220% with inhibitor.

markers.name: ABCC1
markers.note: Activity confirmed with MK 571.

markers.name: SLC7A5
markers.note: One of the BBB-enriched transporters detected in both protocols.

markers.name: PLVAP
markers.note: Its absence is a positive sign: PLVAP is downregulated as the barrier matures and stays on in peripheral vessels.

markers.name: KRT18
markers.note: Reported as present in all cells of the differentiating population in Lippmann 2012, while K14 and p63 were absent. Central to the later claim that these cells are epithelial rather than endothelial.

markers.name: TP63
markers.note: Reported absent in Lippmann 2012; worth checking given the identity debate.

protocols.name: Neural/endothelial co-differentiation then selective purification
protocols.principle: hPSCs are allowed to co-differentiate in an unconditioned medium so that endothelial progenitors arise inside an embryonic-brain-like environment of neural progenitors and neurons; those neural cells supply WNT7A/WNT7B, nuclear beta-catenin accumulates in the endothelium, and the cells acquire barrier properties. A collagen IV/fibronectin matrix then selects them out.
protocols.efficiency: About 30% GLUT-1+/PECAM-1+ cells at 6 days of UM, rising to 66% after 2 days of EC medium (11.6 BMECs per input hPSC); essentially 100% purity after selective passaging. TEER averaged 860 +/- 260 ohm.cm2 over 30 experiments with a maximum of 1,450 +/- 140 ohm.cm2 on astrocyte co-culture; sucrose permeability 3.4 x 10^-5 cm/min
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs passaged onto Matrigel and expanded 2-3 days in mTeSR1. Cell-line-dependent yield; IMR90-4 and DF19-9-11T iPSCs purified well, H9 hESC-derived cells did not.
tips: The functional panel that distinguishes these cells is the combination, not any one marker: tight junctions plus elevated GLUT-1 plus polarised efflux. P-glycoprotein, BCRP and MRP activity were all confirmed with cyclosporin A, Ko143 and MK 571.
PLVAP and SLCO1A2 transcripts were absent, which is what you want: PLVAP is downregulated as the barrier matures, and SLCO1A2/Oatp14 is rodent-specific.
Permeability of seven radiolabelled compounds correlated with in vivo rodent brain uptake at R2 = 0.98, with a 40-fold dynamic range between diazepam and sucrose.
Subculturing too early (after only 4 days of UM) gives cells that express BBB markers but never reach confluence and have malformed, discontinuous junctions.
pitfalls: Line-dependent: H9-derived BMECs could not be separated from non-brain PECAM-1+/GLUT-1-negative endothelium on collagen/fibronectin, because all endothelium likes that matrix.
The medium is undefined (knockout serum replacement, platelet-poor plasma serum), so batch and line variability in yield is expected - see Qian 2017 for the defined replacement.
Wnt inhibition with XAV-939 lowered GLUT-1+ cells from 64% to 46% but left claudin-5 and occludin untouched, so beta-catenin is only part of the specification.

Identity caveat: Lu TM, Houghton S, Magdeldin T, et al., PNAS 2021;118:e2016950118 (PMID 33542154, doi 10.1073/pnas.2016950118) report that hPSC-derived cells made this way are transcriptionally epithelial rather than endothelial and need ETS factors to acquire a true vascular fate. Treat these cultures as a barrier model, not as authenticated brain endothelium, and state which you mean.
unverified: Lippmann and colleagues tested K14, p63 and K18 epithelial markers and reported K14 and p63 absent but K18 present in all cells of the differentiating population; this is relevant to the later epithelial-identity debate and is reported here as the source states it.

protocols.name: Defined route: CHIR99021 to mesoderm, then retinoic acid
protocols.principle: Brain endothelium comes from mesoderm, so canonical WNT activation with CHIR99021 is used first to take hPSCs through primitive streak and intermediate mesoderm to endothelial progenitors; retinoic acid then confers the BBB phenotype. Everything is chemically defined and the barrier is tighter than the co-differentiation route.
protocols.efficiency: Nearly 100% brachyury+ at 24 h, >90% PAX2+ at day 4, nearly 100% VEGFR2+ at day 5 and nearly 100% CD31+ at day 10; TEER above 3,000 ohm.cm2 in monoculture (around 4,000 with retinoic acid), rising a further ~30% with pericyte then astrocyte/neuron co-culture. Transcriptome correlates with primary human BMECs at r = 0.77 and expresses 206 of 234 BBB-relevant tight-junction/transporter genes
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs singularised with Accutase and plated on Matrigel (or vitronectin/Synthemax) at 35,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 with 10 uM Y-27632, then expanded three days. Seeding density is critical and 35,000 cells/cm2 was optimal for all three lines tested.
materials: Primary human pericytes, hPSC-derived astrocytes and neurons (optional)
tips: Seeding density is the single most sensitive parameter: only 35,000 cells/cm2 gave substantial barrier function. Other densities still gave >90% CD31+ and ~100% P-gp+ cells but with patchy claudin-5 and occludin and TEER stuck around 1,000 ohm.cm2.
Retinoic acid is not needed to make endothelium, only to make it barrier-like; it is the step to check if TEER is low but CD31 is high.
Fully defined matrices work: vitronectin performed closer to Matrigel than Synthemax did.
Compared head to head, this defined route gave higher TEER and lower batch-to-batch variation than the undefined co-differentiation protocol.
pitfalls: The mechanism by which density acts was not determined, so it has to be re-optimised empirically for a new line or lab.
Occludin and ZO-1 are expressed by nearly all cells even without retinoic acid, so those two markers will not warn you about a leaky monolayer - claudin-5 localisation and TEER will.

Identity caveat, as for Lippmann 2012: Lu TM, Houghton S, Magdeldin T, et al., PNAS 2021;118:e2016950118 (PMID 33542154, doi 10.1073/pnas.2016950118) argue these cells are misidentified epithelium that requires ETS factors for a vascular fate. The barrier phenotype is real and useful; the endothelial identity is contested.

stages.name: Primitive streak induction

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: canonical WNT activation; drives primitive streak

stages.name: Mesoderm to endothelial progenitors
stages.feeding: Daily medium change for 5 days

stages.checkpoint: >90% PAX2+ intermediate mesoderm at day 4; nearly 100% VEGFR2+ endothelial progenitors at day 5

stages.name: Retinoic acid-driven BBB specification
stages.base_medium: hECSR1: human endothelial serum-free medium with 1x B27

factors.name: Retinoic acid
factors.role: confers BBB phenotype; raises tight-junction and efflux transporter genes 3-20 fold

stages.feeding: Per schedule, 2 days
actions: Switch to hECSR1 on day 6 for two days
stages.checkpoint: CDH5 strongly induced; CLDN5, OCLN, TJP1 and ABCB1 up. Without retinoic acid only about 60% of the cells express claudin-5 and junctional distribution is patchy

stages.name: Replating and barrier formation
stages.base_medium: hECSR1 at replating, then hECSR2 (hECSR1 without retinoic acid or bFGF) from day 9

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: improves attachment, used in the no-retinoic-acid comparison

stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Dissociate with Accutase on day 8 and replate at 1 x 10^6 cells/cm2 onto Matrigel-coated plates or Transwell inserts (collagen IV 400 ug/mL + fibronectin 100 ug/mL if differentiating on vitronectin/Synthemax)
Switch to hECSR2 on day 9 for longer-term maintenance
stages.checkpoint: TEER peaks 2 days after replating and plateaus above 2,000 ohm.cm2 through day 7; essentially 100% CD31+, with vWF, acetylated LDL uptake, VEGF-dependent tube formation and TNF-alpha-inducible ICAM-1; P-gp, BCRP and MRP accumulation assays show 150-220% increases with their specific inhibitors, and P-gp efflux is polarised basolateral-to-apical

stages.name: Neurovascular unit co-culture (optional)
stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Co-culture day-8 cells on Transwells with primary human pericytes for 24 h, then with hPSC EZ sphere-derived astrocytes and neurons (1:3) for three more days
stages.checkpoint: A further ~30% TEER rise at day 2 and a sustained elevation versus monoculture

cell_types.notes: Be explicit about what these cells are. Both protocols produce a monolayer with a barrier far tighter than primary human BMECs (339 +/- 107 ohm.cm2 in the best biopsy-derived cultures) or immortalised lines (hCMEC/D3, about 199 ohm.cm2), with correct transporter expression and polarised efflux - an excellent permeability screening platform. But Lu TM, Houghton S, Magdeldin T, et al., PNAS 2021;118:e2016950118 (PMID 33542154, doi 10.1073/pnas.2016950118) argue that cells made this way are transcriptionally epithelial rather than endothelial, and that ETS transcription factors are needed to give them a true vascular fate; the Lippmann paper itself reports cytokeratin 18 in all cells of the differentiating population. The practical consequence: call them BMEC-like or a BBB barrier model, check epithelial markers if identity matters to your claim, and do not use them as a model of brain angiogenesis. On the technical side, the defined protocol is more reproducible but extremely sensitive to one number - the initial seeding density of 35,000 cells/cm2.

cell_types.name: Neural progenitor cells
cell_types.summary: Proliferating PAX6+/SOX2+ neuroepithelial cells, the common ancestor of every CNS neuron and glial cell. Almost all CNS differentiation protocols pass through this stage, so it is the point at which regional identity is set and the stage most often banked, expanded or patterned.
cell_types.maturation_note: PAX6 by day 7-11 and >80-95% purity by day 11-15; rosettes with apical ZO-1 appear after the first passage. Patterning has to be applied in a narrow window (around day 5 to day 18 depending on protocol) - after that, regional identity is largely fixed.

morphology.endpoint: A dense sheet of small, tightly packed columnar cells with almost no cytoplasm visible between nuclei, organised into radial rosettes with a bright central lumen. Mitotic figures sit at the lumen. Flatter, more spread cells at the colony edges are usually non-neural contamination.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat, compact colonies of small cells with sharp borders and a high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio.

stages.label: Even monolayer
stages.look: The culture has filled in to a uniform near-confluent sheet; gaps or uneven density here predict patchy induction.

stages.label: Neuroectoderm
stages.look: Cells become smaller and more uniform, and the sheet starts to look multilayered and refractile under phase.

stages.label: Neuroepithelium
stages.look: A thick, pseudostratified sheet of columnar cells; the surface looks optically bright and slightly ridged.

stages.label: Neural rosettes
stages.look: Clear radial rosettes 100-300 um across with a bright central lumen; three to ten per colony is typical.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be gone by about day 5 of dual SMAD inhibition; persistence means incomplete induction.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Lost rapidly after SB431542 is added - the Activin/Nodal block is what collapses it.

markers.name: FGF5
markers.note: Peaks around day 5 with OTX2, marking the transient epiblast-like state between pluripotency and neural fate.

markers.name: SOX1
markers.note: The earliest neural marker in dual SMAD inhibition, appearing before ZIC1 and PAX6.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: The standard purity readout: >80% at day 11 (Chambers) and >95% at day 15 with a retinoid (Shi).

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Pan-neural-stem-cell; also expressed in pluripotent cells, so never use it alone.

markers.name: NES
markers.note: General neural stem/progenitor marker; broad but useful for morphology.

markers.name: TJP1
markers.note: Apical ZO-1 ringing the rosette lumen is the sign of a properly polarised neuroepithelium.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Anterior/telencephalic identity; raised by WNT inhibition with XAV939 or DKK1.

markers.name: OTX2
markers.note: Anterior marker retained through neural commitment; also an epiblast marker at day 5.

markers.name: NGFR
markers.note: Marks the neural crest fraction. Low plating density pushes the culture this way; with PAX6-negative cells also expressing AP2, HNK1 and PAX7.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Neural crest; should be absent in a CNS progenitor prep.

markers.name: HOXB4
markers.note: Caudal identity. Absent in anterior/cortical cultures; expected (deliberately) in spinal protocols.

markers.name: T
markers.note: Mesoderm escape; suppressed by SB431542.

functional_assays: Rosette formation after passage
Interkinetic nuclear migration by time-lapse
Apical mitoses (phospho-histone H3 at the lumen)
Response to patterning factors (SHH, RA, WNT)
qc: PAX6+ >= 80% by flow or ICC at day 11 (Chambers 2009)
OCT4 negative by day 5-7
T (brachyury) and SOX17 not detectable by qPCR
p75/HNK1 neural crest fraction low
Apical ZO-1 in rosettes after the first passage

protocols.name: Dual-SMAD inhibition (Noggin + SB431542)
protocols.principle: Blocking BMP and Activin/Nodal/TGF-beta signalling at the same time strips away the signals that keep hPSCs pluripotent or push them to mesendoderm and trophoblast, so an adherent monolayer converts almost entirely to PAX6+ neuroepithelium in under two weeks.
protocols.efficiency: >80% PAX6+ cells at day 11; 82% reporter-positive neural precursors at day 13 by flow, about 3-fold more than the MS5 stromal-feeder protocol
protocols.start_requirements: hESC/hiPSC dissociated to single cells with Accutase, pre-plated on gelatin to remove feeders, then plated on Matrigel at 10,000-25,000 cells/cm2 (18,000 cells/cm2 optimal) in MEF-conditioned hESC medium with 10 ng/mL FGF2 and ROCK inhibitor; expand ~3 days to near confluence before day 0. Plating density sets the CNS vs neural crest ratio.
tips: The authors note comparable neural conversion when the inhibitors are given only for the first 5 days, which saves a lot of recombinant Noggin.
Most labs now swap Noggin for the small-molecule ALK2/3 inhibitor LDN-193189 (100 nM); that LSB variant is the backbone of the Maroof, Tchieu and Kim/Studer protocols.
Early neuroepithelium here is non-polarised; rosettes with apical ZO-1 appear after the first passage.
pitfalls: Low plating density shifts the output to PAX6-negative neural crest (AP2, HNK1, PAX7, p75) instead of CNS.
Very high density blunts the response to patterning factors, so pattern around day 5 and passage near day 11.
SB431542 alone drives CDX2/trophoblast; Noggin alone leaves <10% PAX6+ - both inhibitors are needed.
unverified: SB431542 dose: the published methods state 10 nM, which is widely treated as a typographical error; 10 uM is the dose used in the authors' later LSB protocols. Confirm against your own reference before use.
Y-27632 concentration not stated in the paper's methods.

Withdraw ROCK inhibitor after 24 h and let the culture reach near confluence
stages.checkpoint: Even, near-confluent monolayer with no gaps - uneven density gives patchy induction

stages.name: Dual SMAD inhibition

factors.name: Noggin
factors.role: BMP antagonist; suppresses CDX2/trophoblast and endoderm

factors.name: SB431542
factors.conc: 10 uM (the paper's methods text prints 10 nM)
factors.role: ALK4/5/7 inhibitor; collapses NANOG and blocks mesoderm

stages.feeding: Daily change
actions: Switch to KSR medium with both inhibitors on day 0
Expect OCT4 to be lost by about day 5
stages.checkpoint: Peak FGF5 and OTX2 around day 5 marks the transient epiblast-like state; OCT4 should be gone

stages.name: SMAD block narrowed, N2 ramp
stages.base_medium: KSR medium progressively replaced by N2 medium (25%, 50%, 75% every two days)
stages.feeding: Medium change every two days with increasing N2 fraction
actions: Withdraw SB431542 on day 5
Step the N2 fraction up every two days while keeping Noggin
Score PAX6 by day 11; passage at day 11-12 if you intend to pattern or make rosettes

protocols.name: LSB (+XAV939) to dorsal forebrain NSCs and rosettes
protocols.principle: A fully small-molecule update of dual-SMAD inhibition in Essential 6 medium: LDN-193189 replaces Noggin, and a short pulse of the tankyrase inhibitor XAV939 holds the cells anterior, giving dorsal forebrain neural stem cells that can be re-plated as droplets to form rosettes.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated to single cells and plated on Matrigel at 2.5-3.0 x 10^5 cells/cm2 in Essential 8 with 10 uM Y-27632 the day before day 0.
tips: The same paper gives the ventral spinal cord variant: LSB from day 0 with 1 uM retinoic acid plus 1 uM purmorphamine added from day 1 to day 12 - a convenient way to get regionally matched progenitors.
These NSCs are neurogenic for months; glial competence has to be forced (see the NFIA astrocyte protocol).
pitfalls: Passaging rosette-stage NSCs at low density lets them differentiate spontaneously.
Dropping XAV939 can let iPSC lines drift posterior and lose FOXG1.
unverified: Concentrations of SHH, FGF8, BDNF and ascorbic acid in N2-BASF are not given in the paper text.
Exact droplet cell number is garbled in the available full text.

source.authors: Tchieu J, Calder EL, Guttikonda SR, et al.
source.title: NFIA is a gliogenic switch enabling rapid derivation of functional human astrocytes from pluripotent stem cells.

stages.name: Dual SMAD inhibition (anteriorised)

factors.name: XAV939
factors.role: tankyrase/WNT inhibitor, days 0-2 only; reinforces forebrain (FOXG1) identity - recommended for iPSC lines

stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Start LSB on day 0 and change medium every day through day 8
Add XAV939 for the first three days only, then continue with LSB alone
stages.checkpoint: Uniform neuroepithelial sheet by day 8

stages.name: Rosette formation
stages.base_medium: N2 medium with BDNF, ascorbic acid, SHH and FGF8 (N2-BASF)

factors.name: SHH
factors.role: component of the N2-BASF rosette medium

factors.name: FGF8
factors.role: component of the N2-BASF rosette medium

stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Dissociate with Accutase for 30 min, pass through a 40 um strainer
Re-plate as high-density droplets on air-dried poly-ornithine/laminin/fibronectin, let them attach 15-20 min, then overlay with medium
Expect rosettes 2-3 days later (around day 11-12)
stages.checkpoint: Radially organised rosettes; re-plate at high density (3.5 x 10^5 cells/cm2) to stop spontaneous differentiation

protocols.name: STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction (monolayer protocol)
protocols.principle: Single hPSCs are plated at very high density and kept in neural induction medium with a dual-SMAD-inhibiting supplement, which pushes them to CNS-type neural progenitors and suppresses non-CNS fates. Three passages in the same medium yield expandable PAX6/SOX1/Nestin-positive NPCs.
protocols.efficiency: Expected by ICC: PAX6, SOX1 and Nestin each ≥ 80 - 90%; SOX10 (neural crest) ≤ 10%; OCT4 negligible
protocols.start_requirements: High-quality feeder-free hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus, TeSR-E8 or TeSR-AOF (SMADi supplement highly recommended for TeSR-E8 cells). Dissociate to single cells with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (8 - 10 min, 37°C) and plate 2 x 10^5 cells/cm2 (2 x 10^6 cells in 2 mL per well of a 6-well plate; 2 - 2.5 x 10^5 cells/cm2 recommended) on PLO/laminin (15 µg/mL PLO, 10 µg/mL laminin) or Matrigel, in induction medium with 10 µM Y-27632.
materials: STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (08581; 2 Pack 08582)
Poly-L-ornithine (Sigma P4957) and laminin (Sigma L2020) or Corning Matrigel hESC-Qualified Matrix (Corning 354277)
STEMdiff Neural Progenitor Medium (05833) for NPC expansion
STEMdiff Neural Progenitor Freezing Medium (05838), optional
tips: Complete medium (0.5 mL supplement per 250 mL) keeps 2 weeks at 2 - 8°C, or can be frozen in aliquots at -20°C; do not re-freeze.
If cells die or peel off before day 6, lower the day-0 seeding density.
Morphology alone does not confirm induction: stain at least two neural markers, and never rely on Nestin alone because neural crest cells also express it.
The manual also describes an automated 96-well version (1 - 2 x 10^5 cells/cm2 on Matrigel) that is fixed after 6 - 9 days.
pitfalls: Passaging before day 6 because the well looks confluent reduces induction efficiency.
Using the cells before passage 3 (day 18 - 21) risks carry-over of OCT4+ cells, poor expansion and poor downstream neural differentiation.
Low-quality or partly differentiated hPSCs at the start give poor induction.
unverified: Protocol schematic (manual Figure 1) is an image; day numbers here come from the written steps only.
Stage boundaries use the earliest day of each range the manual gives (passage 1 day 6 - 9, passage 2 day 12 - 15, passage 3 day 18 - 21).

protocols.name: STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction (embryoid body protocol)
protocols.principle: hPSCs are aggregated into uniform 10,000-cell embryoid bodies in AggreWell800 plates in SMAD-inhibiting induction medium, then plated so that neural rosettes form. Rosettes are lifted selectively with a non-enzymatic selection reagent and replated to give CNS-type NPCs.
protocols.efficiency: Expected by ICC: PAX6, SOX1 and Nestin each ≥ 80 - 90%; SOX10 (neural crest) ≤ 10%; OCT4 negligible. Rosette selection works best when ≥ 75% of attached EBs are rosette-rich on day 8
protocols.start_requirements: High-quality feeder-free hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8 (SMADi supplement highly recommended for TeSR-E8 cells). Dissociate to single cells with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent and seed 3 x 10^6 cells per well of an AggreWell800 24-well plate (10,000 cells per microwell) pre-treated with Anti-Adherence Rinsing Solution, in induction medium with 10 µM Y-27632 (2 mL final per well).
materials: STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (08581; 2 Pack 08582)
37 µm Reversible Strainer (27215 small or 27250 large)
Poly-L-ornithine (Sigma P4957) and laminin (Sigma L2020) or Corning Matrigel hESC-Qualified Matrix (Corning 354277)
ACCUTASE (07920) and STEMdiff Neural Progenitor Medium (05833) for NPC passaging
tips: Heavy cell death on day 13, the day after selection, is typical and does not reduce the final NPC yield.
Do not over-select rosettes: leaving some behind costs a little yield but keeps non-CNS cells out.
The selection-reagent incubation time may need optimising per line.
The forebrain neuron PIS quotes an average of 3 NPCs per input hPSC for this EB route (27 for the monolayer route).
pitfalls: Breaking EBs into small clusters or single cells when harvesting or plating causes cell death and low NPC yield; use wide-bore tips.
More than 20,000 cells per microwell overflows the microwells; 10,000 is recommended.
Fast pipetting or shaking the plate during feeds dislodges EBs from the microwells.
unverified: Protocol schematic (manual Figure 1) is an image; day numbers here come from the written steps only.
Downstream kit sheets describe rosette selection on day 11 - 12; the manual's protocol heading says day 12.

protocols.name: Gibco PSC Neural Induction Medium (7-day monolayer NSC induction)
protocols.principle: A serum-free Neurobasal-based medium with a single 50X supplement converts adherent hPSC clumps into neural stem cells in seven days without embryoid bodies or manual rosette picking. The same supplement in a Neurobasal/Advanced DMEM/F-12 mix is then used to expand the NSCs.
protocols.efficiency: Vendor product page: NSCs show >80% SOX1, SOX2 and Nestin expression with <1% OCT4; the user guide notes only about 15-50% are PAX6-positive
protocols.start_requirements: High-quality feeder-free hPSCs (Essential 8 on vitronectin or Geltrex, or StemPro hESC SFM on Geltrex) at about 70-80% confluence, with differentiated colonies removed. Passage as small clumps (not single cells) onto a 6-well plate coated with the same matrix at 2.5-3 × 10^5 cells per well in 2.5 mL PSC medium, so the wells are 15-25% confluent the next day. 10 µM Y-27632 overnight at splitting is optional.
materials: PSC Neural Induction Medium (A1647801: 500 mL Neurobasal Medium + 10 mL Neural Induction Supplement 50X)
Advanced DMEM/F-12 (12634) for the expansion medium
Geltrex LDEV-Free hESC-qualified Reduced Growth Factor Basement Membrane Matrix (A1413301 or A1413302), used 1:100
Optional: Human Neural Stem Cell Immunocytochemistry Kit (A24354)
tips: Schedule from Thermo protocol MAN0008031 Rev. A.0; day 0 is the first day in induction medium, one day after splitting.
Complete medium keeps for 2 weeks at 2-8°C in the dark; warm it for no more than 10 minutes at 37°C.
Use plates or dishes rather than flasks so that non-neural colonies can be picked off.
For hPSCs grown in Essential 8 that lift during induction, the guide suggests coating with 10 µg/mL vitronectin.
Flat non-neural contaminants in early NSC passages can be removed by a short (3-4 min, room temperature) Accutase pre-treatment that detaches them first.
The vendor reports more than 20 million NSCs from 1 million PSCs.

cell_types.notes: Plating density is the hidden variable: Chambers and colleagues showed it sets the ratio of CNS to neural crest progeny, with high density favouring PAX6+ CNS cells. cell_types.name: Cortical excitatory neurons
cell_types.summary: Glutamatergic projection neurons of the cerebral cortex, about 80% of cortical neurons, generated in a fixed deep-to-superficial temporal order. They are the workhorse of hPSC disease modelling for Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, autism and epilepsy, and the substrate for most human synaptic-function assays.
cell_types.maturation_note: Directed differentiation: TBR1+ layer-6 neurons within days of neurogenesis onset, BRN2/CUX1 from days 25-30, SATB2 from days 65-80, astrocytes from about day 60. AMPA-mediated synapses by day 50 and action-potential trains by day 65. Transcription-factor programming compresses this to about 14 days but gives an immature layer 2/3-like neuron with no NMDA receptors at 3 weeks.

morphology.endpoint: A dense network of small, round-to-pyramidal cell bodies connected by long, branched neurites that cross and bundle into fascicles. In directed-differentiation cultures the neurons sit in clumps around residual rosettes with flat astrocytes appearing underneath after about two months.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact flat colonies with sharp edges; neural induction only starts once they are about 95% confluent.

stages.label: Cortical neuroepithelium
stages.look: A thick, bright pseudostratified sheet of columnar cells with no visible gaps.

stages.label: Cortical rosettes
stages.look: Radial rosettes with apical lumens; mitoses at the lumen and a rim of smaller Tbr2+ cells at the periphery.

stages.label: Early neurogenesis
stages.look: Short neurites emerge from the rosette edges; a mesh of fine processes starts to cover the space between rosettes.

stages.label: Layered cortical network
stages.look: Dense neurite network with bundled fascicles, neuronal cell bodies piled above the progenitor layer.

stages.label: Mixed neurons and astrocytes
stages.look: Flat stellate astrocytes spread under the neuronal network from about day 60 onwards.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent; in NGN2 programming, SOX2, OCT4 and NANOG immunoreactivity is gone by day 21.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: >95% at day 15 in the retinoid-dependent Shi/Livesey protocol; only ~25% without retinoids.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Telencephalic identity. Also induced strongly in NGN2 iN cells.

markers.name: EMX1
markers.note: Dorsal telencephalic; high in cortical rosettes and absent in ventralised cultures.

markers.name: EOMES
markers.note: Basal/intermediate progenitors at the rosette rim; about 15% of rosette cells at day 25, roughly half of them still cycling.

markers.name: TBR1
markers.note: First projection-neuron subtype to appear; peaks at about 41% of cells at day 76 in cortical spheroids.

markers.name: BCL11B
markers.note: Subcortical projection neurons; high early then declining. Only ~3% of cells co-express CTIP2 and SATB2, as expected for mutually exclusive programmes.

markers.name: SATB2
markers.note: Late marker, from days 65-80 in 2D and rising up to 7-fold between days 52 and 137 in spheroids - the honest test of whether a culture has been run long enough.

markers.name: POU3F2
markers.note: Layer 2-4 and late progenitors; peaks before SATB2. Also high in NGN2 iN cells.

markers.name: MAP2
markers.note: Pan-neuronal dendritic marker; used to score conversion efficiency in programming protocols.

markers.name: RBFOX3
markers.note: Only appears in human forebrain after about 20 weeks gestation; 36 +/- 4% of cells at day 76 in spheroids.

markers.name: SLC17A7
markers.note: Presynaptic glutamate transporter; co-localises with PSD95 at excitatory synapses. NGN2 neurons express mostly SLC17A6 (VGLUT2) with VGLUT1 in about 20% of cells.

markers.name: DLG4
markers.note: About 90% of PSD95 puncta sit within one puncta-diameter of synaptophysin, i.e. they are real synapses.

markers.name: GAD1
markers.note: Should be absent: cortical interneurons come from the ventral telencephalon and are not made by these protocols. Its appearance means the culture has been ventralised.

functional_assays: Whole-cell patch clamp: action potential trains, TTX-sensitive sodium currents
Spontaneous and evoked EPSCs blocked by CNQX/NBQX
Calcium imaging (Fura-2 or GCaMP) of network activity
Acute slice recording from cortical spheroids
BrdU/EdU birthdating to confirm the deep-to-superficial order
Super-resolution or array tomography of pre/post-synaptic puncta
qc: PAX6+ > 90-95% at day 15 before the onset of neurogenesis
Roughly equal deep (TBR1/CTIP2) and upper (SATB2/BRN2) layer neurons by day 70 in directed differentiation
CNQX-sensitive mEPSCs recordable by day 50
No GAD67+ cells in a dorsal cortical prep
For NGN2 programming: >90% of transduced cells MAP2+ or NeuN+

protocols.name: Retinoid + dual SMAD inhibition: cortical rosettes to layered projection neurons
protocols.principle: Dual SMAD inhibition in a 1:1 N2/B27 medium plus retinoid signalling turns hPSCs into dorsal forebrain rosettes containing apical and basal progenitors; withdrawing FGF2 then lets them run a months-long, developmentally ordered wave of neurogenesis from deep- to upper-layer neurons.
protocols.efficiency: >95% PAX6+/OTX1/2+/vimentin+ cortical progenitors 15 days after induction; roughly equal numbers of deep- and upper-layer projection neurons by day 70; without retinoids only ~25% PAX6+
protocols.start_requirements: hESC/hiPSC dissociated with Accutase, pre-plated 1 h on gelatin to deplete feeders, then plated on Matrigel-coated 12-well plates in MEF-conditioned hESC medium with 10 ng/mL FGF2. Neural induction only begins once the monolayer is 95% confluent.
materials: N2 and B27 (with vitamin A) supplements
tips: The step-by-step version of this method is Shi Y, Kirwan P, Livesey FJ, Nat Protoc 2012;7:1836-46 (PMID 22976355, doi 10.1038/nprot.2012.116), described there as an 80-day three-stage process.
No GABAergic interneurons arise under these conditions - the cortex gets its interneurons from the ventral telencephalon, so add them separately if you want balanced networks.
Early rosettes stay plastic: purmorphamine ventralises them and yields GAD67+ interneurons instead.
pitfalls: Dropping the retinoid leaves only scattered PAX6+ patches (~25%) - this is the step most often got wrong.
Inhibiting hedgehog signalling does not help cortical induction in human cells, contrary to the mouse rule of thumb.
Upper-layer (SATB2+) neurons simply need time; cultures ended at day 40 will look deep-layer biased.
unverified: Retinoid identities are given (retinol acetate, all-trans retinol) but concentrations are not stated in the paper's methods.
Day boundaries for induction are a range (8-11 days) in the source; 10 is used here as the typical value.

protocols.name: NGN2 forced expression (one transcription factor, ~2 weeks)
protocols.principle: Doxycycline-inducible neurogenin-2 converts hPSCs directly into excitatory, layer 2/3-like forebrain neurons in under two weeks, bypassing progenitor stages; mouse glia are added to support synapse formation.
protocols.efficiency: Nearly 100% of surviving transduced cells become neurons; single-cell profiling shows a homogeneous excitatory population whose properties are indistinguishable across one ESC and two iPSC lines
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs in mTeSR1 dissociated with Accutase and plated on Matrigel-coated coverslips with 2 uM thiazovivin; H1 ESC 1 x 10^5 and iPSC 1.5 x 10^5 cells per well of a 24-well plate on day -2.
tips: NeuroD1 works about as well as NGN2 in this system; the authors chose NGN2 and stayed with it.
The neurons are telencephalic and excitatory (BRN2, CUX1, FOXG1, vGLUT2 with some vGLUT1) and read as relatively immature layer 2/3; they lack vGAT and GAD.
Co-culture with mouse cortical neurons rather than glia alone adds inhibitory inputs and lets the human neurons integrate into a network.
pitfalls: Astrocyte support is doing real work here: without mouse glia, synapse formation is poor.
The population is deliberately homogeneous, which is a liability if your phenotype lives in a specific neuronal subtype.
NMDA receptors are essentially absent at 3 weeks - plan longer culture if you need them.

protocols.name: STEMdiff Forebrain Neuron Differentiation + Maturation
protocols.principle: CNS-type NPCs made with the SMADi neural induction kit are turned into forebrain neuron precursors over 6 days in differentiation medium, then replated and matured for at least 14 days in a BrainPhys-based medium into a mixed population of excitatory and inhibitory FOXG1-positive neurons.
protocols.start_requirements: Starts from NPCs, not hPSCs: generate them with STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (Catalog #08581) by the monolayer protocol (passage 3, day 18 - 21) or the EB protocol (after rosette selection, day 11/12); NPCs expanded for ≤ 5 passages or thawed NPCs in STEMdiff Neural Progenitor Medium (05833) also work. Plate single NPCs (ACCUTASE) at 80,000 - 125,000 cells/cm2 on PLO/laminin (15 µg/mL PLO, 5 µg/mL laminin) in 2 mL per well of a 6-well plate for 24 h before switching medium. Day numbers follow the PIS, which counts from day 0 of neural induction with STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (monolayer route shown; where the PIS gives a range, the earliest day is used). duration_days counts from NPC plating.
materials: STEMdiff Forebrain Neuron Differentiation Kit (08600, 100 mL; 100-1691, 500 mL)
STEMdiff Forebrain Neuron Maturation Kit (08605, 125 mL; 100-1659, 625 mL)
STEMdiff Neural Progenitor Medium (05833) if starting from expanded or frozen NPCs
CryoStor CS10 (07930) for optional freezing of precursors
tips: Both complete media keep up to 4 weeks at 2 - 8°C; protect the BrainPhys-based maturation medium from light.
NPC and precursor seeding densities need optimising per line and per application.
Thawed precursors are typically 70 - 90% viable; add 10 µM Y-27632 during resuspension and plating if recovery is poor.
One differentiation kit gives on average 20 million precursors; one maturation kit supports up to 4.5 million neurons for 14 days.
pitfalls: Neurons generally cannot be passaged once maturation has begun, so seed precursors straight into the final cultureware.
Fast medium changes detach neurons: add medium dropwise against the vessel wall.
NPCs expanded beyond 5 passages differentiate less well.
unverified: No purity percentage for the neurons is given in the PIS, so efficiency is null.
The two protocol diagrams are images; days come from the written steps (EB route: differentiation medium day 12/13, passage day 18/19; monolayer route: day 19 - 22 and day 25 - 28).
Day 39 is day 25 plus the stated minimum of 14 days of maturation; the PIS does not print that day number.
