protocols.name: Quick-Neuron Excitatory - SeV Kit
protocols.principle: A temperature-sensitive Sendai virus delivers a proprietary transcription-factor set to hPSCs in suspension; the virus replicates at 33 C, is switched off by shifting to 37 C on day 2, and puromycin selection removes untransduced cells, giving footprint-free glutamatergic neurons in 10 days.
protocols.efficiency: The release specification for the matching ready-made cell product (EX-SeV-HC-CW50065) is over 80% TUBB3+ and over 50% VGLUT1+/TUBB3+ at day 7 post-differentiation; no separate figure is published for user runs with the kit
protocols.start_requirements: Source hPSCs must have been maintained by single-cell passaging (StemFit Basic04, StemFit AK02N or StemFlex) and be at least 14 days post-thaw. Wells of a 6-well plate are precoated on day -3 with iMatrix-511 silk at 0.25 ug/cm2 in 2 mL chilled PBS and held at 4 C (or coated on day 0 and warmed 2 h at 37 C). Starting cultures must be 50-70% confluent and never above 90%. ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 is used at 10 uM stock diluted 1:1000 (final 10 uM) in the pre-harvest and plating media. A puromycin kill curve must be run in advance; the vendor's internal range is 0.5-2 ug/mL. This kit needs about 3.3 x 10^6 viable hPSCs, usually 3 wells of a 6-well plate at 50-70% confluency, and a stable 33 C, 5% CO2 incubator. One kit covers 6 wells of a 6-well plate.
materials: Quick-Neuron Excitatory - SeV Kit (EX-SeV): QN-SeV-P, Component N, Component G1, Component G2, Component P
0.01% poly-L-ornithine (Sigma P4957) and laminin mouse protein natural (Thermo 23017015) or Geltrex (A15696-01) for the replating plate
StemFit Basic04 Complete Type (AMSBio SF041-001), StemFit AK02N or StemFlex (Thermo A3349401)
TrypLE Select Enzyme 1X (Thermo 12563011) and 0.02% EDTA in DPBS (Sigma E8008) for Solution D1
ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 (Selleckchem S1049) and DMSO (Sigma D2650)
Optional STEM-CELLBANKER (AMSBIO 11890) for cryopreserving at the day-3 passage
Quick-Neuron Excitatory Maintenance Medium (EX-MM) for day 10 onward
tips: Set the 33 C incubator up and let it stabilise before day 0; the whole early schedule depends on it
Sendai virus is sensitive to shear - mix by tapping the tube, never vortexing or pipetting
Run two untransduced wells alongside, one with puromycin, to prove the selection works
The user guide is written assuming day 0 is a Monday (Tuesday if you plan to freeze rather than passage on day 3)
pitfalls: Starting cultures above 90% confluency are explicitly ruled out, and cells must be at least 14 days post-thaw
Biosafety level 2 containment is required for the Sendai virus even though it is non-pathogenic in humans
At the day-3 passage, over-pipetting damages neurons that have already detached
unverified: No purity figure is published for user differentiations; the quoted percentages are release specifications for the ready-made neuron product
No stated viability expectation at the day-3 passage for live replating (the freezing appendix quotes over 50% post-thaw viability)

cell_types.notes: Choose the route by what you need. Directed differentiation gives the real developmental sequence, progenitor diversity (including outer radial glia) and all layer identities, but takes 70-100 days and varies between lines. Transcription-factor programming gives a homogeneous, reproducible population in two weeks - the Zhang paper's central point was that NGN2 overrides epigenetic differences between lines - but the neurons are immature layer 2/3-like cells, lack NMDA receptors at 3 weeks, and need glia (usually mouse astrocytes) to form synapses. The i3Neuron version removes the virus from the workflow altogether. No protocol here makes interneurons: they must be added separately.

cell_types.name: Spinal motor neurons
cell_types.summary: Cholinergic neurons of the ventral spinal cord that project to skeletal muscle, derived through the OLIG2+ pMN progenitor domain by caudalising with WNT/retinoic acid and ventralising with a SHH agonist. They are the central cell type for ALS and spinal muscular atrophy modelling and for neuromuscular junction assays.
cell_types.maturation_note: OLIG2+ progenitors by day 12, MNX1/ISL1+ neurons by day 18, and CHAT+ functionally mature motor neurons after a further 10 days of Notch inhibition. Notch inhibition is what makes the difference: without it only about 47% of cells are CHAT+ after two weeks, with it 91%.

morphology.endpoint: Large neuronal cell bodies, noticeably bigger than cortical neurons, with thick primary processes and long axons that often run in bundles. In Notch-inhibited cultures the background is clean, with no small dividing cells between the neurons.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Colonies split 1:6 the day before induction; no spontaneous differentiation.

stages.label: Caudal neuroepithelium
stages.look: A uniform dense sheet of small cells, more than 98% SOX1+, that looks the same as any neuroepithelium under phase - the HOX identity is only visible by staining.

stages.label: OLIG2+ pMN progenitors
stages.look: Still a dense progenitor monolayer; expandable, and spheres re-form readily when the cells are lifted.

stages.label: Motor neuron precursors
stages.look: Round suspension aggregates from which neurons emerge once plated; MNX1/ISL1 positive.

stages.label: Mature motor neurons
stages.look: Large cell bodies with thick processes on Matrigel or an astrocyte feeder; no proliferating cells remain after Compound E.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent.

markers.name: SOX1
markers.note: >98% at day 6 with CHIR + SB431542 + DMH-1; CHIR also raises the absolute yield about 2.8-fold.

markers.name: HOXA3
markers.note: Confirms caudalisation; without CHIR the cells stay rostral and express OTX2 instead.

markers.name: OLIG2
markers.note: 95 +/- 3% at day 12 with CHIR/SB/DMH-1/RA/purmorphamine; the expandable progenitor stage.

markers.name: NKX2-2
markers.note: The marker most often missed: with RA + SHH alone up to 40% of OLIG2+ cells also express NKX2-2, which blocks their differentiation into motor neurons. WNT keeps it off; good cultures have <0.5% double positives.

markers.name: MNX1
markers.note: 90 +/- 9% at day 18 in the Du protocol.

markers.name: ISL1
markers.note: 95 +/- 3% at day 18; also one of the programming factors in the hNIL cassette.

markers.name: CHAT
markers.note: 91 +/- 6% of MAP2+ cells after 10 days of Compound E, versus 47 +/- 9% without it.

markers.name: FOXP1
markers.note: FOXP1+/LHX3-negative marks limb-innervating lateral motor column identity, the subtype enriched by the Amoroso protocol.

markers.name: LHX3
markers.note: Columnar subtype marker; also one of the hNIL programming factors.

markers.name: MAP2
markers.note: Pan-neuronal; the denominator for CHAT+ percentages.

markers.name: NEFL
markers.note: Reduced about 45% in SOD1 D90A motor neurons but not in GABA neurons from the same line - a motor-neuron-specific disease readout.

markers.name: MKI67
markers.note: Should be undetectable after Compound E; 40-50% of cells are Ki-67+ during expansion.

markers.name: GAD1
markers.note: What you get if SHH signalling is blocked (cyclopamine instead of purmorphamine) - a useful isogenic control but a contaminant otherwise.

functional_assays: Patch clamp: action potentials on depolarising current injection
Neuromuscular junction formation with C2C12 myotubes (alpha-bungarotoxin clusters on CHAT+ neurites)
In ovo grafting into chick spinal cord with ventral root axon projection
SYP-NanoLuc axonal length assay on astrocyte feeders for screening
qPCR for full-length SMN (SMA) and NEFL (ALS)
qc: OLIG2+ >= 95% at day 12 with OLIG2/NKX2-2 double positives < 1%
MNX1+ or ISL1+ >= 90% at day 18
CHAT+ >= 90% of MAP2+ cells after Notch inhibition
Ki-67 negative after Compound E treatment
MNP expansion limited to about 5 passages before motor neuron potential declines

protocols.name: Small-molecule OLIG2+ motor neuron progenitors, expandable
protocols.principle: CHIR99021 with dual SMAD inhibition makes caudal neuroepithelium in one step; adding retinoic acid and purmorphamine ventralises it to a near-pure OLIG2+ (pMN) progenitor, with WNT suppressing the neighbouring NKX2-2+ p3 fate. The progenitors can be expanded, and a Notch inhibitor then synchronises their conversion into mature motor neurons.
protocols.efficiency: >98% SOX1+ neuroepithelium at day 6; 95 +/- 3% OLIG2+ progenitors at day 12 with <0.5% OLIG2/NKX2-2 double positives; 90 +/- 9% MNX1+ and 95 +/- 3% ISL1+ at day 18; 91 +/- 6% of MAP2+ neurons CHAT+ after 10 days of Compound E; reproducible in IMR90, ALS (SOD1 D90A, A4V) and SMA lines
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated with Dispase (1 mg/mL) and split 1:6 onto irradiated MEFs or Matrigel; the next day switch to the chemically defined neural medium (1:1 DMEM/F12 : Neurobasal, 0.5x N2, 0.5x B27, 0.1 mM ascorbic acid, Glutamax, pen/strep).
tips: Check NKX2-2 as well as OLIG2: RA + SHH alone give mixed ventral progenitors in which up to ~40% of OLIG2+ cells also express NKX2-2, and that mixture is a common reason OLIG2-high cultures end up motor-neuron-poor.
Swapping purmorphamine for cyclopamine in the same schedule yields OLIG2-negative spinal GABA neurons, a convenient isogenic non-motor-neuron control.
Compound E both increases CHAT+ yield and shortens maturation, so it is worth the cost.
pitfalls: Pushing purmorphamine higher to suppress NKX2-2 is toxic; the authors instead lowered the SHH threshold with BMP inhibition.
Without valproic acid, RA drives premature neurogenesis during expansion and OLIG2 is lost.
Expansion beyond about 5 passages progressively loses motor neuron potential.

source.authors: Du ZW, Chen H, Liu H, et al.
source.title: Generation and expansion of highly pure motor neuron progenitors from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.name: i3LMNs: NGN2 + ISL1 + LHX3 (hNIL) at a safe-harbour locus
protocols.principle: Adding ISL1 and LHX3 to inducible NGN2 at a safe-harbour locus programmes iPSCs directly into lower motor neurons on the same three-day induction schedule as i3Neurons, with a Notch inhibitor from day 1.
protocols.start_requirements: A clonal iPSC line with doxycycline-inducible hNIL (NGN2, ISL1, LHX3) transgenes, healthy and not over-confluent; seed one 10 cm dish with 1.5 x 10^6 cells (2 x 10^4 iPSC/cm2).
materials: iPSC line with inducible hNIL at a safe-harbour locus
tips: The first three days are essentially identical to the i3Neuron protocol, including the same induction medium.
PLO gives the best morphology but the weakest adhesion; PEI and PDL stick better but PEI is toxic if coating is done sloppily and PDL varies between lots.
pitfalls: Same Tet-On caveat as i3Neurons: a second doxycycline-driven transgene will also be induced.
Dense long-term cultures detach in sheets, especially during immunostaining washes.
unverified: Compositions of Induction Medium and Motor Neuron Culture Medium are in a recipe table not present in the available full text.
No differentiation efficiency or purity figure is stated for the iLMN protocol in the retrievable text.

protocols.name: STEMdiff Motor Neuron Differentiation + Maturation
protocols.principle: hPSCs are aggregated into small embryoid bodies in AggreWell400 plates and taken through four sequential serum-free media that build motor neuron progenitors by day 9. The EBs are then dissociated, plated on PLO/laminin to become post-mitotic motor neurons by day 14, and matured in a BrainPhys-based medium to day 28 or later.
protocols.efficiency: > 40% mature motor neurons. Expected by ICC: day 14 class III β-tubulin > 80%, ISL1 > 40%, NKX6.1 > 40%; day 28 class III β-tubulin > 80%, ISL1 > 40%, HB9/MNX1 > 40%, ChAT > 40%
protocols.start_requirements: Directly from hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1 or mTeSR Plus. Dissociate to single cells with ACCUTASE (6 - 8 min) and seed 3.6 x 10^5 cells per well of an AggreWell400 24-well plate (300 cells per microwell; test 200 - 400 for new lines) pre-treated with Anti-Adherence Rinsing Solution, in 2 mL Motor Neuron Differentiation Medium 1 with 10 µM Y-27632.
tips: 300 cells per microwell suits most lines, but test 200 - 400 per microwell for a new line and judge by EB formation on day 1, growth on days 2 - 4 and day-14 markers.
Differentiation media 1 - 4 keep 2 weeks at 2 - 8°C and the maturation medium 4 weeks; Media 2 and 4 are made from leftover Media 1 and 3.
Coat 3 wells on each of two 24-well plates on day 9 so one set can be fixed for the day-14 check while the other matures.
Coating here uses 15 µg/mL PLO then 10 µg/mL laminin.
pitfalls: Trituration or standard tips when lifting EBs on day 9 damages them; use wide-bore tips and no pipetting up and down.
Bubbles and more than about 10 pipetting strokes during EB dissociation hurt viability.
Dispensing medium quickly into the AggreWell plate knocks EBs out of the microwells.
unverified: Protocol diagram is an image; days come from the written steps.

The component table names the supplements 'STEMdiff Motor Neuron Supplement A/B/C' while the media table calls them 'Motor Neuron Differentiation Supplement A/B/C'; the component-table names are used here.
The PIS covers the AggreWell400 method only; a suspension-plate variant is available from the vendor on request and is not described.

Y-27632

protocols.name: Quick-Neuron Motor - SeV Kit
protocols.principle: Sendai-virus delivery of a motor-neuron transcription-factor set, with 33 C transduction, puromycin selection, a 37 C shift on day 2, a day-3 passage, and an extra small-molecule component (K) added from day 4 to drive HB9 expression by day 10.
protocols.efficiency: The release specification for the matching ready-made cell product (MT-SeV-HC-CW50065) is over 80% TUBB3+, over 50% ChAT+/TUBB3+ and over 50% HB9+/TUBB3+ at day 7; the user guide states HB9-positive cells appear from day 7 and that nearly all cells are HB9-positive by day 10
protocols.start_requirements: Source hPSCs must have been maintained by single-cell passaging (StemFit Basic04, StemFit AK02N or StemFlex) and be at least 14 days post-thaw. Wells of a 6-well plate are precoated on day -3 with iMatrix-511 silk at 0.25 ug/cm2 in 2 mL chilled PBS and held at 4 C (or coated on day 0 and warmed 2 h at 37 C). Starting cultures must be 50-70% confluent and never above 90%. ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 is used at 10 uM stock diluted 1:1000 (final 10 uM) in the pre-harvest and plating media. A puromycin kill curve must be run in advance; the vendor's internal range is 0.5-2 ug/mL. The kit needs about 3.3 x 10^6 viable hPSCs (3 wells of a 6-well plate at 50-70% confluency) and a stable 33 C, 5% CO2 incubator; it covers 6 wells of a 6-well plate.
materials: Quick-Neuron Motor - SeV Kit (MT-SeV): QN-SeV-P, Component N1, Component A, Component K, Component P
0.01% poly-L-ornithine (Sigma P4957) and laminin mouse protein natural (Thermo 23017015) or Geltrex (A15696-01) for the replating plate
StemFit Basic04 Complete Type (AMSBio SF041-001), StemFit AK02N or StemFlex (Thermo A3349401)
TrypLE Select Enzyme 1X (Thermo 12563011) and 0.02% EDTA in DPBS (Sigma E8008) for Solution D1
ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 (Selleckchem S1049) and DMSO (Sigma D2650)
Optional STEM-CELLBANKER (AMSBIO 11890) for cryopreserving at the day-3 passage
tips: Component K is supplied at small volume and diluted in DMSO before use - make the working dilution the day it is needed
Holding the culture to day 10 rather than stopping at day 7 is what raises the HB9-positive fraction
Run the puromycin kill curve before day 0
pitfalls: BSL-2 containment required for the Sendai virus
Starting cells must be 50-70% confluent and at least 14 days post-thaw
Excessive pipetting at the day-3 passage damages already-detached neurons
unverified: No purity figure published for user differentiations with the kit itself
The 'nearly all cells HB9-positive' day-10 statement is qualitative, with no percentage

cell_types.notes: Two things set the good protocols apart from the old 1-2 month, 30-70% efficient ones. First, WNT activation: CHAR99021 both caudalises in a single step and, crucially, separates the OLIG2 (pMN) and NKX2-2 (p3) domains - staining for NKX2-2 as well as OLIG2 is the most useful diagnostic if a culture is OLIG2-high but motor-neuron-poor. Second, Notch inhibition (Compound E or DAPT) at the differentiation step, which synchronises the progenitors and removes residual dividing cells. Related protocols worth comparing: Maury Y, Come J, Piskorowski RA, et al., Nat Biotechnol 2015;33:89-96 (PMID 25383599, doi 10.1038/nbt.3049), a combinatorial small-molecule screen that produced 14-day spinal and cranial motor neuron protocols and first highlighted the role of canonical WNT; and Amoroso MW, Croft GF, Williams DJ, et al., J Neurosci 2013;33:574-86 (PMID 23303937, doi 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0906-12.2013), which reaches up to 50% motor neurons in 3 weeks and preferentially gives limb-innervating FOXP1+/LHX3-negative lateral motor column neurons. Neither of those two could be verified at the level of stage concentrations in this session, so they are cited rather than written out.

cell_types.name: Oligodendrocytes and OPCs
cell_types.summary: The myelinating glia of the CNS, derived through the OLIG2+ pMN domain and defined operationally by live O4 surface staining and then by MBP. They are used for multiple sclerosis and leukodystrophy modelling, for remyelination screens, and for the trophic support of axons that fails in ALS.
cell_types.maturation_note: The small-molecule route takes 75 days to O4+ OPCs and a further 3 weeks of growth-factor withdrawal for MBP+ oligodendrocytes. Transcription-factor routes compress this dramatically: SOX10 alone gives O4+ cells by day 22 (and about 89% by day 15 from a single-copy inducible line), with MBP+ cells from day 7 of induction. Myelination in co-culture takes about 20 further days.

morphology.endpoint: Small, phase-dark cell bodies with dense, highly branched processes that spread into flat membrane sheets; mature cells look almost web-like. O4 live staining is the practical way to find them, because the morphology overlaps with other glia early on.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Seeded sparsely (10,000 cells/cm2 in the Douvaras protocol) for adherent induction.

stages.label: OLIG2+ progenitors
stages.look: Multilayered dense structures; PAX6+ at day 7 then OLIG2+ by day 12.

stages.label: Spheres
stages.look: Smooth free-floating aggregates (at least 100 cells each) in which the OLIG2+ population is enriched.

stages.label: Early O4+ OPCs
stages.look: Cells migrating out of plated spheres, beginning to show the characteristic fine ramified processes.

stages.label: Late O4+ OPCs
stages.look: Small bodies with dense, highly branched processes; O4 live staining is strongly positive and these cells no longer divide.

stages.label: Mature oligodendrocytes
stages.look: Flat membrane sheets and highly branched processes, MBP positive, wrapping axons in co-culture.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Appears by day 7 of adherent induction with retinoic acid.

markers.name: OLIG2
markers.note: 70.1% at day 12 with SAG, 57.7% with recombinant SHH, 40.6% with retinoic acid alone. Day-12 OLIG2 predicts the final MBP yield, so it is the stage to optimise.

markers.name: NKX2-2
markers.note: Co-expressed with OLIG2 in cells committing to the oligodendrocyte lineage - the opposite of its meaning in motor neuron protocols, where it is a contaminant.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: The master regulator and the single sufficient programming factor; 97 +/- 8% of SOX10+ cells are also O4+.

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Early OPC marker that most O4+ cells have lost by day 75. Notably absent in SOX10-programmed cultures, which appear to skip the OPC stage - so do not use it as a checkpoint there.

markers.name: CSPG4
markers.note: Retained in day-75 O4+ cells after PDGFRA is lost; also retained in OPCs after grafting.

markers.name: O4 antigen
markers.alias: O4 sulfatide (not a gene product; antibody-defined)
markers.note: The operational purity readout and the basis for live staining and FACS. O4+ cells are post-mitotic (Ki-67 negative) while surrounding progenitors still divide.

markers.name: MBP
markers.note: 34 +/- 4% of O4+ cells after >=3 weeks of growth-factor withdrawal in the small-molecule route; about 10-21% of cells at day 22 in SOX10 programming. All MBP+ cells are post-mitotic.

markers.name: PLP1
markers.note: 20 +/- 3% of SOX10-induced cells, rising to about 95% of O4-purified cells.

markers.name: MOG
markers.note: Co-expressed in about 72% of MBP+ cells.

markers.name: MKI67
markers.note: 40-50% of progenitors are Ki-67+ during OPC expansion; O4+ and MBP+ cells must be negative.

markers.name: GFAP
markers.note: About 15% of cells in the small-molecule route; absent in SOX10-programmed cultures.

markers.name: MAP2
markers.note: About 20% of cells in the small-molecule route; under 5% in SOX10 programming.

markers.name: PMP22
markers.note: Worth checking because SOX10 also drives Schwann cell fate; no PMP22+ cells were found in the hPSC oligodendrocyte cultures.

functional_assays: Live O4 surface staining and FACS purification (cells freeze and thaw without losing morphology)
Myelination of hPSC-derived cortical neurons in co-culture (MBP sheaths wrapping TUJ1+ axons)
Myelination in shiverer mouse brain slices or after neonatal transplantation
Electron microscopy for compact multilayer myelin and g-ratio
96/384-well MBP-area myelination screens (T3, clobetasol, miconazole, pranlukast as positive controls)
qc: OLIG2+ >= 60-70% at day 12 as the gate on the whole run
O4+ >= 50% by live staining or flow at the endpoint (day 75 small-molecule, day 22 SOX10)
MBP+ cells present and Ki-67 negative after growth factor withdrawal
No PMP22+ Schwann cells
Astrocyte (GFAP) and neuronal (TUJ1) fractions quantified, or sorted away

protocols.name: Adherent dual SMAD inhibition with low-dose retinoid: O4+ OPCs by day 75
protocols.principle: Starting retinoic acid at day 0 together with dual SMAD inhibition, then adding a smoothened agonist from day 8, recapitulates the pMN domain of the spinal cord and gives a large OLIG2+ population by day 12; aggregating the cells into spheres then enriches that population and restricts it to the oligodendrocyte lineage.
protocols.efficiency: 70.1% OLIG2+ at day 12 with SAG; up to 70% O4+ cells at day 75 from the RUES1 hESC line and 43.6-62.1% from four PPMS patient iPSC lines; 34 +/- 4% of O4+ OPCs become MBP+ after >=3 weeks of growth factor withdrawal. Residual cultures are about 15% GFAP+ and 20% MAP2+
protocols.start_requirements: hESC/hiPSC plated at 10,000 cells/cm2 at day 0 in adherent (not suspension) culture for dual SMAD inhibition.
tips: The step-by-step version is Douvaras P, Fossati V, Nat Protoc 2015;10:1143-54 (PMID 26134954, doi 10.1038/nprot.2015.075).
Retinoid dose is the counter-intuitive part: 100 nM, roughly a hundredth of the dose commonly used, gave the best OLIG2 yields, and worked even without exogenous SHH by inducing endogenous SHH.
SAG outperformed recombinant SHH and is cheaper.
By day 75 most O4+ cells have lost PDGFRA but keep NG2, so do not expect PDGFRA to mark late OPCs.
pitfalls: 75 days is still a long run, and the culture is never pure - expect roughly 15% astrocytes and 20% neurons alongside the OPCs unless you sort.
Spheres smaller than about 100 cells do not form.
Line-to-line variation is real: 44-70% O4+ across six lines.
unverified: Concentrations of PDGF-AA, HGF, IGF-1 and NT-3 and the exact dual-SMAD inhibitor doses are in the supplementary media tables, which were not retrievable.
Day boundaries for the PDGF medium overlap the sphere stage in the source (growth factors from day 20 while spheres run to day 30); represented here as overlapping stages.

source.authors: Douvaras P, Wang J, Zimmer M, et al.
source.title: Efficient generation of myelinating oligodendrocytes from primary progressive multiple sclerosis patients by induced pluripotent stem cells.

factors.name: all-trans retinoic acid
factors.role: caudalisation from day 0; about 100-fold lower than the dose most groups use, and it upregulates OLIG2 even without exogenous SHH

stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Plate at only 10,000 cells/cm2 at day 0 and induce adherently
Keep retinoic acid from the very start
stages.checkpoint: PAX6+ cells by day 7

stages.name: Ventralisation to OLIG2+ progenitors

factors.name: SAG (smoothened agonist)
factors.role: ventralisation; more effective here than 100 ng/mL recombinant SHH

stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Add SAG at day 8
stages.checkpoint: Multilayered structures by day 12; 70.1% OLIG2+ (vs 57.7% with recombinant SHH, 40.6% with RA alone)

stages.name: Sphere aggregation
stages.base_medium: Neural medium with retinoic acid and SAG, low-attachment plates
stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Lift adherent cells at day 12 and seed into low-attachment plates to form spheres
Note that at least 100 cells are needed per sphere
stages.checkpoint: Only OLIG2-GFP+ cells form aggregates, so the aggregation step itself enriches the OLIG2 population

stages.name: OPC expansion
stages.base_medium: PDGF medium, on poly-L-ornithine/laminin from day 30
stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Add PDGF-AA, HGF, IGF-1 and NT-3 from day 20
Plate spheres onto poly-L-ornithine/laminin at day 30 and let cells migrate out
Live-stain with O4 antibody from about day 50; the population rises sharply around day 75
FACS-purify O4+ cells; they freeze and thaw without losing morphology
stages.checkpoint: Highly ramified O4+ cells co-expressing OLIG2, SOX10 and NG2; O4+ cells are non-dividing while 40-50% of the remaining progenitors are Ki-67+

stages.name: Oligodendrocyte maturation
stages.feeding: Per schedule for at least 3 weeks
actions: Withdraw growth factors and keep for >=3 weeks
stages.checkpoint: 34 +/- 4% MBP+ mature oligodendrocytes; in vivo, compact myelin with major dense and intraperiod lines and about 31% of host axons ensheathed at 16 weeks in shiverer mice

protocols.name: SOX10 alone: O4+ oligodendrocytes in about 22 days
protocols.principle: Overexpressing the single transcription factor SOX10 in caudalised, ventralised neural precursors is enough to drive them to O4+ and MBP+ oligodendrocytes in about ten days, skipping the intermediate OPC stage; SOX10 cannot do this in uncommitted hPSCs.
protocols.efficiency: Lentiviral SOX10 in day-12 NPCs: 54.05 +/- 2.52% O4+ at day 22, with 97.15 +/- 8.19% of SOX10+ cells also O4+ and 21.48 +/- 2.09% of SOX10+ cells MBP+; across eight lines (including two PPMS and two familial ALS iPSC lines) 50-65% O4+ and about 10% MBP+ at day 22. A single-copy doxycycline-inducible SOX10 line at the AAVS1 locus reaches 89.3 +/- 0.6% O4+ by day 15
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated to single cells two days before day 0; neural induction is run in N2B27 medium. The NPCs must already be caudal/ventral (OLIG2-competent) - SOX10 in naive hPSCs gives no oligodendrocytes.
materials: Inducible SOX10 lentivirus (or an AAVS1 inducible SOX10 line)
tips: SOX8 and SOX9 also induce O4 (37-50%) but SOX10 is the best single factor, and adding any of the other five candidate factors to SOX10 gave no further improvement.
No PDGFRA+ or NG2+ cells appear, which suggests SOX10 generates late OPCs/oligodendrocytes directly without an intermediate OPC stage - do not screen for NG2 as a checkpoint.
The single-copy AAVS1 line removes random-integration and transduction-efficiency variability and is the better option for screening.
In the authors' own screen, clobetasol gave the biggest increase in MBP (3-4 fold over DMSO, more than T3), pranlukast 1.5-2.5 fold and miconazole about as much as T3, while DAPT gave no increase.
pitfalls: SOX10 in uncommitted hPSCs produces nothing - the NPC stage and its OLIG2 competence are essential.
Lentiviral delivery leaves about 24% Ki-67+ cells in the culture at day 22 (the MBP+ cells themselves are post-mitotic).
Lines differ: one iPSC line with lower day-12 OLIG2 (30.7% vs 51.7%) gave correspondingly fewer MBP+ cells.
unverified: T3 concentration in the co-culture medium is not stated in the available text.
Composition of the oligodendrocyte differentiation and co-culture media is in the supplementary experimental procedures, which were not retrievable.

Ehrlich M, Mozafari S, Glatza M, et al., PNAS 2017;114:E2243-E2252 (PMID 28246330, doi 10.1073/pnas.1614412114) reports up to 70% O4+ in 28 days with SOX10 + OLIG2 + NKX6.2; its stage concentrations could not be verified because the PMC record returned no full text.

source.authors: Garcia-Leon JA, Kumar M, Boon R, et al.
source.title: SOX10 Single Transcription Factor-Based Fast and Efficient Generation of Oligodendrocytes from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells.

factors.name: Smoothened agonist
factors.role: ventralisation, added day 8 after the SMAD inhibitors are withdrawn

stages.feeding: Per schedule

Withdraw SB431542 and LDN-193189 at day 8 and add the smoothened agonist

cell_types.notes: Two surprises in the small-molecule literature are worth knowing. First, the useful retinoic acid dose is about a hundred times lower than most groups had been using (100 nM), and at that dose RA alone induces OLIG2 by raising endogenous SHH. Second, SAG outperforms recombinant SHH and is far cheaper. Transcription-factor routes have largely displaced the 100+ day protocols for screening work: SOX10 alone suffices (Garcia-Leon), while Ehrlich M, Mozafari S, Glatza M, et al., PNAS 2017;114:E2243-E2252 (PMID 28246330, doi 10.1073/pnas.1614412114) reported up to 70% O4+ in 28 days with SOX10 + OLIG2 + NKX6.2; the difference is probably in how the starting NPCs were made. Neither route makes a pure culture without sorting on O4, and MBP+ fractions stay well below the O4+ fraction in every protocol.

cell_types.name: Astrocytes
cell_types.summary: The most abundant glial cell of the CNS, responsible for potassium and glutamate homeostasis, synaptogenesis, metabolic support and the inflammatory response, and regionally diverse. hPSC-derived astrocytes are used for neuron-glia co-culture, for APOE and other glial-autonomous disease mechanisms in Alzheimer's disease and ALS, and as a feeder layer that matures hPSC-derived neurons.
cell_types.maturation_note: Human gliogenesis is intrinsically late - the switch takes 6-9 months in vivo and 3-6 months in conventional culture. The three routes differ almost entirely in how they get past that: long neurosphere expansion (about 120 days), sparse seeding into a low-serum astrocyte medium (<30 days), or forcing NFIA, which confers glial competence in 5 days. Morphology keeps changing with passage, from large flat cells to long, complex processes.

morphology.endpoint: Flat, polygonal to stellate cells with large nuclei and several broad processes, growing as a loose monolayer with visible gaps. With passage and in co-culture they become more ramified, with long thin branches. Polygonal, piled-up, phase-dark cells usually mean a reactive phenotype from too much serum.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Standard compact colonies; some routes start instead from banked NPCs.

stages.label: Neuroepithelium and rosettes
stages.look: Radial rosettes; this is the window in which regional identity is set by RA or SHH.

stages.label: Expanding spheres
stages.look: Smooth free-floating aggregates; triturate weekly to suppress neurogenesis and avoid dark necrotic centres.

stages.label: Astroglial progenitors ('astrospheres')
stages.look: Spheres that re-form after dissociation and are now about 80% S100B+ and CD44+ but only about 10% GFAP+.

stages.label: Immature astrocytes
stages.look: Flat stellate cells plated sparsely on poly-ornithine/laminin; without laminin they attach but do not flatten, which makes staining hard to read.

stages.label: Mature astrocyte monolayer
stages.look: Large stellate S100B+/GFAP+ cells with long processes, non-proliferating in the absence of mitogens.

markers.name: S100B
markers.note: The more reliable of the two classic markers: about 80% at day 90 in astrospheres and ~90% at 30 days in the NPC/astrocyte-medium route. S100B+/GFAP-negative cells are immature rather than wrong.

markers.name: GFAP
markers.note: The marker everyone quotes and the more variable one, both in hPSC-derived and in primary astrocytes - about 10% at day 90 of astrosphere culture but >90% after day 120, and 82% at 30 days in the NPC route. Use a panel, not GFAP alone.

markers.name: CD44
markers.note: The key sortable marker of glial competence: 65% CD44+ after 10 days of NFIA, and the basis of live FACS enrichment before astrocyte differentiation.

markers.name: NFIA
markers.note: Must be transient: sustained high NFIA arrests cells in G1 and blocks GFAP even in the presence of LIF.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Glial transcription factor; with NFIB it is the basis of the Canals programming route.

markers.name: AQP4
markers.note: Used as a knock-in reporter locus (AQP4-H2B-GFP) to time astrocyte appearance.

markers.name: SLC1A3
markers.note: Glutamate transporter; positive within 30 days in the NPC/astrocyte-medium route.

markers.name: SLC1A2
markers.note: The main adult glutamate transporter and a reasonable maturity readout.

markers.name: ALDH1L1
markers.note: Pan-astrocyte marker, less variable than GFAP.

markers.name: MAP2
markers.note: Neuronal contamination; should be absent after day 120 in astrosphere cultures, but the NPC-medium route retains low levels of neuronal transcripts.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Quality control for leftover neuroepithelium.

markers.name: OLIG2
markers.note: Check with O4 that the glial output has not gone down the oligodendrocyte route.

markers.name: LCN2
markers.note: Reactive/A1-like marker, induced by serum within days - the reason low-serum protocols matter.

markers.name: IL6
markers.note: Dose-dependent secretion after 24 h of poly(I:C), LPS or amyloid-beta 42; the parent NPCs secrete none, which makes it a clean functional release test.

functional_assays: Spontaneous and glutamate/ATP/KCl-evoked calcium transients
Glutamate uptake
IL-6 and IL-8 secretion after poly(I:C), LPS or amyloid-beta 42
Phagocytosis of pHrodo-labelled myelin or zymosan
Enhancement of microglial phagocytosis by astrocyte-conditioned medium
Support of neuronal maturation in co-culture (synapsin-1 puncta, mEPSC frequency)
Protection against glutamate excitotoxicity
Electrophysiology: minimal sodium currents, no action potentials
qc: S100B+ >= 80-90% by flow (preferred over GFAP as the primary purity readout)
GFAP+ >= 80% where the protocol claims it, acknowledging high variability
No MAP2+ or TUJ1+ neurons and no O4+ oligodendrocytes
Non-reactive baseline: low LCN2/C3, with inducible IL-6 on stimulation
Calcium response to ATP or glutamate

protocols.name: Astrospheres: long-term neuroepithelial expansion to regional astrocytes
protocols.principle: Neuroepithelial clusters are patterned early (or left alone for dorsal forebrain identity), then expanded as free-floating spheres with EGF and FGF2 and triturated weekly to suppress neurogenesis; after about three months the spheres have switched to gliogenic and release of mitogens plus CNTF gives nearly pure astrocytes.
protocols.efficiency: At day 90 about 80% S100B+, about 80% CD44+ and about 10% GFAP+; from astrospheres cultured past day 120, nearly all cells are S100B+ and >90% are S100B+/GFAP+ within a week of mitogen withdrawal, with no neurons detectable
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC-derived neuroepithelial cells at day 10 of differentiation (columnar epithelium in every colony), generated from colonies with no sign of spontaneous differentiation. Base medium throughout is neural medium (DMEM/F12 + NEAA + N2 + heparin 2 ug/mL).
tips: Patterning has to happen at the neuroepithelial stage (days 10-21); after that the regional identity of the astrocytes is fixed. Unpatterned cultures default to dorsal telencephalic.
Without laminin the cells attach but do not flatten, which makes immunostaining hard to read; 1% serum for the first 24 h is an alternative way to get attachment.
Markers for astroglial progenitors are poor: S100B and CD44 come up before GFAP, and GFAP-negative/S100B-positive cells are immature rather than wrong.
pitfalls: Incomplete neural induction is the main failure: non-neural cells proliferate fast and take over.
Trypsin is not tolerated - the cells recover badly.
Replating below about 100,000 cells/mL stops astroglial progenitors proliferating.
Letting single spheres grow too large gives dark necrotic centres.

source.authors: Krencik R, Zhang SC
source.title: Directed differentiation of functional astroglial subtypes from human pluripotent stem cells.

stages.name: Regional patterning of neuroepithelium (optional)
stages.feeding: Replace half the medium every 2-3 days
actions: Mechanically remove non-neural colonies that lack rosettes
Add morphogens from day 10 and keep them to day 21 for full patterning; omit them for dorsal telencephalic astrocytes
At day 15 lift the rosette-containing clusters with a pipette and transfer to T25 flasks (8 mL per flask)
stages.checkpoint: 3-10 clearly distinguishable rosettes per colony at day 15; clusters should not be broken into single cells

stages.name: Gliogenic switch
stages.feeding: Replace 75% of the medium every 2-3 days
actions: Add EGF and FGF2 from day 21; morphogens are no longer needed
Break large spheres weekly with a flame-polished Pasteur pipette (0.2-0.5 mm aperture) to suppress neurogenesis
Discard any spheres that attach firmly or form monolayers
stages.checkpoint: Day 90: 'astrospheres' that are ~80% S100B+ and ~80% CD44+; check that PAX6, MAP2 and O4 cells are absent

stages.name: Astroglial progenitor amplification
stages.feeding: Replace 75% every 2-3 days
actions: Dissociate with Accutase (never trypsin) and replate at >=100,000 cells/mL in T25 flasks
Progenitors re-aggregate into new astrospheres; expand for 6-8 months in total if large numbers are needed
stages.checkpoint: Spheres re-form; rapidly dividing fibroblast-like cells that never re-form spheres mean a non-neural/neural-crest contamination

stages.name: Terminal differentiation

factors.name: CNTF
factors.role: activates gliogenic gene expression via JAK signalling

stages.feeding: Medium change every 2 days for 6 days
actions: Dissociate astrospheres to single cells and plate at 10,000 cells/cm2 on poly-L-ornithine/laminin coverslips
Let the cells attach for 3-5 h, then add neural medium with CNTF for 6 days
stages.checkpoint: Flat stellate S100B+/GFAP+ cells, no proliferation (no EGF/FGF2); glutamate uptake, calcium waves, minimal sodium currents and no action potentials

protocols.name: Commercial astrocyte medium on forebrain NPCs (<30 days)
protocols.principle: Rather than engineering the gliogenic switch, forebrain NPCs are seeded very sparsely into a low-serum astrocyte medium; this alone yields replicative, non-reactive astrocytes within 30 days and works across dozens of patient lines.
protocols.efficiency: Across 42 NPC lines from 30 individuals, an average of 90% S100B+ and 82% GFAP+ by flow cytometry at 30 days; transcriptomes cluster with primary human fetal astrocytes (r = 0.945) and read as non-reactive
protocols.start_requirements: Forebrain-patterned NPCs maintained at high density on Matrigel in NPC medium (DMEM/F12, 1x N2, 1x B27-RA, 1 mg/mL laminin, 20 ng/mL FGF2), split 1:3-1:4 weekly with Accutase and used at low passage. NPC quality is the main predictor of success.
materials: Commercial astrocyte medium with 2% FBS and growth supplement
DMEM/F12, N2, B27-RA, laminin, FGF2 (for NPC maintenance)
tips: Use S100B rather than GFAP to judge the population: GFAP is the more variable marker both here and in primary astrocytes. Better still, use a panel or transcriptomics.
A simple functional release test: these astrocytes secrete IL-6 (and IL-8) in a dose-dependent way after 24 h of poly(I:C), LPS or amyloid-beta 42, whereas the parent NPCs secrete nothing.
The real advantage is throughput - dozens of lines in parallel, expandable and freezable, which is what case-control studies need.
pitfalls: Some NPC lines only work from very low-passage stocks, and not necessarily on the first attempt.
Seeding too densely, or skipping the single-cell dissociation, blocks the transition.
The protocol relies on a proprietary commercial medium, so composition is not defined and lots vary; the authors screened 11 conditions and only two commercial media worked.
unverified: The medium is proprietary; the only defined component the paper gives is 1-2% FBS.
Regional identity varies between lines and is not controlled by this protocol.

source.authors: TCW J, Wang M, Pimenova AA, et al.
source.title: An Efficient Platform for Astrocyte Differentiation from Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells.

stages.name: Sparse seeding into astrocyte medium
stages.base_medium: Commercial astrocyte medium with 2% FBS and astrocyte growth supplement (ScienCell 1801 in the paper)

factors.name: Fetal bovine serum
factors.role: minimal serum exposure; more serum pushes the cells reactive

stages.feeding: Per vendor schedule
actions: Dissociate NPCs to single cells and seed at 15,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel - near-single-cell density is critical
Switch straight into astrocyte medium; no intermediate stage
stages.checkpoint: Astrocyte morphology within 10 days

stages.name: Astrocyte maturation
stages.feeding: Per vendor schedule
actions: Continue to day 30; the astrocytes are replicative, can be expanded for months and cryopreserved
stages.checkpoint: Star-shaped morphology by day 30; ~90% S100B+ / ~82% GFAP+ by flow; ALDH1L1, vimentin, GLAST and GLUT1 positive

protocols.name: NFIA forced expression: gliogenic switch in days, not months
protocols.principle: NFIA is the molecular switch for human glial competence. A transient pulse of NFIA makes neurogenic NSCs glial-competent (CD44+) in about five days, and NFIA then has to be withdrawn so that LIF can drive GFAP expression - sustained high NFIA arrests the cells in G1 and blocks differentiation.
protocols.efficiency: From an inducible NFIA hPSC line: 65% CD44+ after 10 days of NFIA, then 42% GFAP+ after 15 days of LIF. In transduced long-term NSCs, >60% GFAP+ by 56 days and nearly 100% by 77 days. Regional (cortical vs spinal) astrocytes give GFAP+ cells by 6-7 days of differentiation
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC-derived NSCs (cortical by LSB+XAV939, or ventral spinal by LSB + 1 uM retinoic acid + 1 uM purmorphamine), maintained on poly-ornithine/laminin/fibronectin in N2 medium with 10 ng/mL FGF2, 10 ng/mL EGF and 1:1000 B27; plated at 3.5 x 10^5 cells/cm2 for transduction.
materials: FUW-tetO-NFIA and M2-rtTA lentivirus (or an inducible NFIA hPSC line)
tips: NFIA has to come back down: keeping doxycycline on blocks GFAP even with LIF. Titrating the doxycycline dose down also permits GFAP induction, which fits the G1-arrest mechanism.
Because the NSCs can be patterned first, you get region-matched astrocytes - useful for ALS (spinal) versus cortical disease models.
TGF-beta1 treatment of plain NSCs induces endogenous NFIA and eventually GFAP+ cells, but much less efficiently than forced NFIA, so it is not a drop-in substitute.

Canals I, Ginisty A, Quist E, et al., Nat Methods 2018;15:693-696 (PMID 30127505, doi 10.1038/s41592-018-0103-2) is the main alternative transcription-factor route: SOX9 plus NFIB overexpressed in hPSCs gives homogeneous induced astrocytes with adult-like properties.
pitfalls: Success depends on how well the NSCs are transduced; an inducible line avoids that variable.
The pulse is reversible - remove doxycycline and keep the cells in NSC medium and they revert to a neurogenic state and lose glial competence.
Glial-competent cells migrate extensively along white matter after grafting, which is a feature for some experiments and a confound for others.

source.authors: Tchieu J, Calder EL, Guttikonda SR, et al.
source.title: NFIA is a gliogenic switch enabling rapid derivation of functional human astrocytes from pluripotent stem cells.

stages.name: NFIA induction
stages.base_medium: NSC medium (N2 + 10 ng/mL FGF2 + 10 ng/mL EGF + B27 1:1000)

factors.name: Doxycycline
factors.role: induces FUW-tetO-NFIA (lentivirus or an inducible hPSC line)

stages.feeding: Daily medium change, minimum 5 days
actions: Transduce NSCs with tetO-NFIA and M2-rtTA lentivirus for 16-20 h, or use an inducible NFIA line
Add doxycycline and change medium daily; glial competence appears within 5 days
Detach with 0.05% trypsin and label for CD44
stages.checkpoint: CD44+ (65% from the inducible line after 10 days); NFIA lengthens G1 and raises CDKN1A (p21)

stages.name: NFIA withdrawal and astrocyte differentiation
stages.base_medium: Astrocyte induction medium: N2 + 10 ng/mL HB-EGF + 10 ng/mL LIF, no doxycycline

factors.name: LIF
factors.role: drives GFAP once NFIA has fallen; most efficient of the glial factors tested

stages.feeding: Weekly passaging for the first 4 weeks after sorting, then every other week
actions: FACS-sort live CD44+ cells and replate in astrocyte medium without doxycycline
Keep LIF for about 15 days
stages.checkpoint: GFAP+/S100B+ cells with complex processes, loss of Ki-67; transcriptome correlates with primary fetal astrocytes; robust calcium transients to KCl and ATP (stronger than commercial primary fetal astrocytes)

protocols.name: STEMdiff Astrocyte Differentiation + Astrocyte Maturation Kit
protocols.principle: NPCs from the SMADi neural induction kit are switched to astrocyte differentiation medium and passaged weekly for about three weeks to give astrocytic precursors, which are then carried through two weekly passages in maturation medium to become S100β/GFAP-positive astrocytes. This entry uses the standard STEMdiff Astrocyte Maturation Kit (100-0016).
protocols.efficiency: > 70% S100β-positive and > 60% GFAP-positive astrocytes; < 15% doublecortin-positive neurons; from hPSCs in as little as 7 weeks
protocols.start_requirements: Starts from NPCs, not hPSCs: generate them with STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (Catalog #08581). Monolayer route: passage day 18 - 21 (passage 3) NPCs with ACCUTASE and seed 1.5 - 2 x 10^5 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in 2 mL induction medium for 24 h. EB route: place day 11 - 12 selected rosettes on Matrigel in induction medium for 24 h. Day numbers follow the PIS, which counts from day 0 of neural induction with STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (monolayer route shown; where the PIS gives a range, the earliest day is used). duration_days counts from NPC plating.
tips: Both complete media keep up to 2 weeks at 2 - 8°C.
The 7-day intervals can be 6 - 8 days; passage at 80 - 90% confluence.
Maturation Supplement B varies from light yellow to brown between lots without affecting performance.
NPC plating density may need optimising per line.
pitfalls: Results depend on the line and on the quality of the starting NPCs.
Use tissue culture-treated ware fully covered by Matrigel; incompletely coated wells should not be used.
unverified: Protocol diagrams are images; days come from the written steps.

The length of the second passage in maturation medium is not stated; it is taken as 7 days like the first, giving day 54 and duration_days 36 (1 day plating + 21 days differentiation + 14 days maturation).
The PIS does not say whether this maturation medium contains serum; the companion sheet only describes the other kit (100-1666) as serum-free.

protocols.name: STEMdiff Astrocyte Differentiation + Serum-Free Maturation Kit
protocols.principle: Same astrocyte differentiation medium as the standard workflow (about three weeks with passaging every 6 - 8 days), followed by three weeks in a fully serum-free maturation medium. This entry uses the STEMdiff Astrocyte Serum-Free Maturation Kit (100-1666); the maturation phase is 20 - 21 days rather than two passages.
protocols.efficiency: > 70% S100β-positive and > 60% GFAP-positive astrocytes; < 15% doublecortin-positive neurons; from hPSCs in as little as 7 weeks
protocols.start_requirements: Starts from NPCs, not hPSCs: generate them with STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (Catalog #08581) by the EB or monolayer protocol, or use NPCs expanded in STEMdiff Neural Progenitor Medium, or thawed Human iPSC-Derived Neural Progenitor Cells (200-0620). Monolayer route: at ~80 - 90% confluence (about day 18 - 21) harvest with ACCUTASE and seed 1.5 - 2 x 10^5 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in 2 mL induction medium for 24 h (expanded or thawed NPCs are plated in Neural Progenitor Medium). Day numbers follow the PIS, which counts from day 0 of neural induction with STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (monolayer route shown; where the PIS gives a range, the earliest day is used). duration_days counts from NPC plating.
materials: STEMdiff Neural Progenitor Medium (05833) if starting from expanded or thawed NPCs
tips: Both complete media keep up to 2 weeks at 2 - 8°C; do not freeze the complete maturation medium.
Thawed precursors or astrocytes are plated at 1.5 - 2 x 10^5 cells/cm2 in maturation medium with 10 µM Y-27632.
NPC plating density may need optimising per line.
pitfalls: Astrocyte differentiation needs a high-quality NPC population to start with.
Minimise the time cells sit in freezing medium at room temperature when banking.
unverified: Figures 1 - 3 are images; days come from the written steps.
Days 40 and 61 are calculated from day 19 plus 21 days of differentiation plus 21 days of maturation; the PIS gives these as 'day 20 - 21' of each phase, not as running day numbers.
The 'as little as 7 weeks' claim does not match the written schedule on the monolayer route (about 61 days from hPSCs); on the EB route it is about 54 days.
Y-27632 is listed as Catalog #72302 in the materials table but #72304 in the thawing note.

protocols.name: Quick-Glia Astrocyte - SeV Kit
protocols.principle: Sendai virus delivering astrocytic transcription factors at 33 C, followed by a 37 C shift on day 2 and a switch into a commercial astrocyte medium on day 4, carries hPSCs to CD44/S100B/ALDH1L1-positive astrocytes by day 28, with GFAP rising further by day 42.
protocols.start_requirements: Source hPSCs must have been maintained by single-cell passaging (StemFit Basic04, StemFit AK02N or StemFlex) and be at least 14 days post-thaw. Wells of a 6-well plate are precoated on day -3 with iMatrix-511 silk at 0.25 ug/cm2 in 2 mL chilled PBS and held at 4 C (or coated on day 0 and warmed 2 h at 37 C). Starting cultures must be 50-70% confluent and never above 90%. ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 is used at 10 uM stock diluted 1:1000 (final 10 uM) in the pre-harvest and plating media. A puromycin kill curve must be run in advance; the vendor's internal range is 0.5-2 ug/mL. This kit needs about 2 x 10^6 viable hPSCs (2 wells of a 6-well plate at 50-70% confluency), a stable 33 C, 5% CO2 incubator, and a ScienCell Astrocyte Medium Kit (ScienCell 1801) plus Geltrex for the day-17 passage. No puromycin selection step is used. One kit covers 6 wells of a 6-well plate.
materials: Quick-Glia Astrocyte - SeV Kit (AS-SeV): QGA-SeV, Component N1, Component GA1, Component GA2
ScienCell Astrocyte Medium Kit (ScienCell 1801: basal medium, astrocyte growth supplement, FBS, penicillin-streptomycin)
Geltrex hESC-qualified reduced growth factor basement membrane matrix (Thermo A1569601)
StemFit Basic04 Complete Type (AMSBio SF041-001), StemFit AK02N or StemFlex (Thermo A3349401)
TrypLE Select Enzyme 1X (Thermo 12563011) and 0.02% EDTA in DPBS (Sigma E8008) for Solution D1
ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 (Selleckchem S1049) and DMSO (Sigma D2650)
Optional STEM-CELLBANKER (AMSBIO 11890) for cryopreserving at the day-3 passage
tips: Unlike the Quick-Neuron kits, this one has no puromycin selection step
Visible cell death the day after the 37 C shift is expected; the guide includes recovery images to compare against
Keeping the culture at higher confluency after day 28 raises GFAP expression
pitfalls: BSL-2 containment is required for the Sendai virus
A month of culture with a mid-run passage - contamination and feeding discipline matter more here than in the 7-10 day kits
The recommended replating density may not suit every hPSC line because growth rates differ
unverified: No purity percentage is published for this kit; evidence offered is marker detection, qPCR and transcriptome correlation rather than a positive-cell fraction
Post-thaw viability is quoted as approximately 80% for cells frozen at the day-17 passage, but no yield per starting well is given

cell_types.notes: Pick the route by what the experiment needs. The astrosphere protocol is slow (about 4 months) but gives regionally specified, functionally characterised astrocytes and progenitors that expand for 6-8 months. The NPC-plus-commercial-medium route is fast and scales to dozens of patient lines, which is what case-control studies need, but relies on a proprietary medium and does not control regional identity. Forced NFIA gives glial competence in 5 days and, because the NSCs can be patterned first, region-matched astrocytes - at the cost of a transgene and a mandatory withdrawal step. GFAP is a genuinely unreliable single marker; use S100B plus a panel or transcriptomics. Serum is the main lever on reactivity: keep it at 1-2% or omit it, and treat a polygonal, piled-up morphology as a warning.

cell_types.name: Midbrain dopaminergic neurons
cell_types.summary: Substantia nigra and ventral tegmental dopamine neurons, defined by co-expression of the floor-plate factor FOXA2 with the midbrain factor LMX1A on top of tyrosine hydroxylase. They are the cell lost in Parkinson's disease and the most clinically advanced hPSC-derived neuron, with the Studer and Lund protocols now feeding first-in-human trials.
cell_types.maturation_note: Engraftable precursors by day 16-25. In vitro the neurons are still immature at day 40 (resting potential about -35 mV, single action potential only); by day 60-75 they have adult-like properties, HCN and KCNQ currents, 1-3 Hz pacemaking and calcium-dependent dopamine release. Behavioural recovery after grafting takes 3-5 months.

morphology.endpoint: A dense carpet of small neuronal cell bodies with very long, thin, often bundled neurites; after 50+ days the processes form thick fascicles and the culture looks fibrous. Re-plating at high density is part of the protocol, so the monolayer is thick and uneven.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Dense single-cell monolayer plated at 4 x 10^5 cells/cm2 - much denser than most neural inductions.

stages.label: Ventralised neuroepithelium
stages.look: Uniform, tightly packed sheet; no rosettes should form, which distinguishes the floor-plate route from the rosette route.

stages.label: Midbrain floor plate
stages.look: A flat, compact sheet of small cells; the key readout here is immunostaining (FOXA2/LMX1A/EN1), not morphology.

stages.label: mDA precursors
stages.look: Cells start to round up and extend short processes; this is the cryopreservation and grafting stage.

stages.label: Young mDA neurons
stages.look: Clear neuronal morphology with branched neurites over a background of flatter cells.

stages.label: Mature mDA network
stages.look: Long fasciculated neurites and larger, angular, often multipolar cell bodies (the GIRK2+/A9-like ones).

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent before grafting; residual pluripotent cells are the main teratoma risk.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Floor-plate identity. Requires strong SHH activation (purmorphamine with or without recombinant SHH).

markers.name: LMX1A
markers.note: Induced in FOXA2+ cells by CHIR99021; FOXA2/LMX1A co-expression is the midbrain signature and the day-11 go/no-go check.

markers.name: OTX2
markers.note: Must be retained: sustained high CHIR loses OTX2 and the culture turns hindbrain.

markers.name: EN1
markers.note: The marker the CHIR-boost protocol was built around; robust EN1 at day 11 predicts clean midbrain identity, and EN1 knockout lines lose the benefit of the boost.

markers.name: NR4A2
markers.note: Marks cell-cycle exit; the Kriks grafting stage (about day 25) was chosen around its onset.

markers.name: TH
markers.note: Necessary but not sufficient - rosette-derived cultures also make TH+ cells, which lack FOXA2/LMX1A and overgrow after grafting.

markers.name: PITX3
markers.note: Midbrain-specific; confirmed in TH+ cells in grafts.

markers.name: SLC6A3
markers.note: Late maturation marker; its expression level sets how quickly grafts restore function.

markers.name: KCNJ6
markers.note: A9 identity; 65% of TH+ cells in CHIR-boost grafts at 6 months. GIRK2+/TH+ cells are larger, angular and often multipolar.

markers.name: CALB1
markers.note: A10 identity; 23% of TH+ cells in the same grafts, smaller and rounder, concentrated in the graft centre.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Forebrain contamination; suppressed by the CHIR boost. High PAX6 at day 11 means the patterning failed.

markers.name: HOXA2
markers.note: Hindbrain contamination, promoted by FGF8 and by sustained high CHIR.

markers.name: TPH2
markers.note: Serotonergic cells are <1% in good grafts; they have been linked to graft-induced dyskinesia, so worth counting.

functional_assays: HPLC for dopamine, DOPAC and HVA, and KCl-evoked, calcium-dependent release
Patch clamp: slow 1-3 Hz spontaneous pacemaking with subthreshold oscillation
HCN (Ih) and KCNQ (M) currents at day 60+
6-OHDA-lesioned rodent grafting with amphetamine-induced rotation, stepping and cylinder tests
Post-thaw viability after cryopreservation of day-16 precursors
qc: Day 11: FOXA2+/LMX1A+ co-expression with OTX2 retained and EN1 robustly induced
Day 11: PAX6 low (forebrain) and hindbrain markers low
TH+ cells must co-express FOXA2, LMX1A and NURR1 - TH alone is not acceptance
Ki-67+ cells < 1% before grafting
Serotonergic (5-HT) cells < 1%
Post-thaw viability > 80% for cryopreserved day-16 precursors

protocols.name: Midbrain floor-plate route (LSB/S/F8/CHIR)
protocols.principle: Strong SHH activation makes FOXA2+ floor plate, and adding the GSK3-beta inhibitor CHIR99021 induces LMX1A in those floor-plate cells - the FOXA2/LMX1A co-expression that is unique to the midbrain. Floor-plate-derived dopamine neurons engraft, whereas rosette-derived ones overgrow.
protocols.efficiency: Significantly higher percentage of TH+ cells than the rosette route, with ~8-fold higher dopamine content by HPLC; the paper does not state a single purity figure
protocols.start_requirements: hESC (H9, H1) or hiPSC lines taken into a modified dual-SMAD-inhibition floor-plate induction; the patterning window for CHIR is days 3-11, so the culture must be ready to respond by day 3.
materials: Ascorbic acid, BDNF, GDNF, TGF-beta3, dibutyryl-cAMP
tips: FOXA2/LMX1A co-expression at day 11 is the go/no-go checkpoint; TH alone is not enough, because rosette-derived cultures also make TH+ cells that lack FOXA2 and LMX1A.
Day 25, around the time NURR1 comes on and cells exit the cell cycle, is the grafting stage the authors chose.
Few GABA or serotonergic neurons are produced (<1% in grafts), which matters for graft-induced dyskinesia risk.
pitfalls: Rosette-derived grafts in the same study showed massive neural overgrowth (>20 mm3) and retained FOXG1+ forebrain and Ki-67+ proliferating cells - the comparison that makes the floor-plate route worth the effort.
Dropping CHIR gives FOXA2+ cells with no LMX1A (hypothalamic-like); LSB alone gives LMX1A without FOXA2.
Functional recovery in rodents takes 3-4 months after grafting, so short studies will look negative.
unverified: Working concentrations of LDN-193189, SB431542, SHH C25II, purmorphamine, FGF8, CHIR99021 and the maturation factors are in the paper's supplementary methods, which were not retrievable; the main text gives the schedule but not the doses. Use the Kim 2021 doses below, or the paper's supplement.

protocols.name: Biphasic WNT (CHIR boost) - clinical-grade midbrain DA neurons
protocols.principle: Low CHIR first caudalises to midbrain/hindbrain, then a short high-dose CHIR 'boost' locks in midbrain identity by driving EN1 while suppressing both diencephalic/subthalamic and hindbrain markers - without exogenous FGF8 and without the FGF8-associated fibroblast and choroid-plexus contaminants.
protocols.efficiency: Highly consistent marker panel across 16 independent differentiations at days 10/16/20; in vivo, 9,173 +/- 2,576 TH+/hNA+ cells survived at 5.5 months, 65% of TH+ cells GIRK2+ and 23% CALB1+
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs on vitronectin in Essential 8, passaged with EDTA, used between passage 35-55; dissociated with Accutase and plated at 4 x 10^5 cells/cm2 on Geltrex for day 0.
materials: BDNF, GDNF, TGF-beta3, ascorbic acid, dibutyryl-cAMP
tips: Timing of the boost matters: boosting at day 3 strongly induced an unwanted non-mDA progenitor marker, and boosting above 7.5 uM caused dose-dependent cell death - day 4 at 7.5 uM was the optimum.

CHIR potency is medium-dependent: KSR-based media contain lysophosphatidic acid that blunts CHIR, which is why 'standard' doses range from 0.4-1 uM in defined medium but ~3 uM in KSR. Titrate for your medium and lot.
Late FGF8b gives EN1 levels as good as the boost but raises COL1A1 (perivascular fibroblast-like) and other contaminants - the reason this protocol avoids exogenous FGF8.
EN1 knockout lines lose the benefit of the boost, which is the authors' evidence that EN1 is the mediator.
pitfalls: Batch-to-batch variability in EN1 induction at a fixed CHIR dose is the classic failure mode; small dose differences flip the culture to hindbrain or diencephalic fate.
Holding high CHIR throughout ('High Chir') loses OTX2 and induces hindbrain markers.
Initial graft survival is usually under 10% of the cells injected, so dose accordingly.
A9 versus A10 proportions are still not controllable.

protocols.name: STEMdiff Midbrain Neuron Differentiation + Maturation
protocols.principle: NPCs from the SMADi neural induction kit are patterned to midbrain neuronal precursors in differentiation medium supplemented with recombinant Shh, then replated and matured for at least 2 weeks in a BrainPhys-based medium to give neurons that include TH-positive dopaminergic cells.
protocols.efficiency: ≥ 15% TH-positive dopaminergic neurons; ≥ 90% class III β-tubulin-positive neurons; < 10% GFAP-positive astrocytes
protocols.start_requirements: Starts from NPCs, not hPSCs: generate them with STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (Catalog #08581). Monolayer route: passage day 18 - 21 (passage 3) NPCs with ACCUTASE and seed 80,000 - 125,000 cells/cm2 on PLO/laminin (15 µg/mL PLO, 10 µg/mL laminin) in 2 mL induction medium for 24 h. EB route: midbrain medium is applied much earlier, on day 6, one day after EBs are replated. Day numbers follow the PIS, which counts from day 0 of neural induction with STEMdiff SMADi Neural Induction Kit (monolayer route shown; where the PIS gives a range, the earliest day is used). duration_days counts from NPC plating.
materials: STEMdiff Neural Rosette Selection Reagent (05832) for the EB route
tips: Both complete media keep up to 1 month at 2 - 8°C; protect the maturation medium from light.
On the EB route the best day to start midbrain medium after replating varies from day 1 to day 4 depending on the line.
Seeding densities of NPCs and precursors should be optimised per line.
pitfalls: Shh is not included in the kit and must be added to the differentiation medium at 200 ng/mL.
Neurons detach easily: change only half the medium, dropwise against the wall.
unverified: The two protocol diagrams are images; days come from the written steps.
The monolayer NPC density is printed as '80 - 125,000 cells/cm2'; read here as 80,000 - 125,000 cells/cm2, matching the forebrain kit sheet.
The number of days in differentiation medium on the monolayer route is not stated as such; 6 days follows from day 19 - 22 to day 25 - 28.
Day 39 is day 25 plus the stated minimum of 2 weeks of maturation; the PIS does not print that day number.

protocols.name: Gibco PSC Dopaminergic Neuron Differentiation Kit (floor plate route, ~35 days)
protocols.principle: Three supplements drive a three-step floor-plate route: specification of hPSCs into midbrain floor plate progenitors, expansion of those progenitors (adherent passages, then spheres), and maturation into TH-positive midbrain dopaminergic neurons. Progenitors can be banked at passage 2.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained feeder-free in Essential 8 or Essential 8 Flex on vitronectin (VTN-N), about 70-85% confluent with differentiated colonies removed; MEF-grown lines need at least 4 passages in Essential 8 first. On day -1 seed single cells on vitronectin-coated plates (10 µg/mL coating) at 3.0-5.0 × 10^4 viable cells/cm² in Essential 8 + 10 µM Y-27632 (density given for H9; tune it so the well is fully confluent by day 7).
materials: PSC Dopaminergic Neuron Differentiation Kit (Floor Plate Specification Supplement 20X, 5 mL; Floor Plate Cell Expansion Kit: 500 mL Base + 10 mL Supplement 50X; Dopaminergic Neuron Maturation Supplement 50X, 10 mL)
Nunclon Sphera flasks or dishes for suspension culture
Optional: Human Dopaminergic Neuron Immunocytochemistry Kit (A29515)
tips: Schedule from Thermo user guide MAN0015919 Rev. 2.0; days are counted from the first day in specification medium (seeding is day -1).
Run a 48-well density series for 7 days and stain FOXA2/OTX2 before committing a new line to the full 35 days.
Supplements are heat-sensitive: no more than 1 h at 37°C, complete media used within 2 weeks at 4°C, one refreeze at most.
Each supplement is also sold separately (A3146801, A3165801, A3147401), useful when optimisation consumes extra specification medium.
Some lines differentiate without the sphere step (one extra adherent passage, plate for maturation on day 21), but the guide recommends spheres for untested lines.
Lines maintained in mTeSR1 can be started directly; the guide suggests Neurobasal base plus 1X B-27 in the maturation medium for them.
One optional extra passage (to passage 3) gives another 4-6-fold progenitor expansion; further passaging lowers FOXA2 in the resulting TH neurons.
pitfalls: Do not continue past specification if FOXA2/OTX2 double-positive cells are below 60%.
Slow-growing lines that are not confluent by day 6-7 specify poorly; raise the seeding density.
Fast aspiration or dispensing during specification strips cells; over-confluent layers can peel (Geltrex 1:100 is the suggested fallback).
Laminin coats lose function if they dry; residual poly-D-lysine is toxic, so rinse thoroughly.
Tissue-culture-treated plastic in the sphere step lets cells attach or fuse into one large sphere.
unverified: No numeric final purity (% TH+) is stated in the user guide or on the product page; efficiency left null.
The exact split ratio at the day-12 passage is given both as a fixed density (2.0 × 10^5 cells/cm²) and as roughly 1:4-6; the density is used here.

cell_types.notes: This is the cell type where protocols genuinely disagree, and the disagreement is about CHIR99021. Published doses span 0.4-1 uM in defined medium and about 3 uM in KSR-based medium, because knockout serum replacement contains lysophosphatidic acid that blunts CHIR; the CHIR-boost protocol adds a second, 7.5 uM phase from day 4. Kim and colleagues documented dramatic batch-to-batch swings in EN1 induction at an identical 0.7 uM dose, so the dose must be titrated per medium, per lot and per line, with EN1 at day 11 as the readout. The FGF8 question is similarly unsettled: Kirkeby/Nolbrant use late FGF8b to refine midbrain identity (Nolbrant S, Heuer A, Parmar M, Kirkeby A, Nat Protoc 2017;12:1962-79; PMID 28858290, doi 10.1038/nprot.2017.078), while Kim and colleagues avoid it because it raises COL1A1+ and hindbrain contaminants. Kirkeby A, Grealish S, Wolf DA, et al., Cell Rep 2012;1:703-14 (PMID 22813745, doi 10.1016/j.celrep.2012.04.009) is the original dose-dependent WNT patterning paper.

cell_types.name: Cortical GABAergic interneurons
cell_types.summary: Inhibitory, locally projecting neurons that make up about 20% of cortical neurons and are born in the ventral telencephalon before migrating tangentially into the cortex. Their dysfunction is implicated in schizophrenia, autism and epilepsy, and they are needed to build balanced excitatory-inhibitory networks from hPSCs.
cell_types.maturation_note: MGE-like progenitors at day 18 and migratory precursors by day 32, but functional maturation is genuinely slow: on a mouse cortical feeder the neurons reach fairly mature properties in about 30 days of co-culture, while the companion study reports an intrinsic timeline of up to 7 months for full subtype maturation, mirroring human development. Programming with ASCL1+DLX2 reaches synaptic maturity in about 5 weeks and keeps improving to 7 weeks.

morphology.endpoint: Small, often bipolar or multipolar neurons with fine, highly branched neurites, usually sitting on top of a feeder layer of cortical neurons and glia. Interneurons are visibly smaller and more delicate than the pyramidal neurons they sit on.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact flat colonies; XLSB starts on the attached monolayer.

stages.label: Forebrain neuroepithelium
stages.look: Uniform dense neuroepithelial sheet; FOXG1 and PAX6 positive, before any SHH exposure.

stages.label: MGE-like progenitors
stages.look: Still a progenitor monolayer, Nestin and Ki-67 positive; identity is defined by NKX2-1 and OLIG2 staining.

stages.label: Migratory precursors
stages.look: Ki-67 falls, DCX and TUJ1 rise; the cells are bipolar or unipolar with a leading process, the migratory morphology.

stages.label: Maturing interneurons
stages.look: Fine, densely branched neurites over the cortical feeder, with VGAT puncta along dendrites of neighbouring cells.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Telencephalic identity; raised by XAV939. >90% of NKX2-1+ cells co-express it in the day 10-18 condition, whereas early SHH (days 2-18) suppresses it and gives hypothalamic cells.

markers.name: NKX2-1
markers.note: Ventral prosencephalic progenitors. Unlike mouse, human hPSC-derived interneurons keep expressing it after becoming postmitotic, so loss of NKX2-1 is not a maturity readout here.

markers.name: OLIG2
markers.note: Nearly 80% of NKX2-1+ cells in the day 10-18 window; separates the ganglionic eminence from the OLIG2-negative preoptic anlage.

markers.name: LHX6
markers.note: Selectively enriched in the day 10-18 condition at day 32 - the best discriminator of MGE-like versus hypothalamic or cholinergic output.

markers.name: DLX2
markers.note: Pan-DLX staining is 88-92% positive in programmed GABAergic neurons; DLX2 is the second programming factor.

markers.name: GAD1
markers.note: With GAD2 (GAD65), 83-94% positive in programmed cultures.

markers.name: SLC32A1
markers.note: Presynaptic GABA transporter; its puncta should line up with postsynaptic gephyrin.

markers.name: GABA
markers.note: About 80% of sorted GFP+ cells after co-culture in the Maroof protocol; 81-89% in programmed cultures.

markers.name: SST
markers.note: About 37% of programmed AD-iN cells at 5 weeks; appears only in the day 10-18 condition in directed differentiation. Higher SHH favours SST over PV.

markers.name: PVALB
markers.note: The hardest subtype: about 5% of GFP+ cells by automated imaging, and only a subset look convincingly interneuron-like. PV is expressed late even in primate development.

markers.name: RAX
markers.note: Enriched when SHH is given early (days 2-18); the signature of the wrong ventral fate.

markers.name: TH
markers.note: Large numbers of TH+ cells in the early-SHH condition, consistent with NKX2-1-lineage hypothalamic neurons.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Counter-intuitive but real: FOXA2 is transiently expressed in the human telencephalic ganglionic eminence and in hPSC-derived NKX2-1+ cells, though not in mouse. Do not read it as floor-plate contamination.

Migration after transplantation into neonatal or adult mouse cortex
Bicuculline- or picrotoxin-sensitive spontaneous IPSCs
Evoked IPSCs on extracellular field stimulation
VGAT/gephyrin co-localisation
Co-culture with NGN2 glutamatergic neurons to show mixed EPSC/IPSC activity

Day 32: LHX6 protein detectable (MGE identity) and RAX absent
GABA+ >= 80% of sorted cells after co-culture, or >= 85% in programmed cultures
Bicuculline- or picrotoxin-sensitive IPSCs recordable
VIP and calretinin absent if an MGE-restricted population is intended

protocols.name: XLSB + timed SHH: NKX2-1+ MGE-like progenitors to cortical interneurons
protocols.principle: WNT inhibition with XAV939 secures forebrain (FOXG1) identity, and then the timing of SHH activation decides which ventral progenitor you get: late SHH (days 10-18) gives FOXG1+/OLIG2+ MGE-like progenitors that migrate like cortical interneurons and mature into SST+ and PV+ cells.
protocols.efficiency: >90% of NKX2.1::GFP+ cells co-express FOXG1 in the day 10-18 condition and nearly 80% co-express OLIG2; after co-culture about 80% of sorted GFP+ cells are GABA+, with roughly 5% of total GFP+ cells PV+ by automated imaging
protocols.start_requirements: hESC/hiPSC on MEFs, dissociated with Accutase; KSR medium for induction switching to N2, then Neurobasal/B27 for neuronal differentiation. An NKX2-1 reporter line makes FACS enrichment possible but is not essential.
tips: Timing of SHH, not its dose, is the lever: days 2-18 gives FOXG1-negative hypothalamic cells (RAX+, many TH+ and nNOS+), days 6-18 gives FOXG1+/OLIG2-negative cells enriched for cholinergic (ChAT+) neurons, days 10-18 gives the MGE-like interneuron progenitors.

Maturation is environment-dependent: on mouse cortical feeders the neurons mature noticeably faster than on hESC-derived human cortical feeders, which may simply reflect more astrocytes in the mouse prep.

Nicholas CR, Chen J, Tang Y, et al., Cell Stem Cell 2013;12:573-86 (PMID 23642366, doi 10.1016/j.stem.2013.04.005) is the companion study: MGE-like progenitors mature over an intrinsic timeline of up to 7 months, which is the realistic horizon for fully mature subtypes.
pitfalls: Human hPSC-derived interneurons keep expressing NKX2-1 after they become postmitotic, unlike mouse cells where Nkx2-1 is extinguished before they enter the cortex - so NKX2-1 loss is not a good maturity readout here, and some cells may be striatal rather than cortical interneurons.
PV+ cells are rare (~5%) and only a subset look convincingly interneuron-like; PV is a late marker.
Transplanted precursors stay immature for months, with immature growth cones at 3 months post-graft.
unverified: The paper lists SHH C25II over a 50-500 ng/mL range and purmorphamine at 1-2 uM; the stated maximal condition is 5 nM SHH with 1 uM purmorphamine. FGF2 at 5-10 ng/mL is listed among reagents but its schedule is not given in the main text.

protocols.name: ASCL1 + DLX2 programming (AD-iN cells)
protocols.principle: Transient expression of ASCL1 with DLX2 converts hPSCs in one step into an essentially pure GABAergic population with forebrain (ganglionic eminence) identity, reaching synaptic maturity in about five weeks without passing through a patterned progenitor.
protocols.efficiency: 93.2 +/- 3.4% of cells MAP2+ at 4 weeks; with ASCL1+MYT1L+DLX2, 91.9 +/- 6.6% pan-DLX+, 81.4 +/- 4.7% GABA+ and 83.5 +/- 6.7% GAD67/65+; with ASCL1+DLX2 alone at 5 weeks, 93.5 +/- 2.7% FOXG1+, 89.1 +/- 3.5% GABA+ and 94.4 +/- 4.2% GAD65/67+; intrinsic properties indistinguishable across one ESC and three iPSC lines
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs in mTeSR1 dissociated with Accutase and plated on Matrigel-coated six-well plates with 2 uM thiazovivin on day -2 (H1 about 5 x 10^5, iPSC 7.5 x 10^5 cells per well).
tips: ASCL1 + DLX2 alone is sufficient; MYT1L mainly speeds up early morphological complexity, and endogenous MYT1L comes on by day 4 anyway.
Subtype markers come out in largely non-overlapping subpopulations: about 37% SST+, 28% calbindin+, 9% calretinin+ at 5 weeks, with ISL1 in roughly 20% and only a small fraction PV+.
14 days of doxycycline is enough for cell-fate stability: the grafted cells stay GABAergic and keep maturing in the mouse brain for 3 months without the transgene.
pitfalls: These are programmed rather than developmentally patterned neurons: the population spans MGE, LGE and CGE-like signatures plus olfactory bulb, striatal and prethalamic identities, so it is not a pure cortical interneuron model.
PV+ cells remain rare, and adding subtype transcription factors on top of ASCL1+DLX2 did not change the subtype mix.
CTIP2, NKX2-1, SP8 and DARPP-32 cells are essentially absent, so this is not a route to striatal projection neurons.
unverified: Puromycin and hygromycin concentrations are not stated in the methods text.
Doxycycline and Ara-C are quoted in the paper as 2 g/L; reproduced as printed.

protocols.start_requirements: Source hPSCs must have been maintained by single-cell passaging (StemFit Basic04, StemFit AK02N or StemFlex) and be at least 14 days post-thaw.
