cell_types.notes: Timing, not dose, is the control knob in directed differentiation: the same SHH concentration gives hypothalamic cells at days 2-18, cholinergic neurons at days 6-18, and MGE-like interneuron progenitors at days 10-18. Expect slow maturation - the companion paper (Nicholas CR, Chen J, Tang Y, et al., Cell Stem Cell 2013;12:573-86; PMID 23642366, doi 10.1016/j.stem.2013.04.005) found an intrinsic timeline of up to 7 months, and grafted precursors still look immature at 3 months. Mouse cortical feeders accelerate maturation noticeably more than human ones do, which is a confound to keep in mind when comparing papers. Transcription-factor programming (ASCL1+DLX2) gets to mature inhibitory synapses in about 5 weeks but produces a mixture of MGE-, LGE- and CGE-like identities plus olfactory bulb and prethalamic cells, so it is a GABAergic neuron model rather than a cortical interneuron model. PV+ neurons remain scarce in every published route.

cell_types.name: Cerebral (brain) organoids
cell_types.summary: Self-organising 3D tissues that reproduce the cytoarchitecture of the developing human cortex - ventricle-like lumens, a ventricular and subventricular zone, inner and outer radial glia, and layered projection neurons - and later astrocytes. They are used for human-specific neurodevelopment, microcephaly and other developmental disorders, and for questions that need tissue-level organisation.
cell_types.maturation_note: SOX2/PAX6 neuroepithelium by day 12-20, neurons from one month, multiple brain regions and layer identities by 2-3 months, astrocytes and inhibitory precursors by 6 months. Cortical spheroids map transcriptionally to 19-24 post-conception weeks at 2.5 months. Progenitor zones disappear by 5-6 months and self-patterned organoids then start to shrink.

morphology.endpoint: An opaque sphere of a few millimetres with translucent lobes at the surface. In section, rosette-like ventricular zones with bright lumens are ringed by a dense neuronal mantle; pigmented patches mark retinal tissue in self-patterned organoids.

stages.label: Embryoid bodies
stages.look: 9,000 cells per well in a U- or V-bottom low-attachment plate; dead cells around the aggregate on day 1 are normal.

stages.label: Brightened EBs
stages.look: 500-600 um aggregates with smooth edges and a translucent surface - the signal to move to induction medium.

stages.label: Neuroepithelium on the EB surface
stages.look: Radially organised, optically translucent pseudostratified tissue around the outside of the aggregate.

stages.label: Neuroepithelial buds
stages.look: Large continuous epithelial buds with fluid-filled, ventricle-like cavities protruding from the Matrigel droplet; migratory fibroblast-like cells spread into the gel.

stages.label: Expanded cortical tissue
stages.look: A millimetre-scale organoid too large for a standard tissue-culture scope; neuroepithelial loops with a dense neuronal mantle, visible only in section.

stages.label: Mature organoid with glia
stages.look: Progenitor zones have shrunk away; tissue is mostly neurons with S100B+/GFAP+ astrocytes threaded through the neuropil.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Inner radial glia inside the ventricular zone and outer radial glia beyond it; both phospho-vimentin+ in mitosis but dividing at different positions.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Expressed in 100% of dorsally patterned organoids at 1, 3 and 6 months; >85% of cells at day 18 in cortical spheroids.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Forebrain identity; in self-patterned organoids it marks the forebrain region among several.

markers.name: EMX1
markers.note: Dorsal identity; 89% of dorsally patterned organoids across lines and timepoints.

markers.name: EOMES
markers.note: Defines a subventricular-zone-like rim around each ventricular zone.

markers.name: HOPX
markers.note: Outer radial glia, the progenitor type expanded in human cortex; present in dorsally patterned organoids from 3 months.

markers.name: TBR1
markers.note: Peaks at about 41% of cells at day 76 in cortical spheroids.

markers.name: BCL11B
markers.note: Expressed by 3 months and maintained; only about 3% of cells co-express CTIP2 and SATB2, as expected.

markers.name: SATB2
markers.note: Upper-layer identity; rises up to 7-fold from day 52 to day 137 and is the honest test of culture duration.

markers.name: S100B
markers.note: Astrocytes are genuinely late: 2.7% GFAP+ at day 35, about 8% at day 76 and almost 20% at day 180 in cortical spheroids.

markers.name: GFAP
markers.note: Early on it marks radial glial processes inside the ventricular zone rather than astrocytes - read it together with position and morphology.

markers.name: TTR
markers.note: A normal region of self-patterned organoids (highly convoluted cuboidal epithelium) but an unwanted identity in a dorsally patterned preparation.

markers.name: NKX2-1
markers.note: Present in self-patterned organoids; should be minimal under dorsal patterning.

markers.name: MKI67
markers.note: Positive in all 3-month organoids tested; its disappearance by 5-6 months marks the end of neurogenesis.

Calcium imaging of intact or sliced organoids (Fluo-4, Fura-2)
Single-cell RNA-seq with intraclass correlation or mutual information for reproducibility
Array tomography and electron microscopy for synapses and glycogen granules
EdU/BrdU birthdating for the order of layer genesis
Live imaging of interkinetic nuclear migration in radial glia
qc: EBs 500-600 um, brightened with smooth edges before neural induction
Radially organised neuroepithelium before Matrigel embedding
PAX6 and MAP2 positive in essentially all organoids by 1-3 months; EMX1 positive for dorsal patterning
CTIP2 and SATB2 present by 3 months
Control organoids from the same batch and medium analysed alongside every experimental group
Low cleaved caspase-3 and low hypoxia signature in the core

protocols.name: Self-patterned cerebral organoids (Matrigel droplet + agitation)
protocols.principle: Embryoid bodies are given a minimal neural induction medium that will not support mesoderm or endoderm, then embedded in a Matrigel droplet that provides the missing basement membrane so continuous, correctly oriented neuroepithelium can bud out; agitation then supplies enough oxygen and nutrients for the tissue to grow into multiple brain regions without added patterning factors.
protocols.efficiency: If EBs clear and brighten properly, 60-80% go on to show neuroectoderm; neuroepithelial buds then form in 30-80% of organoids. Batch-to-batch variability is substantial and is the protocol's main limitation
protocols.start_requirements: hESC or iPSC colonies, feeder-dependent or feeder-free, 70-80% confluent in one well of a 6-well plate with no more than 5-10% differentiation and clear colony borders. One well yields roughly a 96-well plate of EBs.
materials: N2, B27 (with and without vitamin A)
tips: Three timing decisions make or break a batch: start only from colonies with optimal morphology, move EBs to induction medium at the right size and brightness, and get the tissues into Matrigel as soon as radial organisation appears.
An orbital shaker is a practical substitute for the spinner flask and lets many conditions run in parallel; the authors saw no morphological difference.
Progenitor zones shrink and disappear by 5-6 months and organoids then start shrinking after 6-7 months, though they can be kept over a year.
Non-radial translucent buds are not ideal but usually do not ruin the organoid, as long as radial organisation is present somewhere.
pitfalls: Variability between preparations is large, so a phenotype must be robust enough to sit outside the normal range; always grow control organoids in the same batch and the same medium.
No meninges and no vasculature, which caps growth and gives necrotic cores without agitation.
Regional identity is self-patterned and stochastic - a given organoid may be mostly non-forebrain (see Velasco 2019 for the quantified comparison).
Six-layer cortical architecture is never achieved; only a rudimentary deep/superficial split.
unverified: 2-mercaptoethanol is added as 87.5 uL of a 1:100 dilution per 250 mL; final molarity not stated.
The source gives the whole-organoid culture period as open-ended (up to a year); 60 days is used here as the typical analysis window.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation

factors.name: bFGF (FGF2)
factors.role: low FGF2 for the first ~4 days

factors.name: Y-27632 (ROCK inhibitor)
factors.role: limits cell death during aggregation; first ~4 days only

Feed with plain hESC medium (no ROCK inhibitor, no bFGF) while EBs are 350-600 um

stages.name: Neural induction
stages.base_medium: Neural induction medium: DMEM/F12 + 1% N2 + 1% GlutaMAX + 1% NEAA + 1 ug/mL heparin
stages.feeding: Add another 500 uL of induction medium 48 h after transfer
actions: Transfer each EB with a cut 200 uL tip (1-1.5 mm opening) into 500 uL of neural induction medium in a low-attachment 24-well plate
Never scoop EBs with a spatula - it damages them
stages.checkpoint: After 4-5 days the outer surface shows radially organised pseudostratified neuroepithelium; move to Matrigel promptly, late transfer compromises later morphology

stages.name: Matrigel embedding and static culture
stages.base_medium: Cerebral organoid differentiation medium (1:1 DMEM/F12 : Neurobasal, 0.5% N2, 1:4000 insulin, GlutaMAX, NEAA, 1:100 B27 without vitamin A, 3.5 uL/L 2-mercaptoethanol, pen/strep)

factors.name: B27 without vitamin A
factors.role: no retinoid at this stage, to avoid caudalising the tissue

stages.feeding: Feed at 48 h; full medium change by tilting the dish and letting droplets settle
actions: Make a 4x4 grid of dimples in Parafilm, transfer one tissue per dimple with a cut 200 uL tip, remove excess medium and drip about 30 uL Matrigel over each
Centre the tissue in the droplet with a 10 uL tip before the Matrigel sets, then polymerise 20-30 min at 37 C
Add 5 mL differentiation medium (no vitamin A) and shake the droplets off the Parafilm
Keep static for 4 days
stages.checkpoint: Within 1-3 days, buds of expanded neuroepithelium with fluid-filled cavities; migratory fibroblast-like cells spreading into the Matrigel are normal and seem to help budding

stages.name: Agitated growth and regional diversification
stages.base_medium: Cerebral organoid differentiation medium with B27 containing vitamin A
stages.feeding: Full medium change every 3-4 days on a shaker, or weekly in a spinner flask
actions: Transfer embedded organoids with a cut 1 mL tip (about 3 mm opening) to a 125 mL spinning bioreactor in 75-100 mL medium, or to an orbital shaker at 85 rpm
Do not put more than 32 organoids in one 125 mL flask or they fuse
Section and immunostain rather than trying to image whole organoids after day 15-20
stages.checkpoint: Day 12-20: SOX2/PAX6 neuroepithelium around ventricle-like cavities. From one month: TUJ1/DCX neurons, FOXG1 forebrain, TTR choroid plexus, PROX1/FZD9 hippocampus, NKX2-1 ventral forebrain, pigmented retina; inner and outer radial glia (both SOX2+, phospho-vimentin+ in mitosis) dividing at different positions; TBR2 intermediate progenitors; RELN/TBR1 preplate

protocols.name: Human cortical spheroids (hCS) - no scaffold, no replating
protocols.principle: Intact hPSC colonies are lifted into suspension, neuralised with dorsomorphin and SB431542, then expanded with FGF2 and EGF; the long mitogen exposure lets the progenitors run through neurogenesis and then switch to gliogenesis, so the spheroids end up with laminated cortical neurons and non-reactive astrocytes from the same genetic background, in a form thin enough to slice and patch.
protocols.efficiency: By day 18, over 85% of cells PAX6+ and more than 80% of those FOXG1+; at ~7 weeks 78.8 +/- 2.5% TUBB3+ and 36.2 +/- 3.6% NEUN+; GFAP+ cells 2.7 +/- 0.7% at day 35, about 8% at day 76 and almost 20% at day 180; reproducible across seven iPSC lines from five subjects
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs grown on inactivated DR4 mouse embryonic fibroblast feeders; intact colonies are detached with low-concentration dispase (0.7 mg/mL) for about 30 min - not dissociated to single cells.
tips: Transcriptionally these spheroids map to the late mid-fetal human cortex (19-24 post-conception weeks) at 2.5 months, later than 2D monolayer or other 3D methods.

Astrocytes arise spontaneously - no CNTF, LIF or serum - which is why they read as non-reactive. Adding serum flips them to a reactive, polygonal phenotype with LCN2 and other reactive transcripts up.
The method is deliberately simple: no replating, no Matrigel embedding, no bioreactor; just low-attachment plates with twice-weekly medium changes.
Only dorsal telencephalic excitatory neurons are made - there are no interneurons here either.
pitfalls: Starting from single cells instead of intact colonies changes the method; the colony-lifting step is part of the design.
Superficial-layer neurons only reach parity with deep layers after months; ending at day 52 gives a deep-layer-biased culture.
Daily medium changes for the first 10 days are labour-intensive and are where contamination creeps in.
unverified: Y-27632 concentration for the first 24 h is not stated in the methods.

source.title: Functional cortical neurons and astrocytes from human pluripotent stem cells in 3D culture.

stages.name: Spheroid formation and neural induction
stages.base_medium: hiPSC medium without FGF2 (DMEM/F12 with 20% knockout serum, NEAA, GlutaMAX, 0.1 nM 2-mercaptoethanol)
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Transfer the detached colonies into ultra-low-attachment 100 mm plates; they fold into spheres within hours
Give both SMAD inhibitors for the first five days
stages.checkpoint: Uniform floating spheroids

stages.name: Progenitor expansion
stages.base_medium: Neural medium: Neurobasal + B27 without vitamin A + GlutaMAX + pen/strep

factors.name: EGF
factors.role: progenitor expansion; the long exposure is what later drives the gliogenic switch

stages.feeding: Daily for the first 10 days, then every other day for 9 days
actions: Move the spheroids to neural medium with FGF2 and EGF on day 6
stages.checkpoint: Day 18: >85% PAX6+, >80% FOXG1+; spheroids >300 um by two weeks

stages.name: Neuronal differentiation
stages.feeding: Every other day
actions: Swap FGF2/EGF for BDNF and NT-3 on day 25
stages.checkpoint: Ventricular-zone-like rosettes around N-cadherin+ lumens with a TBR2+ SVZ-like rim; PAX6+ radial glia with GFAP+ processes and interkinetic nuclear migration

stages.name: Maturation, lamination and astrogenesis
stages.base_medium: Neural medium only, no growth factors
stages.feeding: Medium change every 4 days
actions: From day 43 use plain neural medium; spheroids reach up to 4 mm by 2.5 months and can be kept 9 months
Slice to 250 um for acute recordings, or dissociate for monolayer work
stages.checkpoint: TBR1 peaks at ~40.7% of cells at day 76; superficial markers (SATB2, BRN2, CUX1/2) rise up to 7-fold from day 52 to 137 and end roughly equal to deep layers; neurons laminate concentrically around the ventricular zone; 88.8% show spontaneous synaptic activity abolished by NBQX+D-AP5

protocols.name: Dorsally patterned forebrain organoids (reproducible cell diversity)
protocols.principle: Rather than letting organoids pattern themselves, WNT and TGF-beta are inhibited for the first 18 days to fix a dorsal forebrain identity; adapted to spinner-flask bioreactors, this gives large organoids whose cell-type composition is as reproducible between organoids as between individual human or mouse brains.
protocols.efficiency: About 90% efficiency of forebrain cell-type generation (93/103 organoids); 95% of 21 organoids profiled by single-cell RNA-seq gave a near-indistinguishable set of cell types; 100% expressed PAX6 and MAP2 at 1, 3 and 6 months, 89% also EMX1; intraclass correlation of cell-type proportions 0.85 at 3 months versus 0.39 for self-patterned whole-brain organoids
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs on Geltrex in mTeSR1, 80-90% confluent, below passage 50, mycoplasma-negative, karyotypically normal, with tightly packed round cells and large nucleoli.
tips: If you need quantitative, organoid-to-organoid comparisons, this patterned model is the one with the published reproducibility numbers; the self-patterned whole-brain model gave forebrain cells in only 4 of 19 organoids in the same study.
Exogenous patterning does not cost you fidelity: dorsally patterned and self-patterned organoids correlated equally well (0.67-0.80) with human fetal cortex cells.
Three months is already enough for most neurodevelopmental questions; six months is needed for astrocytes and later-born types.
Reproducibility held across five stem cell lines, three independent batches and both sexes.
pitfalls: Starting material quality is explicitly the gate: below passage 50, mycoplasma-free, normal karyotype, 80-90% confluent with undifferentiated morphology.
Occasional organoids stall - one of 12 at six months expressed no neuronal markers at all and had to be excluded.
The protocol consumes many lots of FBS, KSR and Matrigel over a long differentiation (13, 4 and 23 lots respectively in this study), so lot variability has to be tracked.
unverified: This is a modification of Kadoshima et al.; the B27 concentration in CDM IV is not numerically stated in the methods.

source.authors: Velasco S, Kedaigle AJ, Simmons SK, et al.
source.title: Individual brain organoids reproducibly form cell diversity of the human cerebral cortex.

stages.name: Aggregation and dorsal patterning
stages.base_medium: Cortical Differentiation Medium I: Glasgow-MEM, 20% knockout serum replacement, 0.1 mM MEM-NEAA, 1 mM pyruvate, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, pen/strep

factors.name: IWR1
factors.role: WNT inhibitor; holds dorsal forebrain identity, days 0-18

stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Dissociate to single cells with Accutase and reaggregate 9,000 cells per well in ultra-low-adhesion V-bottom 96-well plates on day 0
Keep Y-27632 to day 6 and IWR1 + SB431542 to day 18
stages.checkpoint: By one month, EMX1+/PAX6+ dorsalised progenitors lining ventricle-like cavities with MAP2+ neurons

stages.name: Orbital agitation
stages.base_medium: Cortical Differentiation Medium II: DMEM/F12, 2 mM GlutaMAX, 1% N2, 1% chemically defined lipid concentrate, 0.25 ug/mL fungizone, pen/strep
stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Move the aggregates to ultra-low-attachment dishes under orbital agitation at 70 rpm on day 18
stages.checkpoint: Consistent, roughly spherical aggregates

stages.name: Bioreactor growth
stages.base_medium: Cortical Differentiation Medium III: CDM II + 10% FBS + 5 ug/mL heparin + 1% Matrigel

factors.name: Matrigel
factors.role: soluble extracellular matrix; avoids the need for droplet embedding

stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Transfer to spinner-flask bioreactors at 56 rpm on day 35; this removes the need for 40% O2, bisecting the aggregates, or high-oxygen-permeability dishes
stages.checkpoint: By 3 months, CTIP2+ and SATB2+ cortical projection neurons, FOXG1, HOPX+ outer radial glia, TBR1, TBR2/EOMES, Reelin; VGluT1/PSD95 co-localisation indicating excitatory synapses

stages.name: Long-term culture and astrogenesis
stages.base_medium: Cortical Differentiation Medium IV: CDM III + B27 supplement + 2% Matrigel
stages.feeding: Per schedule
actions: Switch to CDM IV from day 70 and maintain at least 6 months
stages.checkpoint: At 6 months, substantial S100B+/GFAP+ astrocytes plus cycling and immature inhibitory interneuron precursors; markers of apoptosis and hypoxia stay low

protocols.name: STEMdiff Cerebral Organoid Kit (unguided)
protocols.principle: Unguided, Lancaster-style organoids: hPSC aggregates formed in 96-well U-bottom plates are neurally induced, embedded in Matrigel droplets to expand neuroepithelium, and matured on an orbital shaker. The Maturation Kit supplies more maturation medium for culture beyond day 40.
protocols.efficiency: 50 - 60% success rate for obtaining organoids with dense cores by day 40 (varies with cell line)
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1 or TeSR-E8 (mTeSR Plus cells may need fewer cells), no more than 70 - 80% confluent with < 10% differentiation. Dissociate one well of a 6-well plate with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (8 - 10 min) and seed 9000 cells in 100 µL per well of a 96-well round-bottom ultra-low attachment plate, in Organoid Formation Medium with 10 µM Y-27632. No matrix at seeding; Matrigel is used for embedding on day 7.
materials: STEMdiff Cerebral Organoid Maturation Kit (08571) for culture beyond day 40
6-Well Ultra-Low Adherent Plates for Suspension Culture (100-0083)
tips: Each prepared medium keeps up to 2 weeks at 2 - 8°C.
If neuroepithelium is slow to appear, the induction phase can be extended to day 10 - 11 before embedding.
Chill tips and plastics that touch Matrigel at -20°C for at least 30 min and keep Matrigel on ice.
For shakers with a different throw, convert the listed RCF (0.11808 g for 6-well plates) to RPM.
pitfalls: Poor-quality hPSCs (OCT3/4 and TRA-1-60 below 90%) are the main cause of failed aggregates and outgrowths; restart rather than continue.
Carrying over too much formation medium into induction (more than ~10 - 20 µL) causes debris and outgrowths.
A wrong shaker speed breaks up organoids; long cultures need fewer organoids per well or more medium.
unverified: Protocol diagram (Figure 1) is an image; days come from the written section headings.
The PIS moves 1 - 2 organoids per 24-well well for induction but 12 - 16 per 6-well well after embedding; both are as printed.

stages.name: Organoid formation

factors.name: STEMdiff Cerebral Organoid Basal Medium 1
factors.role: basal medium, 40 mL per 50 mL (composition proprietary)

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor in the day-0 Seeding Medium only

stages.feeding: Add 100 µL Organoid Formation Medium per well on day 2 and day 4; nothing removed
actions: Make Seeding Medium (formation medium + 10 µM Y-27632)
Dissociate hPSCs to single cells, spin 300 x g for 5 min, count and dilute to 90,000 cells/mL
Dispense 100 µL per well (9000 cells) and leave untouched for at least 24 h
Test 25,000 - 90,000 cells/mL for a new line
stages.checkpoint: Day 5: organoids > 300 µm (typically 400 - 600 µm) with round, smooth edges

stages.name: Induction

factors.name: STEMdiff Cerebral Organoid Basal Medium 1
factors.role: basal medium, 49.5 mL per 50 mL (composition proprietary)

stages.feeding: No change for 48 h
actions: Put 0.5 mL Induction Medium in each well of a 24-well ultra-low attachment plate
Move 1 - 2 organoids per well with a wide-bore 200 µL tip, carrying over as little old medium as possible
Shake the plate gently so organoids do not touch
stages.checkpoint: Smooth edges that turn optically translucent

stages.name: Expansion in Matrigel

factors.name: STEMdiff Cerebral Organoid Basal Medium 2
factors.role: basal medium, 24.25 mL per 25 mL (composition proprietary)

stages.feeding: No change for 3 days
actions: Collect 12 - 16 organoids at a time on an embedding sheet or Parafilm and remove excess medium
Drop 15 µL cold Matrigel on each, centre the organoid and set 30 min at 37°C
Wash the droplets into a well of a 6-well ultra-low adherent plate with 3 mL Expansion Medium
stages.checkpoint: Budding of the organoid surface shows expanded neuroepithelium

stages.name: Maturation on orbital shaker

factors.name: STEMdiff Cerebral Organoid Basal Medium 2
factors.role: basal medium, 98 mL per 100 mL (composition proprietary)

stages.feeding: Full medium change every 3 - 4 days, 3 mL per well of a 6-well plate
actions: Day 10: remove all medium without disturbing the droplets and add 3 mL Maturation Medium
Put the plate on an orbital shaker in the incubator (65 RPM for a 6-well plate on a 25 mm-throw INFORS Celltron)
Thin out to 8 organoids per well at day 40 and 4 per well at day 60+
Beyond day 40 continue with medium from the Maturation Kit (08571)
stages.checkpoint: Day 40: dense cores with translucent edges; sections show PAX6+ radial progenitor zones, TBR2+ intermediate progenitors and MAP2+ neurons with CTIP2/TBR1 and SATB2 layers

protocols.name: STEMdiff Dorsal Forebrain Organoid Differentiation Kit
protocols.principle: Guided, matrix-free organoids adapted from the Paşca-lab spheroid method: AggreWell-formed hPSC aggregates are expanded and then differentiated in suspension to give tissue resembling early dorsal pallium (cortex). Dorsal and ventral organoids can later be fused into assembloids.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8, no more than 70 - 80% confluent with < 10% differentiation. Dissociate a 100 mm dish to single cells with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (8 - 10 min at 37°C) and seed 3 x 10^6 cells per well of an AggreWell800 24-well plate (10,000 cells per microwell) pre-treated with Anti-Adherence Rinsing Solution, in 2 mL Seeding Medium (STEMdiff Neural Organoid Basal Medium 1 + 10 µM Y-27632). Matrix-free throughout.
materials: STEMdiff Dorsal Forebrain Organoid Differentiation Kit (08620)
STEMdiff Neural Organoid Maintenance Kit (100-0120) for culture beyond day 50
tips: Prepared media keep up to 3 weeks at 2 - 8°C; Seeding Medium is used at once.
Basal Medium 2 is viscous, so pipette slowly and expect to need force when washing aggregates off the strainer.
The dorsal kit has no Supplement D; that is the only difference from the ventral kit's media.
One kit is described as enough for over 500 organoids.
pitfalls: More than 40 aggregates per well, or aggregates left touching, fuse and cut the yield.
Rough handling of the AggreWell plate during days 1 - 5 displaces aggregates into neighbouring microwells and causes early fusion.
Bright yellow medium on feed days means too many organoids per well.
unverified: No efficiency figure, marker panel or assessment day is given in this PIS, so efficiency is null.
Protocol diagram (Figure 1) is an image; days come from the written section headings.
duration_days is the end of the differentiation phase (day 43); the PIS does not name a first analysis day.
The maintenance stage is open-ended ('Day 43+'); day 50 is used as its end only because the PIS says the Maintenance Kit is needed for culture beyond 50 days.

protocols.name: StemMACS Cerebral OrganoidDiff Kit XF (matrix-free, 30 days)
protocols.principle: Four media made from two basal media and four supplements take single hPSCs through aggregate formation in ultra-low-attachment 96-well plates, two neural induction steps and a shaking cultivation step, without any embedding in extracellular matrix.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in StemMACS iPS-Brew XF or PSC-Brew XF in 6-well plates, no more than 85% confluent. Dissociate to single cells with TrypLE Select (5 min at 37°C, stopped with soybean trypsin inhibitor; viability >90%) and seed 6,000-15,000 cells per well in 150 µL EB Formation Medium in 96-well ultra-low-attachment round-bottom plates (titrate for a new line). No matrix is used and the data sheet does not call for a separate ROCK inhibitor.
materials: StemMACS Cerebral OrganoidDiff Kit XF, human (Basal Medium 1 XF 500 mL; Basal Medium 2 XF 2 × 125 mL; EB Formation Supplement 20X, 2 mL; Induction 1 Supplement 30X, 2.4 mL; Induction 2 Supplement 70X, 2.4 mL; Cultivation Supplement 50X, 6.6 mL)
StemMACS iPS-Brew XF (130-104-368) or StemMACS PSC-Brew XF (130-127-865) for hPSC expansion
Optional: StemMACS Cerebral Organoid Cultivation Medium XF (130-139-359) for culture beyond day 30
tips: Schedule from the Miltenyi data sheet for order no. 130-136-490 (document 140-007-452.01).
One kit makes two 96-well plates, i.e. up to 192 organoids.
Prepare each complete medium on the day of first use and bring it to room temperature; aliquot and refreeze unused supplement once.
Thaw supplements at 2-8°C overnight and shake well.
pitfalls: Starting cultures above 85% confluence or with viability under 90% form poor aggregates.
Organoids are easily aspirated during the 96-well medium changes.
Shaker speed is model-dependent; 47 rpm is the vendor's setting, not a universal value.
unverified: No numeric success rate or regional-marker efficiency is stated on the product page or data sheet; efficiency left null.

cell_types.notes: Reproducibility is the issue that separates these protocols, and it has been measured. Self-patterned whole-brain organoids had an intraclass correlation of cell-type proportions of 0.39, with only 4 of 19 organoids generating substantial forebrain; dorsally patterned forebrain organoids scored 0.85 at 3 months, with organoid-to-organoid variation comparable to that between individual human or mouse brains. If you need quantitative comparisons, pattern the organoids. Self-patterning is still the right choice when you want multiple interacting regions (choroid plexus, hippocampus, retina) in one tissue. All three models lack vasculature and meninges, which caps growth and is why agitation is non-negotiable, and none achieves six-layer cortical architecture.

cell_types.name: Neural crest cells
cell_types.summary: Neural crest cells are a transient migratory population that arises at the border between neural plate and non-neural ectoderm and goes on to make peripheral neurons and glia, melanocytes, and craniofacial cartilage, bone and smooth muscle. hPSC-derived neural crest is used as the common entry point to sensory neurons, Schwann cells, melanocytes and enteric neurons, and to model neurocristopathies.
cell_types.maturation_note: SOX10 reporter expression appears around day 6 and peaks near day 11 in dual-SMAD-inhibition plus WNT protocols; cells can be sorted on p75/HNK1 or SOX10 and then expanded for many passages before lineage differentiation.

morphology.endpoint: A loose, non-epithelial sheet of small stellate to spindle-shaped cells with several short processes, far less tightly packed than the starting colonies. Patches of residual neuroepithelium or rosette-like whorls are common and are the main contaminant you will see.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat compact colonies of small cells with sharp borders, replated at low density so single cells and small clusters are still visible.

stages.label: Neural plate border epithelium
stages.look: A confluent, uniform epithelial sheet with no clear colony edges; nuclei are densely packed and the sheet looks featureless at low power.

stages.label: Early neural crest
stages.look: Cells loosen and become stellate with short processes, and begin to crawl over one another; the sheet looks grainier and less epithelial than at day 4.

stages.label: Migratory neural crest
stages.look: Clearly migratory stellate and spindle cells spread across the dish. Any remaining tight rosettes or bright neuroepithelial whorls mark residual CNS-type cells.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be lost; Hackland et al. report loss of OCT4 by day 7 in their defined protocol.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: The core neural crest readout; SOX10 reporter lines are the standard way to score these protocols.

markers.name: NGFR
markers.note: Surface marker used for FACS enrichment. Not specific on its own: it is also expressed by neural cells, so pair it with SOX10 or HNK1.

markers.name: B3GAT1
markers.note: Marks a subset of early crest; Bajpai et al. found only about 30% of migratory cells HNK1+ while 95% were SOX9/p75/AP2a+.

markers.name: TFAP2A
markers.note: Neural plate border and crest marker; retained in non-neural ectoderm too, so read it with GATA2/3.

markers.name: PAX3
markers.note: Border marker; co-expression with SOX10 is good evidence of genuine crest identity.

markers.name: PAX7
markers.note: Co-expressed with SOX10 in the day-7 cultures of the top-down inhibition protocol.

markers.name: SNAI2
markers.note: EMT/migration programme; induced as cells leave the epithelial sheet.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Expressed by about 95% of cells migrating out of attached rosettes in the Bajpai method.

markers.name: ETS1
markers.note: Cranial crest marker; detected at day 7 in the top-down inhibition protocol.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Should be low. High SOX2/PAX6 means the culture drifted to central neuroepithelium.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Menendez et al. report under 5% PAX6+ cells in a good run of the BIO/SB431542 protocol.

markers.name: GATA3
markers.note: With GATA2, flags non-neural ectoderm, which is what you get if BMP signalling is too high.

functional_assays: Migration out of attached rosettes or spheres
Differentiation into peripheral neurons, glia and mesenchymal progenitors
In ovo grafting into chick dorsal neural tube
qc: SOX10 and p75 co-expression by flow at day 7-11
PAX6 under 5% of cells (BIO/SB431542 protocol)
Loss of OCT4 by day 7
Confirm tri-lineage potential: peripheral neuron, glia, mesenchymal progenitor

protocols.name: SBio: WNT on, Activin/Nodal off (single step, chemically defined)
protocols.principle: Activating canonical WNT with a GSK3 inhibitor while blocking Activin/Nodal and TGF-beta with SB431542 pushes hPSCs straight to neural crest without a rosette intermediate or cell sorting.
protocols.efficiency: Over 90% of treated cells positive for neural crest markers; under 5% PAX6+
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs maintained in a defined medium containing heregulin-beta, Activin A, LR-IGF and FGF2. Dissociate and plate at 1 x 10^5 cells/cm2 to start differentiation.
materials: Chemically defined hPSC medium without Activin A
poly-L-ornithine and laminin for downstream neuron plating
tips: The step-by-step version of this method with troubleshooting is published as Menendez et al., Nat Protoc 2013;8:203-12 (PMID 23288320, doi 10.1038/nprot.2012.156), which quotes about 15 days to neural crest stem cells.
Noggin is not needed: the authors report no major effect when it is omitted.
Daily feeding matters; this is a single-step protocol with no medium switches to rescue a starved culture.
pitfalls: Seeding density changes the CNS-versus-crest balance, so keep 1 x 10^5 cells/cm2 constant between runs.
The paper reports results with BIO; CHIR99021 is used at much lower doses in other defined protocols, so do not transfer the 2 µM number to a different GSK3 inhibitor.
unverified: Matrix for the neural crest step itself is not specified in the paper (Geltrex is used for hPSC maintenance and for other steps)
Full base medium formulation is not given in the text
Exact p75+/HNK1+ percentages appear only in the flow cytometry figures
Passage interval and split ratio during expansion are not stated

factors.name: SB431542
factors.role: ALK4/5/7 inhibitor; blocks Activin/Nodal and TGF-beta

actions: Plate dissociated hPSCs at 1 x 10^5 cells/cm2

Feed daily and watch the sheet lose its epithelial look from about day 6

protocols.name: Top-down inhibition (TDi): BMP4 saturation plus DMH1, xeno-free
protocols.principle: Endogenous BMP4 varies between runs and between lines, which makes neural crest yield erratic. Flooding the culture with BMP4 to saturate the response and then dialling the signal back down with the BMP type-1 receptor inhibitor DMH1 fixes BMP activity at the level crest needs, whatever the cells secrete.
protocols.efficiency: Reproducible SOX10 induction across WA09, Shef6 and Miff-1; without TDi the same medium gave 5-80% p75++ cells between runs
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1 on Matrigel. Seed at 10,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in E6 medium with 10 µM Y-27632 and leave 24 h before switching to induction medium.
tips: BMP4 activity differs between suppliers and lots: titrate your BMP4 in the presence of 1 µM DMH1 and pick the dose where crest induction saturates.
Varying BMP4 between 13 and 17 ng/mL did not change SOX10 induction, so the window around 15 ng/mL is forgiving.
The CHIR99021 and SB431542 doses here are 5-fold and 10-fold lower than in BSA-containing protocols; do not carry doses across media.
Day 7 cells can be moved to non-adherent culture on 1% agarose in N2-supplemented DMEM/F12 with ROCK inhibitor for the first 24 h.
pitfalls: Using DMH1 alone or BMP4 alone fails: DMH1 alone leaves PAX3/PAX6/SOX2 neural cells, BMP4 alone induces GATA2/GATA3 non-neural ectoderm.
Noggin was repressive in this system, so BMP-ligand traps are not interchangeable with the receptor inhibitor.
Heterogeneity persists even with TDi: expect some rosette-like structures and non-SOX10 cells at day 7.
The authors could not generate MITF+ melanocytes from TDi crest, so check downstream potency for your lineage of interest.
unverified: Numerical day-7 SOX10+ percentage for TDi (reported in figures, not in the text)
Whether melanocyte competence is lost under TDi, which the authors leave open

protocols.name: Rosette outgrowth: migratory crest from attached neuroectodermal spheres
protocols.principle: hESCs are taken through suspension neuroectodermal spheres that contain neural rosettes. The spheres attach, crest-like cells crawl out, and the rosettes are dissected away, giving a crest population without sorting.
protocols.efficiency: About 95% of migratory cells SOX9+, p75+ and AP2-alpha+; about 30% HNK1+
protocols.start_requirements: WA09 (H9) hESCs on Matrigel with irradiated MEFs in medium with 8 ng/mL bFGF. Depleted of MEFs and Matrigel, then harvested as clusters with 1 mg/mL collagenase IV for 30-40 min.
materials: Matrigel and irradiated MEFs for hESC maintenance
tips: A second crop (P1) of crest can be collected by re-plating the dissected rosettes and harvesting the cells that migrate out again.
This method needs no FACS, which is useful when you want crest from a line with no reporter.
pitfalls: Only 50-80% of spheres attach, so yield per experiment varies.
Incomplete rosette dissection leaves SOX2+ neuroepithelium that will overgrow the crest.
The original culture used MEF feeders and is not xeno-free.
unverified: Exact day the cultures are considered finished (the paper gives a window of days 6-9 for migration, with analysis at 1, 4 or 7 weeks of further differentiation)

Dissociate to single cells with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (8 - 10 min at 37°C) and plate 2 x 10^5 cells/cm2 (2 x 10^6 cells in 2 mL per well of a 6-well plate) on Matrigel in neural crest differentiation medium with 10 µM Y-27632.
tips: Complete medium keeps up to 2 weeks at 2 - 8°C.
Neural crest markers should persist for at least two passages.
The sensory neuron kit sheet asks for ≥ 70% SOX10+ cells before using these cells downstream.
pitfalls: Results vary with the cell line.
The PIS gives no density for replating neural crest cells; contact the vendor for continued culture.

Protocol diagram is an image; days come from the written steps.

cell_types.notes: Protocols disagree about BMP: some require BMP inhibition for crest, others are repressed by it, and endogenous BMP4 output differs between lines and even between runs of the same line, which is exactly what the top-down inhibition method was built to control. Yield is also density-dependent, so fix your seeding density first. SOX10 reporter lines make these protocols far easier to score; with a wild-type line, use p75 together with SOX10 or HNK1 rather than p75 alone, since p75 is also expressed by neural cells. Expect residual neuroepithelium in every method.

cell_types.name: Sensory neurons (nociceptors)
cell_types.summary: Sensory neurons of the dorsal root and trigeminal ganglia detect pain, temperature, itch and touch; nociceptors are the small-diameter subset carrying TRP channels and NaV1.7-1.9. hPSC-derived sensory neurons are used for analgesic screening, channelopathy and neuropathy modelling, and for studying human-specific mechanosensation.
cell_types.maturation_note: BRN3A/ISL1 neurons by day 12 and NTRK1 in over 60% of cells by day 10; peripherin is ubiquitous by day 15, ion channels (SCN9A/10A/11A, P2RX3, TRPV1, TRPM8) are up by day 15, and ganglion-like clusters with substance P and CGRP appear by day 30.

morphology.endpoint: Small round, bright, phase-dense cell bodies sitting on top of the culture with long thin neurites forming a dense web. By a month the somata drift together into ganglion-like clumps linked by thick neurite bundles.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Compact colonies grown to confluence before induction; borders still sharp.

stages.label: Neuralised sheet
stages.look: A dense, uniform sheet of small cells with no colony structure; almost all cells are nestin-positive at this point.

stages.label: Young neurons on a crest bed
stages.look: Round phase-bright cell bodies with one or two thin processes appear above a flatter layer of crest-like cells; the neurites are short and sparse.

stages.label: Neurite network
stages.look: A connected mesh of long neurites between bright, rounded somata; the flat background layer is thinning out.

stages.label: Ganglion-like clusters
stages.look: Somata gathered into dark clusters joined by thick fascicles of neurites, like small ganglia in a dish.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be gone by the end of the first week.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Marks the obligatory crest intermediate: 80% SOX10::GFP+ by day 12 under LSB3i. Residual SOX10+ precursors should be below 5% after passaging.

markers.name: TUBB3
markers.note: Pan-neuronal; about 75% TUJ1+ with the three-inhibitor cocktail, lower (33-40%) in some iPSC lines before passaging.

markers.name: POU4F1
markers.note: With ISL1, the pair that makes these neurons sensory rather than CNS; homogeneous by day 12.

markers.name: ISL1
markers.note: Read together with BRN3A.

markers.name: NTRK1
markers.note: Over 60% of cells by FACS at day 10; also the handle for sorting to enrich nociceptors.

markers.name: PRPH
markers.note: Peripheral rather than central identity; ubiquitous in BRN3A/ISL1 cells by day 15.

markers.name: SCN10A
markers.note: Nociceptor-selective sodium channel; up by day 15 along with SCN9A and SCN11A.

markers.name: P2RX3
markers.note: Strongly induced; the dominant phenotype in LSB3i cultures is P2RX3-positive.

markers.name: TRPV1
markers.note: Induced by day 15 but weaker than P2RX3; only some cells respond to capsaicin.

markers.name: PIEZO2
markers.note: Required for rapidly adapting mechanically activated current in hPSC touch receptors; the readout for mechanosensory subtypes.

markers.name: TAC1
markers.note: With CGRP, seen in over 60% of neurons at day 30 after NTRK1 sorting.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Marks the CNS fate you get without WNT activation; should be absent.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Abolished by the three-inhibitor cocktail; its persistence means the culture went central.

functional_assays: Calcium imaging with capsaicin, AITC, menthol or alpha,beta-meATP
Whole-cell patch clamp for TTX-sensitive action potentials
Piezo-driven mechanical indentation for mechanically activated currents
Cold and heat ramp responses
qc: Over 60% NTRK1+ by flow at day 10 (LSB3i)
BRN3A and ISL1 co-expression in the neuronal population
Residual SOX10+ precursors under 5% after passaging
Voltage-gated sodium currents and evoked action potentials in patch clamp

protocols.name: LSB3i: dual-SMAD inhibition plus three small molecules (accelerated nociceptors)
protocols.principle: Dual-SMAD inhibition neuralises hPSCs; adding a WNT agonist with FGF and Notch inhibition from day 2 diverts the culture through a SOX10+ neural crest intermediate and compresses nociceptor differentiation into about ten days.
protocols.efficiency: About 75% TUJ1+ neurons; over 60% NTRK1+ by FACS at day 10; 33-40% TUJ1+ in two iPSC lines before passaging
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated to single cells, pre-plated on gelatin for 30 min to remove MEFs, then plated on Matrigel at 20,000-40,000 cells/cm2 in conditioned hESC medium with 10 ng/mL FGF-2 and 10 µM Y-27632. Start induction when fully confluent.
materials: Knockout DMEM and Knockout Serum Replacement
tips: CHIR99021 is the load-bearing factor: with CHIR plus one of the other two you still get 53-58% neurons, with either alone you get few.
Passaging bulk cultures raises neuronal yield in slower lines, so a low day-10 count is often a timing lag rather than a failed run.
Sorting on NTRK1 is the cleanest way to get a defined nociceptor population for pharmacology.
pitfalls: Starting before the monolayer is fully confluent costs efficiency.
Lines differ substantially: two iPSC lines gave 33% and 40% TUJ1+ where hESCs gave 75%.
Cultures skew to P2RX3-positive, TRPV1-negative neurons, so do not assume a capsaicin response in every cell.
RUNX1 is broad at day 8 but falls by day 15, which does not match mouse data; treat subtype assignment with care.

source.authors: Chambers SM, Qi Y, Mica Y, Lee G, et al.
source.title: Combined small-molecule inhibition accelerates developmental timing and converts human pluripotent stem cells into nociceptors

protocols.name: NGN2 plus BRN3A transcriptional programming (inducible, CLYBL safe harbour)
protocols.principle: Doxycycline-inducible co-expression of NGN2 and BRN3A from a single cassette in the CLYBL safe-harbour locus converts iPSCs directly into a homogeneous sensory neuron subtype in two weeks, with no small-molecule patterning; running the same induction on neural-crest-derived cells yields two further subtypes including low-threshold mechanoreceptors.
protocols.efficiency: Reported as a homogeneous culture of a single sensory neuron subtype; no percentage given in the text
protocols.start_requirements: An iPSC line engineered with a doxycycline-inducible NGN2-T2A-BRN3A cassette inserted at both CLYBL alleles (TALEN-mediated), maintained on Matrigel in E8 with daily feeds and split every 4-6 days with Accutase plus 10 µM Y-27632 on the day of passage.
tips: Use clones with the cassette in both CLYBL alleles; the authors did, to get robust expression.
Doxycycline before day 14 is needed: earlier withdrawal lowered efficiency and increased death.

For the neural-crest route, make spheroids in AggreWell 400, then plate in NDM with bFGF, EGF and 10 µM SB431542 (SB431542 stopped from day 6); crest cells migrate out after 1-2 weeks and are replated at 40,000 cells/cm2 as a new day 0. One day of doxycycline plus 50 nM retinoic acid from day 0 gives the low-threshold mechanoreceptor subtype.
pitfalls: This needs a genome-engineered line, so it is not a drop-in protocol for an arbitrary patient iPSC.
The subtype produced by direct induction has not been observed in mice, so mouse data may not transfer; the authors validated it against adult human DRG.
A transgene-free small-molecule protocol gives a different subtype mix, so results are not interchangeable with LSB3i.
unverified: Purity as a percentage (described as homogeneous but not quantified in the text)
bFGF and EGF concentrations for the neural-crest variant are stated in the paper as 20 µg/mL, which is inconsistent with usual ng/mL usage and looks like a unit error in the source

protocols.start_requirements: Source hPSCs must have been maintained by single-cell passaging (StemFit Basic04, StemFit AK02N or StemFlex) and be at least 14 days post-thaw. Starting cultures must be 50-70% confluent and never above 90%. ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 is used at 10 uM stock diluted 1:1000 (final 10 uM) in the pre-harvest and plating media. A puromycin kill curve must be run in advance; the vendor's internal range is 0.5-2 ug/mL. About 4.6 x 10^6 viable hPSCs are needed; cells are plated at three densities (0.6, 0.7 and 0.8 x 10^6 per well of a 6-well plate), two wells each. No 33 C incubator is needed. Transfection uses Lipofectamine MessengerMAX (an alternative must reach at least 80% efficiency). cell_types.notes: Two very different routes: small-molecule patterning through a crest intermediate (fast, works in any line, mixed subtypes, skewed to P2RX3+ TRPV1-low nociceptors) and transcription-factor programming (homogeneous, needs an engineered line, subtype set by the factor combination). Line-to-line variability in the small-molecule route is large, and passaging is part of the protocol rather than an optional clean-up step: it removes residual SOX10+ progenitors and raises neuronal yield. Schrenk-Siemens et al. (Nat Neurosci 2015;18:10-16, PMID 25469543, doi 10.1038/nn.3894) is the reference for PIEZO2-dependent mechanotransduction in hPSC-derived touch receptors and is worth reading alongside these; its culture details were not confirmed in this session.

cell_types.name: Schwann cells
cell_types.summary: Schwann cells are the myelinating and non-myelinating glia of the peripheral nervous system; they wrap axons, speed conduction and secrete neurotrophic factors. hPSC-derived Schwann cells and their precursors are used for myelin repair and nerve regeneration studies, for Charcot-Marie-Tooth and neurofibromatosis modelling, and as a feeder for axon growth.
cell_types.maturation_note: Schwann cell precursors are homogeneous by day 18 (over 99% SOX10+) and can be expanded for more than 35 passages; converting them to Schwann cells takes about a further 7 days, and myelin segments appear only after about 28 days of co-culture with dorsal root ganglion neurons.

morphology.endpoint: Long, slender bipolar cells with two tapering processes, aligned in parallel swirls and often in loose bundles, looking more like a fibroblast culture that has been combed than a random spindle culture.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies replated on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel before the medium switch.

stages.label: Neural rosettes
stages.look: Radial rosettes with bright centres within a dense neuroepithelial sheet; this is the point of replating.

stages.label: Elongating precursors
stages.look: Cells become elongated and slender, leaving the rosette pattern behind; the culture looks increasingly uniform.

stages.label: Schwann cell precursors
stages.look: A highly homogeneous, fast-dividing population of thin bipolar cells; almost every nucleus is SOX10-positive.

stages.label: Schwann cells
stages.look: Longer, flatter bipolar cells arranged in parallel arrays, often in tight bundles.

protocols.name: Two-step SCP route: SB431542 plus CT99021, then NRG1
protocols.principle: Six days of TGF-beta and GSK3 inhibition neuralises hPSCs into rosettes; simply adding neuregulin-1 to the same medium converts them into Schwann cell precursors, which expand indefinitely and can then be matured with forskolin, retinoic acid and PDGF-BB.
protocols.efficiency: Over 99% SOX10+ cells at day 18; no purification or sorting step needed
protocols.start_requirements: Colonised hPSCs replated onto growth-factor-reduced Matrigel-coated dishes; the medium is switched from hPSC medium to NDM the next day.
tips: Leaving out any one of NRG1, SB431542 or CT99021 blocks precursor formation, so all three are needed in the second step.
Bank precursors at 100 ng/mL NRG1: they are stable for more than 35 passages, so you only need to run the first 18 days once.
For myelination, co-culture the Schwann cells with embryonic rat DRG neurons with ascorbic acid and allow about 28 days.
pitfalls: The Schwann cell step uses 1% FBS, so the end of the protocol is not fully defined.
Myelin segment yield in co-culture was low (about 1.5 segments per well), so this is a qualitative rather than quantitative myelination assay.
unverified: Seeding density for the initial replating
Passage interval and split ratio during precursor expansion
Ascorbic acid concentration in the myelination co-culture

protocols.name: p75-sorted neural crest stem cells matured in heregulin-beta1
protocols.principle: Embryoid bodies are neuralised in a medium half-conditioned by PA6 stromal cells, p75+ crest cells are FACS-purified and expanded, then held in heregulin-beta1 for six weeks to become S100B+/GFAP+ Schwann cells.
protocols.efficiency: p75+ sort yielded about 46% of total cells at day 14; after six weeks of differentiation about 85% S100B+ and about 78% GFAP+
protocols.start_requirements: hESC or iPSC colonies lifted and grown as embryoid bodies in suspension on a rocking platform.
tips: Thawed sorted NCSCs showed over 90% viability, so the crest stage is a convenient bank point.
This route gives you a crest stem cell population that also makes peripheral neurons and mesenchymal derivatives, useful if you want more than glia.
pitfalls: PA6-conditioned medium makes the protocol harder to standardise and is not xeno-free.
It is slow: six weeks of differentiation after a two-week induction, versus about 25 days for the NRG1 two-step route.
MBP transcript was detected only at low level, so myelination competence needs a co-culture assay to demonstrate.
unverified: EGF, BMP and SB431542 are not part of this protocol despite being common in crest induction; the paper uses none
HNK1 was not used for sorting
MBP+ percentage is not reported

cell_types.notes: The practical difference between these two is the bank point and the timeline: the NRG1 two-step route gives a stable, expandable, near-pure (over 99% SOX10+) precursor at day 18 that you can freeze and return to, while the p75-sorted route needs FACS and six weeks of differentiation and ends at about 85% S100B+. Neither produces myelin on its own: MBP appears only in neuron co-culture, after roughly four weeks. If you are modelling a myelin gene (PMP22, MPZ), plan the co-culture from the start, since transcript-level readouts in monoculture will understate the phenotype.

cell_types.name: Optic cup / retinal organoids
cell_types.summary: Mouse ESC aggregates in serum-free floating culture with added extracellular matrix form a neuroepithelium that spontaneously generates retinal epithelium, evaginates optic vesicles and then invaginates into a two-walled optic cup, with neural retina inside and pigment epithelium outside. In extended culture the neural retina stratifies into the proper layers, which is why these organoids are the standard source of mouse photoreceptors for transplantation and retinal development work.
cell_types.maturation_note: Cup morphology appears by about day 9-10; stratified retina with photoreceptors needs several more weeks, usually at raised oxygen with retinoic acid and taurine added from around day 14.

morphology.endpoint: A floating aggregate carrying one or more cup-shaped structures: a bright, thick, laminated inner wall (neural retina) curving around a lumen, with a thinner outer wall that darkens with pigment as the culture goes on. A visible hinge marks the rim of each cup.

stages.label: Quick reaggregation
stages.look: Dissociated ESCs settling into the U-bottom well; aggregation begins within half an hour and is largely done within hours.

stages.label: Compact aggregate
stages.look: A smooth round aggregate whose surface starts to change once matrix has been added.

stages.label: Polarised neuroepithelium
stages.look: A hollow neuroepithelial shell with apical surface inward; faint retinal reporter patches begin to appear.

stages.label: Optic vesicles
stages.look: Thickened retinal patches bulge out from the aggregate surface as rounded vesicles, several per aggregate.

stages.label: Optic cups
stages.look: The distal part of each vesicle has folded inward, giving a double-walled cup with a bright laminated rim and a clear hinge.

stages.label: Stratified retina
stages.look: A thick, layered retinal wall with a dense outer photoreceptor zone; pigment is visible in the apposed epithelium in pigmented lines.

protocols.name: SFEBq optic cup: self-organising retinal epithelium in floating aggregates
protocols.principle: ESCs are quickly reaggregated in a low-adhesion U-bottom well in serum-free medium; with extracellular matrix added on day 1 the aggregate forms a neuroepithelium, patches of which turn on retinal identity, bulge out as vesicles and then invaginate on their own into a two-walled optic cup.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ESCs (commonly an Rx::GFP reporter line) maintained feeder-free; dissociate to single cells, count with dead-cell exclusion, and plate immediately into low-adhesion wells.
tips: Each aggregate typically produces more than one retinal patch, so one well can yield several cups.
Pigment epithelium identity in the outer wall is induced by signals from the neighbouring non-retinal neuroepithelium, so do not trim the aggregate too aggressively.
Matrigel lot varies; later protocols from several labs stress routine lot testing.
pitfalls: Inaccurate cell counting: seeding density strongly determines whether eyefield tissue forms at all.
Matrigel omitted or at the wrong concentration, which kills retinal induction.
High ESC passage number or a poor starting state, after which retinal reporter expression simply does not appear.
unverified: The Nature 2011 and Nat Protoc 2012 full texts were not accessible in this session. Cell number (3,000 per well), 2% growth-factor-reduced Matrigel on day 1 and the GMEM/KSR base are taken from papers restating the SFEBq protocol: Takata 2016 (Data Brief, Eiraku lab), Gonzalez-Cordero 2013 (Nat Biotechnol, which states 1.5% KSR), Assawachananont 2014 (which describes raising KSR from 1.5% to 5% relative to the original) and Hiler 2016 (Nat Protoc).
Reported percentages of aggregates forming optic cups in the original paper were not verified.
Exact day of transfer to maturation medium and the oxygen tension used in the original are not confirmed; restating protocols vary (day 7-9, 40% O2).
The medium in Eiraku's own later work is a chemically defined medium rather than GMEM/KSR, so base-medium details differ between versions.

protocols.name: Whole-aggregate 3D retinal differentiation for photoreceptor production
protocols.principle: The same floating-aggregate route, but the retinal tissue is left inside the mother aggregate instead of being dissected out, and the culture is carried on for weeks in a simple maturation medium with retinoic acid and taurine so that transplantable photoreceptor precursors accumulate.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ESCs (EK.CCE, 129/SvEv) maintained as previously described, dissociated to single cells.
tips: Keeping the retina inside the whole aggregate avoids the dissection step and still yields large numbers of photoreceptor precursors.
Replating at lower density late in the culture keeps the aggregates from fusing.
pitfalls: Aggregates fusing or crowding if plated too densely during maturation.
Scoring optic-cup formation inconsistently; this paper gives explicit morphological criteria (hinge region, protruding thickened neuroepithelium).
unverified: The fraction of aggregates forming optic cups is not stated as a single headline figure in the text read here.
Oxygen tension is not stated for this protocol.

protocols.name: Trisection protocol: higher retinal organoid yield without evagination
protocols.principle: Rather than selecting the minority of aggregates that evaginate an optic vesicle, the whole eyefield-stage neuroepithelium is cut into three at day 10, so that retinal tissue hidden in the main body of the aggregate is also harvested.
protocols.efficiency: Starting aggregates form with 100% efficiency; eyefield induction occurs in 81% (81% +/- 10% RAX+ organoids at day 7), and trisection raises the yield of retinal organoids to 183%
protocols.start_requirements: E14TG2a wild-type or hPAX6-GFP transgenic mouse ESCs in ESC medium with 1,000 U/ml LIF and 1 uM PD0325901, passaged every 2-3 days with TrypLE Express.
materials: ESC medium with LIF and PD0325901
tips: Seeding density decides eyefield efficiency: lower seeding (1,500-3,000 cells/well) gave 80% +/- 4% RAX+ organoids, while higher seeding (6,000-9,000 cells/well) gave only 10% +/- 4%.
Most eyefield tissue sits in the main body of the aggregate rather than in an evagination - only 35% +/- 10% of aggregates had RAX+ evaginations, so selecting evaginations throws most of it away.
Not every evagination is retinal: 31% +/- 7% were RAX-negative.
pitfalls: Seeding too many cells per well, which collapses eyefield induction.
Discarding the mother aggregate body, where most retinal tissue actually is.
This protocol does not reproduce optic-cup invagination morphology; it trades that for yield.
unverified: Exact cell number per well for the standard condition, the composition of the differentiation and maturation media and the Matrigel product details are in the supplementary experimental procedures, which were not read in this session.
Whether the day-0 medium matches the original SFEBq formulation is not confirmed here.

cell_types.notes: Two variables dominate: how many cells go into each well and which Matrigel lot is used. Different labs have pulled the protocol in different directions - raising KSR and adding a retinoic-acid-receptor antagonist for transplantable sheets (Assawachananont 2014), switching to N2/B27 with raised oxygen from the onset of photoreceptor differentiation (Decembrini 2014, which reports ~79% +/- 4.3% of aggregates with at least one retinal structure for its best clone), or cutting the whole eyefield neuroepithelium into three to triple the yield at the cost of cup morphology (Volkner 2016). cell_types.name: Retinal pigment epithelium
cell_types.summary: The retinal pigment epithelium is a single pigmented hexagonal layer behind the photoreceptors that recycles retinoid, phagocytoses shed outer segments and maintains the outer blood-retinal barrier. hPSC-RPE is the most clinically advanced hPSC derivative, used in trials for age-related macular degeneration and Stargardt disease, and widely used for inherited retinal disease modelling and drug testing.
cell_types.maturation_note: Pigmented patches appear from about day 14 in directed protocols, but the hexagonal, transepithelial-resistant monolayer with RPE65, BEST1 and RLBP1 requires a passage and then roughly another month; Maruotti et al. detected those maturation markers about 60 days after their single whole-dish passage.

morphology.endpoint: A confluent sheet of tightly packed hexagonal cells with dark brown granular cytoplasm and crisp borders, often with fluid-filled domes where the layer has pumped itself off the plastic.

pitfalls: Nicotinamide and Activin A are described as used in some experiments rather than universally, so the exact combination to reproduce needs care.

cell_types.notes: RPE is the easiest cell type in this slice to get and the easiest to over-claim: pigment at day 14 is not mature RPE. Expect to passage once, which both enriches (from roughly 50-80% to over 95% in both small-molecule protocols) and triggers the hexagonal polarised morphology, and then wait about another month for RPE65, BEST1 and RLBP1. Chetomin dose is strongly line-dependent and toxic above 20 nM in some lines. Check VSX2 is absent, since the neural retina is the competing fate, and remember that pigmented cells arising spontaneously in any hPSC culture are usually RPE, which is why RPE is also a contaminant to rule out when you are aiming at melanocytes.

cell_types.name: Retinal organoids (photoreceptors)
cell_types.summary: Retinal organoids are self-organising laminated neural retina containing all major retinal cell types, with photoreceptors that develop inner and outer segment structures and become light-responsive. They are used for inherited retinal degeneration modelling, photoreceptor transplantation research, gene therapy testing and studies of human photoreceptor development.
cell_types.maturation_note: Neural retina domains are picked at days 21-30; CRX and recoverin photoreceptors are present by about day 80, ARR3+ cones and NRL+ rods differentiate by about day 140, and outer-segment discs with light responsiveness need the better part of a year. Organoids can be held well past 400 days.

morphology.endpoint: A free-floating spheroid 1-2 mm across with a bright, optically clear laminated rim enclosing a darker core; at late stages the surface carries fine hair-like appendages where photoreceptor segments project outward.

protocols.name: Autonomous 3D retinal cups with light-responsive photoreceptors
protocols.principle: hiPSC aggregates weaned into a minimal neural induction medium recapitulate retinal development largely on their own: horseshoe-shaped neural retina domains form on the dish, are dissected out in the fourth week, and self-assemble into laminated cups whose photoreceptors mature with serum, taurine and a timed retinoic acid window.
protocols.efficiency: Neural retina domain formation at day 20: 85.0 ± 3.0%, 88.3 ± 3.5% and 62.3 ± 4.6% in three lines; excised domains 71.0 ± 7.3% VSX2+ versus 19.0 ± 7.2% MITF+
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs maintained on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel in mTeSR1, passaged every 5-7 days at about 80% confluence, with visibly differentiated colonies marked and removed mechanically before passaging.
tips: Shorter retinoic acid windows (weeks 7-14 or 10-14) were tested specifically because prolonged exposure at 1 µM appeared to hold back photoreceptor maturation; opsin expression is sensitive to this choice.
Pick domains by shape: the horseshoe-shaped, dome-forming regions are the neural retina, the darker pigmenting neighbours are RPE.
Mark and mechanically remove differentiated colonies before passaging the starting hiPSCs; input culture quality propagates into domain yield.
pitfalls: Domain formation efficiency differed substantially between lines (62-88%), and a line effect on opsin expression cannot be ruled out.
The long-term medium contains 10% FBS, so late-stage culture is not defined.
Dissection is manual and takes practice; cutting into the RPE domain raises the MITF+ fraction of the organoid.

cell_types.notes: These are long, manual, 3D cultures where the two things that actually determine success are the quality of the starting hPSC culture and your eye for which domains to dissect. Domain formation efficiency varies by line (62-88% in one study) and organoids from different lines reach the same developmental point on different days, which is why the morphological staging scheme matters more than the day count. Photoreceptor maturation is the slow part: markers by day 80-140, outer segments and light responses much later. The retinoic acid window is a real variable, with prolonged 1 µM exposure appearing to hold back opsin expression, and late-stage media in both open protocols contain serum, so they are not defined.

cell_types.name: Inner ear organoids (hair cells)
cell_types.summary: Inner ear organoids contain sensory epithelia with mechanosensitive hair cells bearing stereocilia bundles, supporting cells and associated neurons, resembling vestibular end organs. They are used to study human otic development and hereditary deafness, and to test ototoxic and otoprotective compounds, since human hair cells are otherwise almost unobtainable.
cell_types.maturation_note: Otic pit-like protrusions are identifiable at days 15-16, vesicles form after the Matrigel-embedded CHIR99021 step, and hair cells (ATOH1 reporter) appear as early as day 39; organoids were maintained in spinner flasks for up to 180 days, with electrophysiology performed around day 62 onward.

morphology.endpoint: A dark, irregular aggregate a millimetre or so across studded with translucent fluid-filled vesicles; inside each vesicle a patch of sensory epithelium carries hair cells whose bundles point into the lumen.

protocols.name: Matrigel-embedded otic induction with staged SB/FGF/LDN then CHIR99021
protocols.principle: Dilute Matrigel with FGF-2 and TGF-beta inhibition epithelialises the surface of an hPSC aggregate into non-neural ectoderm; adding FGF-2 with BMP inhibition induces otic placode; embedding in undiluted Matrigel gives the mechanical support for the placode to invaginate, and WNT activation with CHIR99021 drives otic vesicle formation that matures into sensory epithelium in floating culture.
protocols.efficiency: 90.9 ± 5.2% of Matrigel-embedded CHIR99021-treated aggregates formed vesicles; eGFP+ hair cells from day 39
protocols.start_requirements: WA25 hESCs or mND2-0 iPSCs cultured in Essential 8 or E8 Flex on recombinant human vitronectin-coated 6-well plates, passaged at 80% confluence or every 4-5 days at 1:10-1:20 with 0.5 mM EDTA in DPBS. Pluripotency checked by SOX2, OCT4 and SSEA-1 staining.
materials: 125 mL spinner flask and in-incubator stir plate or orbital shaker
N2 and B27 without vitamin A
tips: Both agitated formats (spinner flask and orbital shaker) gave similar results, so use whichever you have.
The day 15-16 PAX2/PAX8 check on a few sacrificed aggregates is worth doing: it tells you whether a four-month run is on track before you commit to it.
Matrigel embedding is doing mechanical work, not just signalling: aggregates in minimal medium without it produced migratory cells but no vesicles.
The CHIR99021 addition at day 8 is optional; the authors found it may improve otic placode-like induction but is not required.
pitfalls: BMP4 requirement is line-dependent: WA25 worked with SB alone (LSB over-inhibited), while mND2-0 iPSCs needed 2.5 ng/mL BMP4, so titrate per line.
Organoids also make epidermal epithelium (TFAP2A+ KRT5+), and as late as day 35 vesicles can be partly incorporated into it; this is part of the system rather than a failure.
The authors note two medium components that are poorly defined or imperfectly matched to human cells as a source of variability.
Hair cells resemble vestibular rather than cochlear cells, so this is not a cochlear hair cell model.
unverified: Numerical MYO7A+ percentage per organoid
Whether routine karyotyping was done (the authors state it was not, and instead kept passage number low)

cell_types.notes: A single well-specified protocol dominates this cell type, and it is demanding: four stages, a Matrigel embedding step, agitated long-term culture and a run length of two to six months. Two things decide the outcome. First, the BMP4 dose in the non-neural ectoderm step is line-dependent (one hESC line needed none, one iPSC line needed 2.5 ng/mL), so titrate before a long run. Second, the day 15-16 otic pit check on a few sacrificed aggregates is the only early readout you get. Expect epidermal epithelium alongside the otic vesicles, and expect vestibular-type rather than cochlear hair cells.

cell_types.name: Corneal epithelial cells
cell_types.summary: The corneal epithelium is the stratified surface-ectoderm-derived layer that forms the transparent front of the eye, maintained by limbal stem cells. hPSC-derived corneal epithelial cells are used to build transplantable epithelial sheets for limbal stem cell deficiency, and the SEAM system in which they arise is also a model of coordinated whole-eye development.
cell_types.maturation_note: Concentric SEAM zones appear at about weeks 3-4; non-epithelial zones are removed around week 7 and corneal epithelial progenitors are sorted at weeks 10-15; sorted cells then need a further 14-21 days to build a stratified sheet. The whole process is 100-120 days.

morphology.endpoint: A compact sheet of small, uniform polygonal epithelial cells with tight bright borders, stratifying into several layers; the sheet can be lifted as one piece.

stages.label: Zone cleanup

stages.label: Corneal epithelial progenitors

stages.label: Stratified corneal epithelial sheet

protocols.name: SEAM method: self-formed four-zone colonies, then FACS and sheet fabrication
protocols.principle: On laminin-511 E8 fragment in a serum-free differentiation medium, a proportion of iPSC colonies spontaneously organise into circular colonies of four concentric zones corresponding to neuroectoderm, neural crest, ocular surface ectoderm and surface ectoderm. The ocular surface zone is freed by pipetting away the others and sorted by FACS, then expanded and differentiated into a transplantable corneal epithelial sheet.
protocols.efficiency: A proportion of iPS cell colonies form SEAMs; the paper does not state a numerical differentiation efficiency
protocols.start_requirements: Human iPS cells adapted to a feeder-free system. Experience with iPSC culture and FACS is stated by the authors as a prerequisite.
materials: FACS with antibodies against SSEA-4, ITGB4 and TRA-1-60
cell culture inserts for sheet fabrication
tips: The whole protocol runs 100-120 days from iPSC preparation to a differentiated sheet, so schedule it as a quarter-long experiment.
The same SEAM yields retinal, lens and surface ectoderm lineages, so it is also a platform for studying coordinated eye development rather than only a corneal protocol.
For the exact reagent concentrations and the week-by-week schedule, the same group's Scientific Reports 2018 methods (see the companion protocol) spell them out in an open-access paper.
pitfalls: Only a proportion of colonies form SEAMs, so starting colony density and uniformity matter.
The multi-lineage nature of the SEAM is also its weakness: differentiation efficiency for corneal cells alone is not high, which is why sorting is mandatory.
FACS experience is a genuine prerequisite, not a formality.
unverified: All reagent concentrations and the exact day-by-day schedule in the Nature Protocols text (the full text was not accessible in this session; the companion entry below carries the values from the same group's open-access methods)

protocols.name: SEAM with CD200 negative selection (concentrations and week-by-week schedule)
protocols.principle: The same SEAM differentiation written out with concrete media and timings, plus CD200 as a negative sort marker: screening surface markers showed that removing CD200+ cells eliminates the non-corneal colonies that survive the conventional TRA-1-60/SSEA-4/ITGB4 gate.
protocols.efficiency: Most cells isolated on the conventional TRA-1-60/SSEA-4/ITGB4 gate were corneal epithelial lineage, but non-corneal colonies persisted; adding CD200 negative selection gave superior purification
protocols.start_requirements: Human iPSC line 201B7, passaged at least three times on mitomycin-C-treated MEF feeders, then moved to a feeder-free system on laminin-511 E8 fragments in StemFit for 7 days.
materials: antibodies against SSEA-4, ITGB4/CD104, TRA-1-60 and CD200
tips: This is the open-access source for the concentrations and the week-by-week timeline of the SEAM method, from the group that developed it.
No single marker selects corneal epithelial cells on its own: the authors are explicit that the combination is what works, with CD200 as the negative gate.
Week 7 is the pipetting point for removing zones 1 and 2; doing it late lets the inner zones overgrow.
pitfalls: Serial passaging uses mitomycin-C-treated 3T3 feeders, so that part is not feeder-free.
The sort window is broad (weeks 10-15) and the exact week differs between reports, so record which you used.
Timing varies: this schedule totals roughly 15-18 weeks including sheet formation, longer than the 100-120 days quoted in the protocol paper.

cell_types.notes: The SEAM is not a directed protocol in the usual sense: the colonies pattern themselves and your job is to recognise and physically isolate the right ring, which means this method rewards careful microscopy more than careful pipetting of growth factors. Laminin-511 E8 fragment is not interchangeable with other laminins here, since it was the only isoform that produced SEAMs in the authors' hands. Sorting is mandatory, with no single marker sufficient, and the whole thing takes three to four months. Because the same colony also makes retina, RPE and lens, always exclude RAX, MITF and crystallin-positive cells from the final sheet.

cell_types.name: Keratinocytes
cell_types.summary: Keratinocytes are the surface-ectoderm-derived cells that build the stratified epidermis, dividing in the basal layer and differentiating upward into cornified squames. hPSC-derived keratinocytes are used to model epidermolysis bullosa and other genodermatoses, to build epidermal equivalents and skin grafts, and to test topical agents and irritants.
cell_types.maturation_note: Epithelial morphology dominates by about day 14 and keratinocyte-like cells with TP63 and KRT14 appear by day 24; in the retinoic acid/BMP4 route KRT14 reaches about 45% at day 30 and over 70% after the first passage. Terminal differentiation (KRT1, involucrin, filaggrin) needs high calcium or an air-liquid interface.

morphology.endpoint: A cobblestone sheet of small polygonal cells with bright, crisp borders growing in tightly packed islands that merge; cells at island edges are larger and flatter.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies picked and plated on a Geltrex/collagen-I-coated dish.

stages.label: Surface ectoderm induction
stages.look: Colonies flatten and spread; cells at the periphery begin to look cuboidal rather than tightly pluripotent.

stages.label: Epithelial outgrowth
stages.look: Most cells in the outgrown colony are epithelial, polygonal and evenly sized, with visible cell-cell borders.

stages.label: Keratinocyte-like cells
stages.look: Cells migrating away from the colony take on classic keratinocyte shape: small, polygonal, bright-bordered, growing in compact clusters.

stages.label: Enriched keratinocyte monolayer
stages.look: A uniform cobblestone monolayer after rapid-attachment selection on collagen; few large flat non-keratinocyte cells remain.

protocols.name: Retinoic acid plus BMP4 in defined keratinocyte serum-free medium
protocols.principle: Retinoic acid drives hPSCs to surface ectoderm while BMP4 blocks the neural alternative; afterwards a defined keratinocyte medium alone selects and expands the keratinocyte progeny, which can be purified further by sorting on integrins.
protocols.efficiency: 44.7 ± 9.7% KRT14+ at day 30; 71.4 ± 10.5% after the first passage; 97.8% KRT14+ after sorting ITGA6-high/ITGB4-high cells
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs subcultured on Matrigel for one day before induction. Three initiation media were compared (DM, FAD and defined keratinocyte serum-free medium); KSFM gave the best efficiency and was used throughout.
materials: anti-ITGA6 and anti-ITGB4 antibodies for FACS
tips: Medium choice matters more than it looks: KSFM beat both DM and FAD for efficiency in a direct comparison.
The first passage roughly doubles KRT14 purity without any sorting, so passage before you judge a run.
This protocol was built for a disease model: COL7A1 is the readout that separates recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa lines from controls.
pitfalls: Day-30 purity is only about 45%, so plan on at least one passage or a sort.
The Methods give the retinoic acid/BMP4 exposure as 4 days while the figure legend describes additions on days 0 and 2; follow the figure's dosing schedule within a 4-day window.
