cell_types.name: Melanocytes
cell_types.summary: Melanocytes are neural-crest-derived pigment cells that sit at the epidermal basement membrane and in hair follicles, making melanin in melanosomes and transferring it to keratinocytes. hPSC-derived melanocytes are used to model pigmentation disorders such as Waardenburg syndrome and Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome, to study melanoma initiation, and as a candidate cell therapy for vitiligo.
cell_types.maturation_note: In the dual-SMAD-inhibition route, melanoblasts are sorted at day 11 and the first pigmented cells appear about six days after sorting, with most clusters pigmented by day 20 and pellets visibly dark by passage five. The embryoid body route is much slower: pigment appears 3-4 weeks after the post-EB dissociation and most cells are pigmented 4-6 weeks after that.

morphology.endpoint: Dendritic cells with a small cell body and several fine branching processes, filled with brown-black granules. Confluent cultures look dusty brown by eye and the cell pellet is visibly dark.

protocols.name: Dual-SMAD inhibition plus WNT, then BMP4/EDN3 (BE) melanoblast sorting
protocols.principle: Dual-SMAD inhibition with a timed CHIR99021 pulse makes neural crest at the expense of CNS fates; adding BMP4 and endothelin-3 from day 6 converts part of that crest into KIT+ melanocyte-competent melanoblasts, which are FACS-sorted at day 11 and matured in a defined pigmentation medium.
protocols.efficiency: 37 ± 3% SOX10+/KIT+ melanoblasts at day 11 under BMP4+EDN3 (9 ± 2% without); after sorting and maturation, an essentially pure melanocyte population
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs plated to about 80% confluence; the protocol is run with a SOX10::GFP reporter line to score induction, and 10 µM ROCK inhibitor is used at replating.
materials: FACS with SOX10 reporter and anti-KIT antibody
tips: Day 2 is not approximate: moving the CHIR99021 start by one or two days almost abolishes SOX10 induction. A single day of CHIR gives about 70% of the maximal yield.
SCF added at day 6 did not improve melanoblast induction, contrary to expectation from other species; BMP4 and EDN3 are what work at that point.
Early retinoic acid gives caudal (HOXB2/HOXB4+) melanocytes if you need a trunk rather than cranial identity.
Seeding density shifts the CNS-versus-crest balance, so keep it fixed.
pitfalls: Spontaneous or dual-SMAD-only differentiation also makes pigmented cells, but they are mostly retinal pigment epithelium, not melanocytes; always confirm dendritic morphology plus MITF, and consider checking RPE65.
The protocol depends on FACS; with a non-reporter line you need an alternative SOX10 readout.
Derived melanocytes lack HOX gene expression relative to primary foreskin or breast melanocytes, consistent with an anterior identity.

cell_types.name: Hair-bearing skin organoids
cell_types.summary: Skin organoids are cystic aggregates that co-induce surface ectoderm and cranial neural crest so that epidermis and dermis self-assemble, then produce pigmented hair follicles with sebaceous glands, Merkel cells and a sensory nerve network. They are used to study human hair follicle development, to model skin and appendage disease, and as a potential source of appendage-bearing grafts.
cell_types.maturation_note: Hair follicles start appearing around day 60; placode-to-peg transitions concentrate in days 75-90, follicles with sebaceous glands and a bulge region appear by days 110-130, and cultures can be held to about 150 days. Beyond that, follicle morphology degrades.

morphology.endpoint: A translucent cyst a few millimetres across with a smooth epithelial surface, a dense opaque core and, radiating outward, dozens of hair follicles with dark bulbs and visible shafts, plus a cartilaginous tail-like projection at one pole.

stages.label: Hair placodes and pegs

stages.label: Hair-bearing skin organoid
stages.look: Dozens of pigmented follicles with dark bulbs and protruding shafts, giving the organoid a bristly outline.

protocols.name: Co-induction of surface ectoderm and cranial neural crest in one aggregate
protocols.principle: Stepwise modulation of TGF-beta and FGF signalling in a single hPSC aggregate induces cranial surface epithelium and neural crest side by side, so epidermis and dermis assemble together and go on to make hair follicles the way fetal skin does.
protocols.efficiency: Hair-bearing organoids: 87.4 ± 3.5% (WA25, 181/212), 87.2 ± 4.1% (DSP-GFP, 177/212), 71% (WA01, 92/130 in an independent validation); average 48 follicles per organoid
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC colonies dissociated with Accutase to single cells in E8 with 10 µM Y-27632, counted, then resuspended in E8 with 20 µM Y-27632 for aggregation.
tips: The step-by-step version with characterisation guidance is Lee et al., Nat Protoc 2022;17:1266-1305 (PMID 35322210, doi 10.1038/s41596-022-00681-y).
Constant agitation makes follicle formation more consistent, though follicles do occasionally form in static culture.
For grafting, remove the cartilaginous tail with tungsten needles first; 55% of xenografts (15/27) gave 2-5 mm outgrown hairs.
An independent operator unfamiliar with the system reproduced it (92 hair-bearing organoids from 130, WA01), so the protocol does travel.
pitfalls: It is a four-to-five-month experiment: plan incubator space and feeding schedules before starting.
Beyond about 150 days follicle morphology degrades, so this is the practical upper limit.
Pigmentation varies by line (53.5% versus 76.2% of hair-bearing organoids), so albino follicles are expected, not a failure.
The organoid is cystic with the epidermis facing inward, which is the opposite of planar skin; grafting is needed for it to unfurl.
unverified: The FGF concentration in the day-3 crest induction step is stated as 50 µg/mL in the paper's methods, which is inconsistent with the 4 ng/mL used three days earlier and looks like a unit error in the source; confirm against the Nature Protocols version before use

protocols.name: Nature Protocols version: 150-day skin organoid generation and characterisation
protocols.principle: The same TGF-beta/FGF-modulated co-induction written up as a step-by-step protocol, with defined conditions over a two-week induction window and a staged description of hair follicle development that can be used to tell whether a culture is on schedule.

Conventional skin equivalents last 2-3 weeks and have no appendages; the long timeline here is the price of getting follicles at all.

source.title: Generation and characterization of hair-bearing skin organoids from human pluripotent stem cells

stages.name: Induction of surface ectoderm and cranial neural crest
stages.base_medium: Defined culture conditions over a two-week induction period
stages.feeding: Per the stepwise schedule in the protocol
actions: Run the defined two-week induction that drives pluripotent cells to surface ectoderm and cranial neural crest, which become the epidermis and dermis of each organoid unit
stages.checkpoint: Each aggregate contains both an epithelial surface and a crest-derived mesenchymal compartment

stages.name: Organoid maturation and epidermal stratification
stages.base_medium: Organoid maturation medium in agitated suspension
stages.feeding: Scheduled half and full medium changes
actions: Maintain in agitated suspension while the epidermis stratifies inward and fibroblasts accumulate around it
Expect appendage-free cystic organoids through the first month
stages.checkpoint: Over about a month the epidermal layer stratifies inward with apical layers facing the core

stages.name: Hair follicle development
stages.feeding: Scheduled changes with increased volume as organoids grow
actions: Watch for hair follicles from about day 60
Score placode-to-peg transitions, which concentrate in days 75-90
By days 110-130 expect follicles with sebaceous glands and a bulge region containing Merkel cells and NFATC1+ stem-cell-like cells
stages.checkpoint: By about day 130 organoids reach full complexity: stratified skin layers, pigmented hair follicles, sebaceous glands, Merkel cells and sensory neurons, comparable to week-18 fetal skin

stages.name: Extended culture
stages.feeding: As above
actions: Hold cultures up to about 150 days; expect a mix of follicle stages rather than a synchronised population
stages.checkpoint: Organoids remain viable to about day 150

cell_types.notes: This is a demanding, months-long 3D culture and the single most important variable is the two-week induction window, which has to produce both surface ectoderm and cranial neural crest in the same aggregate; everything after that is feeding and patience. Expect asynchronous follicles, line-dependent pigmentation, and a cystic geometry with the epidermis facing inward, which only unfurls on grafting. The organoids correspond to second-trimester fetal facial skin rather than adult skin, so they are a developmental model first.

cell_types.name: Gastruloids / 2D micropattern gastrulation models
cell_types.summary: Gastruloids are hPSC colonies or aggregates that self-organise into ordered domains of the three germ layers, reproducing aspects of gastrulation that cannot be studied in human embryos. They are used to study signalling and patterning (BMP, WNT, Nodal), axis formation, and the effects of mutations or drugs on early development.
cell_types.maturation_note: Radial germ-layer rings are complete 42-48 h after BMP4 on micropatterns; 3D human gastruloids show anteroposterior organisation by 72 h. Neither model goes on to form organs.

morphology.endpoint: Micropatterns: perfectly round colonies with a dense central disc, a thick ring two to three cells deep partway out, and larger, spread cells at the edge. 3D gastruloids: small aggregates that break symmetry and elongate.

stages.label: Confined pluripotent discs
stages.look: Circular colonies filling each adhesive island edge to edge a few hours after seeding.

stages.label: Ring formation
stages.look: Within 24 h of BMP4 a dense ring of cells forms at a reproducible radius, with flatter cells inside and outside.

stages.label: Patterned colony
stages.look: Dense SOX2+ centre, a multilayered primitive-streak-like ring, and large spread CDX2+ cells at the border.

stages.label: Elongated 3D gastruloid
stages.look: In the 3D version, aggregates become elongated with a distinct pole by 72 h.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Uniform before BMP4; afterwards persists in the mesendoderm rings and is lost from centre and edge.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Down-regulated in the centre as SOX2 rises.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Central disc: prospective ectoderm.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Ring outside the SOX2 centre: primitive streak / mesoderm.

markers.name: EOMES
markers.note: Mesendoderm; overlaps BRA and extends outwards.

markers.name: SNAI1
markers.note: Marks cells undergoing EMT in the lower layers of the ring.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Ring outside BRA: definitive endoderm-like cells.

markers.name: GATA6
markers.note: Mesendoderm marker overlapping EOMES.

markers.name: CDX2
markers.note: Outer ring: trophoblast-like / extra-embryonic-like cells at the edge; also overlaps BRA in mesoderm.

markers.name: SMAD1
markers.note: BMP response becomes restricted to the colony edge by 24 h.

markers.name: CDH1
markers.note: Internalised in the streak-like ring as cells undergo EMT.

functional_assays: Immunofluorescence of whole colonies with radial intensity profiles averaged over many colonies
Live imaging of signalling reporters
Perturbation with SB431542 (removes BRA and SOX17 domains) or siRNA against inhibitors
qc: Colonies are confluent with no holes before BMP4 is added
Concentric SOX2 (centre), BRA, SOX17 and CDX2 (edge) domains at 42-48 h in 500-1000 µm colonies

protocols.name: Micropatterned colonies + BMP4 (original method, PDL/Matrigel, conditioned medium)
protocols.principle: Confining hESCs to circular adhesive islands makes colony geometry reproducible; uniform BMP4 then triggers self-organised signalling (BMP response limited to the edge, a Nodal gradient further in) that lays down trophoblast-like, endoderm, mesoderm and ectoderm rings from the edge inwards.
protocols.start_requirements: RUES2 hESCs on Matrigel in MEF-conditioned medium with 20 ng/ml bFGF. CYTOO micropatterned coverslips coated with 50 µg/ml poly-D-lysine (2 h), washed by serial dilution without drying, then Matrigel 1:100 in DMEM/F12 overnight at 4 °C.
tips: Colony size matters: the pattern is measured from the edge inwards, so colonies of 250 µm or less lack the SOX2 centre
Similar patterns were obtained with RUES1 and H1, on laminin-521, and in mTeSR1
SB431542 removes the mesendoderm rings, leaving CDX2+ edge and SOX2+ centre
pitfalls: Never let the Matrigel-coated coverslip warm up or dry before seeding: adhesion becomes patchy
Uneven seeding gives angular irregularities; exclude colonies with empty areas
Identity of the outer CDX2+ cells (trophoblast-like versus amnion-like) is debated
unverified: Whether bFGF is kept in the medium during BMP4 treatment is not explicit in this paper (the later protocol keeps 20 ng/ml)
Day numbers assume BMP4 is added about 24 h after seeding ('overnight')

source.authors: Warmflash A, Sorre B, Etoc F, Siggia ED, Brivanlou AH
source.title: A method to recapitulate early embryonic spatial patterning in human embryonic stem cells

stages.name: Seeding on micropatterns

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor; 1 h pre-treatment and the first 2 h after seeding

stages.feeding: Replace with inhibitor-free medium 2 h after seeding; then overnight
actions: Pre-treat cells with Y-27632 for 1 h, wash and dissociate with trypsin
Resuspend 5 x 10^5 cells in 2.5 ml medium with Y-27632 and place over the coverslip in a 35 mm dish
After 2 h change to MEF-conditioned medium without Y-27632 and incubate overnight
stages.checkpoint: Every island filled by a round, confluent colony expressing OCT4, SOX2 and NANOG

stages.name: BMP4-induced patterning
stages.feeding: Single dose; fix at about 42 h
actions: Add BMP4
Fix and stain at 42 h
stages.checkpoint: Dense ring visible within 24 h; SOX2 centre, BRA ring, SOX17 ring and CDX2 edge at 42 h

protocols.name: Micropatterned colonies + BMP4 (protocol version, laminin-521; mTeSR1 option)
protocols.principle: The protocol-paper version of the micropattern assay: a single laminin-521 coating replaces the two-step poly-D-lysine/Matrigel coating, and a chemically defined mTeSR1 variant is given alongside conditioned medium.
protocols.start_requirements: hESCs (RUES2, ESI017; also used with RUES1, H1 and iPSCs) from a dish at 60-80% confluence, mycoplasma-negative. CYTOO Arena chips coated with laminin-521 at 5 µg/ml (optimise 5-20 µg/ml per batch) in PBS with calcium and magnesium for 2 h at 37 °C or overnight at 4 °C, washed without letting the chip dry.
materials: MEF-conditioned medium (HUESM conditioned on irradiated MEFs) or mTeSR1
Antibodies to SOX2, BRA, SOX17, CDX2; DAPI
tips: mTeSR1 variant: seed in mTeSR1 with 10 µM Y-27632 (a higher cell number than for conditioned medium), change to mTeSR1 without inhibitor after 2 h, and add 50 ng/ml BMP4 in mTeSR1 just 3 h later, because cells retract more in mTeSR1
Higher seeding density shrinks the outer rings and enlarges the central ectoderm domain; tune density for the pattern wanted
Image the whole chip as a tiled montage and average radial profiles over colonies
pitfalls: Holes in a colony act as extra edges and distort the pattern; colonies must be confluent before BMP4
Laminin-521 batches vary; re-optimise concentration
In mTeSR1 colonies may transiently retract at 12-24 h and then recover
unverified: Cell numbers per chip could not be read: exponents were lost in the text version (printed as '5 × 10– 1 × 10cells' for conditioned medium and '1-1.5 × 10cells' for mTeSR1). 5 x 10^5 - 1 x 10^6 and 1-1.5 x 10^6 are likely, given 5 x 10^5 in Warmflash 2014, but must be checked against the paper

source.authors: Deglincerti A, Etoc F, Guerra MC, et al.
source.title: Self-organization of human embryonic stem cells on micropatterns

stages.name: Seeding on micropatterns

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor during the first 2 h

stages.feeding: After 2 h wash once and change to medium without Y-27632; incubate 12-18 h
actions: Dissociate with Accutase (5-7 min, room temperature) to single cells
Add the single-cell suspension in 2.5 ml to the chip in a 35 mm dish (cell number: see unverified note; Warmflash 2014 used 5 x 10^5)
After 2 h wash with PBS and add medium without Y-27632
stages.checkpoint: Tightly packed circular colonies with no gaps

stages.name: BMP4-induced patterning
stages.feeding: Single dose for 48 h
actions: Replace medium with BMP4-containing medium
Incubate 48 h, then fix in 4% paraformaldehyde for 20 min and immunostain
stages.checkpoint: SOX2 centre, then BRA, SOX17 and CDX2 rings; dense centre and spread border cells by phase contrast

protocols.name: 3D human gastruloids (CHIR pre-treatment, then aggregation)
protocols.principle: hESCs pre-treated with the WNT agonist CHIR99021 ('Chiron') are aggregated in defined numbers in small wells; the aggregates break symmetry, elongate and organise derivatives of the three germ layers along an anteroposterior axis, with somitogenesis-like gene expression by 72 h, without forming extra-embryonic tissue.
protocols.start_requirements: hESCs maintained in Nutristem on vitronectin (per the authors' Protocol Exchange entry). Cell density and colony size at the time of pre-treatment are described as critical; cells are monitored daily to choose the time point. A CHIR99021 pre-treatment of the adherent culture precedes aggregation (dose and length not confirmed).
tips: A step-by-step protocol by the authors exists on Protocol Exchange: 'Generating Human Gastruloids from Human Embryonic Stem Cells' (DOI 10.21203/rs.3.pex-812/v1); follow it for the numbers
Secondary reports note that cells kept in other pluripotency media such as mTeSR1 or Essential 8 did not form elongated gastruloids
pitfalls: Outcome depends strongly on starting cell density and on the hESC line; expect to titrate CHIR99021 for each line
72 h human gastruloids model a post-implantation stage; check your institution's rules on embryo models
unverified: Paper and protocol full texts were not accessible (paywall; Protocol Exchange now redirects elsewhere): CHIR99021 dose and pre-treatment length, cells per well, aggregation medium, plate type, ROCK inhibitor dose, medium changes and elongation efficiency are all unconfirmed and left null
The split of the 72 h into a day 0-1 aggregation stage and a day 1-3 elongation stage is nominal, for the timeline only
The Protocol Exchange DOI was taken from the Europe PMC record and has no PMID

source.authors: Moris N, Anlas K, van den Brink SC, et al.
source.title: An in vitro model of early anteroposterior organization during human development

stages.name: Aggregate formation

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: WNT agonist; pre-treatment and/or during aggregation

actions: Dissociate the pre-treated culture and place a defined number of cells in each small well so that one tight aggregate forms per well
stages.checkpoint: One compact aggregate per well

stages.name: Elongation and patterning
actions: Continue culture; analyse at 72 h after aggregation
stages.checkpoint: Elongated aggregates with anteroposterior organisation at 72 h

cell_types.notes: Two different things share the name: flat micropatterned colonies treated with BMP4 (radial germ-layer rings, very reproducible, need micropatterned chips and tiled imaging) and 3D aggregates (axial elongation, more variable). Both are filed under mesoderm for convenience but contain all three germ layers. These are models of early human development and may fall under institutional oversight for embryo models.

cell_types.name: Gastruloids
cell_types.summary: Gastruloids are small aggregates of mouse ESCs that break symmetry, specify the three germ layers and elongate along an anteroposterior axis, reproducing post-occipital embryonic patterning including collinear Hox expression. They are used as an accessible stand-in for the post-implantation embryo, for axis formation, somitogenesis and signalling studies that would be impractical with embryos.
cell_types.maturation_note: Elongation is clearest at 114-120 h; past 120 h in a 96-well plate the structures adhere and lose organisation, so extended culture to 168 h is done in larger volumes on an orbital shaker.

morphology.endpoint: An elongated, roughly tadpole-shaped structure a few hundred micrometres long: one end bright and smooth under phase contrast (the elongating posterior), the other rounded and darker with a loose coat of shed cells (anterior). Internal epithelial structures become visible in extended culture.

stages.label: Single cells in a droplet
stages.look: Dispersed single cells sitting in a 40 ul droplet at the bottom of a U-bottom well.

stages.label: Coalescing aggregate
stages.look: Cells have fallen together into a ragged ball in which individual cells are already hard to tell apart.

stages.label: Clean spheroid
stages.look: A smooth, free-floating sphere about 150-200 um across; the well floor is mostly clean.

stages.label: Ovoid after the Wnt pulse
stages.look: Grown further, with local narrowing giving an ovoid outline and a thin rough coating of extruded cells.

stages.label: Elongating axis
stages.look: A clear long axis appears, bright and smooth at one end, round and dark at the other.

stages.label: Elongated gastruloid
stages.look: A long extension projecting from the darker rounded anterior mass; at least 70% of a good plate is elongating by this point.

markers.name: T
markers.note: The defining readout: it localises to one end, which is what defines the posterior pole. (Marks: Posterior / primitive streak.)

markers.name: Sox2
markers.note: Expressed in a domain extending away from the T-positive tip; marks tubular neural epithelia in late aggregates. (Marks: Neural / neuromesodermal.)

markers.name: Sox1
markers.note: Neural progenitor marker, reported with a Sox1::GFP reporter; anterior Sox1 with posterior T is the patterning criterion.

markers.name: Cdx2
markers.note: Posterior marker that extends away from the T-expressing tip, giving a dorsoventral-like organisation. (Marks: Posterior / caudal epiblast.)

markers.name: Sox17
markers.note: Marks endodermal pockets, typically in the anterior part of the structure.

markers.name: Foxa2
markers.note: Used alongside Sox17 to confirm endodermal identity. (Marks: Endoderm / axial mesendoderm.)

markers.name: Otx2
markers.note: Found in anterior epithelia and neural rosettes; central to the anterior neural phenotype of Wnt-inhibited aggregates.

markers.name: Tbx6
markers.note: Paraxial mesoderm marker; a TBX6::EYFP reporter line was used to score responses to signals.

markers.name: Cdh1
markers.note: Used to follow epithelial organisation within the aggregate. (Marks: Epithelium.)

markers.name: Nodal
markers.note: Timed interaction between Nodal and Wnt is what localises T expression to one end.

markers.name: Pou5f1
markers.note: Starting state marker; should fall away as germ-layer markers come up. (Marks: Pluripotent.)

markers.name: Hoxb1
markers.note: Hox genes come on collinearly along the extending axis, the hallmark of post-occipital identity. (Marks: Axial elongation.)

markers.name: Mixl1
markers.note: Should be off in the starting epiblast-like aggregate; useful as a negative control before patterning. (Marks: Mesendoderm.)

functional_assays: Live imaging of elongation and reporter dynamics
Quantification of elongation (length and shape descriptors) per plate
Collinear Hox expression along the axis
Scoring of anteroposterior patterning (posterior T/Bra with anterior Sox1)
qc: Aggregates 150-200 um across and free-floating at 48 h before the Wnt pulse
At least 70% of gastruloids elongating by 114 h under optimal conditions (Girgin 2018 Protocol Exchange)
One aggregate per well with no satellite aggregates
Posterior-localised T/Bra expression rather than multiple poles

protocols.name: Small ESC aggregates with a 24 h Wnt pulse (JoVE version)
protocols.principle: About 300-400 ESCs are aggregated in a U-bottom well in plain N2B27; after 48 h a single 24 h pulse of a GSK3 inhibitor breaks the aggregate's symmetry, and it then elongates along a single axis over the next two days.
protocols.start_requirements: ESCs maintained in ESLIF on gelatin-coated T25 flasks, at least two passages after thawing and no more than ~15 passages, grown to 40-60% confluency; never use over-confluent cells.
tips: Accurate counting is the single most important step: roughly 400 cells per 40 ul well.
The second PBS wash, which removes residual serum, was a key optimisation.
Because a residual volume stays in the well, the delivered CHIR99021 concentration is lower than nominal (about 2.37 uM on the pulse day, with carry-over afterwards).
pitfalls: Over-confluent or stressed starting cultures give large embryoid bodies instead of gastruloids.
Culture beyond ~5-6 days in a 96-well plate: the aggregates sink, adhere and lose their organisation.
Coating the plate with gelatin or fibronectin, which must not be done.
unverified: No percentage of elongating aggregates is given in this paper; it reports representative morphology rather than a scored efficiency.

source.authors: Baillie-Johnson P, van den Brink SC, Balayo T, Turner DA, Martinez Arias A
source.title: Generation of Aggregates of Mouse Embryonic Stem Cells that Show Symmetry Breaking, Polarization and Emergent Collective Behaviour In Vitro

stages.name: Aggregation in N2B27
stages.feeding: 40 ul droplet per well; no feeding for 48 h
actions: Trypsinise to a true single-cell suspension and count carefully
Wash the cells twice in PBS to remove carried-over serum
Resuspend at 10 cells/ul in N2B27 (5 x 10^4 cells in 5 ml fills one 96-well plate)
Pipette 40 ul per well into a non-treated U-bottom 96-well plate
Incubate 48 h undisturbed
stages.checkpoint: One clean spherical aggregate per well, about 150-200 um across, moving freely and not stuck to the plastic

stages.name: Wnt pulse

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.conc: 3 uM (added as 150 ul of a 3 uM solution; effective concentration in the well ~2.37 uM after dilution)
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; switches Wnt on for 24 h

stages.feeding: Add 150 ul of the secondary medium to each well
actions: Add 150 ul of 3 uM CHIR99021 in N2B27 per well with a multichannel pipette
Pipette firmly enough to dislodge any aggregate starting to stick
Incubate 24 h
stages.checkpoint: Aggregates still free-floating at the end of the pulse; shed cells around them are normal

stages.name: Washout and elongation
stages.feeding: 150 ul exchanged every 24 h
actions: Remove 150 ul from the side of each well with the pipette held at about 30 degrees
Add 150 ul fresh N2B27 with enough force to move the aggregates
Repeat every 24 h to the end of the time course (typically 120 h)
stages.checkpoint: By 96-120 h most aggregates have a clear long axis, with a bright smooth posterior tip and a darker rounded anterior end

protocols.name: Standard gastruloid protocol with extended shaking culture to 168 h
protocols.principle: The same 300-cell aggregate plus 24 h Wnt pulse, written up with exact cell densities per cell type and an extended phase in which gastruloids are moved to a larger volume on an orbital shaker, which lets the axis keep elongating to day 7.
protocols.efficiency: At least 70% of gastruloids should be elongating by 114 h under optimal conditions
protocols.start_requirements: ESCs in ESLIF on 0.1% gelatin-coated plastic, passaged every other day, at least two passages post-thaw and ideally under 30 passages, at 40-60% confluency (around 1.8 x 10^4 cells/cm2 recommended).
tips: Optimum viewing time for the elongation is about 114-120 h.
Cells grown in 2i conditions also work, but elongation is slightly delayed relative to serum/LIF cells.
iPSC lines generally need more starting cells (600-800 per well) than ESC lines (300).
pitfalls: Many small satellite aggregates per well mean the cell density was underestimated when counting.
Evaporation from the 40 ul droplets during the first 48 h, worst in peripheral wells.
Aggregates adhering after 120 h unless moved to the shaking extended culture.
N2B27 batch variation, which shows up as aggregates decompacting from the edge inwards.
unverified: This is a Protocol Exchange article; its DOI (10.1038/protex.2018.094) comes from the Cambridge repository record for the accepted manuscript, not from a PubMed entry, and it has no PMID. Numbers were read from the accepted manuscript PDF.
Marker and patterning claims are in the associated Nature paper (Beccari 2018), not in this protocol.

source.authors: Girgin M, Turner DA, Baillie-Johnson P, Cossy AC, Beccari L, Moris N, Lutolf MP, Duboule D, Martinez Arias A
source.title: Generating Gastruloids from Mouse Embryonic Stem Cells

stages.name: Aggregation
stages.base_medium: N2B27 (NDiff227 or home-made from Neurobasal and DMEM/F12 with N2 and B27)
stages.feeding: 40 ul droplet per well, undisturbed for 48 h
actions: Trypsinise, neutralise and wash the cells twice in PBS
Resuspend in N2B27 at 7.5 cells/ul for ESCs (20 cells/ul for iPSCs)
Pipette 40 ul per well of a non-treated U-bottom 96-well plate, giving 300 cells per well (800 for iPSCs)
Return the plate to the incubator for 48 h
stages.checkpoint: A single compact aggregate per well, smooth and slightly larger than at 24 h; cell number is tuned per line to give ~150 um diameter at 48 h

stages.name: Wnt pulse

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; a single 24 h pulse

stages.feeding: 150 ul of secondary medium added per well
actions: Prepare 3 uM CHIR99021 in N2B27 (16 ml is ample for one plate)
Add 150 ul per well
Incubate 24 h
stages.checkpoint: At 72 h aggregates have grown, some show local narrowing and an ovoid shape, with a thin rough coat of shed cells

stages.name: Daily washout
stages.feeding: 150 ul exchanged at 72, 96 and 120 h
actions: Remove 150 ul from the side of each well with the pipette at an angle
Add 150 ul fresh pre-warmed N2B27 with enough force to move the gastruloid
stages.checkpoint: At 96 h many aggregates have a clear long axis: one end bright and smooth (posterior, elongating), the other round and dark with loose cells (anterior)

stages.name: Extended shaking culture
stages.feeding: 700 ul per well; 400 ul exchanged at 144 h
actions: At 120 h transfer gastruloids individually into low-attachment 24-well plates in 700 ul N2B27, using a P1000 tip cut about 5 mm from the end
Incubate on an incubator-compatible orbital shaker at 40 rpm for 48 h
Exchange 400 ul of medium at 144 h
stages.checkpoint: By 168 h the elongation is long and thin, internal epithelial structures are visible by phase contrast, and the anterior end may be broad

protocols.name: Gastruloids from epiblast-like aggregates with Wnt inhibition (anterior neural)
protocols.principle: Starting from epiblast-like aggregates formed in microwells rather than from naive ESCs, and inhibiting rather than activating Wnt early on, gives structures that elongate without any exogenous Wnt pulse and go on to form anterior neural tissue that standard gastruloids lack.
protocols.efficiency: About 50% of aggregates show posterior T/BRA with anterior SOX1 at 144 h with the Wnt inhibitor, against about 10% without it; classical gastruloids never showed SOX1 anterior to T/BRA in this comparison
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ESCs in s2iL (DMEM+GlutaMAX, 10% ESC-qualified FBS, pyruvate, NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol, pen/strep, 3 uM CHIR99021, 1 uM PD0325901, LIF), seeded at 50,000-60,000 cells per 6-well and cultured 2-3 days; dissociate with Accutase and wash twice in PBS.
materials: PEG microwell arrays (400 um wells, 121 per array)
tips: Elongation and patterning depend strictly on the initial aggregate size: smaller aggregates do not hold the elongated shape.
A step-by-step bench version of this protocol is published separately (Girgin 2023, Bio-protocol), including the standard 300-cell gastruloid arm for comparison.
pitfalls: Shaking or swirling during seeding, which spoils the even distribution across microwells.
Damaging aggregates during the pick-and-transfer step.
Without the Wnt inhibitor, anteroposterior patterning is rare (~10%).

source.authors: Girgin MU, Broguiere N, Mattolini L, Lutolf MP
source.title: Gastruloids generated without exogenous Wnt activation develop anterior neural tissues

stages.name: Epiblast-like aggregate formation
stages.base_medium: N2B27 (DMEM/F12 + Neurobasal, 0.5x N2, 0.5x B27, 0.5x GlutaMAX, pyruvate, NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol)

factors.name: XAV939
factors.role: Tankyrase inhibitor; blocks Wnt and is what allows anterior neural tissue later

stages.feeding: 35 ul of cell suspension onto the array, then 1 ml medium; no change for 72 h
actions: Equilibrate 400 um PEG microwell arrays with 50 ul medium for 30 min at 37 C
Seed 35 ul of a 484,000 cells/ml suspension to give 100-150 cells per microwell
Let cells sediment for 20-30 min, then add 1 ml medium gently from the side
Culture at least 72 h
stages.checkpoint: Smooth aggregates, for 100 cells/well no more than about 220 um in diameter

stages.name: Transfer to 96-well plates
stages.feeding: 180 ul N2B27 per well with the aggregate added in 10 ul
actions: At about 72-80 h flush the aggregates off the array with N2B27 into a non-treated 10 cm dish
Pick single, undamaged, size-matched aggregates in 10 ul under a stereomicroscope
Transfer each into a well of an ultra-low-attachment U-bottom 96-well plate containing 180 ul N2B27
stages.checkpoint: One intact aggregate with smooth edges per well

stages.name: Elongation without exogenous Wnt
stages.feeding: 150 ul exchanged every 24 h until 168 h
actions: Change 150 ul of medium every 24 h with a multichannel pipette
Score morphology and reporter expression at 144 and 168 h
stages.checkpoint: Axial elongation with posterior T/BRA at the tip and anterior SOX1, plus SOX17-positive anterior endodermal pockets and OTX2-positive neural rosettes

cell_types.notes: Starting cell number is the critical variable: around 300 (plus or minus 100) cells, roughly 100 um across, works; above about 600 cells the aggregates grow as disorganised embryoid bodies and below about 200 they fail to respond. iPSC lines generally need more cells than ESC lines. Timing of the Wnt pulse matters as much as the dose - the 48-72 h window gives maximum elongation, while pulses applied earlier or later give variable or multi-polar responses, and the response is also cell-line dependent. Because a residual volume stays in the well during medium changes, the delivered CHIR99021 concentration is below nominal and carries over for a day or two.

cell_types.name: Three germ layers (embryoid bodies / trilineage test)
cell_types.summary: Embryoid bodies are floating aggregates of pluripotent cells that differentiate spontaneously and yield a mixture of all three germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm), not mesoderm alone. They are used as the classic functional test of pluripotency for a new iPSC line and as the first step of many older directed-differentiation methods.
cell_types.maturation_note: Germ-layer transcripts are usually scored after roughly 1.5-2 weeks of spontaneous differentiation; cystic EBs and occasional beating areas appear later. Directed (monolayer) trilineage tests are faster but are mostly done with commercial kits.

morphology.endpoint: Round to irregular floating aggregates, some with fluid-filled cysts; after plating, EBs flatten into a heterogeneous outgrowth with neural-looking, epithelial and mesenchymal patches.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact, sharp-edged colonies at 60-80% confluence, ready to be lifted as clumps or single cells.

stages.label: Fresh aggregates
stages.look: Small, smooth, bright aggregates floating in low-attachment dishes or sitting one per well.

stages.label: Growing embryoid bodies
stages.look: Larger, darker spheres; some start to show a clear outer layer and internal cavities.

stages.label: Cystic / mixed EBs
stages.look: Heterogeneous bodies, some cystic and translucent, containing derivatives of all three germ layers.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should fall as EBs differentiate; persistent expression means poor differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Lost early during spontaneous differentiation.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Neuroectoderm readout commonly used in trilineage panels.

markers.name: NEFL
markers.note: Ectoderm marker used in the original human EB paper (neurofilament 68 kDa).

markers.name: TUBB3

protocols.name: Feeder-free EBs in defined E8/E6 medium with PVA
protocols.principle: Cells from defined E8 cultures are lifted with EDTA and aggregated in E8 containing polyvinyl alcohol and ROCK inhibitor (self-aggregation, hanging drops or AggreWell), then left to differentiate spontaneously in E6, which is E8 without FGF2 and TGF-beta.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs on Matrigel or vitronectin in E8. Passage 1:3 or 1:4 two days before (day -2) with 10 µM Y-27632, change to E8 without inhibitor on day -1, and start at 60-80% confluence.
materials: Ultra-low attachment dishes or poly-HEMA (20 mg/ml in 95% ethanol) coated petri dishes
tips: Hanging drops or AggreWell give EBs of uniform size; self-aggregation is quickest but sizes vary
Use only the inner part of the timeline you need: many labs harvest RNA at about day 10-14

The human EB assay goes back to Itskovitz-Eldor et al. 2000 (Mol Med 6:88-95, PMID 10859025), who showed zeta-globin (mesoderm), neurofilament 68 kDa (ectoderm) and alpha-fetoprotein (endoderm) in suspension EBs from human ES cells

For one uniform EB per well, the spin-EB method (Ng et al. 2008, Nat Protoc 3:768-76, PMID 18451785, DOI 10.1038/nprot.2008.42) pellets a fixed number of single cells in round-bottom low-attachment 96-well plates in defined APEL medium; a 2020 protocol from the same lab (Nafria et al., PMID 33377024) uses roughly 5,000-6,000 cells per well
pitfalls: EBs stick to ordinary tissue-culture plastic; use low-attachment or poly-HEMA surfaces
Losing EBs during medium changes is the usual cause of low yield; let them settle first
unverified: The source page does not describe how germ layers are assessed; marker panel here comes from the other sources and general practice
ROCK inhibitor concentration during EB formation is not stated (10 µM is given for passaging)
No DOI is listed for this StemBook protocol; PMID 28211653 is the NCBI Bookshelf record matched by title in Europe PMC

Itskovitz-Eldor 2000 and Ng 2008 are not given as separate protocols because only their abstracts could be read (scanned PDF and paywall): their media, cell numbers, spin settings and day numbers are unconfirmed

protocols.name: STEMdiff Trilineage Differentiation Kit (three parallel monolayer arms)
protocols.principle: A functional pluripotency assay: single-cell hPSCs are plated in three sets of wells and each set is fed daily with one complete, ready-to-use medium that drives it to ectoderm, mesoderm or endoderm. It is an endpoint assay read by lineage markers within a week, not a way to make cells for further differentiation.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-AOF, used when they are ready for passaging (mostly large, compact colonies with multilayered centres); scrape off differentiated areas first. Dissociate to single cells with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent and plate on Corning Matrigel hESC-Qualified Matrix (24-well format in the PIS) in maintenance medium + 10 µM Y-27632. Densities: ectoderm 200,000 cells/cm2, mesoderm 50,000 cells/cm2, endoderm 200,000 cells/cm2.
materials: STEMdiff Trilineage Differentiation Kit (05230): Ectoderm Medium 175 mL, Mesoderm Medium 100 mL, Endoderm Medium 100 mL
Example antibodies: Anti-Human Nestin clone 10C2 (60091), Anti-Human CD56 clone HCD56 (60021), Anti-Human CD184 clone 12G5 (60089)
tips: Thawed Ectoderm and Mesoderm Medium keep 2 weeks at 2-8°C; Endoderm Medium only 1 week. Aliquots can be frozen once at -20°C; do not refreeze.
Do not filter the media.
The kit is validated for lines kept in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-AOF.
pitfalls: The mesoderm arm is seeded four-fold lower than the other two; using one density for all wells will distort the result.
This is an endpoint assay; the PIS says it is not optimized for producing cells for downstream differentiation.
Moving the plate in the first 24 h after plating gives uneven monolayers.
unverified: Efficiency: the PIS gives no percentage for any germ layer.
The PIS says to repeat the daily change 'until day 5' (mesoderm, endoderm) or 'day 7' (ectoderm) and to harvest on those same days; whether a final feed is given on the harvest day is not explicit.
The protocol diagram is an image and was not available.

protocols.name: StemMACS Trilineage Differentiation Kit (7-day monolayer pluripotency assay)
protocols.principle: A functional pluripotency test: single cells are seeded in three parallel wells and directed for seven days toward mesoderm, endoderm and ectoderm with four ready-to-use media, then scored by flow cytometry or immunostaining instead of embryoid bodies or teratomas.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in a PSC maintenance medium such as StemMACS iPS-Brew XF, dissociated to a single-cell suspension (0.05% trypsin/EDTA 5 min, stopped with soybean trypsin inhibitor). Seed on Matrigel hESC-qualified (1:80) in 12-well plates: 150,000 cells per well for mesoderm, 250,000 for endoderm, 200,000 for ectoderm (24-well: 80,000 / 130,000 / 100,000; equivalent to about 40,000, 66,000 and 53,000 cells/cm²). Add ROCK inhibitor (10 µM Y-27632 or 2 µM thiazovivin) for the initial plating only.
materials: StemMACS Trilineage Differentiation Kit, human (MesoDiff Medium I 36 mL, MesoDiff Medium II 72 mL, EndoDiff Medium 60 mL, EctoDiff Medium 84 mL; for 12 assays)
PSC cultivation medium, e.g. StemMACS iPS-Brew XF (130-104-368)
ROCK inhibitor: StemMACS Y27632 (130-103-922) or StemMACS Thiazovivin (130-104-461)
Corning Matrigel hESC-qualified Matrix and DMEM/F12 (no HEPES) for dilution
Antibodies for readout (e.g. CD144, CD140b, CD184, SOX17, PAX6, SOX2)
tips: Schedule from the Miltenyi data sheet for order no. 130-115-660 (document 140-005-218.03).
12-well format suits flow cytometry; 24-well is enough for immunostaining.
Media arrive frozen: thaw at 2-8°C overnight, then use within 2 weeks; aliquots can be kept at -20°C.
Several lines can be tested in parallel; seeding numbers may need adjusting per line.
For flow cytometry, harvest as for hPSCs with half the volumes.
pitfalls: Clumps instead of a true single-cell suspension invalidate the seeding numbers; the data sheet treats single cells as mandatory.
ROCK inhibitor is for the initial plating only.
Changing the mesoderm well on days 2 or 3 departs from the protocol.
unverified: The kit is a qualitative/quantitative assay; no expected percentage of marker-positive cells is given, so efficiency is null.

protocols.name: Human PSC Functional Identification Kit (trilineage)
protocols.principle: One shared RPMI-based differentiation base plus three separate factor supplements runs parallel ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm inductions from the same hPSC line, so pluripotency can be shown in vitro by OTX2, brachyury and SOX17 staining instead of a teratoma assay.
protocols.start_requirements: Wells coated with Cultrex RGF BME PathClear (3433-005-01) or Cultrex UltiMatrix (BME001) diluted 1:40 in DMEM/F-12, 1-2 h at room temperature, 0.5 mL per well of a 24-well plate with a sterile coverslip in each well for ICC. hPSCs are dissociated with Accutase and replated in ExCellerate iPSC Expansion Medium with 5 uM Y-27632 at 4-5 x 10^4 cells/cm2 (about 2 x 10^6 cells across one 24-well plate). Start the mesoderm arm at 50-60% confluency and the ectoderm and endoderm arms at 60-75%. One kit makes 200 mL of medium, enough for one 24-well plate per germ layer.
materials: Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Functional Identification Kit (SC027B)
Cultrex RGF BME PathClear (3433-005-01) or Cultrex UltiMatrix (BME001)
RPMI; DMEM/F-12; GlutaminePlus (B90210) or GlutaMAX; optional penicillin-streptomycin; PBS
Y-27632; Accutase; Trypan Blue; very low endotoxin BSA; 12 mm coverslips and forceps
Flow Cytometry Fixation Buffer (FC004) and Permeabilization/Wash Buffer I (FC005) for the flow route
NorthernLights NL557 donkey anti-goat secondary (NL001) and mounting medium (CTS011)
tips: Run the three arms side by side from one seeding batch so the comparison is fair
The arms need slightly different starting confluencies: mesoderm 50-60%, ectoderm and endoderm 60-75%
Seeding onto coverslips up front saves transferring fragile cultures later
pitfalls: The mesoderm arm finishes a day or two before the other two; do not hold it longer waiting for them
This kit verifies pluripotency - it is not meant to supply usable quantities of any one germ layer (the lineage-specific SC019B/SC030B/SC031B kits are)
A no-primary control is essential; the germ-layer antibodies are polyclonal goat reagents
unverified: No stated positive-cell percentages for any of the three arms
The product page advertises 5 days while the written procedure spans 4 differentiation days plus staining

cell_types.name: Endothelial cells
cell_types.summary: The cells lining blood vessels. hPSC-derived endothelial cells are used for vascular disease modelling, barrier and inflammation assays, angiogenesis assays and to vascularise organoids and engineered tissues.
cell_types.maturation_note: CD144+/CD34+ cells by day 5-6; sorted cells mature and expand over a further 1-2 weeks but lose proliferative capacity with passage.

morphology.endpoint: After sorting, a cobblestone monolayer of polygonal cells that become elongated when sparse; unsorted day-6 cultures show endothelial islands among mesenchymal cells.

protocols.name: CHIR99021 + BMP4 mesoderm, then VEGF + forskolin (6 days)
protocols.principle: GSK3 inhibition plus BMP4 converts a sparse hPSC monolayer to lateral mesoderm in three days; a short exposure to high VEGF-A with forskolin (cAMP/PKA activation) then drives endothelial commitment, and CD144+ cells are purified magnetically on day 6.
protocols.efficiency: 62-89% CD144+ cells before sorting; about 96% after CD144 MACS
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in mTeSR1 on Matrigel, passaged with Accutase. Day 0: seed single cells at 37,000-47,000 cells/cm2 on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel in mTeSR1 + 10 µM Y-27632.
tips: Expansion: fibronectin-coated flasks (about 2 µg/cm2), StemPro-34 + 50 ng/ml VEGF-A.
The same day 1-4 mesoderm is the starting point for the smooth muscle protocol.
The paper's figure text describes the cells as CD31+, CD34+, KDR+, CD105+, vWF+ and negative for CD43/CD45.
pitfalls: Confluency on day 1 is the main determinant of efficiency: too dense gives heavy death by day 4, too sparse a low yield.
Efficiency below 20% suggests inactive growth factors or wrong media; 20-50% usually means density or medium volume needs adjusting. Titrate density and GSK3 inhibitor dose per line.
A minor ACTA2+ mural population is always present before sorting.
unverified: Step values are taken from the authors' own Protocol Exchange write-up (Challet Meylan L, Patsch C, Thoma E; doi 10.1038/protex.2015.055 for endothelial cells, doi 10.1038/protex.2015.056 for smooth muscle cells) because the online Methods of the Nat Cell Biol paper could not be accessed.
Duration of endothelial expansion after sorting is not specified.

protocols.name: CHIR99021 alone in LaSR basal medium, CD34 sort on day 5
protocols.principle: Two days of Wnt activation in a minimal medium (Advanced DMEM/F12 with ascorbic acid) is enough to generate CD34+CD31+ endothelial progenitors without added VEGF or FGF; sorted progenitors mature into endothelial cells in EGM-2.
protocols.efficiency: More than 50% CD34+CD31+ progenitors reported in multiple lines (about 25% in the initial medium screen); >99% CD31+/VE-cadherin+ after purification and expansion
protocols.start_requirements: Singularised hPSCs seeded on Matrigel at 50,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 + 5 µM Y-27632 on day -3; mTeSR1 changed daily until day 0.
tips: Seeding density strongly affects yield; the authors screened 12,000-300,000 cells/cm2.
Sorted cells went through about 20 population doublings over 2 months.
pitfalls: Basal medium matters: RPMI/B27 and serum-containing endothelial medium gave no CD34+CD31+ cells in this scheme.
Endogenous MEK signalling is required; MEK inhibition abolishes the progenitors.
The CD34+ fraction is bipotent and also gives smooth muscle cells in other media.

protocols.name: STEMdiff Endothelial Differentiation and Expansion Kits (monolayer)
protocols.principle: Sparsely seeded hPSCs get 2 days of STEMdiff Mesoderm Induction Medium (bought separately) and then 4 days of Endothelial Induction Medium, giving CD31+CD34+CD144+ cells by day 7 without sorting. Passaging in Endothelial Expansion Medium on an animal component-free substrate then purifies and expands them.
protocols.efficiency: By day 7, 50 - 80% of cells are positive for CD31, CD34 and CD144 (assessment section: > 50%, CD45 negative); typically ≥ 99% CD144+CD31+ by passage 2 in expansion medium
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8 on Corning Matrigel, confluent and ready to passage. On day 0 seed single cells on a Matrigel-coated 6-well plate in the maintenance medium + 10 µM Y-27632 at 5000 - 10,000 cells/cm2 (mTeSR1 or TeSR-E8; e.g. 5 - 10 x 10^4 per well) or 3500 - 7500 cells/cm2 (mTeSR Plus; e.g. 3.5 - 7.5 x 10^4 per well).

STEMdiff Endothelial Expansion Medium Kit (Catalog #08007) or Expansion Culture Kit (Catalog #100-1218) for further expansion

Heparin Solution (Catalog #07980), needed for complete expansion medium
tips: Seeding density depends on the line and on the maintenance medium; mTeSR Plus cultures are seeded lower than mTeSR1 or TeSR-E8 cultures
Filter complete Expansion Medium through a 0.2 - 0.22 µm PES unit; it keeps 2 weeks at 2-8°C and can be refiltered if a precipitate forms

cell_types.name: Vascular smooth muscle cells
cell_types.summary: Contractile cells of the vessel wall that set vascular tone and switch between contractile and synthetic states in disease. hPSC-derived smooth muscle cells are used to model aortopathies and atherosclerosis and to build vessel grafts and co-cultures with endothelium.

cell_types.maturation_note: PDGFRB+ cells by day 6; contractile proteins (CNN1, TAGLN, MYH11) accumulate over 1-2 further weeks and depend on the maturation medium.

morphology.endpoint: Elongated spindle cells growing in a hill-and-valley pattern; contractile-biased cultures are larger, flatter and slow-growing with visible filament bundles.

protocols.principle: The same three-day CHIR99021 + BMP4 mesoderm used for endothelial cells is switched to PDGF-BB and Activin A, which gives almost exclusively PDGFRB+ mural cells; replating conditions then bias them to a synthetic or a contractile phenotype.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in mTeSR1 on Matrigel. Day 0: seed single cells at 37,000-47,000 cells/cm2 on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel in mTeSR1 + 10 µM Y-27632.
tips: Residual CD144+ cells can be removed by MACS if needed.
Serum and high PDGF-BB were deliberately avoided, so cells proliferate slowly, especially under the contractile condition.
pitfalls: Pure populations of one phenotype are hard to maintain; with prolonged culture the synthetic phenotype dominates.
Density on day 1 controls efficiency, as for the endothelial arm.

protocols.name: Origin-specific smooth muscle via lateral plate mesoderm (PDGF-BB + TGF-beta1)
protocols.principle: hPSCs are first patterned into a defined embryonic intermediate (lateral plate mesoderm here; neuroectoderm or paraxial mesoderm in the alternative arms), then all intermediates are differentiated with PDGF-BB and TGF-beta1 for 12 days to give smooth muscle cells that retain origin-specific behaviour.
protocols.efficiency: >80% MYH11+/ACTA2+ cells after 12 days of PDGF-BB + TGF-beta1 from all three intermediates
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in chemically defined medium (CDM) with Activin A and FGF2.
tips: Alternative origins: neuroectoderm with FGF2 12 ng/ml + SB431542 10 µM for 7 days; paraxial mesoderm with FGF2 20 ng/ml + LY294002 10 µM after the 36 h early-mesoderm step; both then get the same PDGF-BB + TGF-beta1 treatment.
A step-by-step version was published as Cheung et al. 2014 Nat Protoc (PMID 24675733, doi 10.1038/nprot.2014.059).

Choose the intermediate to match the embryonic origin of the vessel being modelled (for example neuroectoderm/neural crest for the ascending aorta and arch, paraxial mesoderm for the descending aorta).
pitfalls: A small fraction of cells (2-8%) express the pericyte marker CSPG4 (NG2) during differentiation.
The CDM system with Activin/FGF2 maintenance is different from mTeSR1/E8 culture; adaptation may be needed.
unverified: Duration of the paraxial mesoderm step is not stated explicitly in the sentence read (it parallels the 3.5-day lateral plate step).
The 2014 Nat Protoc version could not be accessed, so any refinements there are not included.

cell_types.name: Cardiomyocytes
cell_types.summary: Contracting heart muscle cells made from mouse ES or iPS cells, either as beating clusters in serum-grown embryoid bodies or as enriched monolayers after growth-factor-directed cardiac mesoderm induction. They are used to study early heart development, gene function in knockout lines, electrophysiology and drug effects on beating.
cell_types.maturation_note: First beating at about day 7-8; hanging-drop cultures are classed as early (about day 7-10), intermediate (about day 12-14) and late (about day 15-25) as the cells mature.

morphology.endpoint: Rhythmically contracting patches, strands or sheets. In plated embryoid bodies the beating areas sit within a mixed outgrowth of flat non-muscle cells; in the directed monolayer method larger synchronised sheets form.

stages.label: Undifferentiated ES colonies
stages.look: Domed, tightly packed colonies with bright, sharp edges; individual cells are hard to make out.

stages.label: Embryoid bodies
stages.look: Small, smooth, round floating aggregates of even size (one per hanging drop, or many in a non-adherent dish).

stages.label: Plated cardiac mesoderm / EB outgrowth
stages.look: After plating, cells attach and spread into a dense sheet of small cells; plated EBs show a dark core with cells migrating outwards.

stages.label: First beating areas
stages.look: Small clusters start to twitch, then contract rhythmically; in EB outgrowths they appear as discrete beating islands.

stages.label: Established contracting sheets
stages.look: Larger, more strongly and regularly contracting areas and strands that pull on the surrounding cells.

protocols.name: Serum-free EBs with titrated activin A + BMP4 + VEGF (Keller lab)
protocols.principle: Embryoid bodies are formed without factors, then dissociated and re-aggregated for a short pulse of activin A, BMP4 and VEGF that is tuned to give Flk-1+/PdgfR-α+ cardiac mesoderm; the cells are then plated as a monolayer in VEGF, bFGF and FGF10 to become contracting cardiomyocytes. Very small changes in the activin/BMP4 doses switch the outcome between cardiac and blood mesoderm, so the doses are titrated for each cell line.
protocols.start_requirements: Undifferentiated mouse ESC/iPSC, feeder-free or feeder-depleted (the E14 implementation used here grew cells on gelatin in GMEM + 15% FBS + LIF, passaged every 2-3 days). Single-cell suspension by trypsin; seed 75,000 cells/ml in SFD medium in non-adherent dishes with no added growth factors.
materials: Antibodies to Flk-1 (Kdr) and PdgfR-α for flow
tips: This protocol is line-dependent by design: the paper's central finding is that each mouse (and human) line needs its own activin A/BMP4 optimum. Run a small activin × BMP4 matrix for every new line and BMP4/activin lot, reading out Flk-1/PdgfR-α at the end of the induction step.

Published doses for this same scheme differ between labs and lines: activin A 8 ng/ml + BMP4 0.5 ng/ml (E14-Tg2a; Cirino 2020), activin A 8 ng/ml + BMP4 1 ng/ml (Bardot 2017), and activin 6 ng/ml + BMP4 12.5 ng/ml as printed for A2Lox cells (Bouveret 2015). Treat any single number as a starting point.
Later versions add a Wnt inhibitor at the plating step (XAV at 10 µM in Bardot 2017; IWR1 at 5 µM in Bouveret 2015) to push cardiac mesoderm towards cardiomyocytes.
Flk-1 and PdgfR-α co-expression is the in-process control; do not carry a batch forward if the double-positive population is small.
pitfalls: Copying the activin/BMP4 doses from another lab without titration is the commonest reason for failure; too much BMP4 or the wrong activin level yields Flk-1+ PdgfR-α− (blood/endothelial) mesoderm instead.
Growth-factor activity varies by lot, so re-titrate when a new lot arrives.
Timing is tight (48 h EBs, then about 40 h induction); delaying dissociation shifts the mesoderm that forms.
unverified: The original Cell Stem Cell full text was not accessible in this session; day-by-day numbers (75,000 cells/ml, 48 h EBs, 40 h induction, 6 × 10⁴ cells per 24-well, StemPro-34 with VEGF 5, bFGF 10, FGF10 50 ng/ml) are taken from Cirino et al. 2020 (Front Cell Dev Biol, PMID 33015063, DOI 10.3389/fcell.2020.571501), an E14-Tg2a implementation that cites Kattman 2011.
Activin A 8 ng/ml and BMP4 0.5 ng/ml are the E14-Tg2a values in Cirino 2020, not confirmed as the values Kattman 2011 reports for its own lines.
Cell density for the re-aggregation step is not stated in the restating paper.
Ascorbic acid concentration: Cirino 2020 prints '5 mg/ml', which is probably the stock; Keller-lab SFD recipes in other papers use 0.5 mM (about 50 µg/ml).
N2/B27 percentages in SFD not given in the restating paper (other Keller-lab papers use 0.5× N2 and 0.5-1× B27).
Percentage of cTnT+ cells for mouse lines not confirmed from the original paper, so efficiency is left empty.
FGF10 dose differs between restating papers (50 ng/ml in Cirino 2020, 25 ng/ml in Bouveret 2015); the original value was not confirmed.

protocols.name: Classic hanging-drop embryoid bodies in serum (Wobus/Boheler)
protocols.principle: A fixed number of ES cells is aggregated in each hanging drop of serum-containing medium without LIF; the EBs are grown in suspension and then plated on gelatin, where spontaneously beating cardiomyocyte clusters appear in the outgrowths. No growth factors are added: the serum lot and the cell number per drop do the work.
protocols.efficiency: Up to 96% of EBs develop beating areas with a batch-tested serum (Abdul Kadir 2009); this is the fraction of beating EBs, not the fraction of cardiomyocytes among all cells
protocols.start_requirements: Undifferentiated mouse ES cells (lines used in the verified sources: D3, R1, CGR8, E14Tg2a) grown with LIF; make a single-cell suspension and remove LIF. Dilute to 400 cells per 20 µl (2 × 10⁴ cells/ml) in differentiation medium with batch-tested fetal calf serum.
tips: Serum lot matters more than anything else: test several lots and keep the one that gives a high fraction of beating EBs.
Day counts are often written as suspension days + days after plating (for example 5+2 or 7+4); check which convention a paper uses before comparing time points.

Cardiomyocytes from this method are a mix of pacemaker-like, atrial-like and ventricular-like cells that mature with time in culture (stated in the Boheler 2002 abstract); choose early, intermediate or late cultures to match the experiment.
Plating single EBs per well gives a simple quantitative readout (percentage of beating EBs).
pitfalls: Cardiomyocytes are a minority of the cells in each EB; the cultures are mixed and need dissection, reporter selection or sorting for purity.
Cell number per drop changes the outcome; keep it constant (400 cells per 20 µl in the verified sources) and count carefully.
Residual LIF or feeders in the starting suspension delays differentiation.
Drops dry out without a humid chamber; evaporation changes medium osmolarity and kills the aggregates.
unverified: The full text of Boheler 2002 (Circ Res) and of the Wobus 2002 methods chapter (Methods Mol Biol 185:127-156, PMID 11768985) was not accessible in this session; the PubMed record and abstract of Boheler 2002 were checked.

400 cells per 20 µl drop, 2 days in drops, then 3-5 days in suspension, plating on gelatin, beating from about day 7 and the early/intermediate/late day ranges are taken from Abdul Kadir et al. 2009 (J Cell Mol Med, PMID 19438812), which follows the Boheler classification.
2 days hanging drop + 3 days suspension with plating at day 5 is taken from the Wobus lab's own methods in Czyz et al. 2005 (Int J Dev Biol, PMID 15744665), which cites Wobus 2002.

Medium composition (IMDM + 10% FCS, 450 µM MTG, L-glutamine, NEAA, 400 cells per drop) is from the Wobus lab in Wiese et al. 2011 (Int J Cardiol, PMID 19775764), where EBs were plated at day 7; the exact medium and serum percentage in Boheler 2002 were not confirmed.
Number of drops per lid and PBS volume in the dish were not taken from a source.

cell_types.notes: Two very different routes are in common use. The serum hanging-drop method is simple and robust but gives mixed cultures in which cardiomyocytes are a minority. The serum-free activin/BMP4/VEGF method gives enriched cultures but only after the growth-factor doses have been titrated for the particular ES/iPS line and reagent lots. Mouse differentiation runs much faster than human: beating appears after about a week.

cell_types.name: Atrial cardiomyocytes

cell_types.maturation_note: Beating from about day 8-10; atrial identity is usually assessed from day 20-30 and by electrophysiology later still.

morphology.endpoint: Beating sheets or EBs that look like standard hPSC-cardiomyocytes but usually contract faster; subtype cannot be judged by eye.

protocols.name: Monolayer Wnt on/off plus retinoic acid on days 3-6
protocols.principle: A standard CHIR99021 then IWP2 monolayer differentiation in albumin/ascorbate RPMI; adding 1 µM retinoic acid during cardiac mesoderm specification redirects the cells from a ventricular to an atrial fate.
protocols.efficiency: About 87-90% cTnT+ at day 20; in RA-treated cultures about 95% of cardiomyocytes were MLC2a+/MLC2v- at around day 100 (versus about 11% in controls)
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs on Geltrex-coated plates grown to 80-90% confluence.
tips: Run a no-retinoic-acid well in parallel: it gives the matched ventricular control used throughout the paper.
Retinoic acid is light-sensitive; make fresh dilutions and protect from light.
Subtype identity (MLC2a versus MLC2v) sharpens with long culture; the paper's subtype percentages are from about day 100.
pitfalls: Retinoic acid dose and window matter: later papers report that the atrial action-potential phenotype depends on the RA concentration, so do not assume 1 µM on days 3-6 transfers unchanged to every line.
MLC2a alone is not proof of atrial identity in young cultures because all early hPSC-CMs express it; confirm with NR2F2, KCNA5, NPPA or electrophysiology.
unverified: Day labels for the CHIR99021 (0-2) and IWP2 (2-4) steps are inferred from the stated consecutive 48 h treatments; the Methods as read gave durations, not day numbers.
Medium-change frequency and the exact replating day before lactate selection were not captured.
Whether the day-8 B-27 is the insulin-containing formulation is not stated explicitly in the text read.

protocols.efficiency: About 50% NKX2-5-GFP+ cells with retinoic acid versus about 65% in the untreated control
protocols.start_requirements: NKX2-5-eGFP reporter hESCs maintained on irradiated mouse embryonic fibroblasts; harvested and aggregated as spin EBs on day 0.
tips: The no-retinoic-acid arm of the same protocol gives ventricular-like cells for comparison.

pitfalls: Retinoic acid lowers the fraction of NKX2-5+ cells, so total cardiomyocyte yield is below that of the control arm.

protocols.name: Keller/Protze-lab EB protocol: atrial mesoderm plus retinoic acid on days 3-5
protocols.principle: Atrial cardiomyocytes arise from a different mesoderm than ventricular ones: mesoderm is induced with lower BMP4 and Activin A than for the ventricular fate, then retinoic acid is given together with the Wnt inhibitor on days 3-5.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs at about 80% confluence, dissociated to single cells with TrypLE. EBs are kept in suspension on poly-HEMA-coated dishes under 5% O2 until day 11, then ambient oxygen.
tips: The concept and original protocol are from Lee JH et al. 2017 Cell Stem Cell (PMID 28777944, doi 10.1016/j.stem.2017.07.003): atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes derive from distinct mesoderm populations distinguishable by RALDH2 and CD235a.
The matched ventricular arm uses 10 ng/ml BMP4 and 8 ng/ml Activin A on days 1-3 and no retinoic acid.
BMP4 and Activin A doses for mesoderm induction are line-dependent in this system and are normally titrated per line.
pitfalls: Needs a hypoxia incubator and an orbital shaker; more hands-on than monolayer methods.
Giving retinoic acid to the wrong (ventricular-type) mesoderm does not produce good atrial cells; the mesoderm induction doses matter as much as the retinoic acid.
unverified: Concentrations and timings are the current version of the protocol as written in Lim et al. 2024 (same laboratory), who state it follows their earlier protocols 'with modifications'; the Methods of Lee et al. 2017 itself could not be accessed, so differences from the original are not documented here.
No efficiency figure for the atrial arm was captured.

protocols.principle: A confluent hPSC monolayer is taken through three proprietary differentiation media (A, B, C) over 8 days and then held in a maintenance medium, giving beating cTnT+ atrial cardiomyocytes ready to harvest on day 15.
protocols.efficiency: Greater than 80% cTnT+ cells; on average 1 x 10^6 cells harvested per well of a 12-well plate

tips: The 3.5 - 8 x 10^5 cells/well range exists because lines proliferate at different rates; titrate it for each line
Complete Medium A, B or C keeps 2 weeks at 2-8°C and complete Maintenance Medium 4 weeks; warm to room temperature before use
Aliquot thawed supplements and store at -20°C; do not refreeze thawed aliquots
Volumes given are for one well of a 12-well plate

Feeding Maintenance Medium before day 8 of differentiation

cell_types.name: Cardiac organoids / cardioids
cell_types.summary: Self-organising 3D heart-like structures containing cardiomyocytes together with epicardial, endocardial/endothelial and stromal cells, often with internal chambers or cavities. They are used to study early human heart development, congenital heart defects, maternal-diabetes and drug effects, and injury responses.
cell_types.maturation_note: Beating from about day 6-7; chambers and multi-lineage organisation by day 10-15; cultures have been kept beating for at least 8 weeks.

morphology.endpoint: A single beating spheroid per well, with darker dense myocardium and paler cavities or an outer translucent layer; Matrigel-embedded versions show concentric layers.

protocols.name: Self-assembling heart organoids: three-step Wnt modulation in 96-well plates
protocols.principle: Single hPSC aggregates in U-bottom wells receive a Wnt on/off sequence (CHIR99021 with low BMP4 and Activin A, then Wnt-C59) to form chambered myocardium, followed by a short second CHIR99021 pulse on day 7 that induces epicardial tissue on the outside.
protocols.efficiency: Beating organoids from day 6 and robust, regular beating in all organoids by day 10
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in Essential 8 Flex. Day -2: seed 10,000 cells per well of a round-bottom ultra-low-attachment 96-well plate in 100 µl E8 Flex + 2 µM thiazovivin, spin 100 g for 3 min. Day -1: remove 50 µl and add 200 µl fresh E8 Flex.
tips: One organoid per well makes the method compatible with plate-based imaging and screening.
Never aspirate completely; all changes are partial (166 µl of 250 µl) to avoid losing or damaging the organoid.
The same authors published step-by-step versions (J Vis Exp 2021, PMID 34605811; Curr Protoc 2022, PMID 35723517).
pitfalls: CHIR99021 dose is line-dependent; because changes are partial, calculate the final in-well concentration.
Organoids contain several cardiac lineages (myocardial, epicardial, endocardial/endothelial, fibroblast), so whole-organoid readouts are not cardiomyocyte-specific.
unverified: No cell-type composition percentages were captured.

protocols.name: Heart-forming organoids: Matrigel-embedded aggregates with CHIR99021 then IWP2
protocols.principle: A single hPSC aggregate is embedded in a Matrigel droplet and taken through a standard Wnt on/off cardiac differentiation; the matrix lets it pattern into layers with myocardium, endocardial-like cells, septum-transversum-like tissue, foregut endoderm and a vascular network.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in E8 on Geltrex. Day -4: seed 5,000 cells per well of a U-bottom ultra-low-attachment 96-well plate in E8 + 10 µM Y-27632, spin 300 g for 3 min at 4 °C. Day -2: embed each aggregate in a Matrigel droplet, let it set for 1 h, add E8.
tips: An NKX2-5-eGFP reporter line makes the myocardial layer easy to follow.
The authors listed the Matrigel lots that worked, a sign that lot testing is needed.
pitfalls: Only 5,000 cells per aggregate formed organoids; 500, 3,500 and 10,000 failed.
These organoids deliberately contain foregut endoderm (SOX17/SOX2/HNF4A regions) as well as cardiac tissue; they are a model of early heart-foregut development, not a pure cardiac tissue.
unverified: Feeding interval between day 7 and day 10 was not captured.

Spontaneous beating by day 12 (Lian 2013); from about day 7 in CDM3 (Burridge 2014)
TNNT2+ >= 80% by flow at day 15
>95% TNNT2+ after lactate selection (Burridge 2014)

protocols.name: GiWi: Wnt on, then Wnt off (small molecules, RPMI/B27)
protocols.principle: A 24 h pulse of the GSK3 inhibitor CHIR99021 pushes a confluent hPSC monolayer into mesendoderm; blocking Wnt secretion with IWP2 two days later steers that mesoderm to a cardiac fate. No growth factors are needed.
protocols.efficiency: 80-98% cTnT+ cells after two weeks across the six hESC/iPSC lines tested
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs kept in mTeSR1 on hPSC-qualified Matrigel or Synthemax, passaged without enzymes (Versene). At day -4, singularise with Accutase and plate 0.5-1.5 million cells per well of a 12-well plate in mTeSR1 + 5 µM Y-27632; feed mTeSR1 daily on days -3 to -1 so the well is fully confluent on day 0.
tips: Titrate seeding density first (0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5 million per 12-well) and keep the best one for that line.
The CHIR99021 optimum is line-dependent; the authors found 12 µM best for their six lines but recommend testing 6-14 µM.
Insulin is withheld until day 7 because it lowers yield during the early stages.
Cells can be kept beating in RPMI/B27 for months; metabolic (lactate) selection, as in Burridge 2014 or Tohyama 2013 (PMID 23168164), is commonly added afterwards to raise purity.
pitfalls: Sheet death or lifting after the CHIR pulse: density wrong, CHIR dose too high or left on too long.
No beating by day 12 / low cTnT at day 15: suboptimal density, or IWP2 dose or timing off; check brachyury at 24 h and NKX2-5 at day 5.
Timing matters: the 24 h CHIR and 72 h IWP2 time points should be kept to within an hour or two.

source.authors: Lian X, Zhang J, Azarin SM, et al.
source.title: Directed cardiomyocyte differentiation from human pluripotent stem cells by modulating Wnt/β-catenin signaling under fully defined conditions.

stages.name: Mesendoderm induction (Wnt on)
stages.feeding: Single dose, removed after exactly 24 h
actions: Start only when the monolayer is fully confluent
Add 2 ml per 12-well of RPMI/B27-minus-insulin with CHIR99021 and write down the time
Change medium exactly 24 h later
stages.checkpoint: At 24 h at least 90% of cells should be brachyury (TBXT) positive by flow.

stages.name: Rest in basal medium
stages.feeding: One change on day 1, then leave for 48 h
actions: Replace with 2 ml fresh RPMI/B27-minus-insulin on day 1
Do not disturb until day 3

stages.name: Cardiac specification (Wnt off)
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 + B-27 minus insulin (half conditioned, half fresh)
stages.feeding: Single dose at 72 h for 48 h
actions: At 72 h take 1 ml of the old medium from the well and mix with 1 ml fresh medium ('combined medium')
Add IWP2 to the combined medium, rock the plate to lift debris, aspirate the rest and add the 2 ml back
stages.checkpoint: NKX2-5 and ISL1 transcripts appear from day 4, protein from day 5.

stages.name: Progenitor expansion
stages.feeding: One change on day 5
actions: Replace with 2 ml RPMI/B27-minus-insulin

stages.name: Cardiomyocyte maintenance
stages.feeding: Change every 3 days
actions: Switch to complete B-27 on day 7
Feed every 3 days; score beating areas
Quantify cTnT by flow at day 15
stages.checkpoint: cTnT detectable at day 8; first beating around day 8-10 and robust contraction by day 12.

protocols.name: CDM3: chemically defined three-component medium
protocols.principle: Same Wnt on/off logic as GiWi, but B-27 is replaced by a medium of only RPMI 1640, recombinant human albumin and ascorbic acid 2-phosphate, with Wnt-C59 as the Wnt inhibitor. Glucose-free lactate medium then enriches the cardiomyocytes.
protocols.efficiency: 80-95% TNNT2+ by flow at day 15 across the hESC/hiPSC lines tested; >95% after lactate selection
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs adapted to E8 with EDTA passaging for at least 5 passages, on Synthemax II-SC, Matrigel (1:200) or, for long-term adhesion, laminin-521 / laminin-511 E8 fragment. Split 1:10-1:12 with 0.5 mM EDTA (2 µM thiazovivin for the first 24 h) and grow 4 days to about 85% confluence.
materials: Synthemax II-SC, Matrigel or laminin-521 / iMatrix-511
tips: Laminin-based matrices kept the beating sheets attached long term; on vitronectin peptide the sheets tended to peel off around day 15.
Yield reported as more than 3 x 10^5 cardiomyocytes per cm2.
B-27 contains galactose, so lactate selection has to be done in a B-27-free medium such as this one.
At day 15-20 action potentials look immature; ventricular-like cells predominate by day 30-35.
pitfalls: Ascorbic acid 2-phosphate is essential: without it the cells die.
Leaving out albumin does not kill the culture but sharply reduces yield.
The state of the starting hPSC culture drives efficiency; the authors required E8/EDTA adaptation before differentiating.

source.authors: Burridge PW, Matsa E, Shukla P, et al.
source.title: Chemically defined generation of human cardiomyocytes.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction (Wnt on)
stages.base_medium: CDM3 (RPMI 1640 + 500 µg/ml recombinant human albumin + 213 µg/ml L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate)
stages.feeding: Single 48 h exposure
actions: Switch from E8 to CDM3 + CHIR99021 at ~85% confluence
stages.checkpoint: POU5F1 falls and T/MIXL1 rise by day 2 (qPCR).

stages.name: Cardiac specification (Wnt off)
stages.feeding: Single 48 h exposure
actions: Replace medium with CDM3 + Wnt-C59 on day 2

stages.name: Cardiomyocyte differentiation
stages.feeding: Change every 48 h
actions: Change to plain CDM3 on day 4 and every other day
stages.checkpoint: Contracting cells from about day 7.

stages.name: Optional metabolic purification
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 without glucose + 500 µg/ml recombinant human albumin + 213 µg/ml L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate

factors.name: Sodium DL-lactate
factors.role: Sole carbon source; non-cardiomyocytes die without glucose

stages.feeding: Change every 48 h (same schedule as CDM3)
actions: Replace CDM3 with the glucose-free lactate medium from day 10
Return to CDM3 after selection
stages.checkpoint: Purity rises from about 85% to >95% TNNT2+ after 6-10 days without glucose.

protocols.name: STEMdiff Ventricular Cardiomyocyte Kit (monolayer, 15 days)
protocols.principle: A confluent hPSC monolayer is taken through three proprietary differentiation media (A, B, C) over 8 days and then held in a maintenance medium, giving beating cTnT+ ventricular cardiomyocytes ready to harvest on day 15.
protocols.efficiency: Greater than 80% cTnT+ cells; on average 1 x 10^6 cells harvested per well of a 12-well plate
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs kept as clump cultures in mTeSR1 (Catalog #85850), mTeSR Plus (Catalog #100-0276), TeSR-AOF (Catalog #100-0401) or TeSR-E8 (Catalog #05990) on Corning Matrigel (6-well plates), with high OCT4 and TRA-1-60 expression. Dissociate to single cells with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (8-10 min, 37°C) and seed on day -2 at 3.5 - 8 x 10^5 cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 12-well plate in 1 mL TeSR medium + 10 µM Y-27632; Y-27632 is removed on day -1. Wells must be > 95% confluent after 48 h before day 0.
materials: STEMdiff Cardiomyocyte Maintenance Kit (Catalog #05020) for extra maintenance medium
mTeSR1 (Catalog #85850), mTeSR Plus (Catalog #100-0276), TeSR-AOF (Catalog #100-0401) or TeSR-E8 (Catalog #05990)
tips: The 3.5 - 8 x 10^5 cells/well range exists because lines proliferate at different rates; titrate it for each line
Complete Medium A, B or C keeps 2 weeks at 2-8°C and complete Maintenance Medium 4 weeks; warm to room temperature before use
Aliquot thawed supplements and store at -20°C; do not refreeze thawed aliquots
Volumes given are for one well of a 12-well plate
pitfalls: Starting below 95% confluency: the sheet says not to extend the incubation but to reseed at a higher density
Feeding Maintenance Medium before day 8 of differentiation
Aspirating instead of gently pipetting medium off during days 2-14
unverified: Composition of Supplements A, B, C and the maintenance supplement is proprietary (no concentrations given)
The protocol diagram (Figure 1) is an image and was not available in the text; the schedule above is from the written steps and Table 1
The sheet does not give a cTnT+ percentage separately for a specific day; the > 80% figure is stated in the product description

stages.base_medium: mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus, TeSR-AOF or TeSR-E8 (the medium used for maintenance)

Leave undisturbed 24 h, change to medium without Y-27632, leave another 24 h
stages.checkpoint: > 95% confluent 48 h after seeding; if not, do not wait longer, reseed at a higher density
