protocols.name: Gibco PSC Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Kit (three ready-to-use media)
protocols.principle: Three complete, xeno-free media are applied one after another to a sub-confluent Essential 8 monolayer: Differentiation Medium A for two days, Differentiation Medium B for two days, then Cardiomyocyte Maintenance Medium. No factors are added by the user; the confluence at the switch to Medium A is the main variable to tune.
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs in Essential 8 Medium on Geltrex LDEV-free hESC-qualified matrix (recombinant vitronectin for a xeno-free set-up), 70-85% confluent on the day of splitting. Dissociate to single cells with TrypLE and seed a Geltrex-coated 12-well plate at 2 × 10^4 to 1.6 × 10^5 cells per well in Essential 8 with 1X RevitaCell Supplement, aiming for 30-70% confluence (target 35-60%) four days later. RevitaCell is only needed for the first night.
materials: PSC Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Kit (Differentiation Medium A 100 mL, Differentiation Medium B 100 mL, Maintenance Medium 500 mL)
Geltrex LDEV-Free hESC-Qualified Reduced Growth Factor Basement Membrane Matrix (A1413302) or recombinant vitronectin (A14700)
tips: Schedule from Thermo user guide MAN0014534 Rev. B.0; days are counted from PSC seeding (day 0), so the kit media start on day 4.
Confluence at the moment Medium A goes on drives efficiency; the guide asks for a range-finding seeding experiment for every new line.
The product page describes beating cells in as few as 8 days and cultures maintainable for more than 15 days in Maintenance Medium; the Maintenance Medium is also sold separately (A2920801).
The vendor recommends the 12-well format; store all three media at 2-8°C protected from light and do not freeze them.
pitfalls: Too low or too high confluence on day 4 (outside 30-70%) lowers yield; do not start Medium A just because it is day 4.
Cell-cell junctions tighten with time, so dissociating later than about day 14 costs viability.
The cryopreservation procedure in the guide is described by the vendor as not fully optimised.
unverified: No numeric purity (% TNNT2+) is given on the product page or in the user guide, so efficiency is left null.
The catalogue number of the TrypLE reagent is not printed in the user guide text.

stages.name: Seed and expand hPSCs
stages.feeding: 1 mL per well of a 12-well plate; full change daily on days 1, 2 and 3
actions: Coat a 12-well plate with Geltrex and bring it to room temperature
Rinse the hPSCs with DPBS (no Ca/Mg), detach with TrypLE for about 5-7 min at 37°C and pipette to single cells
Spin 200 × g for 4 min, resuspend in Essential 8 + 1X RevitaCell and count
Seed 2 × 10^4 to 1.6 × 10^5 cells per well; for a new line run a density series
Day 1: change to plain Essential 8; repeat on days 2 and 3
stages.checkpoint: About 5-15% confluent on day 1; 30-70% confluent (ideally 35-60%) on day 4 before adding Medium A

stages.name: Differentiation Medium A
stages.base_medium: Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Medium A (ready to use)
stages.feeding: Single change on day 4, 1 mL per 12-well; left for 2 days
actions: Aspirate Essential 8 and add pre-warmed Medium A
Return to 37°C, 5% CO2
stages.checkpoint: By day 6 the layer starts to look opaque; some dead cells floating is normal

stages.name: Differentiation Medium B
stages.base_medium: Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Medium B (ready to use)
stages.feeding: Single change on day 6, 1 mL per 12-well; left for 2 days
actions: Aspirate Medium A and add pre-warmed Medium B
stages.checkpoint: Culture becomes progressively more opaque by day 8; some cell shedding is normal

stages.name: Cardiomyocyte Maintenance Medium
stages.feeding: 1 mL per 12-well on day 8, then every other day (days 10 and 12 and onward)
actions: Switch to Maintenance Medium on day 8 and refeed every second day
Characterise on day 14 (the manual suggests NKX2-5 and TNNT2 immunostaining)

To replate, dissociate between 10 and 14 days after the start of differentiation with TrypLE Express (10-15 min) and reseed on Geltrex at 2 × 10^5 to 1 × 10^6 viable cells/cm² in Maintenance Medium + 1X RevitaCell
stages.checkpoint: Contractions can appear from about day 10; a contracting TNNT2-positive syncytium is expected on day 14

protocols.name: StemMACS CardioDiff Kit XF (8-day xeno-free monolayer)
protocols.principle: One basal medium is combined with three supplements to make three phenol-red-free media that are applied in a fixed daily sequence (mesoderm induction, cultivation, cardiac induction, cultivation) to a single-cell-seeded monolayer on Matrigel, giving cardiomyocytes in 8 days.
protocols.start_requirements: High-quality hPSCs at 75-85% confluence (pluripotency checked by morphology and marker staining). Dissociate to single cells with 0.05% trypsin/EDTA (5 min, stopped with soybean trypsin inhibitor), viability >95%, and seed directly into Mesoderm Induction Medium on Matrigel hESC-qualified-coated 12-well plates, 2 mL per well. For a new clone titrate 125,000, 250,000, 300,000 and 400,000 cells/cm². The data sheet does not call for a ROCK inhibitor.
materials: StemMACS CardioDiff Kit XF, human (2 × 500 mL Basal Medium XF; Mesoderm Induction Supplement 20X, 5 mL; Cardiac Cultivation Supplement 50X, 2 × 10 mL; Cardiac Induction Supplement 20X, 5 mL)
DMEM/F12 with L-glutamine, without HEPES (for Matrigel dilution)
Optional: Multi Tissue Dissociation Kit 3 (130-110-204); StemMACS Cardiac Cultivation Medium XF (130-125-287) for culture beyond day 10
tips: Schedule from the Miltenyi data sheet for order no. 130-125-289 (document 140-005-689.05).
One kit is sized for 48 wells of a 12-well plate; complete media keep up to 4 weeks at 2-8°C.
Thaw supplements overnight at 2-8°C and shake well; dissolve any white precipitate by pipetting.
The vendor states the protocol can be scaled up and that cells can be kept for 30 days or more in the cultivation medium.
pitfalls: Starting cell number is line-dependent; skipping the density titration for a new clone is the commonest cause of poor yield.
Do not mix components between kits or lots.
Dense beating sheets can detach in long cultures.
unverified: No numeric cardiomyocyte purity is stated on the product page or data sheet; efficiency left null.
The data sheet lists 0.05% trypsin/EDTA under reagents but writes 0.5% in the day-10 harvest step; confirm the concentration before harvesting.

protocols.name: hPSC Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Kit (PSCCDK)
protocols.principle: Three sequential serum-free differentiation media apply a growth-factor induction followed by temporal modulation of canonical Wnt signalling (on, then off) to a monolayer hPSC culture, then hand over to a cardiomyocyte growth medium; no embryoid body step is needed and contractions appear from day 7-10.
protocols.efficiency: Vendor claims high efficiency and a confluent sheet of cardiomyocytes from H9 cells; no percentage is stated
protocols.start_requirements: Matrigel hESC-qualified matrix-coated plates (BD 354277), warmed to room temperature before use. hPSCs are maintained feeder-free, ideally in ScienCell STEMium medium (5801) though mTeSR1 or MEF conditioned medium are said to work equally well, and passaged at 80-90% confluency with StemDS dissociation solution (5803). For differentiation the cells are seeded onto Matrigel-coated 12-well plates in maintenance medium containing 5 uM Y-27632. The manual tells first-time users to titrate the seeding density across 0.05-1.5 x 10^6 cells per 12-well; for H9 in STEMium it recommends 0.8-1.0 x 10^5 cells per well in 2 mL (or 4 x 10^5 cells in 5 mL for a T-25). One kit covers two 12-well plates.
materials: hPSC Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Kit (ScienCell 5901: media A, B, C, Cardiomyocyte Growth Medium and its supplement)
StemDS cell dissociation solution (ScienCell 5803) and DPBS without calcium and magnesium (ScienCell 0303)
STEMium hPSC growth medium (ScienCell 5801) or another feeder-free maintenance medium
Optional Cardiomyocyte Selective Medium (ScienCell 5911) for enrichment after passaging
tips: Record the time Medium A goes on; the whole schedule is timed from it and Medium A must come off at 24 h
Titrate the seeding density on the first run - the manual expects it and gives an eight-point range
Cardiomyocytes can be passaged and further enriched in Cardiomyocyte Selective Medium (5911)

No contractions or poor efficiency traces back to seeding density, starting cell quality, or a mis-timed Medium A window
The kit was developed on H9 hESCs in STEMium; other lines may need re-optimisation
unverified: No stated cTnT or alpha-actinin positive percentage
The product page lists the kit as 50 mL while the manual describes five bottles totalling more than that; confirm the configuration with the vendor when ordering

cell_types.notes: Efficiency depends strongly on the hPSC line, seeding density and CHIR99021 dose (12 µM for 24 h in RPMI/B27 versus 6 µM for 48 h in CDM3), so titrate both for each line. The product is an immature, mixed population (mostly ventricular-like with some atrial- and nodal-like cells); use the dedicated atrial or pacemaker protocols when subtype matters.

cell_types.name: Pericytes / mural cells
cell_types.summary: Mural cells wrapped around capillaries that stabilise the endothelium and regulate barrier function and blood flow. hPSC-derived pericyte-like cells are mainly used in blood-brain barrier and neurovascular models, vascular co-cultures and vascularised organoids.
cell_types.maturation_note: Marker-positive cells within 10 days by the mesoderm route and 22-25 days by the neural crest route; function is tested in endothelial co-culture.

morphology.endpoint: Flat, irregular stellate-to-spindle cells with long processes, growing as a loose monolayer; in co-culture they line up along endothelial cords.

stages.label: hPSCs
stages.look: Single-cell-plated hPSCs.

stages.label: Neural crest or mesoderm intermediate
stages.look: Small, migratory cells at high density; passaged repeatedly in the neural crest route.

stages.label: Sorted progenitors
stages.look: Sparse bipolar or stellate cells after replating.

stages.label: Pericyte-like cells
stages.look: Larger, flattened spindle and stellate cells with fine processes.

protocols.name: Brain pericyte-like cells via neural crest (E6-CSFD, then E6 + 10% FBS)
protocols.principle: Forebrain pericytes come from neural crest, so hPSCs are first converted to p75-NGFR+ HNK-1+ neural crest by Wnt activation with TGF-beta and BMP inhibition, sorted, and then pushed to NG2+ PDGFRB+ mural cells with serum.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in E8 on Matrigel at about 70% confluence. Day -1: singularise with Accutase and seed 8.75 x 10^5 cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 6-well plate in E8 + 10 µM Y-27632.
materials: Neural Crest Stem Cell MicroBeads (anti-p75-NGFR) and MACS columns
tips: Original report: Stebbins MJ et al. 2019 Sci Adv (PMID 30891496, doi 10.1126/sciadv.aau7375).

Sorted neural crest can be expanded or frozen and differentiated later.

protocols.name: GiWi cardiac progenitors, then a second CHIR99021 pulse (defined, xeno-free)
protocols.principle: Cardiac progenitors made by Wnt activation then inhibition are replated at low density on day 6 and given CHIR99021 again for two days; reactivating Wnt at this stage turns NKX2-5+/ISL1+ progenitors into WT1+ epicardial cells instead of cardiomyocytes. TGF-beta inhibition then allows long-term expansion.
protocols.efficiency: >90% WT1+ cells at day 12
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs (>95% OCT4+) in mTeSR1 or E8 on Matrigel or Synthemax. At day -3 plate 0.5-2.0 million singularised cells per well of a 12-well plate with ROCK inhibitor and feed daily. For E8-grown cells, pre-condition with 0.1-0.6 µM CHIR99021 on day -1.
tips: Day 5 or day 7 progenitors also work if CHIR99021 is given for the following 2 days.

For expansion, passage confluent cells 1:3 to 1:9 and keep them in LaSR basal or RPMI/Vc/Ins with 0.5 µM A83-01 or 2 µM SB431542; without a TGF-beta inhibitor they undergo EMT into smooth-muscle-like cells within 2-3 passages.
Use Accutase for the day-12 passage; Versene worked better for the authors after about 8 passages.
The same paper gives short add-on steps to turn the epicardial cells into fibroblasts and smooth muscle cells.

unverified: Exact composition of the 'RPMI basal medium' used on days 0-6 (the albumin-free GiWi2 variant) was not captured from the text read; the original GiWi version uses RPMI/B27 minus insulin.

For the diabetic vasculopathy model the authors exposed organoids to high glucose plus inflammatory cytokines and scored collagen IV basement-membrane thickening.
Organoids transplanted under the mouse kidney capsule became perfused and formed arteries, arterioles and venules.
pitfalls: Matrigel and collagen lots vary and the gel must be kept cold and mixed quickly; sprouting quality depends on it.
The first description starts from a bulk suspension of aggregates in a 6-well plate, so aggregate size is not tightly controlled.

protocols.name: GiFGF: CHIR99021 then high-dose bFGF (second heart field route)
protocols.principle: After a one-day CHIR99021 pulse, cardiac mesoderm is switched on day 2 into a defined fibroblast medium with 75 ng/ml bFGF instead of a Wnt inhibitor; FGF signalling drives the progenitors through a second-heart-field-like state to cardiac fibroblasts and prevents cardiomyocyte formation.
protocols.efficiency: 80-90% of cells positive for the fibroblast antigen TE-7 at early passage, rising to about 99% with further passaging
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated with Versene and seeded on Matrigel-coated 6-well plates at 1.5-2.0 x 10^6 cells per well in mTeSR1 + 10 µM Y-27632; fed daily for 5-6 days until 100% confluent.
tips: From day 20, passage with 0.05% trypsin-EDTA into uncoated plastic 6-well plates at 300,000 cells per well in FibroGRO + 2% FBS; feed every other day and split every 4-6 days (5,800 cells/cm2).
Starting bFGF on day 2 was the best window; day 3 or 4 with high bFGF caused extensive cell death after day 6.
pitfalls: Cells activate into alpha-SMA-high myofibroblasts in serum-rich medium (DMEM + 10% FBS) or with TGFB1; keep them in the fibroblast medium for a quiescent phenotype.
TE-7 positivity declines again as the cells approach senescence at high passage.
unverified: CFBM composition is in a supplementary table that was not read; obtain it from the paper before starting.

protocols.name: Epicardial route: cardiac progenitors, epicardial cells, then FGF2 + SB431542
protocols.principle: Cardiac progenitors (CHIR99021 then IWR-1) are replated and converted to epicardial cells with CHIR99021 and retinoic acid, then differentiated into quiescent cardiac fibroblasts in fibroblast growth medium with FGF2 while TGF-beta signalling is blocked to prevent myofibroblast activation.
protocols.efficiency: >90% of cells positive for COL1, DDR2 and TCF21 by flow at day 18 (original Circ Res report)
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs in E8 on Matrigel-coated 6-well plates, 80-90% confluent on day 0.
tips: First described in Zhang H et al. 2019 Circ Res (PMID 31288631, doi 10.1161/CIRCRESAHA.119.315491); the step-by-step values here are from the same group's protocol chapter.
The first 6 days are the same as for cardiomyocytes; replating density on day 6 decides between epicardial cells (sparse) and beating cardiomyocytes (left in place).
With SB431542 in the medium most cells stay quiescent (about 5% alpha-SMA+) up to passage 5; remove the inhibitor at least a day before TGF-beta activation experiments.
pitfalls: Massive death or detachment by day 2 means the CHIR99021 dose or duration needs titrating for that line.
Without the TGF-beta inhibitor the fibroblasts spontaneously become myofibroblasts in culture.
unverified: The Circ Res paper's own Methods are in an online supplement that was not read; small differences from the chapter (the paper describes six days in fibroblast medium to day 18) are possible.

morphology.endpoint: Small, fast and regularly beating clusters or EBs; cells are smaller and less striated than working cardiomyocytes, but identity needs markers or electrophysiology.

protocols.name: Protze-lab EB protocol: BMP4 + retinoic acid with TGF-beta and FGF inhibition
protocols.principle: Low-dose mesoderm induction followed, at the cardiac mesoderm stage, by BMP4 and retinoic acid while Activin/TGF-beta and FGF signalling are blocked; this yields NKX2-5-negative sinoatrial-node-like pacemaker cardiomyocytes instead of working myocardium.
protocols.efficiency: Mixed cultures of NKX2-5-negative pacemaker-like and NKX2-5+ cardiomyocytes; CD34 marks the pacemaker fraction (about 54% of NKX2-5-negative cardiomyocytes were CD34+ at day 25) and CD34 sorting enriches them
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs at about 80% confluence, dissociated to single cells with TrypLE. EBs in suspension on poly-HEMA-coated dishes at 5% O2 until day 11, then ambient oxygen.
tips: Original protocol: Protze SI et al. 2017 Nat Biotechnol (PMID 27941801, doi 10.1038/nbt.3745).
An NKX2-5 reporter line makes it easy to follow the NKX2-5-negative pacemaker fraction; without one, sort SIRPA+ CD90- CD34+ cells.
PD173074 dose and day of addition are line-specific in the authors' hands.
pitfalls: Unsorted cultures still contain NKX2-5+ atrial-like cardiomyocytes and non-myocytes; do not treat them as pure pacemaker cells.
Mesoderm induction doses (BMP4/Activin A) normally need titration for each line in this EB system.
unverified: Values are those written in Lim et al. 2024 (same laboratory, 'previously reported protocols with modifications'); the Methods of Protze et al. 2017 could not be accessed, so the original 2017 concentrations are not confirmed here.
Overall percentage of pacemaker-like cells per culture was not captured as a single figure.

protocols.efficiency: 60-90% TNNT2+ cells at day 19 (same range for the pacemaker and ventricular arms)
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs in mTeSR1 on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel; seed at 2.5-3 x 10^4 cells/cm2 and start when 80-90% confluent.
tips: Ventricular control: BPEL + 5 µM XAV939 from day 3 for 96 h, then BPEL.
Readouts used: SHOX2, TBX3, ISL1, HCN4 up and NKX2-5, MYL2 down versus the ventricular arm.
pitfalls: Leaving out the Wnt inhibitor during days 4-6 collapses the cardiomyocyte fraction (about 10% TNNT2+) and gives proepicardial-like (WT1+, PDPN+) cells instead.
The culture is a mix of sinoatrial head, tail and transition-zone-like cells plus a proepicardial side population (about 10% PDPN+).

cell_types.name: Haematopoietic progenitors
cell_types.summary: Early blood progenitors (primitive erythroid, then definitive erythroid, myeloid and multilineage colony-forming cells) made from mouse ES or iPS cells through a Flk-1+ haemangioblast and haemogenic endothelium stage. They are used to model yolk-sac and early embryonic haematopoiesis and to test gene function in blood specification with knockout or reporter lines.

protocols.name: Serum embryoid bodies with methylcellulose replating (Keller/Choi method)
protocols.principle: ES cells seeded at low density in IMDM with a pre-screened serum lot form embryoid bodies that pass through Flk-1+ haemangioblast, primitive erythroid and then definitive progenitor stages on a fixed timetable, without added cytokines for the first days. Progenitors are counted by dissociating EBs on the right day and replating in methylcellulose with stage-specific cytokines.
protocols.efficiency: A good differentiation serum lot gives about 30-50% FLK1+ cells in day 3-4 EBs; in the original Keller 1993 study more than 85% of EBs contained erythroid precursors by day 6
protocols.start_requirements: ES cells at least one passage (protocol recommends third passage or more) after thawing. Two days before differentiation, seed 4 × 10⁵ ES cells into a gelatinised 25-cm² flask without feeders in ES-IMDM (IMDM, 15% pre-selected FCS, 2% LIF-conditioned medium, 1% non-essential amino acids, 1% L-glutamine, 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ M MTG); change medium the next day. Use bacterial-grade Petri dishes, not tissue-culture dishes, for EBs.
materials: IL-1, IL-6, IL-11, G-CSF, GM-CSF, M-CSF
tips: Replate 3-6 × 10⁴ EB cells per ml of methylcellulose mix in 35-mm bacterial dishes and count colonies 4-7 days later.
Blast colony mix (day 2.75-3 EBs): 10% FCS, 20% D4T conditioned medium, VEGF 5 ng/ml, Kit ligand 1%, plus ascorbic acid 12.5 µg/ml, 2 mM L-glutamine, transferrin 200 µg/ml, 4.5 × 10⁻⁴ M MTG.
Primitive erythroid mix (day 4 EBs): 10% plasma-derived serum, EPO 2 U/ml, 5% PFHM-II.

Definitive erythroid/myeloid mix (day 6-10 EBs): 10% plasma-derived serum, Kit ligand 1%, EPO 2 U/ml, 5% PFHM-II, IL-1 5 ng/ml, IL-3 1%, IL-6 5 ng/ml, IL-11 5-25 ng/ml, G-CSF 2-30 ng/ml, GM-CSF 3-5 ng/ml, M-CSF 2-5 ng/ml.
A serum-free alternative in the same unit replaces FCS with 15% serum replacement plus 5% PFHM-II and uses 8,000-10,000 cells per ml for day 2.75-3 EBs.
The authors find ES cells maintained on feeders differentiate more consistently than cells kept long-term on gelatin, and they set up differentiations within 5-6 passages of thawing.

Order of appearance in the original Keller 1993 study: primitive erythroid precursors first, macrophage and definitive erythroid about 24 h later, then neutrophil/macrophage and multilineage precursors, mast cell precursors last.
pitfalls: Seeding too many cells makes the dish confluent and differentiation inefficient; the cell numbers per ml are empirical and poorly differentiating lines need more cells.
The serum lot decides success; screen lots by FLK1 flow at day 3-4 or by replating before committing.
Blast colony-forming cells are transient (day 2.75-3); harvesting a few hours late misses them.
Secondary EBs also grow in the blast assay; they are compact with no distinguishable single cells and must not be counted as blast colonies.
unverified: The full text of the original report (Keller 1993, Mol Cell Biol 13:473-486, PMID 8417345) is a scanned article and could not be read; only its abstract was used (day-4 and day-6 erythroid precursor figures, order of precursor appearance). The practical numbers here are from Ma 2008, which follows that method.
Volume of ES-IMDM per 25-cm² flask is blank in the source manuscript.

protocols.name: BAFV: serum-free EBs with BMP4, then activin A + bFGF + VEGF
protocols.principle: Four factors given in sequence in serum-free medium are enough: BMP4 makes mesoderm very efficiently, activin A plus bFGF turn that mesoderm into haemangioblasts, and VEGF is needed for committed haematopoietic progenitors.
protocols.efficiency: Reported as a very high frequency of haematopoietic precursors, with most cells in BAFV-treated EBs being CD41+ by day 6 (no single percentage given); Brachyury-GFP+ cells approach 100% by day 3.75 with BMP4
protocols.start_requirements: ES cells (Brachyury-GFP reporter line in the paper; other lines also tested) maintained on irradiated feeders in DMEM + 15% FCS + LIF + 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ M MTG, then passaged twice on gelatin to remove feeders (the second passage in IMDM-based ES medium) before starting. Seed 25,000 cells/ml in 60-mm Petri-grade dishes.
materials: Methylcellulose, D4T conditioned medium, IL-6, plasma-derived serum, PFHM-II and cytokines for colony assays
tips: Blast colony assay used in the paper: 2 × 10⁴ EB cells/ml in 1% methylcellulose with 10% FCS, VEGF 5 ng/ml, IL-6 5 ng/ml and 25% D4T conditioned medium.

Progenitor assay used in the paper: 2 × 10⁴ cells/ml in 1% methylcellulose with 10% plasma-derived serum, 5% PFHM-II, Kit ligand, TPO 5 ng/ml, EPO 2 U/ml, IL-11 25 ng/ml, IL-3, GM-CSF 3 ng/ml, G-CSF 30 ng/ml, M-CSF 5 ng/ml and IL-6 5 ng/ml.
StemPro worked better than knockout serum replacement, DMEM/F12 or IMDM/F12 as the serum-free base in the authors' comparison.
Without any added factor the cells in this medium do not make mesoderm, so every step is under your control; this makes the method good for timing experiments.

A Keller-lab serum-free alternative (Irion 2010, Development) forms EBs for 48 h without factors, induces with activin A, BMP4 and VEGF, and sorts Flk-1+ cells at about day 3.25 (yolk-sac-like wave) and, from re-aggregated Flk-1− cells, again at about day 5.25 (a later wave with T-lymphoid potential).
pitfalls: BMP4 alone gives plenty of mesoderm but few haemangioblasts; activin A and bFGF at day 2.5 are required.
Leaving out VEGF gives haemangioblasts but poor output of committed progenitors.
The timing was worked out on a Brachyury-GFP line; check the kinetics on your own line with Flk1 flow before fixing harvest times.

protocols.name: OP9 stromal co-culture (after Nakano 1994)
protocols.principle: ES cells seeded directly onto a confluent layer of OP9 stromal cells, which lack functional M-CSF, differentiate through Flk-1+ mesoderm into haematopoietic progenitors and mature blood cells without embryoid bodies or added cytokines. This version uses fluorescently tagged (or irradiated) OP9 so that all ES-derived cells, adherent and floating, can be recovered and analysed on any day.
protocols.start_requirements: OP9 cells maintained in αMEM + 20% OP9-tested FBS + 2 mM L-glutamine, medium changed every 2 days and split at 70-90% confluency (never beyond 90%). Three days before each seeding day, plate OP9 at 1 × 10⁴ cells/cm² so the layer is confluent. ES cells grown by your standard method, trypsinised to single cells.
tips: Pre-test the serum: it must support OP9 growth and correct ES differentiation up to day 5.
As an alternative to tagged OP9, irradiate OP9 (8000 rads) and seed at confluent density (7.8 × 10⁴ cells/cm²); this removes the need for repeated replating.

The original OP9 report (Nakano, Kodama and Honjo 1994, Science 265:1098-1101, PMID 8066449) obtained erythroid, myeloid and B-lineage cells without EB formation or added growth factors; adding M-CSF suppressed all lineages except macrophages, which is why M-CSF-deficient OP9 is used.

Standard protocols analyse only floating cells after the day-5 replating; collecting adherent ES-derived cells as well, as here, avoids missing progenitors, which matters when characterising knockout lines.
pitfalls: Overgrown OP9 (beyond about 90% confluency during maintenance) turn into fat cells and lose their supportive activity.
OP9 cells carried over at each passage contaminate downstream assays unless they are tagged, irradiated or sorted out.
Poor serum lots give no whorl colonies at day 5 and stunted blood formation later.

cell_types.notes: What you harvest depends entirely on the day: haemangioblasts are present for only a few hours around day 3, primitive erythroid progenitors a day or two later, definitive progenitors after that. These cultures model embryonic (mainly yolk-sac-type) haematopoiesis and give colony-forming progenitors, not transplantable adult-type stem cells.

cell_types.name: Haematopoietic progenitor cells (CD34+)
cell_types.summary: Multipotent blood progenitors that emerge from haemogenic endothelium in PSC cultures and carry erythroid, myeloid, megakaryocytic and (when the definitive programme is specified) T-lymphoid potential. They are the obligatory intermediate for every other blood and immune cell type on this list, and are used to study the embryonic origins of human haematopoiesis and as the input for immune-cell manufacturing.
cell_types.maturation_note: CD43+ cells appear around day 6-9 and accumulate over the following week. These progenitors are not transplantable HSCs: engraftment of hPSC-derived CD34+ definitive progenitors has not been achieved, and Sturgeon et al. describe them as possible pre-HSCs needing further maturation signals.

morphology.endpoint: Small, round, bright non-adherent cells budding off an adherent endothelial-like monolayer or off the surface of embryoid bodies. The adherent layer looks like a cobbled endothelial sheet; the progenitors collect in the supernatant and in loose clusters on top of it.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies or single-cell seeding
stages.look: Compact, flat colonies with sharp edges, or a sparse layer of single cells attached overnight on Collagen IV / Matrigel.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Colonies flatten and spread into a dense sheet of small uniform cells; in embryoid-body protocols the aggregates become compact and phase-bright.

stages.label: Haemogenic endothelium
stages.look: A flat, cobbled, endothelial-looking monolayer with sharp cell-cell borders; little or nothing is floating yet.

stages.label: Endothelial-to-haematopoietic transition
stages.look: Round, refractile cells round up on the endothelial sheet and release into the medium, often in grape-like clusters.

stages.label: Progenitor harvest
stages.look: The supernatant is full of small round bright cells of fairly uniform size; the adherent sheet below keeps shedding them for days.

markers.name: T

markers.name: KDR
markers.note: With CD235a it separates the primitive (KDR+CD235a+) from the definitive (KDR+CD235a-) programme at day 3 in Sturgeon et al.

markers.name: GYPA

markers.name: CDH5

markers.name: NT5E

markers.name: CD34
markers.note: Standard progenitor readout; in Knorr et al. spin embryoid bodies reached 55.9 +/- 6.4% CD34+ at day 11 from hESCs but far less from iPSCs.

markers.name: SPN
markers.note: Earliest pan-haematopoietic marker in hPSC cultures; present on both primitive and definitive progenitors.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: Appears after CD43; Lachmann et al. saw CD34+CD45+ double-positive cells from day 8 of the directed stage.

markers.name: RUNX1

protocols.name: Wnt switch: definitive or primitive progenitors from serum-free embryoid bodies
protocols.principle: During a narrow day 2-3 window, Wnt-beta-catenin activity decides which haematopoietic programme is specified: CHIR99021 pushes the definitive (T-competent) programme and blocks primitive haematopoiesis, while IWP2 does the opposite. Both programmes then pass through a haemogenic endothelial intermediate.
protocols.efficiency: More than 70% of the day-9 population derived from KDR+CD235a- mesoderm was CD43+ in the primitive arm; definitive output is scored as T-cell potential rather than as a percentage
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained on irradiated mouse embryonic fibroblasts, then plated on Matrigel-coated plastic for 24 h. Dissociate with collagenase B (1 mg/mL) then trypsin-EDTA (0.05%) and scrape to give aggregates, not single cells.
tips: The day 2-3 window is the whole protocol; set the timer.
Line-specific endogenous Wnt: the authors rescued a non-permissive iPSC line purely by adding CHIR99021 on days 2-3.
Sort on CD235a at day 3 if you need clean programmes rather than a mixture.
pitfalls: Haemogenic endothelium markers (CD34, CD144, CD45) cannot tell primitive from definitive - only T-cell potential can.
Hypoxia for the first 8 days matters; the published kinetics assume it.
Definitive CD34+ cells did not engraft mice, so do not read 'definitive' as 'HSC'.
unverified: Activin A concentration for the day 2-3 primitive arm (stated in the paper's methods as 'Activin A' without a dose in the text available to this session)

protocols.name: Chemically defined monolayer on Tenascin C (IF9S)
protocols.principle: A fully defined, xeno-free 2D route: single hPSCs are seeded on Collagen IV or Tenascin C and stepped through mesoderm, haemogenic endothelium and CD43+ progenitors in a home-made IMDM/F12 medium (IF9S), with Tenascin C specifically favouring definitive, T-competent output.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs kept in E8 on vitronectin. Dissociate with 1x TrypLE at about 80% confluency and plate single cells at 5,000-15,000 cells/cm2 (line-dependent) on plates coated with 0.5 ug/cm2 Collagen IV or Tenascin C, in E8 plus 10 uM Y-27632. Allow 24 h attachment before day 0.
tips: Seeding density is line-specific and is the main variable to titrate first.
Tenascin C outperformed Collagen IV specifically for T-lymphoid commitment; Collagen IV is fine for myeloid output.
IF9S is made in-house - weigh the polyvinyl alcohol and lipid concentrate carefully, they were added to raise viability.
pitfalls: Starting from clumps rather than single cells changes the kinetics - this protocol was built around single-cell seeding.
Day 0-5 hypoxia then day 6-9 normoxia is part of the method, not a detail.

protocols.principle: Standard spin-embryoid-body CD34+ cells lack HOXA gene expression, indicating mispatterned mesoderm. stages.checkpoint: Day 0: 16 - 40 attached colonies per well (4 - 10 per cm2), counting even tiny colonies; do not proceed outside this range

stages.name: Stage 1: mesoderm induction (Medium A)
stages.base_medium: Medium A (STEMdiff Hematopoietic Basal Medium + Supplement A)
stages.feeding: Day 0 full change to 1 mL; day 2 half change (remove and add 0.5 mL)
actions: Confirm the colony count, then replace TeSR medium with 1 mL Medium A per well
On day 2 gently remove 0.5 mL and add 0.5 mL fresh Medium A

stages.name: Stage 2: hematopoietic differentiation (Medium B)

stages.feeding: Day 3 full change to 1 mL; half changes (0.5 mL) on days 5, 7 and 10

Days 5, 7, 10: keep the plate flat, remove 0.5 mL without disturbing floating cells, add 0.5 mL Medium B

cell_types.notes: Two separate programmes run in these cultures. Primitive progenitors give erythroid, macrophage, megakaryocyte and NK output but no T cells; only the definitive programme gives T-lymphoid potential, and the surface phenotype of the two haemogenic endothelia is identical, so T-cell potential is the discriminator. Endogenous Wnt levels differ between lines: H1 hESCs made definitive progenitors without help, while the MSC-iPS1 iPSC line needed CHIR99021 on days 2-3 to rescue T-cell potential at all. Expect to re-titrate the CHIR/IWP2 dose and the seeding density for every new line.

cell_types.name: Megakaryocytes and platelets
cell_types.summary: Very large polyploid cells that extend proplatelet processes and shed functional platelets. PSC-derived megakaryocytes are used for platelet-biology and thrombosis research, for modelling inherited platelet disorders, and as the basis of a donor-independent, HLA-engineerable platelet transfusion product.
cell_types.maturation_note: Feng et al. see CD41a+CD42b+ megakaryocytes rise from about 20% to over 80% within 4 days of maturation medium, with proplatelets at 3-4 days and platelet output peaking at day 6 of the maturation step. Moreau et al. reach over 95% CD41a+ by day 15 post-transduction and over 50% CD42a+ mature megakaryocytes by day 20, with cultures running for months.

morphology.endpoint: Very large cells, many with lobulated or multiple nuclei, extending long beaded proplatelet processes into the medium; small bright platelet-sized particles accumulate around them.

stages.label: Pluripotent start
stages.look: Compact colonies on collagen IV, or single cells spun into 500-1,000-cell aggregates for forward programming.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Colonies stretch out and loosen into a spreading sheet.

stages.label: Haemogenic endothelium
stages.look: A complex adherent sheet; about 58% of attached cells are CD31+ at this point in Feng et al.

stages.label: Megakaryocyte progenitors
stages.look: Non-adherent round progenitors harvested over 4-5 consecutive days and cryopreserved.

stages.label: Mature megakaryocytes with proplatelets
stages.look: Very large cells with long beaded proplatelet extensions; small platelet-sized particles everywhere in the supernatant.

markers.name: PECAM1

markers.name: GP9

markers.name: GATA1

markers.name: FLI1
markers.note: Second forward-programming factor.

markers.name: TAL1

markers.name: SELP
markers.note: Alpha-granule protein correctly patterned in programmed megakaryocytes; surface exposure marks platelet activation.

markers.name: VWF
markers.note: Alpha-granule cargo; also high in the CD31+ endothelial intermediate.

markers.name: GYPA
markers.note: The sister lineage from the shared bipotential progenitor; Feng's maturation medium almost eliminates CD235a+ cells.

markers.name: CD14
markers.note: Platelet quality was inversely correlated with the percentage of CD14+ myeloid cells in the starting megakaryocyte culture - worth checking before platelet harvest.

protocols.name: Feeder- and serum-free route to megakaryocyte progenitors and platelets
protocols.principle: Six days on collagen IV with BMP4, VEGF and bFGF give CD31+ haemogenic endothelial-like cells; a thrombopoietin-led expansion cocktail in APEL produces cryopreservable megakaryocyte progenitors; and a maturation medium of STEMspan-ACF with megakaryocyte supplement plus heparin, run at 39 C in 7% CO2, drives maturation and platelet release.
protocols.efficiency: CD41a+CD42b+ megakaryocytes rise from about 20% to over 80% in 4 days of maturation medium; more than 70% of purified platelets are CD41a+CD42b+ (human blood platelets 82% in the same assay)
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free iPSCs dissociated with cell dissociation buffer, resuspended in mTeSR1 with 10 uM Y-27632 and seeded on human collagen IV-coated plates (5 ug/cm2); 24 h at 37 C, 5% CO2, 20% O2 before differentiation starts.
materials: an incubator that can hold 39 C and 7% CO2
tips: Cryopreserving the progenitors decouples the differentiation from the platelet experiments.
CD14+ contamination predicts poor platelet quality - gate for it before committing to a harvest.
A beta-2-microglobulin knockout line gives HLA class I-negative 'universal' platelets, which is what the title refers to.
pitfalls: The 39 C / 7% CO2 maturation step needs a dedicated incubator setting.
Platelet purification needs the full centrifugation series with PGE1, or the platelets activate.
Yields differ between lines even with identical media.
unverified: Absolute platelet yield per input iPSC
Exact cytokine concentrations inside the proprietary megakaryocyte expansion supplement

Cryopreserve in CryoStor
Check CD41a, CD42b, CD31, CD34, CD43, CD13, CD235a and CD14 by flow

stages.name: Megakaryocyte maturation and platelet release
stages.base_medium: STEMspan-ACF with STEMspan Megakaryocyte Expansion Supplement

factors.name: TPO, SCF, IL-6, IL-9
factors.conc: as supplied in the megakaryocyte expansion supplement

factors.name: Y-27632

protocols.name: Forward programming with GATA1, FLI1 and TAL1 (chemically defined)
protocols.principle: Rather than recapitulating development, three transcription factors (GATA1, FLI1, TAL1) are expressed concurrently from lentivirus at the moment of embryoid-body aggregation, with a two-day mesoderm induction; a single-cell dissociation at day 10 followed by TPO plus IL-1-beta then gives highly pure megakaryocyte cultures that proliferate for months and shed functional platelets throughout.
protocols.efficiency: Over 95% CD41a+ by day 15 and over 50% CD42a+ by day 20; purity 97.7 +/- 0.8% versus 21.3 +/- 2.9% for conventional directed differentiation; up to 28.4 +/- 7.8-fold more megakaryocytes than input hPSCs at day 20, and up to 2 x 10^5 mature megakaryocytes per input hPSC over months of culture
protocols.start_requirements: Sub-confluent (50-80%) hPSC cultures dissociated to single cells with TrypLE. Transduce at a multiplicity of infection of 20 with 10 ug/mL protamine sulfate.
materials: lentiviral vectors for GATA1, FLI1 and TAL1
tips: Day 10 is the right moment for the single-cell dissociation; the authors tested alternatives and this gave the best yield.
The megakaryocytes cryopreserve well from day 30-70, which makes the system a bankable supply.
Combining forced-aggregation embryoid bodies with mesoderm induction gave about a 5-fold improvement each over the 2D, pluripotency-maintained starting condition.
pitfalls: Three lentiviral integrations, so not suitable where transgene-free cells are required.
Only about 22% of cells end up triple-transduced, but the megakaryocyte programme then selects them out over time.
Ploidy stays neonatal-like, which limits platelet output per cell.

protocols.name: Immortalised megakaryocyte progenitor cell lines (imMKCL)
protocols.principle: PSC-derived haematopoietic progenitors are immortalised into stable megakaryocyte progenitor lines by overexpressing BMI1 (to suppress senescence), BCL-XL (to suppress apoptosis) and c-MYC (to drive proliferation) under doxycycline control. The lines expand for 4-5 months and survive cryopreservation; switching the three transgenes off produces CD42b+ platelets with function comparable to native platelets.
protocols.efficiency: Lines expand in culture for 4-5 months, including after cryopreservation; halting transgene expression yields CD42b+ platelets with function comparable to native platelets across a range of in vitro and in vivo assays
protocols.start_requirements: Human PSC-derived haematopoietic progenitors (produced by the authors' standard hPSC haematopoietic differentiation), then transduced with doxycycline-controlled BMI1, BCL-XL and c-MYC.
materials: Doxycycline-inducible c-MYC, BMI1 and BCL-XL vectors
tips: Clone selection matters: the paper's claim is for appropriately selected imMKCL clones, not for every line established.
This is the line that feeds the turbulent-flow bioreactor work of Ito et al. 2018, which is where clinical-scale platelet numbers came from.
Expansion and maturation are cleanly separated by the doxycycline switch, which makes scheduling easy.
pitfalls: Full methods were not accessible in this session - the media, doxycycline dose and maturation cocktail must be taken from the paper.
Three oncogenic transgenes; depends on the transgenes being switched off and on the platelets being anuclear for safety.
Platelet release per megakaryocyte in static culture remains low, which is the problem turbulent bioreactors addressed.

Doxycycline concentration

protocols.name: STEMdiff Megakaryocyte Kit (2D, 17 days)
protocols.principle: Sparse hPSC colonies are differentiated for 12 days into megakaryocyte-biased hematopoietic progenitors (Supplement A for 3 days, then Supplement MK1 for 9 days); the floating progenitors are then replated for 5 days in StemSpan SFEM II + Supplement MK2 to mature into polyploid CD41a+CD42b+ megakaryocytes that can shed platelets.
protocols.efficiency: At day 17 the average frequency of viable CD41a+CD42b+ cells is 56 - 77%, with an average of 223 - 425 CD41a+CD42b+ cells per seeded hPSC (n > 12, four ES/iPS lines; line-dependent)
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-AOF on Corning Matrigel. On day -1 passage as aggregates of 100 - 200 µm (Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent, ReLeSR or Dispase) and plate 40 - 80 aggregates per well of a Matrigel-coated 12-well tissue culture-treated plate (10 - 20 aggregates/cm2) in 1 mL of maintenance medium, aiming for 16 - 40 attached colonies per well (4 - 10 colonies/cm2) 24 h later. No ROCK inhibitor is specified; cells are not single-cell seeded.
materials: STEMdiff Megakaryocyte Kit (Catalog #100-0900): Hematopoietic Basal Medium, Supplement A (200X), Supplement MK1 (10X), Supplement MK2 (10X), StemSpan SFEM II
Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (Catalog #100-0485), ReLeSR (Catalog #100-0484) or Dispase (1 U/mL) (Catalog #07923)
Anti-Human CD41a Antibody, Clone HIP8 (Catalog #60114) and an anti-CD42b antibody for flow cytometry
tips: Results depend on the hPSC line; test more than one aggregate plating density
Complete media keep 4 weeks at 2-8°C or 6 months at -20°C
Warm media to room temperature just before use and do not leave them out
pitfalls: Starting with fewer or more attached colonies than the stated window (4 - 10 per cm2) compromises differentiation
Disturbing or discarding the floating progenitors during the half-medium changes from day 7
unverified: Composition of Supplements A, MK1 and MK2 is proprietary
The protocol diagram is an image; its caption text was available and matches the written steps
The product description says the cells express 'CD41a and CD41b' while the rest of the sheet measures CD41a and CD42b; CD42b is used here

cell_types.notes: Platelet release, not megakaryocyte production, is the limiting step: Ito et al. later showed that turbulent flow in a controlled bioreactor is what unlocks clinical-scale platelet yields, scaling to 8 L and 100-billion-order platelets. Megakaryocyte ploidy stays low in all hPSC systems (under about 2% 8N), matching neonatal rather than adult megakaryocytes. Feng's maturation step runs deliberately at 39 C in 7% CO2, which is unusual and worth checking your incubator can do before starting.

cell_types.name: Neutrophils
cell_types.summary: Short-lived phagocytic granulocytes made by taking PSC-derived myeloid progenitors into G-CSF, usually with a retinoic acid agonist to force terminal maturation. They are used to model congenital neutropenia and chronic granulomatous disease, to study chemotaxis, reactive-oxygen-species production and neutrophil extracellular traps, and as a potential granulocyte-transfusion product.
cell_types.maturation_note: The ETV2-mRNA route gives mature neutrophils about 6-8 days after collecting myeloid progenitors at day 8-12, so roughly day 14-20. The embryoid-body factories (Lachmann, Sweeney) take 25-32 days but can be harvested repeatedly. In every system the cells remain somewhat immature: CD66b is low and CD10 is usually absent compared with blood neutrophils.

morphology.endpoint: Small round suspension cells with the lobed or band-shaped nuclei and fine granular cytoplasm of granulocytes on a Wright-Giemsa or May-Grunwald-Giemsa cytospin; the live culture looks like a bright, slightly granular non-adherent population over a layer of adherent macrophages.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer or colony fragments
stages.look: Flat sharp-edged colonies, or single cells plated on collagen IV for mRNA transfection.

stages.label: Haemoendothelial progenitors
stages.look: A spread, cobbled, endothelial-looking adherent layer (ETV2 route) or compact embryoid bodies in suspension.

stages.label: Myeloid progenitors
stages.look: Floating round cells accumulate above the adherent layer and are harvested gently, leaving the layer to produce more.

stages.label: Immature granulocytes
stages.look: Suspension cells with slightly larger nuclei; cytospins show promyelocytes and myelocytes.

stages.label: Mature neutrophils
stages.look: Small round cells, with band and segmented nuclei on cytospin; adherent macrophages remain on the plastic and are left behind.

markers.name: PTPRC

markers.name: FUT4

markers.name: FCGR3B

markers.name: CEACAM8
markers.note: Consistently low in PSC-derived neutrophils - the clearest sign of residual immaturity.

markers.name: MME

markers.name: MPO

markers.name: CXCR2

markers.name: LTF

markers.name: ELANE
markers.note: Granule protease; the gene mutated in some congenital neutropenias these cultures are used to model.

protocols.name: ETV2 modified-mRNA route (fastest, feeder- and serum-free)
protocols.principle: A single transfection of ETV2 modified mRNA converts hiPSCs directly into a haemoendothelial programme with myeloid potential, skipping conventional mesoderm induction. FGF2, GM-CSF and UM171 then produce floating myeloid progenitors that can be harvested in three weekly waves, and G-CSF plus the retinoic acid agonist Am580 drives terminal neutrophil differentiation in 6-8 days.
protocols.efficiency: Up to 1.7 x 10^7 neutrophils from 10^6 hiPSCs when the three weekly progenitor collections are combined; more than 50% of the neutrophils are CD16+, but CD66b is low and CD10 absent
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs on Matrigel-coated plates in E8. For transfection, make a single-cell suspension with HyQtase and plate 2 x 10^5 cells per well of a collagen IV-coated 6-well in 1 mL E8 with 10 uM ROCK inhibitor; add the mRNA complex 30-60 min later.
materials: ETV2 modified mRNA (in vitro transcribed with ARCA cap and pseudouridine)
tips: UM171 barely changes progenitor numbers but makes a large difference to how many neutrophils those progenitors produce - do not drop it.
Harvest the floating fraction gently and keep feeding the adherent layer; three weekly waves is where the total yield comes from.
No feeders, no serum, no sorting at any step.
pitfalls: Requires in-house or custom-synthesised modified mRNA.
The third weekly collection is much smaller - plan the experiment around waves one and two.
Neutrophils are CD66b-low and CD10-negative, so functional assays matter more than the surface panel.

stages.name: Myeloid progenitor production

Add 2 mL fresh medium to the remaining adherent cells after the first harvest, then 2 mL every 2 days
Collect a second wave on days 16-19 and a third on days 23-29

stages.name: Terminal neutrophil differentiation
stages.base_medium: StemSpan H3000 with 100x GlutaMAX, 0.2% ExCyte, gentamycin

protocols.name: Four-step embryoid-body protocol, G-CSF arm (granulocytes) in APEL
protocols.principle: Identical to the macrophage arm of the same protocol up to the myeloid cell-forming complexes, but with G-CSF in place of M-CSF: IL-3 plus G-CSF during specification, then high-dose G-CSF for 7 days of terminal maturation, which yields granulocytes spanning all maturation stages.
protocols.efficiency: 4-5 x 10^6 granulocytes per well of a 6-well plate per week for at least 7 weeks; cytospins show promyelocytes 4%, myelocytes 6%, metamyelocytes 29%, band neutrophils 22%, segmented neutrophils 36%, with about 1% basophils and 2% eosinophils
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs or hESCs on irradiated mouse feeders with bFGF; colonies disrupted to fragments with collagenase V.
tips: G-CSF alone during specification gives almost no shedding; IL-3 has to be there too.
The endothelial-like stroma is the go/no-go checkpoint for the whole run.
GM-CSF in the same positions gives a mixed granulocyte/macrophage output.
pitfalls: CD11b, CD16 and CD66b are all lower than on blood granulocytes, more so in cells used straight from the complexes without the high-dose G-CSF step.
Output tails off after 2-3 months.
The maturation step uses 10% serum.

protocols.name: Four-stage discontinuous culture on OP9 stroma
protocols.principle: Four discrete stages - embryoid body formation, 17 days of haematopoietic induction in a BMP4/SCF/Flt3L/IL-6/TPO cocktail, a week on irradiated OP9 stroma with added IL-3, and a final week on fresh OP9 in G-CSF alone - produce mature neutrophils by day 32, with the kinetics of the key haematopoietic transcription factors mapped stage by stage.
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs seeded into ultra-low-attachment dishes in StemSpan SFEM with 10 uM Y-27632 overnight to form embryoid bodies; undifferentiated iPSCs serve as the day-0 reference.
tips: The value of this paper is the stage-by-stage transcription-factor and microRNA kinetics, which makes it a good reference for working out where a failing differentiation stalled.
Both the adherent and non-adherent fractions can be analysed separately at stage 3.
pitfalls: Uses serum, horse serum and mouse OP9 stroma, so it is not a route to a clinical product.
32 days to mature neutrophils, against about 20 for the ETV2 route.
unverified: Cell yields and final purity percentages

cell_types.notes: All published PSC neutrophils are somewhat immature: expect low CD66b and absent CD10, and a cytospin that spans promyelocyte to segmented forms rather than a uniform mature population. The ETV2 mRNA route is by far the fastest and needs no serum, feeders or sorting, but involves transfecting modified mRNA; the embryoid-body routes need no transfection but take a month and the OP9-based version uses serum and mouse stroma.

cell_types.name: Macrophages / monocytes
cell_types.summary: Large phagocytic myeloid cells derived through a yolk-sac-like, MYB-independent primitive haematopoietic programme, together with the CD14+ monocytes that precede them. They are used for infection and innate-immunity modelling, atherosclerosis and lipid-handling work, phagocytosis and efferocytosis assays, and as the starting material for microglia protocols.
cell_types.maturation_note: In embryoid-body factories (van Wilgenburg, Lachmann) monocyte-like cells appear in the supernatant from 2-4 weeks and can then be harvested weekly for 2-3 months; each harvest needs a further 5-7 days in M-CSF to become a macrophage. The directed monolayer route (Cao) delivers CD14+ monocytes on day 15 and M0 macrophages 4 days later.

morphology.endpoint: Large, firmly adherent 'fried-egg' cells with a broad ruffled cytoplasm, visible vacuoles and a single eccentric nucleus. Mature cultures are flat and spread out, and many cells contain phase-dark phagocytic vesicles.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact flat colonies with sharp borders, or single cells being spun into uniform aggregates.

stages.label: Embryoid bodies / mesoderm
stages.look: Smooth round aggregates of even size (forced aggregation) or irregular aggregates (mechanical lifting); some become cystic.

stages.label: Haematopoietic factory
stages.look: Embryoid bodies have attached and spread into an endothelial-like stromal outgrowth - in Lachmann's hands this endothelial look is the quality criterion for success.

stages.label: Monocyte shedding
stages.look: Round, bright, loosely attached cells accumulate in the supernatant around and above the attached aggregates and can be poured off weekly.

stages.label: Macrophages
stages.look: After 5-7 days in M-CSF the harvested cells flatten into large vacuolated fried-egg macrophages that stick hard to plastic.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be gone by the myeloid stage; Lachmann et al. follow its loss alongside T (Brachyury).

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Cao et al. report more than 60% CD140a+ cells after 2 days of BMP4/Activin A/CHIR99021 mesoderm induction.

markers.name: CDH5
markers.note: Around 40% of cells are VE-cadherin+CD34+ on day 5 in Cao et al., and most of those are CD73-negative haemogenic endothelium.

markers.name: SPN
markers.note: Day-9 marker of emerging blood cells in the directed monolayer route.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: All harvested myeloid cells should be CD45+.

markers.name: CD14
markers.note: Main purity readout; Cao et al. enriched day-15 CD14+ cells to over 90% with CD14 microbeads.

markers.name: ITGAM
markers.note: Broad myeloid marker; present on both the macrophage and granulocyte arms of the Lachmann protocol.

markers.name: CD163
markers.note: Expressed on M-CSF-primed macrophages and absent on the granulocyte arm, which makes it a useful arm-check in the Lachmann system.

markers.name: MRC1
markers.note: Rises on IL-4 polarisation.

markers.name: CD68
markers.note: Lysosomal macrophage marker; stains the vacuolated cytoplasm.

markers.name: CSF1R
markers.note: Explains the M-CSF dependence of every step after the progenitor stage.

markers.name: MYB
markers.note: These macrophages arise through a MYB-independent, yolk-sac-like programme (Buchrieser/Haenseler); strong MYB dependence would indicate a different, definitive origin.

markers.name: TRA-1-60
markers.note: Should be undetectable in harvested myeloid cells - Lachmann et al. check this explicitly.

functional_assays: Zymosan or bacterial bioparticle phagocytosis
Acetylated-LDL uptake and Oil Red O staining
Efferocytosis of apoptotic cells
Cytokine release after LPS + IFN-gamma (M1) or IL-4 (M2)
Chemotaxis
Tumour-cell phagocytosis
qc: CD14+ purity by flow before downstream use (over 90% after bead enrichment in Cao et al.)
No TRA-1-60, CD34 or CD19 on the harvested cells (Lachmann et al.)
Phagocytosis of labelled particles as a release test
Confirm the endothelial-like stromal outgrowth before expecting monocyte shedding (Lachmann et al.)

protocols.name: Embryoid-body monocyte factory in X-VIVO 15 (defined and quick variants)
protocols.principle: Embryoid bodies are made either by mechanical lifting (quick protocol) or by forced aggregation in defined medium with BMP4/VEGF/SCF (defined protocol), then transferred to plastic in X-VIVO 15 with M-CSF and IL-3. The attached bodies become a factory that sheds monocyte-like cells into the supernatant weekly for months; each harvest matures into macrophages in M-CSF alone.
protocols.efficiency: Monocyte-like cells harvestable weekly from 2-3 weeks onward; CD45+CD14+ cells rose from about 1% at 12 days to about 9% at 33 days inside the differentiation culture, and harvested cells mature to a homogeneous macrophage population
protocols.start_requirements: Defined variant: hPSCs on Synthemax in mTeSR1, passaged with collagenase IV, plated at about 10,000 cells/cm2. Quick variant: hPSCs on mitomycin-C-inactivated MEFs in KO-DMEM/KOSR/bFGF medium, passaged by micro-dissection.
tips: Big embryoid bodies win: the authors found 10,000-cell bodies gave better monocyte yields than smaller ones.
One body per 96-well is a neat format for screening; AggreWell gives 300 bodies at once for scale.
A lentivirally transduced, puromycin-selected line keeps transgene expression all the way through differentiation.
pitfalls: Expect a lot of debris early on - that is normal, not failure.
Harvest gently; spraying medium over the attached bodies drags unwanted cells into the harvest.
The culture is asynchronous, so each weekly harvest is a slightly different population.
unverified: Percentage of harvested cells that are CD14+ immediately at harvest (reported as kinetics inside the culture rather than a harvest purity)

stages.name: Embryoid body formation
stages.base_medium: mTeSR1 (defined protocol, spin embryoid bodies) or PSC medium (quick protocol, mechanically lifted aggregates)
stages.feeding: 96-well ultra-low-attachment plates: 1e4 cells per well in 100 uL, spun 800 rpm 3 min, half-medium change on day 2. AggreWell 800: 4e6 cells per well, spun 800 rpm 3 min, fed daily to about 75% exchange.
actions: Choose large aggregates - 10,000 cells per embryoid body gave better monocyte yields than smaller ones
Spin to aggregate so bodies are uniform
Feed down the side of the well so bodies are not washed out
stages.checkpoint: Uniform round embryoid bodies at day 4, ready to transfer

stages.name: Directed myeloid differentiation (the factory)
stages.base_medium: X-VIVO 15 with 2 mM GlutaMAX, penicillin/streptomycin, 0.055 mM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: About 10 embryoid bodies per well of a 6-well plate in 3 mL; replace two thirds of the medium every 5 days
actions: Transfer bodies to standard tissue-culture plastic so they attach
Let the attached bodies spread for 2-3 weeks
Harvest non-adherent cells from the supernatant weekly once they appear
stages.checkpoint: Round monocyte-like cells visible in the supernatant from week 2-3; harvests continue for months

stages.name: Macrophage maturation
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 + 10% FCS, or X-VIVO 15 for serum-free work; 2 mM glutamine, penicillin/streptomycin
stages.feeding: Plate harvested monocytes at 1.5e6 per well of a 6-well plate (or 3e5 per 24-well) and culture 5-7 days

Give 5-7 days in M-CSF before any assay
For polarisation, add IFN-gamma (100 U/mL) + LPS (100 ng/mL) or IL-4 (50 ng/mL) for the last 16 h
stages.checkpoint: Flat, vacuolated, firmly adherent fried-egg macrophages that phagocytose zymosan

protocols.name: Four-step embryoid-body protocol, M-CSF arm (macrophages) in APEL
protocols.principle: A four-step route: feeder culture, orbital-shaker embryoid bodies, attachment of the largest bodies in APEL with IL-3 plus M-CSF to build 'myeloid cell-forming complexes', then terminal maturation of the shed cells in high-dose M-CSF. Swapping M-CSF for G-CSF in the same protocol produces granulocytes instead.
protocols.efficiency: Cells shed continuously from day 12-16 for 2-3 months; the granulocyte arm of the same protocol yielded 4-5 x 10^6 cells per well per week for at least 7 weeks
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs or hESCs on irradiated mouse feeder cells with bFGF. Disrupt colonies to fragments with collagenase V.
tips: No endothelial-like stroma means no monocyte shedding - stop and restart rather than waiting.
Pick the largest embryoid bodies by hand; the authors specify manual selection.
GM-CSF at the same positions gives a mixed macrophage/granulocyte output if that is what you want.
pitfalls: Output declines after 2-3 months as the culture exhausts.
Macrophages from the M-CSF arm lean M2-like out of the box, which matters if you want a naive M0 baseline.
unverified: Macrophage-arm weekly cell yield per well (the quantified yield in the paper is for the granulocyte arm)

protocols.name: Defined monolayer route to CD14+ monocytes in 15 days (IF9S)
protocols.principle: A synchronous 2D route in serum-free IF9S medium under normoxia: 2 days of mesoderm, 3 days of haemogenic endothelium, 4 days of haematopoietic progenitors, then 6 days of M-CSF/IL-3/IL-6 to give cryopreservable CD14+ monocytes that are polarised to M0, M1 or M2 macrophages on demand.
protocols.efficiency: CD14 bead enrichment gives over 90% pure monocytes on day 15 with 30-50% post-thaw recovery; after 4 days in M-CSF essentially all monocytes become M0 macrophages at over 90% confluency
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs in TeSR-E8 on vitronectin at about 80% confluency. On day -1 dissociate to small clumps with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (5 min, room temperature) and seed onto Matrigel-coated plates (75 ug/mL) at about 10,000 cells/cm2, roughly a 1:30 split, in TeSR-E8 for 24 h.
tips: Everything runs in normoxia, which removes the need for a tri-gas incubator.
Monocytes cryopreserve and thaw well, so one differentiation can supply many experiments; let them settle 48 h after thaw without disturbance.
FCS coating of the plate is what gets the monocytes to adhere and flatten.
pitfalls: Most day-9 CD43+ cells are erythro-megakaryocytic, not myeloid - do not read day-9 CD43 as monocyte yield.
Thawing recovery is only 30-50%, so freeze generously.
unverified: Absolute monocyte yield per input hiPSC (reported in the paper as a yield figure that could not be read in full in this session)

Keep cultures at 21% O2 - this protocol was adapted for normoxia

actions: Refresh medium on day 2
Check the cobbled endothelial sheet

stages.feeding: Refresh on day 5 and day 7

Watch non-adherent progenitors emerge from the endothelial sheet

protocols.name: STEMdiff Monocyte Kit (CD14+ monocytes, the macrophage precursor)
protocols.principle: A 2D culture goes through mesoderm (Medium A, 3 days) and hematopoietic (Medium B, 4 days) stages and is then kept in Monocyte Differentiation Medium, where CD14+ monocytes are shed into the supernatant and can be collected repeatedly from day 14. The kit stops at monocytes, the precursor of macrophages; the sheet itself does not describe a macrophage step.
protocols.efficiency: Peak CD14+ frequency typically 60 - 80%; maximum CD14+ output generally between day 17 and day 22
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8 on Corning Matrigel. On day -1 passage as aggregates of 100 - 200 µm (Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent, ReLeSR or Dispase) and plate 100 - 200 aggregates per well of a Matrigel-coated 6-well plate (10 - 20 aggregates/cm2) in 2 mL of maintenance medium, aiming for 40 - 100 attached colonies per well (4 - 10 colonies/cm2) 24 h later. No ROCK inhibitor is specified; cells are not single-cell seeded.
materials: STEMdiff Monocyte Kit (Catalog #05320): Hematopoietic Basal Medium, Supplement A (200X), Supplement B (200X), Monocyte Differentiation Supplement (100X), StemSpan SFEM II
Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (Catalog #100-0485), ReLeSR (Catalog #100-0484) or Dispase (1 U/mL) (Catalog #07923)
tips: Harvest during the day 17 - 22 window for the most cells; frequency can stay high after day 22 but yield falls
Complete Medium A or B keeps 4 weeks at 2-8°C or 6 months at -20°C; Monocyte Differentiation Medium keeps 4 weeks at 2-8°C
Aggregate plating density may need testing for each line
Monocytes still need a separate macrophage differentiation step that this sheet does not cover
pitfalls: Starting with fewer or more attached colonies than the stated window (4 - 10 per cm2) compromises differentiation
Leaving media at room temperature for long periods (warm only what is needed)
unverified: The monocyte sheet contains no macrophage differentiation step, medium or catalogue number; none is given here
No end day for the harvest period is stated; day 22 is the end of the stated peak-production window, not a protocol end point
Composition of the supplements is proprietary
The protocol diagram is an image and was not available in the text

stages.base_medium: mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8 (the medium used for maintenance)

Passage hPSCs as 100 - 200 µm aggregates and count aggregates ≥ 50 µm in triplicate 5 µL samples
Plate 100 - 200 aggregates per well (10 - 20 per cm2); if working by split ratio, 1 in 40 to 1 in 200
Distribute with short back-and-forth and side-to-side motions and do not disturb for 24 h

On day 2 gently remove 1.25 mL and add 1.25 mL fresh Medium A

Day 5: remove 1.25 mL and add 1.25 mL fresh Medium B

Repeat the full change every 2-3 days
Day 14: first optional harvest (or just change medium)

stages.name: Repeated monocyte harvests
stages.base_medium: Monocyte Differentiation Medium (StemSpan SFEM II + STEMdiff Monocyte Differentiation Supplement)
stages.feeding: Every 2-3 days: either harvest and refeed with 2 mL, or full change without harvesting
actions: Take off all medium, use it to rinse loosely attached monocytes from the well, and collect
Refeed the well with 2 mL Monocyte Differentiation Medium
Spin the collected cells 300 x g 5 min and resuspend for assays
To collect more per harvest, feed 4 mL or top up with 2 mL without removing medium so cells accumulate over 3-4 days
stages.checkpoint: CD14+ purity by flow cytometry; peak frequency typically 60 - 80%, highest yield between day 17 and day 22

cell_types.notes: These cells are primitive, yolk-sac-like macrophages rather than monocyte-derived macrophages from definitive HSCs, which is why they are the correct starting point for microglia and other tissue-resident macrophages but a caveat for modelling adult blood monocytes. Yields swing widely between lines and even between parallel wells; plating density at the aggregate step is the main lever. The weekly-harvest embryoid-body systems are cheap and run for months but are asynchronous; the directed monolayer route is synchronous and cryopreservable but finite.

cell_types.name: Dendritic cells
cell_types.summary: Professional antigen-presenting cells generated by taking PSC-derived myeloid progenitors into GM-CSF and IL-4, with pharmacological conditioning to push them towards a tolerogenic CD141+ phenotype. They are used for vaccine and antigen-presentation studies, for tolerance-induction and transplantation work, and for modelling monocyte/DC immunodeficiencies such as IRF8 deficiency.
cell_types.maturation_note: Haematopoietic cells appear around days 10-14, macrophages at days 14-18, and DC precursors are harvested between days 21 and 30 (routinely day 24); another 5 days of conditioning plus 48 h of a maturation cocktail completes the process.

morphology.endpoint: Lightly adherent or suspended cells with long cytoplasmic protrusions and veils, which become more prominent over time; firmly adherent fried-egg macrophages are left behind on the plate during harvest.

stages.label: Colony fragments in ultra-low-attachment plates
stages.look: Clusters of iPSC colony fragments, visible to the naked eye, floating in growth-factor-supplemented mTeSR1.

stages.label: Early embryoid bodies
stages.look: Clusters have rounded into early embryoid bodies; plenty of cell debris is normal at this point.

stages.label: Haematopoietic output

stages.label: Macrophage phase

protocols.name: Stepwise growth-factor withdrawal to CD141+ tolerogenic DCs
protocols.principle: Colony fragments are aggregated in mTeSR1 with GM-CSF, BMP-4, SCF and VEGF, and XVIVO-15 differentiation medium is then introduced gradually while growth factors are withdrawn one at a time (BMP-4 at day 5, VEGF at day 9, SCF at day 14), leaving GM-CSF alone to sustain DC precursors. IL-4 is ramped in once macrophages appear, and the harvested immature DCs are conditioned with IL-10, rapamycin, dexamethasone or vitamin D3 to reinforce tolerogenicity.
protocols.efficiency: Median 85.5% CD11c+ (SD 11.94) across 16 consecutive experiments; CD141+ cells enriched by depleting CD1c+ cells
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs on Matrigel in mTeSR1, harvested at 80-85% confluency with 0.02% EDTA and mechanical scraping to give small colony fragments. Count a sacrificial well to work out how many wells can be set up at 3 x 10^6 cells per well.
tips: Never set the culture up in XVIVO-15 - introduce it gradually during feeding or the cells die.
Sacrifice one well for counting rather than including it, since dissociated cells are prone to apoptosis.
Positive selection on CD141 kills cells; deplete CD1c+ cells instead for an untouched CD141+ population.
pitfalls: Timing varies between experiments and between parallel wells; day 24 is routine but day 30 is common.
Uneven dispersal of clusters makes them clump and adhere and can wreck the run.
Vitamin D3 and dexamethasone both cut yield or viability; IL-10 is the better-behaved conditioning agent in this system.

protocols.name: DC subset differentiation from engineered iPSCs (cDC1, cDC2, pDC)
protocols.principle: CRISPR-edited (IRF8-knockout) iPSC and ESC lines are taken through haemogenic endothelium and the endothelial-to-haematopoietic transition, and the resulting progenitors are differentiated into CD141+ cDC1, CD1c+ cDC2 and CD303+ plasmacytoid DCs, allowing a human DC immunodeficiency to be modelled subset by subset.
protocols.efficiency: IRF8-deficient lines showed impaired cDC1 and pDC development with largely preserved cDC2 output, and a granulocyte bias at the expense of monocytes under unrestricted conditions

materials: antibodies against CD141, CD1c, CD303, HLA-DR
tips: This is the route to take when the question is about a specific DC subset or a DC immunodeficiency rather than bulk DC production.

cell_types.notes: Expect a fetal-like phenotype: abundant IL-10, little IL-12, and lower MHC class II than monocyte-derived DCs, partly reflecting epigenetic memory of the reprogrammed cell type. Yield and timing vary a lot between experiments and even between parallel wells, so build in slack; it is not unusual to wait until day 30 for enough precursors. Setting cultures up directly in XVIVO-15 kills the cells, so the switch out of mTeSR1 must be gradual.

cell_types.name: Erythroid cells (red blood cells)
cell_types.summary: Haemoglobinised erythroid cells, from proerythroblast to (partly) enucleated reticulocyte, produced by expanding PSC-derived progenitors in EPO-driven serum-free medium. They are used to study globin switching and enucleation, to model red-cell disorders, for drug testing, and as a long-term route towards cultured transfusion products.
cell_types.maturation_note: Olivier et al. reach over 95% CD235a+ cells by day 31, with up to about 10% spontaneous enucleation; maturation continues to day 31-36 in EPO then medium alone. Enucleation remains the bottleneck in every published hPSC erythroid protocol.

morphology.endpoint: Small, round, intensely haemoglobinised cells; the pellet is visibly red and cytospins show orthochromatic erythroblasts with condensed nuclei plus a minority of enucleated reticulocytes.

stages.label: Colony squares in suspension

stages.label: Erythroid progenitors

stages.label: Haemoglobinised erythroid cells
stages.look: Small, round, strongly haemoglobinised cells, the pellet frankly red, with some enucleated cells visible on cytospin.

protocols.name: Serum-free, feeder-free erythroid differentiation with small molecules
protocols.principle: A fully defined Stemline II / IBIT system in which four phases (mesoderm, haematopoietic expansion, erythroid liquid culture, erythroid maturation) are driven by cytokine mixes A-D plus a set of small molecules: a GSK3-beta inhibitor for mesoderm, StemRegenin 1 for progenitor expansion, IBMX, beta-estradiol and Pluripotin (SC1) during the erythroid phase.
protocols.efficiency: Over 95% CD235a+ by day 31 with up to about 10% spontaneous enucleation; the method worked across several hESC and iPSC lines including clinical-grade lines
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in Stempro with 20 ng/mL FGF2 on recombinant vitronectin, mechanically passaged about every 7 days with an EZPassage tool. For differentiation, take cultures at 80-100% confluence, cut into squares and plate 200-600 x 10^3 cells per well of an ultra-low-adherence 6-well in 3 mL Stemline II.
materials: IBIT medium components (Iscove's, BSA or HSA, insulin, holo-transferrin, xeno-free lipids)
tips: Most factor top-ups are added as 6x stocks in 0.5 mL rather than by changing medium, which keeps conditioned factors in the well.
Density control between days 7 and 10 is the step that most often decides the run.
Judge this and other protocols on absolute enucleated cells per input hPSC, not on percentage enucleation.
pitfalls: Enucleation is still limited to about 10%.
The cells make embryonic and fetal globins rather than adult beta globin.
A long protocol with many separately timed small molecules - make a written schedule before starting.

protocols.efficiency: An essentially pure CD235a+CD45- leukocyte-free erythroid population with robust expansion and a lifespan of up to 90 days; predominantly fetal gamma and embryonic epsilon globin with much lower beta globin. Transgenic and episomal iPSC lines performed similarly to H1 hESCs.

protocols.name: Immortalised erythroid progenitor lines (HiDEP) from TAL1-expressing iPSCs
protocols.principle: Human iPSCs are first given constitutive TAL1 (which was needed to get useful erythroid output at all), differentiated on OP9 stroma with VEGF and IGF-II, switched to SCF/EPO/dexamethasone, then immortalised with a doxycycline-inducible HPV16 E6/E7 system. After about three months the lines grow feeder-free and indefinitely in serum-free medium, and switching to a differentiation medium with mifepristone and EPO produces enucleated red cells.
protocols.efficiency: All established lines produced enucleated red cells on differentiation, but the authors state plainly that the efficiency of enucleation still needs improvement; the gain is unlimited, bankable expansion rather than a high enucleation rate
protocols.start_requirements: Human iPSC lines (HiPS-RIKEN-3A, -4A) maintained on SNL76/7 feeders, transduced with a CSII-EF-TAL1-IRES-Puro lentivirus with polybrene (8 ug/mL) and selected in puromycin (2 ug/mL). 4 x 10^4 iPSCs are then plated on OP9 feeders in a 100 mm dish.
tips: Enforced TAL1 was essential: three hESC and two iPSC lines gave almost no erythroid output without it.
Once established, these lines remove the differentiation step entirely from downstream experiments - the effort is front-loaded.
The companion HUDEP lines from cord-blood CD34+ cells are made with the same immortalisation strategy and are a useful comparator.
pitfalls: About three months of culture on feeders before the lines become independent.
Two lentiviral transductions, including an oncogenic immortalisation cassette - not a route to a clinical product.
Enucleation efficiency remains the stated weakness.

cell_types.notes: Two problems dominate: these cells make embryonic and fetal globins rather than adult beta globin, and they enucleate poorly. Olivier et al. make the useful point that absolute reticulocyte output per input hPSC can still be higher in a high-expansion, low-enucleation system than in a low-expansion, high-enucleation one, so judge protocols on absolute enucleated cells rather than on percentage enucleation. Keep the cell density below about 10^6/mL during the expansion window or the culture stalls.

cell_types.name: B cells
cell_types.summary: Antibody-producing lymphocytes, which remain the least developed of the hPSC immune lineages: published protocols reach CD19+CD10+ pre-B cells with genuine VDJ rearrangement, and only about 5% of the CD19+ cells acquire surface IgM. There is no published route to class-switched, antibody-secreting plasma cells from human PSCs, so these cultures are for developmental and leukaemia modelling rather than antibody production.
cell_types.maturation_note: Honest assessment: the endpoint is an immature pre-B or immature B cell. French et al. report surface IgM on only about 5% of CD19+ cells, which matched cord-blood-derived B cells in the same system, and Carpenter et al. found no surface IgM at all on their CD45+CD19+CD10+ cells. Expect no plasma cells and no class switching.

morphology.endpoint: Small, round, bright non-adherent lymphocytes, usually in small clusters on a stromal monolayer - indistinguishable by eye from other lymphoid cells, so identity rests entirely on flow cytometry and VDJ analysis.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact flat colonies with sharp edges.

stages.label: Haemogenic endothelium

stages.label: Haematopoietic progenitors

stages.label: Pre-B cells

markers.name: IL7R

markers.name: IGLL1

markers.name: CD3E
markers.note: Lymphoid cultures can produce T and NK cells as well, so check that CD19+ cells are CD3-negative.

Surface IgM flow cytometry

protocols.name: B lymphocytes via a haemogenic endothelium intermediate
protocols.principle: hiPSCs are differentiated to a CD144+CD73-CD43/CD235a- haemogenic endothelial population, which is then taken into B-lymphoid conditions; the resulting CD10+CD19+ cells undergo full VDJ rearrangement and a minority express surface IgM, giving an immature B-cell product that is transcriptionally almost identical to cord-blood-derived B cells.
protocols.efficiency: Surface IgM on about 5% of CD19+ cells, comparable to cord-blood-derived B cells generated in parallel; of more than 47,000 transcripts, only 45 differed significantly from the cord-blood-derived counterparts
protocols.start_requirements: Human iPSC lines taken into haematopoietic differentiation under the authors' lympho-haematopoietic conditions (developed from their earlier hESC work).
materials: antibodies against CD144, CD73, CD43, CD235a, CD10, CD19, IgM
tips: The haemogenic endothelium intermediate is what makes this route interpretable - sort it and you know where the B cells came from.
Run a cord-blood-derived B-cell control in parallel; the sIgM percentage is similar, which is reassuring rather than disappointing.
VDJ rearrangement PCR, not flow cytometry, is the real identity test here.
pitfalls: Full methods were not accessible in this session, so all media and cytokines must be read from the paper.
The product is an immature B cell: about 5% sIgM+, no class switching, no antibody secretion.
Yields are not reported in a way that supports planning for scale.
