protocols.name: Pre-B cells under hESC lympho-haematopoietic conditions
protocols.principle: The first demonstration that human iPSCs can enter the B-lymphoid lineage: iPSCs differentiated under conditions that promote lympho-haematopoiesis from hESCs give CD45+CD19+CD10+ pre-B cells expressing PAX5, IL7R, lambda-like and VpreB transcripts with multiple genomic D-JH rearrangements, but no surface IgM.
protocols.efficiency: Pre-B cells identified as CD45+CD19+CD10+ with multiple genomic D-JH rearrangements; surface IgM and CD5 negative. No quantified yield or purity available from the abstract
protocols.start_requirements: Newly derived human iPSC lines with confirmed pluripotency, differentiated under the conditions the authors had established for lympho-haematopoiesis from hESCs.
materials: antibodies against CD45, CD19, CD10, CD5, IgM
tips: Use this as the historical reference; the 2015 paper from the same group is the better protocol to follow because it adds surface IgM and a defined haemogenic endothelial intermediate.
Demonstrating multilineage output alongside the B cells is a useful internal control on the differentiation.
pitfalls: No surface IgM at all, so the product is a pre-B cell.
Methods detail was not accessible in this session.

cell_types.notes: This lineage is genuinely immature and should be presented as such. French et al. is the better of the two protocols because it shows full VDJ rearrangement, surface IgM on about 5% of CD19+ cells, and a transcriptome almost indistinguishable from cord-blood-derived B cells (only 45 of over 47,000 transcripts significantly different). Neither paper's full methods were accessible in this session, so the media and cytokine schedules must be read from the papers; both rely on stromal co-culture under lympho-haematopoietic conditions originally developed for hESCs. If the goal is antibody production rather than developmental modelling, hPSC-derived B cells are not the right tool today.

cell_types.name: Microglia
cell_types.summary: The brain's resident macrophages, derived through the same primitive, yolk-sac-like myeloid programme that gives rise to them in vivo and then educated with IL-34, TGF-beta1 and CNS ligands. They are used for neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration modelling (TREM2, APOE, CD33 and other GWAS genes), phagocytosis and synaptic-pruning assays, co-culture with neurons or organoids, and xenotransplantation into humanised mouse brain.
cell_types.maturation_note: Progenitors are ready at day 10-12, microglial identity takes a further 25-28 days, and the last 2-3 days add CD200 and CX3CL1 to push homeostasis. Transcriptional maturity improves further in neuronal co-culture or after transplantation; longer than about 6 weeks in monoculture is not advised.

morphology.endpoint: Small cells with a compact nucleus and fine, highly dynamic ramified processes, mostly loosely adherent or non-adherent; cultures look sparse and spidery rather than confluent, with constant membrane ruffling on time-lapse.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Small aggregates of about 100 cells plated sparsely (10-20 per cm2) on Matrigel - plating density is the single most important variable.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Colonies have spread into dense flat patches of small cells.

stages.label: Haematopoietic progenitors
stages.look: Round bright non-adherent cells accumulate above the adherent layer and are simply poured off.

stages.label: Early microglia
stages.look: Small cells with a compact nucleus, visible vacuoles and short processes; still largely in suspension.

stages.label: Mature microglia
stages.look: Finely ramified cells with long thin processes that move constantly; many are lightly adherent to Matrigel.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be absent once progenitors are harvested.

markers.name: SPN
markers.note: The gate that matters at day 10: Abud et al. sorted CD43+ cells at over 90% purity, and McQuade et al. got 90-94% CD43+ simply by collecting the floating cells.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: Day-14 early microglia in Abud et al. were c-kit-negative and CD45+.

markers.name: KIT
markers.note: Loss of c-kit with gain of CD45 marks myeloid commitment during the first two weeks of microglial differentiation.

markers.name: P2RY12
markers.note: The key microglia-versus-macrophage discriminator; Abud et al. quote over 97.2% purity by P2RY12/TREM2 co-expression.

markers.name: TMEM119
markers.note: Homeostatic microglial marker not shared with monocyte-derived macrophages.

markers.name: TREM2
markers.note: Co-stained with P2RY12 as the purity readout; also the gene most often edited in these models.

markers.name: CX3CR1
markers.note: Douvaras et al. sort CD14+CX3CR1+ progenitors between days 25 and 50; CX3CL1 is added at the end of the Abud/McQuade protocols to engage it.

markers.name: PU.1
markers.note: Master myeloid regulator, nuclear in microglia.

markers.name: IBA1
markers.note: Classic morphology stain; marks macrophages as well, so pair it with P2RY12 or TMEM119.

markers.name: CSF1R
markers.note: Receptor for both IL-34 and M-CSF, which is why the two can be combined or substituted in these media.

markers.name: CD14
markers.note: Used as the sort gate in Douvaras et al.; in finished microglia it should be low relative to monocytes.

markers.name: CCR2
markers.note: High CCR2 suggests a monocyte-like rather than microglial identity.

Xenotransplantation into MITRG or humanised mouse brain

Finished cultures over 90% P2RY12+/TREM2+ (Abud et al. report >97%)
Phagocytosis of labelled particles
Avoid culture beyond about 6 weeks in monoculture (McQuade et al.)

protocols.name: iMGL: defined CD43+ progenitors then M-CSF/IL-34/TGF-beta1
protocols.principle: Ten days of fully defined haematopoietic differentiation in a home-made IMDM/F12 base give CD43+ primitive progenitors; 25 days in DMEM/F12-based microglial medium with M-CSF, IL-34 and TGF-beta1 give microglia, and a final 3 days with CD200 and CX3CL1 mimic the CNS environment.
protocols.efficiency: Over 90% CD43+ progenitors at day 10 after FACS; finished iMGLs over 97.2% pure by P2RY12/TREM2 co-expression (n=5)
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs feeder-free on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel in TeSR-E8, fed daily, passaged every 7-8 days. On day -1 dissociate with TrypLE Select and seed single cells at 5 x 10^5 cells/cm2 in E8 plus 10 uM Y-27632 in 1.5 mL per well, 24 h normoxia.
tips: Commercial CD43+ iPSC-derived HPCs can replace the first 10 days and give the same iMGLs.
Feed by addition, not replacement - the cells need their own secreted factors.
Freshly thawed single-use cytokine aliquots make a visible difference to yield and activation state.
pitfalls: Needs a hypoxia incubator and a FACS sorter for the progenitor step - the McQuade 2018 version was written to remove both requirements.
Over-handling activates microglia and will contaminate any inflammatory readout.

stages.feeding: 2 mL per well of a 6-well plate; move to 5% O2 / 5% CO2 from day 0
actions: Collect and spin cells at each medium change (300 x g, 6 min)
Pre-equilibrate media in the hypoxia incubator before use

actions: Keep hypoxic
Handle gently - cells detach easily at this stage

stages.name: Haematopoietic progenitor expansion (normoxia)

Top up rather than replace on days 6 and 8
FACS-sort CD43+ cells on day 10

stages.name: Microglial differentiation
stages.base_medium: iMGL base: phenol-free DMEM/F12 (1:1) with insulin 0.2 mg/mL, holo-transferrin 0.011 mg/mL, sodium selenite 13.4 ug/mL (or 2% ITS-G), 2% B27, 0.5% N2, monothioglycerol 200 uM, GlutaMAX, NEAA, extra insulin 5 ug/mL
stages.feeding: Seed 1-2 x 10^5 CD43+ cells in 2 mL per well on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel; add 1 mL fresh complete medium every 2 days; on day 12 of this stage collect cells, spin and do a 50% medium change
actions: Add cytokines fresh at every feed
Never do a full medium change
At day 12 of the stage, collect, spin and return cells in half-fresh medium
stages.checkpoint: Day-14 early microglia are c-kit-negative CD45+; by the end of the stage P2RY12 and TREM2 are co-expressed

stages.name: CNS maturation
stages.feeding: Three days in the five-factor medium before use
actions: Add CD200 and CX3CL1 for the last 3 days
Use the cells promptly for assays or transplantation
stages.checkpoint: Ramified morphology, P2RY12+/TREM2+ over 90%, ADP-responsive

protocols.name: Simplified iMGL 2.0: no hypoxia, no sorting
protocols.principle: The same microglial differentiation as Abud et al., but the progenitor phase is replaced by a commercially available haematopoietic kit run in normoxia, and the CD43+ progenitors are obtained simply by collecting the non-adherent cells instead of sorting them. The transcriptome of the resulting microglia is essentially the same as the original protocol at higher yield and lower cost.
protocols.efficiency: Non-adherent day-10/12 cells are 90-94% CD43+ without any sorting; microglial yield is substantially higher than the original protocol
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free iPSCs expanded in TeSR-E8. On day -1 passage with ReLeSR into mTeSR-E8 plus 0.5 uM thiazovivin onto Matrigel-coated (1 mg/mL) 6-well plates, as small aggregates of about 100 cells at 10-20 aggregates per cm2. Plate at two or three densities and pick the best well on day 0.
tips: Plate iPSCs at two or three densities and choose the best well on day 0 - too dense impairs mesoderm, too sparse kills yield.
Frozen progenitors should be thawed straight into microglial medium with cytokines and plated at 10,000 cells/cm2; thaw a lot together for better viability.
A small-molecule TGF-beta pathway activator (IDE1) can substitute for TGF-beta1 but gives a transcriptionally distinct product.
pitfalls: Careless collection of the non-adherent progenitors is the main purity failure, since nothing is sorted.
The progenitor phase depends on a commercial kit, so the first 12 days are not fully defined in-house.
unverified: Yield of microglia per input iPSC (described as substantially increased but not read as an absolute number in this session)

source.authors: McQuade A, Coburn M, Tu CH, Hasselmann J, Davtyan H, Blurton-Jones M

stages.name: Haematopoietic progenitor generation (medium A then B)
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff Hematopoietic Kit basal medium (supplement A days 0-3, supplement B days 3-12), 1:200
stages.feeding: 2 mL medium A per well at day 0; 50% change (1 mL) of medium A on day 2; on day 3 remove all medium by tilting and aspirating from the edge, then 2 mL medium B; add 1 mL medium B on days 5, 7 and 9 without removing medium
actions: Start when there are about two 100-cell colonies per cm2 - density is critical
Collect non-adherent cells on day 10 and again on day 12
Do not spray medium across the well when collecting; purity depends on it
Spin collected cells at 300 x g for 5 min and return the conditioned medium to the well
stages.checkpoint: 90-94% CD43+ among the collected non-adherent cells; freeze at 2-4 x 10^6 cells/mL in BamBanker if not used immediately

stages.name: Microglial differentiation
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with 2x insulin-transferrin-selenite, 2x B27, 0.5x N2, GlutaMAX, NEAA, monothioglycerol 400 uM, insulin 5 ug/mL
stages.feeding: Plate progenitors at 10,000 cells/cm2 (1e5 per 35 mm well) on 1 mg/mL Matrigel in 2 mL; add 1 mL fresh medium plus freshly thawed cytokines on days 2, 4, 6, 8, 10; on day 12 collect 6 mL leaving 1 mL conditioned medium, spin, resuspend in 1 mL fresh medium and return; continue 1 mL additions on days 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24; repeat the spin step on day 25
actions: Thaw cytokines immediately before each feed and never refreeze them
Add medium, never fully replace it
Cells grow mostly non-adherently - expect that
stages.checkpoint: Microglial morphology and marker expression; transcriptome comparable to the original iMGL protocol

stages.name: Homeostatic maturation
stages.feeding: Five-cytokine medium from day 25 of microglial differentiation; feed 1 mL on day 27; harvest on day 28 of the stage
actions: Switch to the five-cytokine cocktail
Use cells for sequencing, transplantation or functional assays
If needed, hold 1-2 extra weeks by continued supplementation, but no longer
stages.checkpoint: Ramified homeostatic microglia; post-thaw progenitor viability was typically 70-95% if frozen progenitors were used

protocols.name: Primitive macrophage precursors matured in neuronal co-culture
protocols.principle: Monocyte-like primitive macrophage precursors are produced from AggreWell embryoid bodies in X-VIVO 15 with M-CSF and IL-3, then differentiated in an N2-supplemented Advanced DMEM/F12 microglia medium with IL-34 and GM-CSF - ideally in direct co-culture with iPSC-derived cortical neurons, which drives a microglia-specific expression profile and inflammatory response.
protocols.start_requirements: 3 x 10^6 iPSCs seeded into one AggreWell 800 well in mTeSR1 to form embryoid bodies. In parallel, cortical neural progenitors are made by 12 days of dual SMAD inhibition, replated at day 12, given FGF2 (20 ng/mL) days 13-17, dispased at days 17-18 and frozen at days 25-30.
tips: If the question involves microglia-neuron crosstalk, this is the protocol built for it - the expression profile only becomes microglia-specific in co-culture.
The precursor factory is the same one used for macrophages, so one differentiation can feed both projects.
RFP-labelled precursors make them trackable against unlabelled neurons.
pitfalls: Precursors only appear after about a month, so plan the neuron timeline backwards from that.
Microglia in monoculture in this system are transcriptionally different from the co-cultured cells - do not mix the two sets of data.
unverified: Purity percentages for the microglial product (the paper emphasises efficiency and expression profile rather than a single purity number)

stages.name: Embryoid body formation
stages.feeding: Daily medium plus factors in AggreWell 800
actions: Seed 3e6 iPSCs per AggreWell 800 well
Feed daily for 4 days
stages.checkpoint: Uniform 4-day embryoid bodies

stages.name: Primitive macrophage precursor factory
stages.base_medium: X-VIVO 15 with 2 mM GlutaMAX, penicillin/streptomycin, 0.055 mM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: 15 embryoid bodies per 6-well, 75 per T75 or 150 per T175; fresh medium added weekly
actions: Transfer embryoid bodies to adherent flasks
Expect precursors in the supernatant after about one month
Harvest weekly through a 40 um strainer and replenish medium
stages.checkpoint: Monocyte-like primitive macrophage precursors in the supernatant from about 1 month

stages.name: Microglial differentiation (monoculture or neuronal co-culture)
stages.base_medium: Advanced DMEM/F12 with N2 supplement, 2 mM GlutaMAX, penicillin/streptomycin, 0.055 uM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: Precursors added at 100,000 cells/cm2 onto 14-day-old neurons (or onto plastic/glass for monoculture) and co-cultured at least 14 days before assay
actions: Plate neural progenitors at 100,000 cells/cm2 and culture 14 days first
Add precursors in microglia medium on top
Co-culture at least 14 days before assaying
stages.checkpoint: Microglial morphology and a co-culture-specific expression profile; alternative basal media (X-VIVO 15, RPMI) and M-CSF-containing cocktails were tested but the N2/IL-34/GM-CSF combination was chosen

protocols.name: Monolayer route with CD14+CX3CR1+ sorting
protocols.principle: A single adherent differentiation in mTeSR Custom plus BMP4, then StemPro-34 with sequential haematopoietic and myeloid cytokines, produces CD14+ (or CD14+CX3CR1+) myeloid progenitors between days 25 and 50; these are plated in RPMI with GM-CSF and IL-34 to become microglia.
protocols.start_requirements: Human PSCs in adherent culture, switched directly into mTeSR Custom medium containing BMP4 to start differentiation.
materials: CD14 and CX3CR1 antibodies for sorting
tips: The long day 25-50 harvest window makes this convenient when experiments have to be staggered.
CX3CR1 co-selection gives a more microglia-committed starting population than CD14 alone.
pitfalls: Requires a sort or bead selection, unlike the simplified iMGL route.
No TGF-beta1 in the maturation medium, so the homeostatic signature differs from the Abud/McQuade protocols - compare like with like.
unverified: Purity and yield figures
Exact feeding schedule for the first three stages

stages.name: Haematoendothelial induction
actions: Change to StemPro-34 with the three factors on day 4

stages.name: Myeloid progenitor expansion
stages.feeding: Medium supplemented from day 6
actions: Add the five-factor cocktail from day 6

stages.name: Microglial progenitor production
stages.feeding: From day 14 onward
actions: Switch to the three-factor cocktail at day 14
Between days 25 and 50, isolate CD14+ or CD14+CX3CR1+ cells
stages.checkpoint: CD14+ (ideally CD14+CX3CR1+) progenitors available any time between day 25 and day 50

stages.name: Microglial maturation
stages.feeding: Replenish every 3-4 days for at least 2 weeks
actions: Plate sorted progenitors on tissue-culture plastic or Thermanox coverslips
Refresh medium every 3-4 days for at least 14 days
stages.checkpoint: Microglial morphology and motility on time-lapse after 2 weeks

protocols.name: STEMdiff Microglia Differentiation + Maturation
protocols.principle: Floating hematopoietic progenitors made from hPSCs are cultured for 24 days in microglia differentiation medium with top-up feeding, then moved for 4 - 10 days into maturation medium carrying one extra supplement to give terminally differentiated microglia.
protocols.efficiency: > 80% CD45/CD11b-positive, > 50% TREM2-positive microglia; < 20% morphologically distinct monocytes or macrophages
protocols.start_requirements: Starts from hematopoietic progenitor cells, not hPSCs: make them with STEMdiff Hematopoietic Kit (Catalog #05310) and harvest the suspended cells on day 12 of that protocol; they must be ≥ 90% CD43+ by flow. Seed 1 - 2 x 10^5 cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 6-well plate (1.1 - 2.2 x 10^4 cells/cm2) in 2 mL microglia differentiation medium. Day 0 is the day HPCs are plated. No ROCK inhibitor is specified.
materials: Poly-D-lysine (e.g. Sigma P7280) or Fibronectin (07159) for ICC plates
tips: Both complete media keep up to 4 weeks at 2 - 8°C.
Check CD43 on the progenitors (≥ 90%) before starting.
Marker expression can be checked by flow as early as day 24.
pitfalls: Cell death can increase after more than 10 days in maturation medium.
Feeding is by top-up only; removing medium discards the floating and loosely attached cells.
unverified: Protocol diagram (Figure 1) is an image; days come from the written steps.
The day-12 hematopoietic progenitor protocol itself is in a separate PIS and is not part of this entry.
protocols.product: STEMdiff Microglia Differentiation Kit; STEMdiff Microglia Maturation Kit

stages.name: Microglia differentiation, first half

factors.name: STEMdiff Microglia Basal Medium
factors.role: basal medium, 90 mL per 100 mL (composition proprietary)

stages.feeding: Every other day add 1 mL fresh medium (half the starting volume) without removing any
actions: Harvest floating HPCs and count
Plate 1 - 2 x 10^5 cells in 2 mL per Matrigel-coated well of a 6-well plate
Top up with 1 mL every second day
stages.checkpoint: Culture is semi-adherent with some clumps; that is normal

stages.name: Microglia differentiation, second half

factors.name: STEMdiff Microglia Basal Medium
factors.role: basal medium, 90 mL per 100 mL (composition proprietary)

stages.feeding: Every other day add 1 mL fresh medium without removing any, for 12 days
actions: Day 12: collect the whole suspension (rinse the well with 1 mL DMEM/F-12 for loosely attached cells) and spin 300 x g for 5 min
Leave ~1 mL over the pellet, resuspend and transfer to a new Matrigel-coated well holding 1 mL fresh medium
If a set density is needed, replate at no less than 1.1 x 10^4 cells/cm2
stages.checkpoint: Day 24: cells can be assayed; by flow > 80% CD45+CD11b+ and > 50% TREM2+

stages.name: Microglia maturation

factors.name: STEMdiff Microglia Basal Medium
factors.role: basal medium, 90 mL per 100 mL (composition proprietary)

factors.name: STEMdiff Microglia Supplement 3
factors.role: maturation supplement, 400 µL per 100 mL (composition proprietary)

stages.feeding: Every other day add 1 mL fresh maturation medium without removing any
actions: Day 24: collect and spin the cells as on day 12
Resuspend in the ~1 mL left behind and add to a new coated well holding 1 mL maturation medium
Use Matrigel for most assays; use 10 µg/mL PDL or 1 µg/mL fibronectin coating for ICC
Use the cells between day 28 and day 34
stages.checkpoint: Day 28 - 34: terminally differentiated after 4 - 10 days in maturation medium, with little proliferation after day 28

cell_types.notes: The cytokine trio (M-CSF, IL-34, TGF-beta1) is the heart of all these protocols and is sensitive: McQuade et al. insist on single-use frozen aliquots thawed immediately before feeding, because freeze-thawing them impairs differentiation and activates the cells. Never do a full medium change during microglial differentiation - the cells depend on their own paracrine signals, so always feed by addition. Microglia are easily activated by handling, so plan assays for 4-5 days after a feed or passage, and treat any unexpected inflammatory profile as a handling artefact first.

cell_types.name: T cells
cell_types.summary: Antigen-specific adaptive lymphocytes made by giving PSC-derived haematopoietic progenitors a Notch (DLL1/DLL4) signal plus IL-7 and Flt3L, either on stroma, in a 3D artificial thymic organoid, or on recombinant DL4-coated plastic. They are used for off-the-shelf CAR-T and TCR-T manufacturing and for studying human thymopoiesis.
route: Mature CD8 single-positive (or CD4 SP) T cell
cell_types.maturation_note: CD7 appears in the first fortnight, CD5 next, then CD4/CD8 double positives around week 3; mature single-positive T cells need a further positive-selection/maturation step (OKT3 plus IL-7/IL-2 and dexamethasone in Iriguchi et al.) or weeks 5-7 of organoid culture (Montel-Hagen et al.). Expansion afterwards can add many logs.

morphology.endpoint: Small, round, bright, non-adherent lymphocytes in tight clusters - either shaken out of an organoid at the air-liquid interface or growing as a suspension over a DL4-coated surface or stromal monolayer.

stages.label: Pluripotent or mesodermal start
stages.look: Compact colonies, or a dense monolayer after 3.5 days of mesoderm induction, or 24 h embryoid bodies formed with CHIR99021.

stages.label: Haematopoietic induction
stages.look: Either a compact aggregate at the air-liquid interface on a transwell (ATO) or embryoid bodies in suspension.

stages.label: T-lineage progenitors
stages.look: Small round cells appearing in and around the aggregate or over the DL4-coated surface.

stages.label: Double-positive thymocytes
stages.look: A dense population of small bright lymphocytes; organoids look like opaque compact pellets packed with cells.

stages.label: Mature T cells
stages.look: Uniform small lymphocytes in clusters that scatter when pipetted; blastic and clumping after CD3 stimulation.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be gone; residual pluripotent cells are a teratoma risk in any therapeutic product.

markers.name: CD34
markers.note: Iriguchi et al. sort CD235a-CD14-CD34+CD43+ cells (2,000 per well) onto DL4-coated plates.

markers.name: SPN
markers.note: Appears around day 6 of embryoid-body differentiation and rises over the following week.

markers.name: NCAM1
markers.note: In the ATO protocol the input is CD326-CD56+ embryonic mesodermal progenitors sorted at day 3.5, which made up 45-80% of the culture.

markers.name: CD7
markers.note: First T-lineage marker acquired, within the first 1-2 weeks of differentiation.

markers.name: CD5
markers.note: Upregulated after CD7; CD45+CD5+CD7+ marks T-lineage commitment in the ATO system.

markers.name: CD4
markers.note: With CD8 defines the double-positive stage that dominates around week 3.

markers.name: CD8A
markers.note: CD8alphabeta (not CD8alphaalpha) is the conventional phenotype; CD3-CD8alphaalpha+ cells seen at week 1 in ATOs are innate-like and disappear.

markers.name: CD3E
markers.note: Surface CD3 with TCR-alpha/beta defines the mature product.

markers.name: TRAC
markers.note: TCRalphabeta+CD3+ is the gate; TCR repertoire diversity was sequenced in the ATO paper.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: CD45RA+CD45RO- with CD27, CD28, CCR7 and CD62L marks the naive phenotype reached at week 7 in ATOs.

markers.name: TRDC
markers.note: Themeli et al. found their OP9-DL1-derived T cells had the properties of gamma-delta T cells despite carrying a rearranged alpha-beta TCR - an important caveat for the stromal route.

markers.name: FOXP3
markers.note: Worth checking when the intended product is a conventional effector T cell.

functional_assays: Antigen-specific or CAR-dependent cytotoxicity against target lines
Cytokine production after CD3/CD28 or antigen stimulation
Proliferation after CD3 stimulation
TCR repertoire deep sequencing
In vivo tumour control in xenograft models
qc: CD3+TCRalphabeta+CD8alphabeta+ fraction by flow (the conventional-T readout)
No CD8alphaalpha innate-like skew and no gamma-delta dominance
Naive phenotype (CD45RA+CD45RO-, CD27+, CD28+, CCR7+, CD62L+) if a naive product is required
Antigen- or CAR-specific killing before any in vivo work

protocols.name: PSC artificial thymic organoid (MS5-hDLL4 aggregates at an air-liquid interface)
protocols.principle: Sorted CD326-CD56+ embryonic mesodermal progenitors are aggregated with MS5 stromal cells expressing human DLL4 and cultured as a compact organoid on a transwell at the air-liquid interface: two weeks of haematopoietic induction in EGM2 with a TGF-beta inhibitor, then T-cell differentiation in RPMI/B27 with SCF, Flt3L and IL-7, which supports positive selection and gives naive conventional T cells with a diverse TCR repertoire.
protocols.start_requirements: hESC/hiPSC colonies on Matrigel in mTeSR. Harvest as single cells with TrypLE Express (5 min), then plate 3 x 10^6 cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 6-well in 3 mL X-VIVO 15 with Activin A, BMP4, VEGF, FGF (10 ng/mL each) and 10 uM Y-27632.
tips: The 3D air-liquid interface is what gives conventional CD8alphabeta cells and positive selection; a flat Notch co-culture does not.
Transient CD3-CD8alphaalpha+ innate-like cells at week 1 are expected and disappear by week 3 - do not read them as failure.
TCR-engineered PSCs give near-uniform transgenic TCR expression by week 1 of T-cell induction.
pitfalls: Requires a FACS sort of hEMPs at day 3.5 and a hDLL4-expressing MS5 line.
Volumes are tiny (6 uL per organoid) - the aggregation step takes practice.
Make RB27 weekly; the ascorbate is unstable.
unverified: Absolute T-cell yield per 1e6 input hEMPs at week 7 (figure legend value not readable in this session)
Percentage of CD8SP cells at week 7

source.authors: Montel-Hagen A, Seet CS, Li S, Chick B, Zhu Y, Chang P, Tsai S, Sun V, Lopez S, Chen HC, He C, Chin CJ, Casero D, Crooks GM
source.title: Organoid-Induced Differentiation of Conventional T Cells from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction and hEMP isolation
stages.feeding: Daily medium change with BMP4, VEGF and FGF (no Activin A, no Y-27632) for 3.5 days
actions: Plate single cells at 3e6 per 6-well
Change medium daily
At day 3.5 wash 3x with PBS, release with Accutase (10 min), scrape and FACS-sort CD326-CD56+ hEMPs
stages.checkpoint: 45-80% of the day-3.5 culture should be CD326-CD56+ hEMP before sorting

stages.name: Organoid assembly and haematopoietic induction
stages.feeding: 5 x 10^5 MS5-hDLL4 cells plus 0.5-1 x 10^4 sorted hEMPs per organoid, spun 300 x g 5 min at 4 C, resuspended in 6 uL per organoid, plated on 0.4 um Millicell transwell inserts (up to 2 organoids per insert) over 1 mL medium; complete medium change every 2-3 days
actions: Pellet stroma and hEMPs together and resuspend in only 6 uL
Pipette the slurry onto the transwell membrane so the organoid sits at the air-liquid interface
Change the medium under the insert every 2-3 days
stages.checkpoint: Compact organoid holding together on the membrane

stages.name: Haematopoietic expansion
stages.feeding: Medium changed every 2-3 days for 7 days
actions: Add the three haematopoietic cytokines at day -7
stages.checkpoint: Haematopoietic cells inside the organoid, with CD34- blood cells rising as T-cell conditions begin

stages.name: T cell differentiation
stages.base_medium: RB27: RPMI 1640 with 4% B27, 30 uM L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate, 1% penicillin/streptomycin/glutamine (made fresh weekly)
stages.feeding: Complete medium change every 3-4 days by aspirating around the insert
actions: Switch to RB27 with SCF, Flt3L and IL-7 at day 0
Make RB27 fresh weekly
Harvest organoid cells by adding FACS buffer and disaggregating
stages.checkpoint: CD45+CD5+CD7+ T-lineage cells by about week 1; double-positive predominance by week 3; mature naive CD3+TCRalphabeta+CD8alphabeta+CD45RA+CD45RO- T cells by week 7

protocols.name: Feeder-free T cells on recombinant DL4-coated plates
protocols.principle: A four-step, feeder-free and scalable route: CHIR99021-assisted embryoid bodies give lymphoid-competent progenitors; sorted CD34+CD43+ cells are differentiated on plates coated with recombinant DL4 plus retronectin, where adding SDF-1-alpha and the p38 inhibitor SB203580 synergistically raises double-positive yield; OKT3 then matures them to CD8alphabeta single-positive cytotoxic T cells, which are expanded with a defined cytokine cocktail.
protocols.efficiency: By day 14 of the embryoid-body phase total cell numbers reach about 5 x 10^6 per culture (line-dependent); T-cell yields and double-positive frequencies were highest with SDF-1-alpha plus SB203580 together
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs expanded 6-7 days on iMatrix-511 in StemFit AK03N, dissociated to single cells with 0.5x TryPLE Select. Seed 3-6 x 10^5 cells per well of a 6-well ultra-low-attachment plate.
tips: Needing no feeder cells at any step is the point of this protocol - good for clinical translation.
SDF-1-alpha and SB203580 only give their benefit together; adding one alone mostly fails to improve the double-positive frequency.
A step-by-step version of this protocol is deposited by the authors at Protocol Exchange.
pitfalls: Still needs a FACS sort of the progenitors.
Hypoxia for days 0-7 then normoxia is part of the method.
Re-coating plates with DL4 at each transfer is mandatory; the Notch signal is surface-bound.
unverified: Final percentage of CD8alphabeta single-positive cells and absolute T-cell yield per input iPSC

source.authors: Iriguchi S, Yasui Y, Kawai Y, Arima S, Kunitomo M, Sato T, Ueda T, Minagawa A, Mishima Y, Yanagawa N, Baba Y, Miyake Y, Nakayama K, Takiguchi M, Shinohara T, Nakatsura T, Yasukawa M, Kassai Y, Hayashi A, Kaneko S
source.title: A clinically applicable and scalable method to regenerate T-cells from iPSCs for off-the-shelf T-cell immunotherapy.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: greatly improves embryoid-body formation and later haematopoietic output

stages.feeding: 24 h in ultra-low-attachment plates under hypoxia (5% CO2 / 5% O2 / 90% N2)
actions: Aggregate single cells in pluripotency medium plus CHIR99021 and Y-27632 for 24 h
Keep hypoxic for the first 7 days
stages.checkpoint: Embryoid bodies formed by 24 h

stages.name: Mesoderm and haematoendothelial induction
stages.base_medium: EB basal medium: StemPro-34 with penicillin/streptomycin, 2 mM GlutaMAX, ascorbic acid-2-phosphate 50 ug/mL, monothioglycerol 4 x 10^-4 M, 1x ITS-G

factors.name: SB431542
factors.role: added 24 h after the first medium change

stages.feeding: Day 1: 2 mL per well of basal medium with BMP-4, VEGF and bFGF; day 2: add SB431542; day 4: fresh basal medium with VEGF, bFGF and SCF
actions: Change medium at days 1 and 4
Add SB431542 24 h into the first medium
stages.checkpoint: CD34 upregulated over the first 4 days; CD43+ cells appear at day 6

stages.name: Haematopoietic progenitor expansion
stages.feeding: Replace with fresh day-7 medium every 2-3 days; normoxia (5% CO2) from day 7
actions: Move to normoxia at day 7
Refresh every 2-3 days
At the end, dissociate 11-14 embryoid bodies with TryPLE Select and pass 7 times through a 21-G needle
FACS-sort 2,000 CD235a-CD14-CD34+CD43+ cells per DL4-coated well
stages.checkpoint: About 5 x 10^6 cells per culture by day 14; a clean CD235a-CD14-CD34+CD43+ sort gate

stages.name: T-cell progenitor differentiation on DL4
stages.base_medium: alpha-MEM with 15% FBS, 1x ITS-G, 55 uM 2-mercaptoethanol, ascorbic acid-2-phosphate 50 ug/mL, 2 mM GlutaMAX (serum-free versions with BIT9500 or StemSpan SFEM II also work)

factors.name: SDF-1 alpha (CXCL12)
factors.role: raises double-positive yield; synergises with SB203580

factors.name: SB203580
factors.role: p38 inhibitor; blocks apoptosis during the DN-to-DP transition

stages.feeding: Plates coated overnight at 4 C with rhDL4/Fc (10 ug/mL) mixed 1:1 with retronectin (10 ug/mL), 150 uL per 48-well; 80% medium change every other day; transfer to fresh DL4-coated plates on day 7 and move 1-2 x 10^5 cells per well on day 14 of this stage
actions: Coat plates the day before with DL4 plus retronectin
Change 80% of the medium every other day
Re-plate onto fresh DL4 coating on day 7 of the stage
stages.checkpoint: CD7 within the first week, then CD5, then CD4/CD8-beta double positives by about 3 weeks of this stage

stages.name: Maturation to CD8 single-positive cytotoxic T cells
stages.base_medium: alpha-MEM with 15% FBS, 1x ITS-G, ascorbic acid-2-phosphate 50 ug/mL, 1x penicillin/streptomycin/glutamine

factors.name: dexamethasone
factors.role: supports maturation to CD8 single positives

stages.feeding: 3 days with OKT3, then wash and continue 4 days in the same medium without OKT3
actions: Stimulate day-21 DL4 cells with OKT3 for 3 days
Wash out OKT3 and culture 4 more days
For expansion, activate on CD3/retronectin-coated plates in a defined cytokine cocktail (IL-7, IL-15, IL-21, IL-12, IL-18, TL-1A, Z-VAD) for 3 days, then maintain in IL-7 plus IL-15
stages.checkpoint: CD8alphabeta single-positive T cells that kill antigen-bearing targets

protocols.name: CAR-engineered T-iPSCs differentiated on OP9-DL1
protocols.principle: T cells are reprogrammed to iPSCs, engineered with a second-generation CD19 CAR, then re-differentiated: serum- and feeder-free embryoid bodies give haematopoietic progenitors by day 10, which are seeded on OP9-DL1 stroma with SCF, IL-7 and Flt3L to become T cells, and expanded on CD19-expressing artificial antigen-presenting cells.
protocols.start_requirements: iPSC clones reprogrammed from peripheral-blood T lymphocytes (so that an endogenous rearranged TCR is already present) and transduced with the 1928z CD19 CAR. Treat colonies with dispase for 6 min and transfer to low-attachment plates.
tips: Starting from a T-cell-derived iPSC keeps a pre-rearranged TCR, which shortens and biases differentiation.
Useful as the historical proof that CAR-T cells can be made from iPSCs; the ATO and DL4-plate systems are better routes to conventional alpha-beta T cells.
pitfalls: The authors state plainly that the resulting cells had the properties of gamma-delta T cells despite expressing their endogenous alpha-beta TCR - do not expect a conventional CD8alphabeta product.
Mouse stroma and 20% FBS make this the least clinically compatible of the three routes.
unverified: Percentage CD3+ at days 30-35
Expansion fold-change on 3T3-CD19

source.authors: Themeli M, Kloss CC, Ciriello G, Fedorov VD, Perna F, Gonen M, Sadelain M
source.title: Generation of tumor-targeted human T lymphocytes from induced pluripotent stem cells for cancer therapy.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation and mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: StemPro-34 with 2 mM L-glutamine, 1% NEAA, 10 uM 2-mercaptoethanol, penicillin/streptomycin, ascorbic acid
stages.feeding: Overnight in BMP-4, then BMP-4 plus bFGF until day 4
actions: Dispase colonies for 6 min only
Form embryoid bodies overnight with BMP-4
stages.checkpoint: Mesoderm induced by day 4

stages.name: Haematopoietic specification and expansion
stages.feeding: Cytokine cocktail added from day 4 to day 10
actions: Add the haematopoietic cocktail at day 4
At day 10 dissociate embryoid bodies with Accutase for 20 min to single cells
stages.checkpoint: Day-10 embryoid bodies contain haematopoietic progenitors

stages.name: T-lymphoid differentiation on OP9-DL1
stages.base_medium: OP9 medium: alpha-MEM with 20% FBS, 2 mM L-glutamine, 1% NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol, penicillin/streptomycin, ascorbic acid
stages.feeding: Single cells seeded on OP9-DL1 monolayers; cells analysed at days 30-35
actions: Seed dissociated day-10 cells onto OP9-DL1
Let T cells develop over roughly 3 weeks
Characterise at days 30-35
stages.checkpoint: CD3+ T cells by days 30-35 - but expect a gamma-delta-like phenotype in this system

stages.name: Antigen-driven expansion on 3T3-CD19 aAPCs
stages.feeding: Cells seeded on an irradiated 3T3-CD19 monolayer at a 3:1 ratio
actions: Expand on irradiated CD19-expressing 3T3 cells with IL-7 and IL-15
stages.checkpoint: CAR-dependent expansion and cytokine release

protocols.name: STEMdiff T Cell Kit (EBs to CD34+ cells to CD4+CD8+ DP T cells)
protocols.principle: hPSC embryoid bodies are differentiated for 12 days to CD34+ hematopoietic progenitors, which are selected and grown on a lymphoid coating material for 14 days to CD7+CD5+ lymphoid progenitors and a further 14 days in T Cell Progenitor Maturation Medium to CD4+CD8+ double-positive T cells. An optional 7-day activation step with IL-15 yields CD8 single-positive cells.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8 (the manual works from a 100 mm dish; matrix is not named in the protocol chapter), with differentiated areas removed. Dissociate to single cells with ACCUTASE and seed 3.5 x 10^6 cells per well of an AggreWell400 6-well plate (500 cells per microwell) in 5 mL EB Formation Medium containing 10 µM Y-27632, then centrifuge at 100 x g for 3 min. No confluency requirement is stated.
materials: STEMdiff T Cell Kit (Catalog #100-0194): Hematopoietic - EB Basal Medium (#100-0171), EB Supplement A (#100-0172), EB Supplement B (#100-0173), StemSpan Lymphoid Progenitor Expansion Supplement (10X) (#09915), Lymphoid Differentiation Coating Material (100X) (#09925), T Cell Progenitor Maturation Supplement (10X) (#09930), StemSpan SFEM II (#09605)
EasySep Human CD34 Positive Selection Kit II (Catalog #17856)
Non-tissue culture-treated 6-well and 24-well plates (e.g. Catalog #38040 and #38042)
Optional CD8 SP step: Human Recombinant IL-15 (Catalog #78031) and ImmunoCult Human CD3/CD28/CD2 T Cell Activator (Catalog #10970) or CD3/CD28 T Cell Activator (Catalog #10971)
tips: EB size strongly affects CD34+ output and is line-dependent: titrate the cells per microwell if CD34+ frequency is low
Seeding by total cell number instead of CD34+ number is acceptable if flow cytometry would delay plating
Seeding the maturation stage at the higher end of the density range raises the DP T cell frequency
hPSC-derived cultures are harvested at lymphoid day 28; the day-42 schedule in the manual applies to cord-blood cells only
pitfalls: Adherent cell overgrowth (≥ 50% of the surface) blocks contact with the coating material: move the suspension cells to a freshly coated well
Clumps left after EB dissociation reduce yield at CD34 selection: strain at 37 µm (DNase I may help)
Floating dead cells and debris collect in the centre of the well during maturation; viable cells stay near the coated surface, so aspirate the debris carefully
unverified: No DP T cell percentage or yield is stated in the PIS or manual text (efficiency set to null); only the intermediate benchmarks at EB day 12 and lymphoid day 14 are given

The manual numbers the EB stage (days 0-12) and the lymphoid stage (days 0-28) separately; the day values here are cumulative (lymphoid day 0 = EB day 12, assuming freshly isolated CD34+ cells are seeded the same day)
The protocol diagrams (sections 4.1, 5.1 and 5.2.1) are images and were not available in the text
The matrix for hPSC maintenance is not named in the protocol chapters read
Composition of all supplements and of the coating material is proprietary
In the PIS text the component table is scrambled by extraction; component catalogue numbers were taken from the manual's table

stages.name: EB formation and mesoderm induction (EB protocol days 0-3)
stages.base_medium: EB Formation Medium (EB Medium A + 10 µM Y-27632), then EB Medium A

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor in EB Formation Medium on day 0

stages.feeding: Day 2: half change (2.5 mL) with EB Medium A; day 3: half change with EB Medium B
actions: Pre-treat an AggreWell400 6-well plate with Anti-Adherence Rinsing Solution
Dissociate hPSCs with ACCUTASE (about 10 min at 37°C) to single cells and count
Add 3.5 x 10^6 cells per well in 5 mL EB Formation Medium (500 cells per microwell) and spin 100 x g for 3 min
Leave 2 days, then do the half changes slowly from the top of the well without lifting the EBs
stages.checkpoint: Uniform EBs in the microwells, usually within 24 h (some lines need up to 72 h)

stages.name: Hematopoietic specification in EB Medium B (EB protocol days 3-12)
stages.base_medium: EB Medium B (STEMdiff Hematopoietic - EB Basal Medium + Supplement B)
stages.feeding: Day 5: transfer EBs in 2.5 mL; day 7: add 2.5 mL; day 10: half change (2.5 mL)
actions: Day 5: flush EBs out of the microwells, catch them on a 37 µm reversible strainer, and wash them into 2.5 mL EB Medium B
Plate into one well of a non-tissue culture-treated 6-well plate and spread evenly
Day 7: add 2.5 mL EB Medium B; day 10: replace half the medium
stages.checkpoint: Loosely attached EBs with some adherent outgrowth are acceptable; avoid large fused clumps

stages.name: Lymphoid progenitor expansion (lymphoid protocol days 0-14)
stages.base_medium: StemSpan Lymphoid Progenitor Expansion Medium (StemSpan SFEM II + Lymphoid Progenitor Expansion Supplement)

factors.name: StemSpan Lymphoid Differentiation Coating Material (100X)
factors.role: plate coating, 1 in 100 in D-PBS, 2 h at room temperature or overnight at 2-8°C

stages.feeding: Lymphoid day 3 or 4: add 500 µL; day 7: half change plus transfer to a freshly coated well; day 10 or 11: half change (keep a 3-4 day rhythm)
actions: EB day 12: collect EBs, spin 300 x g, digest in 1 mL Collagenase Type II (2500 U/mL) for 20 min at 37°C, then add 3 mL TrypLE Express for another 20 min
Dilute with 6 mL DMEM/F-12, spin, strain if clumpy, and isolate CD34+ cells with EasySep Human CD34 Positive Selection Kit II (ES/iPS protocol, 2 magnet separations)
Coat a non-tissue culture-treated 24-well plate with Lymphoid Differentiation Coating Material (500 µL/well) and rinse with D-PBS
Seed 2.5 x 10^4 CD34+ cells per well in 500 µL (5 x 10^4 CD34+ cells/mL)
Lymphoid day 7: after the half change, gently resuspend the non-adherent cells and move them to a freshly coated well (earlier if adherent cells pass 50% confluence)
Lymphoid day 14: resuspend and harvest; cells can be frozen here in CryoStor CS10
stages.checkpoint: EB day 12 before selection: ≥ 15% CD34+ and ≥ 1 x 10^5 CD34+ cells per AggreWell400 6-well well; after selection > 50% CD34+. Lymphoid day 14: typically ≥ 20% CD5+CD7+ cells and ≥ 5 CD5+CD7+ cells per input CD34+ cell

stages.name: T cell progenitor maturation to DP T cells (lymphoid protocol days 14-28)
stages.base_medium: StemSpan T Cell Progenitor Maturation Medium (StemSpan SFEM II + T Cell Progenitor Maturation Supplement)

factors.name: StemSpan T Cell Progenitor Maturation Supplement (10X)
factors.role: T cell maturation supplement, 1 in 10 (composition proprietary)

factors.name: StemSpan Lymphoid Differentiation Coating Material (100X)
factors.role: coating for a fresh non-tissue culture-treated plate, 1 in 100 in D-PBS

stages.feeding: Lymphoid day 17 or 18: add 500 µL; day 21 and day 24 or 25: half changes (500 µL)
actions: Optional: remove dead cells by FACS at lymphoid day 14 to improve DP frequency and yield
Reseed on a freshly coated non-tissue culture-treated 24-well plate at 2.5 - 5 x 10^5 cells per well in 500 µL (0.5 - 1 x 10^6 cells/mL)
Feed on the 3-4 day rhythm, aspirating floating debris from the centre of the well without disturbing cells
Lymphoid day 28: resuspend and harvest; the suspension includes DP T cells
stages.checkpoint: Flow cytometry for CD3, CD4, CD8a, CD8β and TCRαβ

cell_types.name: Natural killer cells
cell_types.summary: Cytotoxic innate lymphocytes that kill tumour and virus-infected cells without HLA matching or prior antigen exposure. morphology.endpoint: Small to medium round, bright, non-adherent lymphocytes growing in loose clusters in suspension; after aAPC stimulation the clusters are large and the cells are visibly blastic.

protocols.name: Two-stage spin embryoid body to NK cells, feeder-free or on EL08-1D2
protocols.principle: Defined spin embryoid bodies made from 3,000 cells per well in BPEL with SCF, VEGF and BMP4 generate haematopoietic progenitors in 11 days; the whole bodies are then transferred into NK-supporting cytokines, with no cell sorting and no need for xenogeneic stroma, and the resulting NK cells are expanded on membrane-bound IL-21 aAPCs.

protocols.start_requirements: hESCs or iPSCs adapted to TrypLE single-cell passaging for at least 10 passages on low-density MEFs (later versions of this protocol start from feeder-free hPSCs instead). Dissociate, filter through 70 um and use only pure undifferentiated cultures.
tips: The feeder-free arm is the fully defined option and only costs a little expansion relative to EL08-1D2.
No sorting at any point, which is what makes this scalable.
Check the day-11 CD34/CD45 percentages for a new line before committing to a full run - but a low number does not mean the line cannot make NK cells.
pitfalls: Single-cell adaptation of the starting line took months in this version; use the later feeder-free variant (Zhu and Kaufman) if starting fresh.

cell_types.name: Somites / paraxial mesoderm
cell_types.summary: The transient paraxial mesoderm and somite stages that give rise to skeletal muscle, bone, cartilage and dermis, now reproducible in vitro within 3-6 days by timed Wnt, BMP, TGF-beta, FGF and hedgehog manipulation. They are the common starting point for musculoskeletal differentiation and the platform for studying human segmentation clock timing and segmentation disorders.
cell_types.maturation_note: Everything happens fast and the windows are short: Loh 2016 go pluripotent to anterior primitive streak in 24 h, to paraxial mesoderm by day 2, to 96.8 +/- 5.7% FOXC2-positive early somite by day 3, and to sclerotome or dermomyotome by day 5-6. Paraxial markers collapse within 6 hours of FGF/Wnt withdrawal, so stage transitions must be on time to the hour, not the day.

morphology.endpoint: A dense, uniform, almost featureless monolayer of small tightly packed cells: the somite stages have little distinctive morphology, which is exactly why marker checks matter. In 3D somitoid cultures, by contrast, you see a train of regularly spaced epithelial somite-like blocks budding off an elongating aggregate.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Fine clumps passaged onto Geltrex the day before, cultured overnight in maintenance medium with a ROCK inhibitor.

stages.label: Anterior primitive streak

stages.label: Paraxial mesoderm

stages.label: Early somite

stages.label: Sclerotome

stages.label: Dermomyotome (alternative)

protocols.name: Day-by-day pairwise fate choices: primitive streak, paraxial mesoderm, somite, sclerotome or dermomyotome
protocols.principle: At each branch point, apply the signals that specify the wanted fate while simultaneously blocking the signals that specify its alternative. Wnt on for primitive streak and paraxial mesoderm, Wnt and FGF off for somite, hedgehog on with Wnt off for sclerotome, or Wnt on with hedgehog off for dermomyotome. Each step takes 24 hours.
protocols.efficiency: 96.8 +/- 5.7% FOXC2+ early somite at day 3; 91.6 +/- 5.4% DLL1+ paraxial mesoderm at day 2 (97.0% of sorted DLL1+ cells co-expressed paraxial markers by scRNA-seq); 85.2 +/- 8.4% PDGFRA+ in day 5-6 sclerotome
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs (mainly H7) passaged about 1:12 to 1:20 as fine clumps with Accutase onto Geltrex-coated wells and cultured overnight in mTeSR1 with 1 uM thiazovivin. Differentiation starts the next morning in serum-free CDM2 basal medium.
tips: The underlying logic is explicit: every step both specifies the wanted fate and blocks the alternative, which is why each cocktail contains inhibitors as well as agonists.
The in vivo clock is 12-24 h per step (epiblast, primitive streak, paraxial mesoderm, early somite, sclerotome), and the in vitro protocol mirrors that, so do not stretch the stages.
DLL1 and PDGFRA give you sortable handles on paraxial mesoderm and sclerotome respectively, which is the cleanest way to remove off-target cells.
pitfalls: Marker transitions happen within hours (paraxial genes fall within 6 h of FGF/Wnt inhibition), so late medium changes blur stage identity.
Getting the primitive streak flavour wrong (anterior versus mid) sends everything downstream to lateral rather than paraxial fate.
Day-6 sclerotome formed ectopic bone in mice over 2-3 months, so these cells are potent; treat transplantation experiments accordingly.
unverified: CDM2 basal medium composition is given in the paper's Supplemental Procedures, which could not be read in this session.

factors.conc: 1 uM (or 1 uM XAV939 as an alternative)
factors.role: Wnt off; triggers segmentation into somites

stages.feeding: Single 24 h treatment
actions: Apply the quadruple-inhibition cocktail for 24 h
Expect paraxial markers to be suppressed within about 6 hours
stages.checkpoint: 96.8 +/- 5.7% FOXC2-positive early somite precursors at day 3

stages.name: Dermomyotome (dorsal branch, alternative)

factors.name: Vismodegib
factors.role: hedgehog inhibitor; blocks the sclerotome alternative

factors.name: BMP4
factors.role: sometimes added to the dermomyotome condition

actions: Treat day-3 somites with CHIR99021 plus vismodegib (with or without BMP4) for 48 h
stages.checkpoint: Dermomyotome identity at day 5 (the skeletal muscle precursor branch)

stages.name: Sclerotome (ventral branch)
actions: Treat day-3 somites with the hedgehog agonist plus Wnt-C59 for 48-72 h
Purify sclerotome on PDGFRA if needed
For cartilage, take day-6 sclerotome into 20 ng/ml BMP4 for 3-6 days; for fibroblast-like cells, take day-5 sclerotome into 10 ng/ml TGF-beta1 plus 2 ng/ml PDGF-BB for 72 h
stages.checkpoint: 85.2 +/- 8.4% PDGFRA-positive cells expressing FOXC2, PAX1 and PAX9 at day 5-6

protocols.name: Four-day somite induction benchmarked against human embryo somites
protocols.principle: A two-step, two-medium induction: a CHIR99021 pulse for paraxial mesoderm, then dual BMP and TGF-beta inhibition for somite formation, with the resulting cells compared directly against staged human embryonic somites and then pushed to muscle, bone or cartilage.
protocols.efficiency: Reported as TBX6-positive and PDGFRA-positive/KDR-negative fractions with means +/- SEM in figures; no single headline percentage
protocols.start_requirements: On day -1 dissociate hPSC colonies to single cells with TrypLE Express and seed on Matrigel-coated plates at 25,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 with 10 uM Y-27632.
tips: This four-day block is the shared trunk for the paper's myogenic (CHIR/FGF2 then HGF/IGF1), osteogenic (SAG/FGF2 then StemPro osteogenesis) and chondrogenic (SAG/FGF2 then StemPro chondrogenesis pellet) arms.
PDGFRA-positive/KDR-negative is a quick flow gate separating paraxial from lateral/endothelial mesoderm.
The in vivo benchmarking against staged human somites in the paper is a useful sanity check on your own marker panel.
pitfalls: Only two media are used, so there is little room to correct a drifting culture mid-run; seeding density on day -1 is the main lever.
The protocol does not separate sclerotome from dermomyotome; that happens in the downstream arms.
unverified: No single numeric purity figure for the day-4 somite stage is given in the text.

source.authors: Xi H, Fujiwara W, Gonzalez K, Jan M, et al.
source.title: In Vivo Human Somitogenesis Guides Somite Development from hPSCs

stages.name: Paraxial mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: BDM: DMEM/F12 with 1% ITS-G and 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin
stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Switch mTeSR1 to BDM plus 3 uM CHIR99021 on day 0
Feed daily for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: TBX6-positive paraxial mesoderm by immunofluorescence and flow

stages.name: Somite specification
stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Switch to BDM plus LDN193189 and SB431542 for 2 days
Score PDGFRA and KDR by flow at day 4
stages.checkpoint: PDGFRA-positive/KDR-negative somite-stage population at day 4

protocols.name: Presomitic mesoderm, somite and dermomyotome with a PAX3-GFP reporter
protocols.principle: Induce presomitic mesoderm with simultaneous Wnt activation, FGF, TGF-beta inhibition and BMP inhibition, sort DLL1-positive cells, then specify somite with a lower CHIR99021 dose plus TGF-beta inhibition and dermomyotome by adding BMP4. A PAX3-GFP reporter line quantifies each step.
protocols.efficiency: PAX3-GFP+ somite cells: 52.1 +/- 0.8% with SB431542 alone, 70.7 +/- 0.1% with 5 uM CHIR99021, 74.7 +/- 0.5% with both; only 0.3-0.7% with 10 uM CHIR99021
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs including a PAX3-GFP reporter line, pre-cultured for 3 days before the chemically defined induction begins.
tips: The CHIR99021 dose is stage-specific and non-monotonic: 10 uM is right for presomitic mesoderm and wrong (almost zero PAX3-GFP) for somite induction. This is the most important number in the protocol.
DLL1 sorting after presomitic mesoderm induction materially improves the somite step.
The paper's purpose was modelling fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, so patient-line comparisons are built into the system.
pitfalls: Carrying the presomitic CHIR99021 dose forward into the somite step destroys the induction.
Requires a FACS step and, for easy quantification, a PAX3 reporter.
Marker dynamics were measured in a reporter line; expect to re-titrate for other lines.
unverified: The CDM basal medium composition and the pre-culture medium are referenced to earlier work and were not verified here.

source.authors: Nakajima T, Shibata M, Nishio M, Nagata S, et al.
source.title: Modeling human somite development and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva with induced pluripotent stem cells

stages.name: Presomitic mesoderm induction

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt on for presomitic mesoderm

stages.feeding: 4 days in CDM with the four factors, after 3 days of pre-culture
actions: Pre-culture for 3 days
Induce presomitic mesoderm for 4 days with CHIR99021, FGF2, SB431542 and DMH1
Sort DLL1-positive presomitic mesoderm cells
stages.checkpoint: DLL1-positive presomitic mesoderm by flow at day 4

stages.name: Somite induction

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: lower-dose Wnt activation; note that 10 uM here abolishes somite induction

stages.feeding: 4 days
actions: Treat sorted DLL1-positive cells with 5 uM CHIR99021 plus 10 uM SB431542 for 4 days
Score PAX3-GFP and DLL1 by flow
stages.checkpoint: 74.7 +/- 0.5% PAX3-GFP-positive somite cells with the combined condition

stages.name: Dermomyotome induction
stages.feeding: 3 days
actions: Treat somite cells with 5 uM CHIR99021 plus 10 ng/ml BMP4 for 3 days
For myogenic cells, continue the dermomyotome in 5 uM CHIR99021 for 30 days
stages.checkpoint: Dermomyotome gene expression at day 3 of this stage, with myogenic differentiation on extended CHIR99021 culture

cell_types.notes: These are transient stages, so protocols are defined by timing as much as by reagents, and the CHIR99021 dose is both critical and stage-specific: 10 uM builds presomitic mesoderm in Nakajima 2018 but abolishes the subsequent somite step, where 5 uM is correct; Loh 2016 use 4 uM, then 3 uM, then Wnt inhibition on consecutive days. Always confirm the stage by marker, not by day count. Two sortable surface markers make this tractable: DLL1 for paraxial mesoderm and PDGFRA for sclerotome. For segmentation-clock work the relevant systems are 3D rather than monolayer: Matsuda et al. 2020 (Nature, PMID 32238941) recapitulate a roughly 5-hour human HES7 oscillation from hPSCs, Matsuda et al. 2020 (Science, PMID 32943519) show species-specific clock periods arise from differential biochemical reaction speeds, and Sanaki-Matsumiya et al. 2022 (Nat Commun, PMID 35484123) generate somitoids that bud epithelial somites periodically. Those papers' protocol parameters were not verified here.

cell_types.name: Adipocytes (white and brown)
cell_types.summary: Lipid-droplet-filled cells with the transcriptional programme of white, beige or brown fat, made by taking pluripotent cells to a mesenchymal or paraxial mesoderm progenitor and then applying an adipogenic cocktail (with or without forced PPARG2/PRDM16/CEBPB expression). They are used to study human adipocyte development, insulin signalling and lipolysis, to screen browning agents, and as transplantable thermogenic tissue in metabolic disease models.
cell_types.maturation_note: Once a progenitor pool exists, adipogenic induction is quick: Su 2018 call the beige adipocytes fully mature at day 12, and Ahfeldt 2012 run adipogenic medium for 21 days with doxycycline for the first 16. Getting to the progenitor takes longer (7 days of embryoid bodies plus about 5 days of outgrowth in Ahfeldt; 5 days of mesoderm induction plus 3-6 passages, 20-30 days, in Su). UCP1 induction in beige/brown cells needs a cAMP or beta-3 agonist challenge to be seen properly.

morphology.endpoint: Rounded cells packed with refractile lipid droplets that glow bright white against the plastic; white adipocytes carry one or a few large unilocular droplets, brown and beige cells many small multilocular ones. Oil red O turns the droplets red.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies in a defined medium on Geltrex or Matrigel.

stages.label: Embryoid bodies or mesoderm monolayer
stages.look: In the Ahfeldt route, free-floating aggregates after 7 days in low-adhesion plates; in the Su route, a dense FOXF1-positive monolayer after 5 days of mesoderm induction medium.

stages.label: Mesenchymal progenitors
stages.look: A fibroblast-like, spindle-shaped monolayer that passages readily and is over 96% positive for CD73, CD29, CD44 and CD105 in Ahfeldt 2012.

stages.label: Early lipid accumulation
stages.look: Scattered cells round up and small bright droplets appear in the cytoplasm.

stages.label: Mature adipocytes
stages.look: Most cells rounded and filled with droplets; the monolayer looks granular and highly refractile under phase contrast.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Ahfeldt 2012 note that hPSCs lack the mesenchymal surface markers that the progenitors acquire; residual OCT4 means residual undifferentiated cells.

markers.name: FOXF1
markers.note: Su 2018 report over 95% FOXF1-positive cells after 5 days in mesoderm induction medium; this is the branch point for their beige lineage.

markers.name: NT5E
markers.note: Ahfeldt 2012 found over 96% of the fibroblast-like progenitors positive for CD73, CD29, CD44 and CD105.

markers.name: PDGFRB
markers.note: Su 2018 characterise their FOXF1-derived MSCs as PDGFRB-positive mural cells, the proposed in vivo precursor of beige preadipocytes.

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Marks the subcutaneous adipogenic precursor population that responds to IL-4; Su 2018 validated their primary comparators as at least 95% PDGFRA-positive.

markers.name: PPARG
markers.note: The master adipogenic regulator; in Ahfeldt 2012 it is also the transgene (PPARG2) whose doxycycline-driven expression programmes the cells.

markers.name: CEBPA
markers.note: Ahfeldt 2012 counted CEBPA-positive nuclei: 88% of PPARG2-programmed differentiated progenitors versus 9% of unprogrammed ones.

markers.name: FABP4
markers.alias: aP2, adipocyte fatty acid binding protein
markers.note: Standard mature adipocyte marker in both white and brown cells.

markers.name: ADIPOQ
markers.note: Secreted; measure in conditioned medium as a functional maturity readout.

markers.name: LEP
markers.note: Usually low in vitro relative to primary white fat; useful as a comparative rather than absolute readout.

markers.name: UCP1
markers.note: The thermogenic readout; needs a cAMP or beta-3 adrenergic challenge for a fair measurement. Su 2018 remove rosiglitazone at day 12 and culture 4 more days before the beta-3 response assay.

markers.name: PRDM16
markers.note: Brown determination factor; Ahfeldt 2012 express it (with CEBPB) virally and used a primer that detects only endogenous PRDM16 to show programmed cells sustain the brown programme.

markers.name: PAX3
markers.note: Mohsen-Kanson 2014 identify PAX3 (with PRDM16 and DIO2) as marking brown rather than white adipocyte progenitors, and show ectopic PAX3 converts white progenitors to brown-like.

markers.name: MYH3
markers.note: Worth checking in paraxial-mesoderm-based brown adipocyte routes, since brown fat and skeletal muscle share a progenitor.

functional_assays: Oil red O staining and quantification
Lipolysis assay (glycerol release)
Insulin-stimulated glucose uptake
Oxygen consumption rate and uncoupled respiration (Seahorse)
Beta-3 adrenergic or cAMP-stimulated UCP1 induction
Transplantation and in vivo thermogenesis/energy expenditure measurement
qc: Over 96% of the progenitor pool CD73/CD29/CD44/CD105 positive before induction (Ahfeldt 2012)
CEBPA-positive nuclei around 88% after PPARG2 programming versus about 9% without (Ahfeldt 2012)
Over 95% FOXF1-positive cells at day 5 of mesoderm induction in the beige route (Su 2018)
Lipid droplets in the majority of cells by oil red O, with measurable glycerol release on lipolytic stimulation
For brown/beige cells, UCP1 induction on cAMP or beta-3 agonist challenge, not just baseline UCP1

protocols.name: Programming mesenchymal progenitors with doxycycline-inducible PPARG2 (white) or PPARG2 plus PRDM16/CEBPB (brown)
protocols.principle: Derive a mesenchymal progenitor pool from embryoid bodies, then transduce it with doxycycline-inducible PPARG2 (adding PRDM16 and CEBPB for brown fate) and differentiate in an adipogenic medium. The cells keep their adipocyte identity after the transgene is switched off.
protocols.efficiency: 85-90% programming efficiency to white or brown adipocyte fate; 88% of PPARG2-programmed differentiated progenitors were CEBPA-positive versus 9% of unprogrammed cells; lentiviral transduction efficiency about 98% (s.d. +/- 1%)
protocols.start_requirements: hESCs and hiPSCs cultured feeder-free on Geltrex in mTeSR1.
tips: Transduce at about 40% confluency, 24 h after passaging; this is when the authors found transduction most efficient.
Programmed adipocytes retain their identity after doxycycline withdrawal, so the transgene is a switch rather than a crutch.
The same progenitors can be compared directly with primary adipose-derived stromal vascular cells, which the paper derives in parallel.
pitfalls: Requires lentiviral transduction and therefore a genetically modified product.
Serum and human plasmanate make the system undefined and lot-sensitive.
Use progenitors before passage 8; later passages were not validated.
unverified: Concentrations of the lenti-PRDM16 and lenti-CEBPB supernatants used for brown programming are not stated separately in the methods text read here.

source.authors: Ahfeldt T, Schinzel RT, Lee YK, Hendrickson D, et al.
source.title: Programming human pluripotent stem cells into white and brown adipocytes

stages.name: Embryoid body formation
stages.feeding: Suspension culture for 7 days
actions: Disaggregate hPSCs with dispase into clumps of 5-10 cells
Transfer to low-adhesion 6-well plates (Corning Ultra Low Attachment) in DMEM with 15% FBS and 1% GlutaMAX
Culture in suspension for 7 days
stages.checkpoint: Even embryoid bodies after 7 days in suspension

stages.name: Outgrowth to mesenchymal progenitors
stages.feeding: Until confluent, about 5 days
actions: Replate the embryoid bodies on gelatin-coated 6-well dishes
Grow to confluence (about 5 days)
stages.checkpoint: Confluent outgrowth ready for trypsinisation

stages.name: Mesenchymal progenitor expansion
stages.base_medium: MPC growth medium: DMEM with 15% FBS, 1% GlutaMAX and 2.5 ng/ml FGF2 (bFGF)
stages.feeding: Routine feeding; passage 1:3
actions: Trypsinise with 0.25% trypsin and replate in MPC growth medium
Passage at a 1:3 split ratio and use before passage 8
Check the surface panel: over 96% CD73, CD29, CD44 and CD105 positive

stages.name: Lentiviral transduction

factors.name: lenti-rtTA
factors.conc: 500 ul per well of a 12-well plate (1000 ul per well of a 6-well plate)

factors.name: lenti-PPARG2
factors.conc: 500 ul per well of a 12-well plate (1000 ul per well of a 6-well plate)

factors.name: lenti-PRDM16 and lenti-CEBPB
factors.role: added with PPARG2 to programme brown rather than white adipocytes

actions: Transduce 24 h after passaging, at about 40% confluency
Incubate with viral supernatant for 4 h at 37 C
Remove the virus, wash with PBS and return to growth medium
stages.checkpoint: About 98% transduction efficiency by GFP control

stages.name: Adipogenic differentiation
stages.base_medium: Adipogenic differentiation medium: DMEM with 7.5% knockout serum replacement, 7.5% human plasmanate, 0.5% non-essential amino acids, 1% penicillin-streptomycin

factors.name: Doxycycline
factors.role: induces the PPARG2 (and PRDM16/CEBPB) transgenes; first 16 days only

stages.feeding: Adipogenic medium for 21 days; doxycycline for the first 16 days then withdrawn
actions: Switch to adipogenic differentiation medium with 700 ng/ml doxycycline
Keep doxycycline for 16 days
Withdraw doxycycline and maintain to day 21 or longer
Confirm the cells keep adipocyte identity after transgene withdrawal
stages.checkpoint: Lipid-laden adipocytes with 88% CEBPA-positive nuclei; identity maintained without doxycycline

protocols.name: FOXF1-derived MSCs to beige adipocytes with TGF-beta inhibition (and optional IL-4 priming)
protocols.principle: Take iPSCs through a serum-free mesoderm induction to a FOXF1-positive splanchnic mesoderm, expand PDGFRB-positive mural-like MSCs in a serum-free MSC medium, then differentiate them to beige adipocytes in a cocktail that includes the TGF-beta inhibitor SB431542, which overcomes the poor adipogenic potential of iPSC-derived MSCs.
protocols.efficiency: Over 95% FOXF1-positive cells at day 5 of mesoderm induction; MSC purity reported as highly pure after 3-6 passages
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs reprogrammed by a non-integrating method (skin fibroblast, cord blood or urine derived in this paper), in feeder-free culture.
tips: SB431542 is the key addition: without TGF-beta inhibition iPSC-derived MSCs are poorly adipogenic.
IL-4 pretreatment for 2 days together with SB431542 raised UCP1 synergistically and brought its induction forward, mirroring the in vivo type-2 immune browning pathway.
The same paper gives osteogenic (OsteoLife, 21 days) and chondrogenic (pellet, 24 days) protocols for the same MSCs, which is a convenient trilineage control.
pitfalls: Depends on two proprietary media for the first two stages, so those steps are not chemically defined.
Rosiglitazone must be withdrawn before beta-3 adrenergic assays or the response is masked.
The MSC stage takes 20-30 days and 3-6 passages; rushing it gives a poorly adipogenic culture.
unverified: Composition of STEMdiff Mesoderm Induction Medium and MesenCult-ACF Plus is proprietary and not stated in the paper.

source.authors: Su S, Guntur AR, Nguyen DC, Fakory SS, et al.
source.title: A renewable source of human beige adipocytes for development of therapies to treat metabolic syndrome

stages.name: Mesoderm induction

factors.name: STEMdiff Mesoderm Induction Medium
factors.role: serum-free commercial mesoderm induction medium (composition proprietary)

stages.feeding: Monolayer culture for 5 days per the medium's instructions
actions: Culture iPSCs as a monolayer in mesoderm induction medium from day 1 to day 5
stages.checkpoint: Over 95% FOXF1-positive cells by immunofluorescence, confirmed by qPCR and western blot

stages.name: FOXF1-derived MSC expansion
stages.base_medium: MesenCult-ACF Plus medium (serum-free, STEMCELL Technologies 05445) on MesenCult-ACF attachment substrate
stages.feeding: Continuous culture with passaging; 3-6 passages over 20-30 days
