Passage 3-6 times over 20-30 days
Check the MSC and perivascular panel by flow at about passage 6 (day 30)
stages.checkpoint: Highly pure MSC-like population with mural markers including PDGFRB, and expression of TGF-beta ligands and receptors

stages.name: Beige adipocyte induction

factors.name: SB431542
factors.role: TGF-beta inhibitor; unlocks the adipogenic potential of iPSC-derived MSCs and promotes browning

stages.feeding: Beige induction medium for the first phase of the 12-day differentiation
actions: Switch confluent FD-MSCs to beige adipocyte induction medium
Optionally pre-treat with IL-4 for 2 days, with or without SB431542, which synergistically increases UCP1 and brings its induction forward
stages.checkpoint: Lipid droplets forming and UCP1 transcription rising

stages.name: Beige adipocyte maintenance and maturation

factors.name: Rosiglitazone
factors.role: PPAR gamma agonist; removed at day 12 before beta-3 response assays

stages.feeding: Maintenance medium to full maturity at day 12 of differentiation
actions: Switch to beige maintenance medium (induction medium minus IBMX, dexamethasone and indomethacin)
Call the cells mature at day 12 of differentiation
For beta-3 adrenergic response assays, remove rosiglitazone at day 12 and culture 4 more days
To 'whiten' the cells for comparison, replace the medium with DMEM plus 10% FBS and change 100% every 2 days for 6 days
stages.checkpoint: Mature multilocular adipocytes at day 12 with measurable UCP1 and thermogenic respiration

protocols.name: Brown adipocytes via a paraxial mesoderm intermediate
protocols.principle: Brown fat and skeletal muscle share a paraxial mesoderm origin, so directing hPSCs through a defined paraxial mesoderm progenitor state before adipogenic induction produces functional brown adipocytes at high efficiency rather than the white-biased cells obtained from mesenchymal progenitors.
protocols.efficiency: Described as generating brown adipocytes at high efficiency; no numeric percentage could be confirmed from the accessible text
protocols.start_requirements: Human pluripotent stem cells in feeder-free culture; precise starting density and matrix not verified.
tips: If you need thermogenically competent brown (rather than beige) adipocytes, the developmental origin of the progenitor appears to matter more than the adipogenic cocktail.
The paper includes a molecular map of regulatory networks along the brown adipocyte lineage, useful for benchmarking.
Check for residual skeletal myogenic cells, since the progenitor is shared with muscle.
pitfalls: Protocol parameters could not be verified here, so treat the staging above as a skeleton only.
Paraxial mesoderm is also the muscle progenitor, so myogenic contamination is a plausible off-target.
unverified: All media, growth factor and small-molecule concentrations, stage durations and day boundaries: the Cell Stem Cell paper is not open access and only the abstract could be read in this session (day_start/day_end set to null where unknown).
Numeric differentiation efficiency not confirmed.

source.authors: Zhang L, Avery J, Yin A, Singh AM, et al.
source.title: Generation of functional brown adipocytes from human pluripotent stem cells via progression through a paraxial mesoderm state

stages.name: Paraxial mesoderm induction
actions: Direct hPSCs into a paraxial mesoderm progenitor state (the shared origin of brown fat and skeletal muscle)
Confirm the paraxial identity before adipogenic induction
stages.checkpoint: Paraxial mesoderm progenitor state established

stages.name: Brown adipocyte differentiation
actions: Apply adipogenic differentiation to the paraxial mesoderm progenitors
Assess thermogenic function: glycolysis, uncoupled respiration and lipolysis, and their response to cAMP-dependent signalling
For in vivo work, transplant into the interscapular region of recipient mice and measure thermogenic activity, respiratory exchange ratio and whole-body energy expenditure
stages.checkpoint: Elevated uncoupled respiration and lipolysis responsive to cAMP signalling; in vivo engraftment reduces circulating glucose in hyperglycaemic animals

cell_types.notes: White, beige and brown are three different products and the route determines which you get. Mesenchymal-progenitor routes (Ahfeldt 2012, Su 2018) give white or beige cells; the paraxial mesoderm route (Zhang 2020) is the one aimed at genuine brown adipocytes, consistent with brown fat and skeletal muscle sharing a progenitor. Mohsen-Kanson et al. 2014 (Stem Cells, PMID 24302443) separate brown and white adipocyte progenitors from hiPSCs and identify PAX3, PRDM16 and DIO2 as brown progenitor markers, with BMP4 and HOX genes marking white progenitors; it is not open access and its protocol parameters could not be verified here. Two practical points: iPSC-derived MSCs are poorly adipogenic unless TGF-beta is inhibited (SB431542), and UCP1 must be measured after a cAMP or beta-3 adrenergic challenge, with rosiglitazone withdrawn first, or you will underestimate thermogenic capacity.

cell_types.name: Mesenchymal stromal cells (iMSC)
cell_types.summary: Fibroblast-like, plastic-adherent cells that carry the standard MSC surface signature (CD73, CD90, CD105 positive, CD45 negative) and differentiate to bone, cartilage and fat. The iPSC-derived version gives an inexhaustible, donor-matched substitute for bone-marrow MSCs for regenerative and immunomodulation studies, and is the usual starting material for osteogenic, chondrogenic and adipogenic assays.
cell_types.maturation_note: Surface markers appear fast but the population only becomes stable with passaging: Fukuta 2014 saw CD73/CD105/CD44 rise within 48 h of the medium switch and the transition from neural crest to MSC complete by about passage 3, while Chen 2012 reach a stable MSC-like culture at roughly 20 days. Trilineage potential should be re-checked every few passages.

morphology.endpoint: A confluent lawn of flat, spindle-shaped, fibroblast-like cells with a whorled or parallel arrangement at high density, indistinguishable by eye from bone-marrow MSCs.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies with defined edges on Matrigel or laminin in a defined maintenance medium.

stages.label: Intermediate (neural crest or mesendoderm)
stages.look: Cells migrate out of the colonies as a dense, cuboidal sheet; in the neural crest route the outgrowth is p75/TFAP2A positive while cells still inside the colony stay PAX6 positive.

stages.label: Early MSC-like cells
stages.look: Cells elongate and lose the tight epithelial packing; morphology changes noticeably about 4 days after the medium switch.

stages.label: Expanded iMSC
stages.look: Uniform spindle-shaped fibroblast-like monolayer that tolerates weekly trypsin passaging at low density.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be lost. Fukuta 2014 found pluripotency transcripts below detection and no SSEA4-positive cells in the final iMSCs.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Residual expression means residual undifferentiated cells and teratoma risk.

markers.name: NGFR
markers.note: The sorting gate in the Fukuta route: about 35-41% p75-high cells after 7 days with SB431542 plus CHIR99021. Falls within 48 h of the MSC medium switch.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Neural crest identity; drops rapidly once MSC medium is applied.

markers.name: TFAP2A
markers.note: Marks the migratory outgrowth; declines gradually to passage 3.

markers.name: NT5E
markers.note: Core ISCT positive marker; rises within 48 h of the switch to MSC medium in Fukuta 2014.

markers.name: ENG
markers.note: Core ISCT positive marker; reaches bone-marrow-MSC levels by about passage 2.

markers.name: THY1
markers.note: Core ISCT positive marker, reported for the Chen 2012 iMSCs.

markers.name: CD44
markers.note: Routinely included in the iMSC panel in both routes.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: Must be negative; the ISCT definition requires absence of haematopoietic markers.

markers.name: PECAM1
markers.note: Should be absent; Chen 2012 report CD31-negative iMSCs.

markers.name: RUNX2
markers.note: Read out after osteogenic challenge, not in the undifferentiated iMSC.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Read out after chondrogenic pellet or micromass challenge.

markers.name: PPARG
markers.note: Read out after adipogenic challenge; iPSC-derived MSCs are often poorly adipogenic unless TGF-beta is inhibited.

functional_assays: Trilineage differentiation (alizarin red, safranin-O/alcian blue, oil red O)
Plastic adherence and colony-forming unit fibroblast assay
Population doubling and passage stability
Immunomodulation assays, e.g. interferon-gamma-induced HLA expression
In vivo perfusion recovery in hindlimb ischaemia models
qc: CD73, CD90, CD105 and CD44 positive and CD45 negative by flow (ISCT criteria)
No SSEA4-positive cells and pluripotency transcripts below detection before any in vivo use (Fukuta 2014)
Osteogenic, chondrogenic and adipogenic differentiation demonstrated after derivation
Normal karyotype after expansion

protocols.name: Single small molecule: 10 days of SB431542, then serum MSC medium
protocols.principle: Blocking TGF-beta/activin signalling for ten days drives a confluent hiPSC culture out of pluripotency and into a mesengenic intermediate; switching to a standard serum MSC medium and passaging at decreasing density then selects a stable MSC-like population.
protocols.efficiency: 96% of day-10 SB431542-treated cells were EpCAM-negative/NCAM-positive; the final MSC-like cells are reported as marker-positive without a stated percentage
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs grown in mTeSR1 on Matrigel-coated vessels (Matrigel at 100 ug/ml in DMEM/Ham's F-12, 1 h at room temperature) and allowed to reach confluence before induction.
tips: The protocol needs only one small molecule, which makes it the cheapest route to iMSCs.
Stepping the seeding density down with each passage is part of the selection, not an afterthought.
Expect CD73/CD105 to appear only after the switch to serum MSC medium, not during SB431542 treatment.
pitfalls: Serum-containing MSC medium makes this route less suitable for clinical translation than defined alternatives.
The paper gives marker positivity qualitatively; set your own purity gate.
Non-heat-inactivated serum is specified; lot-to-lot serum variation is a real source of failure.
unverified: Final percentage purity for CD73/CD90/CD105/CD45 in the MSC-like population is not stated in the paper.
The Results section describes the MSC medium as DMEM-HG plus 10% fetal bovine serum while the Methods specify fetal calf serum with gentamicin; the discrepancy is in the source.

source.authors: Chen YS, Pelekanos RA, Ellis RL, Horne R, et al.
source.title: Small molecule mesengenic induction of human induced pluripotent stem cells to generate mesenchymal stem/stromal cells

stages.name: Mesengenic induction
stages.base_medium: KOSR medium without bFGF: DMEM/Ham's F-12 with 20% knockout serum replacement, 1 mM L-glutamine, 10 mM non-essential amino acids

factors.name: SB431542
factors.role: TGF-beta/activin receptor inhibitor; drives exit from pluripotency towards mesenchyme

stages.feeding: KOSR plus SB431542 replaced daily for 10 days
actions: Grow hiPSCs to confluence in mTeSR1 on Matrigel
Switch to KOSR without bFGF plus 10 uM SB431542
Replace the medium daily for 10 days
At day 10 passage as single cells with TrypLE Select
stages.checkpoint: About 96% EpCAM-negative/NCAM-positive cells at day 10; CD73 and CD105 still largely negative at this point

stages.name: MSC selection and expansion
stages.base_medium: DMEM high glucose with 10% non-heat-inactivated fetal calf serum, 2 mM L-glutamine, 50 U/ml penicillin-streptomycin, 20 ug/ml gentamicin
stages.feeding: Routine MSC feeding with passaging at decreasing seeding density
actions: Seed the day-10 cells (MP0) at 40,000 cells/cm2 in MSC medium
Seed MP1 at 20,000 cells/cm2
Seed later passages at 10,000 cells/cm2
Continue to about day 20, by which point the culture is MSC-like
stages.checkpoint: By passage 6 the cells express CD73, CD90, CD105, CD29, CD44 and CD146 and lack CD45, CD34, CD14, CD11b, HLA-DR, CD31 and CD117

protocols.name: Via neural crest: SB431542 plus CHIR99021 in chemically defined medium, then MSC medium
protocols.principle: Cranial neural crest is a physiological source of mesenchymal cells for the craniofacial skeleton. Inhibiting TGF-beta while weakly activating Wnt in a chemically defined medium produces p75-high neural crest cells in 7 days; those cells convert to MSCs over about three passages in MSC medium. Everything can be done xeno-free.
protocols.efficiency: About 35% p75-high cells with SB431542 alone, rising with 1 uM CHIR99021; 40.9 +/- 5.5% under the fully xeno-free StemFit/iMatrix conditions
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs transferred to feeder-free culture: dissociate colonies into clumps of about 10 cells, seed on Matrigel-coated dishes at 2-4 clumps/cm2 and culture in mTeSR1 for 2 days. For the xeno-free version, seed single cells on iMatrix-coated dishes in StemFit and culture 5 days.
tips: CHIR99021 helps only up to 1 uM; higher doses sharply reduce the p75-high fraction.
The protocol is deliberately BMP-independent: adding BMP4 inhibits induction, but so do BMP inhibitors (DMH1, LDN193189, Noggin), so leave BMP signalling alone.
The whole route, including osteogenic induction with STK3, can be run under chemically defined xeno-free conditions.
pitfalls: Seeding density changes the balance between central nervous system and neural crest fate; follow the stated clump and cell densities.
Neural crest cells grow very slowly in the induction medium itself; move them to the EGF/FGF2 medium if you need numbers.
The transition from neural crest to MSC takes until about passage 3, so do not judge marker profiles too early.

stages.name: Neural crest induction
stages.base_medium: Chemically defined medium (CDM): IMDM/Ham's F-12 1:1, 1x chemically defined lipid concentrate, 15 ug/ml apo-transferrin, 450 uM monothioglycerol, 5 mg/ml purified BSA, 7 ug/ml insulin, penicillin-streptomycin

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt activation, dose-dependent up to 1 uM only

stages.feeding: CDM with both compounds, refreshed through the 7-day induction
actions: Replace mTeSR1 (or StemFit) with CDM plus 10 uM SB431542 and 1 uM CHIR99021
Let cells migrate out of the colonies over 7 days (7-10 days under xeno-free conditions)
Harvest and sort on p75 (NGFR) expression to isolate the p75-high fraction, or carry the bulk culture forward
stages.checkpoint: p75-high fraction around 35-41% by flow; outgrowing cells stain for p75 and TFAP2A while cells left in colonies are PAX6-positive

actions: If you need more cells, expand the sorted neural crest cells in CDM with SB431542, EGF and FGF2 rather than the induction medium, which supports very poor growth
Stable expansion was shown over 10 passages with retained TFAP2A expression
stages.checkpoint: Expanded cells keep neural crest morphology and global expression profile (r = 0.96-0.98 versus passage 0)

stages.name: MSC induction and passaging
stages.base_medium: Alpha-MEM with 10% fetal bovine serum (or, xeno-free, STK2 MSC medium on fibronectin-coated dishes)
stages.feeding: Weekly passaging with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA at 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2
actions: Plate neural crest cells at 6.5 x 10^4 cells/cm2 in CDM with 10 uM SB431542 and 1 uM CHIR99021
The next day switch to alpha-MEM plus 10% FBS (or STK2 for defined conditions)
Expect the morphology to change about 4 days later
Passage weekly at 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2; analyse MSC markers 14 days after induction
stages.checkpoint: CD73, CD105 and CD44 positive and CD45 negative by flow; cuboidal morphology becomes fibroblastic by about passage 3

protocols.name: Clonal iMSC lines isolated by CD24-negative/CD105-positive sorting
protocols.principle: Differentiate hiPSCs under a clinically compliant protocol and then purify MSC-like cells by sorting out the CD24-negative, CD105-positive fraction, so the resulting lines are monoclonal and karyotypically stable.
protocols.efficiency: Three monoclonal, karyotypically stable, functional MSC-like cultures were isolated
protocols.start_requirements: Human iPSCs differentiated under what the authors describe as a clinically compliant protocol; the starting culture conditions are not stated in the abstract.
materials: Anti-CD24 and anti-CD105 antibodies for FACS
tips: The CD24-negative/CD105-positive gate is the distinctive part of this protocol and is worth borrowing even on top of other induction routes.
The authors report these iMSCs outperform adult bone-marrow MSCs in a hindlimb ischaemia model, attributed to better survival and engraftment.
A later Methods in Molecular Biology chapter from the same group (Lian et al. 2016, PMID 27236679) sets out the directed differentiation in protocol form.
pitfalls: Clonal derivation means line-to-line variation between clones; characterise each clone separately.
Without the full methods, timings and media here have to be taken from the primary paper.

Day boundaries for both stages are unknown (set to null).

stages.name: MSC differentiation
actions: Induce MSC differentiation from hiPSCs under the authors' clinically compliant protocol
stages.checkpoint: Loss of pluripotency-associated markers

stages.name: Sorting and clonal expansion
actions: Sort cells on CD24-negative and CD105-positive expression
Expand sorted cells as monoclonal lines
Confirm MSC surface antigens, absence of pluripotency markers and trilineage differentiation
stages.checkpoint: MSC surface antigen profile with adipocyte, osteocyte and chondrocyte differentiation and a normal karyotype

protocols.name: STEMdiff Mesenchymal Progenitor Kit (induction, then MesenCult-ACF Plus expansion)
protocols.principle: Defined, animal component-free workflow: four days in STEMdiff-ACF Mesenchymal Induction Medium make early mesoderm, two days in MesenCult-ACF Plus Medium follow, and from day 6 the cells are passaged on Animal Component-Free Cell Attachment Substrate until, by day 21, they look and type like mesenchymal progenitor cells with trilineage potential.
protocols.efficiency: > 90% of cells express CD73, CD105 and CD146 on day 21
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8, ready for passage (large compact colonies with dense centres). On day -2 plate single cells (Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent) on tissue culture-treated 6-well plates coated with Corning Matrigel (mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus) or Vitronectin XF (TeSR-E8) in 3 mL maintenance medium + 10 µM Y-27632 at 5 x 10^4 cells/cm2 (mTeSR1 or TeSR-E8 cultures) or 1-2.5 x 10^4 cells/cm2 (mTeSR Plus cultures); about 30-50% confluent on day -1.
materials: STEMdiff Mesenchymal Progenitor Kit (05240): STEMdiff-ACF Mesenchymal Induction Medium 100 mL, MesenCult-ACF Plus Medium 500 mL, MesenCult-ACF Plus 500X Supplement 1 mL, Animal Component-Free Cell Attachment Substrate 1 mL
Corning Matrigel hESC-Qualified Matrix (Corning 354277) or Vitronectin XF (07180)
tips: Use polypropylene tubes during subculture so the cells do not stick.
Complete MesenCult-ACF Plus Medium keeps only 1 week at 2-8°C and must not be frozen; thawed induction medium keeps 1 month.
Adipogenic differentiation of PSC-derived MPCs works best after day 40 (passage 10 or later); MesenCult differentiation media: adipogenic 05412, osteogenic 05465, chondrogenic 05455.
Use only tissue culture-treated cultureware.
pitfalls: Warming MesenCult-ACF Plus or the dissociation reagents at 37°C; the PIS says room temperature only.
Leaving cells in the ACF enzyme for more than 7 minutes.
Lines kept in mTeSR Plus need a lower plating density (1-2.5 x 10^4 cells/cm2) than those in mTeSR1 or TeSR-E8.
unverified: mTeSR Plus catalogue number: this PIS prints 05825, whereas the other STEMCELL sheets in this set print 100-0276; left out of the materials line.
The exact days of each passage between day 6 and day 21 are not fixed (every 3-6 days at about 80% confluence).
The extracted text has scrambled step numbers in places (table and numbered lists merged), so step cross-references could not be checked.
The protocol diagram is an image and was not available.

stages.name: Phase 1: single-cell plating and recovery
stages.base_medium: TeSR maintenance medium (mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8)
stages.feeding: Day -2: 3 mL plating medium; day -1: change to 2 mL medium without Y-27632
actions: Coat a 6-well plate with Matrigel or Vitronectin XF and bring to room temperature for at least 30 min
Rinse with D-PBS, treat with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent 8-10 min at 37°C and pipette to single cells
Spin 300 x g for 5 min, count and plate at the density for your maintenance medium
Seed spare wells for qPCR on day 4 and flow cytometry on day 21
stages.checkpoint: About 30-50% confluent on day -1

stages.name: Phase 2: early mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff-ACF Mesenchymal Induction Medium (complete as supplied)
stages.feeding: Daily full change, 3 mL per 6-well, on days 0, 1, 2 and 3
actions: Day 0: wash once with 1 mL D-PBS and add room-temperature induction medium
Change daily
stages.checkpoint: Day 4 qPCR: Brachyury, NCAM and MIXL1 up; OCT4, SOX2, NANOG and EpCAM down

stages.name: Phase 3a: switch to MesenCult-ACF Plus
stages.base_medium: Complete MesenCult-ACF Plus Medium (MesenCult-ACF Plus Medium + 500X Supplement + 2 mM L-Glutamine)
stages.feeding: 2 mL per 6-well on day 4 and day 5
actions: Warm the medium to room temperature only, never at 37°C
Day 4: wash once with D-PBS and change to complete MesenCult-ACF Plus
Day 5: change again

stages.name: Phase 3b: passage and expand on ACF attachment substrate
stages.feeding: After the day 6 passage: daily half-medium changes for about 3-6 days; from passage 2 no routine changes unless cells begin to detach
actions: Day 6: detach with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (8-10 min at 37°C, scrape any stragglers), spin 300 x g for 7 min in polypropylene tubes and plate at 1.5-10 x 10^3 cells/cm2 in 3 mL medium + 10 µM Y-27632 on substrate-coated tissue culture-treated plates
Passage at about 80% confluence, every 3-6 days
From the second passage use the Animal Component-Free Cell Dissociation Kit (enzyme 3-6 min at 37°C, never over 7 min, then inhibitor), spin 300 x g for 8 min and plate in 2 mL without Y-27632
Plating density falls with passage: 3-8 x 10^3 (passage 1-2), 1.5-6 x 10^3 (2-3), 1.5-3 x 10^3 cells/cm2 (3-4 and later)
stages.checkpoint: Day 21 (about passage 5-6): spindle MPC-like cells, > 90% CD73+ CD105+ CD146+, negative for CD45, CD34, CD144 and CD31; OCT4 and TRA-1-60 absent

cell_types.notes: Beware of what 'iMSC' means in a given paper: the ISCT surface panel is easy to satisfy and tells you very little about origin or potency. The three routes here arrive at the same flow profile through different embryology (TGF-beta-blocked mesenchyme, cranial neural crest, or sorted CD24-/CD105+ clones), and their differentiation biases differ accordingly. iPSC-derived MSCs are notoriously poorly adipogenic compared with bone-marrow MSCs; Su et al. 2018 overcome this by adding the TGF-beta inhibitor SB431542 during adipogenic induction. Re-test trilineage potential and karyotype every few passages, and confirm the absence of SSEA4-positive cells and pluripotency transcripts before any transplantation experiment.

cell_types.name: Skeletal muscle
cell_types.summary: Myogenic progenitors and multinucleated, striated muscle fibres made from mouse ES or iPS cells, either by steering a monolayer through presomitic mesoderm with Wnt activation and BMP inhibition, or by switching on Pax3 in embryoid bodies and sorting paraxial mesoderm. They are used to study myogenesis, fusion and satellite-cell formation, to model muscular dystrophy (for example mdx cells), and as a source of engraftable progenitors.
cell_types.maturation_note: First myogenin+ myocytes after about 1 week; multinucleated fibres from 10-14 days; striated, contracting fibres with Pax7+ cells alongside at 2-3 weeks. In serum-based medium cultures last more than 2 months; Pax7+ cells decline after 3-4 weeks.

morphology.endpoint: Long, thin, multinucleated fibres, often millimetres in length and lying in parallel bundles, with cross-striations at high power and small mononucleated cells tucked alongside them. In serum-based medium many fibres twitch spontaneously.

stages.label: ES cells plated
stages.look: Small compact ES colonies on gelatin shortly after plating at low density.

stages.label: Mesoderm induction
stages.look: Colonies flatten and merge into a dense sheet of small cells as they respond to the Wnt activator.

stages.label: Pax3+ mesenchyme
stages.look: Loosely packed mesenchymal-looking cells, without the rosettes seen in neural cultures.

stages.label: Myocytes
stages.look: Elongated, spindle-shaped mononucleated myocytes appear in streams and increase in number.

stages.label: Myotubes
stages.look: Myocytes fuse into multinucleated fibres that lengthen and cover large areas of the well.

stages.label: Striated fibres
stages.look: Millimetre-long striated fibres, some contracting, with small Pax7+ cells lying between them.

markers.name: Pou5f1
markers.note: Should be lost during mesoderm induction; residual undifferentiated cells are the teratoma risk in transplantation work.

markers.name: Msgn1
markers.note: Posterior presomitic mesoderm; 45-65% reporter+ cells at day 4 in serum-free RDL medium.

markers.name: Tbx6
markers.note: Co-expressed with the Msgn1 reporter in most cells at day 4.

markers.name: Pax3
markers.note: Anterior presomitic/somitic and early myogenic progenitors; needs LDN193189. Also a neural marker, so confirm the cells are mesenchymal and Sox2-negative.

markers.name: Meox1
markers.note: Somitic marker that rises with Pax3.

markers.name: Pdgfra
markers.note: Paraxial mesoderm surface marker used with Flk-1 for sorting; not specific on its own.

markers.name: Pax7
markers.note: Myogenic progenitor and satellite-like cells lying along fibres at 2-3 weeks; numbers fall after 3-4 weeks.

markers.name: Myf5
markers.note: Early myogenic factor; abundant in proliferating Pax3-induced progenitors.

markers.name: Myod1
markers.note: Committed myoblasts; myotube nuclei are MyoD+ and myogenin+.

markers.name: Myog
markers.note: Differentiating myocytes; 25-30% of cells at day 10 in the serum-free protocol.

markers.name: Myh3
markers.alias: embryonic myosin heavy chain (eMyHC); fast MyHC antibodies also used
markers.note: Sarcomeric myosin in new myotubes; the papers stain with fast, perinatal and slow MyHC antibodies.

markers.name: Dmd
markers.note: Sub-sarcolemmal dystrophin is a maturation sign; absent in mdx-derived fibres.

markers.name: Kdr
markers.note: Lateral plate/haemato-endothelial mesoderm; sort or gate it out (PDGFRa+ Flk-1-).

markers.name: Foxf1
markers.note: Lateral plate mesoderm; rises together with Bmp4 when BMP inhibition is too weak.

functional_assays: Spontaneous contraction of fibres (video)
Fusion index (nuclei in MyHC+ multinucleated cells)
Sarcomere striation by MyHC or titin staining
Engraftment into cardiotoxin-injured or dystrophic mouse muscle (dystrophin+ fibres)
qc: Pax3-GFP+ about 30-50% at day 6 (serum-free) or 20-40% at day 5 (serum-based RDL); about 1% without LDN193189
Myogenin+ cells 25-30% at day 10 (serum-free protocol)
Fusion index about 82% for sorted, expanded Pax3-induced progenitors (Filareto 2013)
Unsorted Pax3-induced embryoid body cells form teratomas; transplant only the PDGFRa+ Flk-1- fraction

protocols.name: Serum-free monolayer: BMP4 priming, then Rspo3 (or CHIR99021) + LDN193189 presomitic mesoderm route
protocols.principle: Mouse ES cells are first pushed to an epiblast-like state, then given a Wnt activator (R-spondin 3 or CHIR99021) together with the BMP inhibitor LDN193189 so that they form presomitic mesoderm instead of lateral plate. HGF, IGF-1 and FGF-2 then carry the Pax3+ cells through myogenesis to striated fibres with associated Pax7+ cells, with no transgene or sorting.
protocols.efficiency: 45-65% Msgn1-reporter+ cells after 4 days; about 30-50% Pax3-GFP+ cells after 6 days in RDL or CDL medium; myogenin+ cells 25-30% of the culture at day 10 (figures from the authors' submitted manuscript).
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ES cells maintained on mitomycin-C-inactivated fibroblast feeders in DMEM + 15% FBS with LIF (1,500 U/ml) and 2i, then passaged once onto gelatin-coated, feeder-free plates before differentiation. Trypsinise and plate on gelatin-coated wells directly into the first differentiation medium.
materials: Reporter ES lines used by the authors: Msgn1-repV, Pax3-GFP, Myog-repV, Pax7-GFP
tips: The follow-up paper from the same lab reports that a serum-based version gives longer-lived, more mature and spontaneously contracting mouse fibres than this serum-free version (see the Chal 2018 protocol).
The number of Pax7+ cells falls after 3-4 weeks in culture.
The human protocol (Chal 2016 Nat Protoc) uses different doses and timing; do not transfer its numbers to mouse cells.
pitfalls: Without strong BMP inhibition the Wnt-treated cells make Bmp4 and drift to a lateral plate fate.
Pax3 also marks neural precursors; Pax3+ cells from this protocol should look mesenchymal and be Sox2-negative.
unverified: Read from the authors' submitted manuscript deposited in HAL (inserm-01484878), not the final Nat Biotechnol version; concentrations, days and percentages may differ slightly in the published Online Methods.
Plating density: the manuscript says only 'various densities' (96-, 24- and 6-well plates); the 2018 follow-up used about 10,000-20,000 cells/cm2.
Feeding interval during days 0-8 is not stated; 'every other day' is given for the long-term phase.
End day 21 is nominal; the authors analysed cultures from day 9 to 3-4 weeks.

factors.name: LDN193189
factors.role: BMP inhibitor; blocks drift to lateral plate mesoderm and allows Pax3+ anterior presomitic fate

actions: Switch to RDL (Rspo3 + DMSO + LDN) or CDL (CHIR + DMSO + LDN) medium for 4 days

actions: Replace RDL/CDL with HIFL medium for 2 days

protocols.name: Serum-based monolayer: Rspo3/DMSO/LDN (RDL), brief FGF inhibition, then 2% horse serum
protocols.principle: The mouse-specific refinement: presomitic mesoderm is induced with R-spondin 3 (or CHIR99021), DMSO and LDN193189 in serum-containing medium; a 2-day step without Wnt activator and with an FGF receptor inhibitor then releases the cells into myogenesis, and 2% horse serum supports long-lived, contracting fibres.
protocols.efficiency: Up to 20-40% Pax3-GFP+ cells by day 5 in RDL medium (about 1% without LDN193189); roughly 10,000-15,000 fibres within 3-5 weeks from a well seeded with 20,000-30,000 ES cells.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ES cells maintained as in Chal 2015 (feeders, serum, LIF and 2i, with one feeder-free passage before use). Plate about 10,000-20,000 cells/cm2 on gelatin-coated dishes.
materials: Antibodies for sorting or QC: PDGFRa (APA5), VEGFR2/Flk-1 (Avas12a)
tips: Myocytes did not form when cells were left in RDL/CDL after day 6 or grown in plain 15% FBS medium.
LDN193189 works best when present from day 0 of the RDL step.
Pax7+ cells are plentiful at 2-3 weeks and drop sharply after 4 weeks.
The paper's Methods call PD173074 a MEK inhibitor while the Results call it an FGF inhibitor; it is sold as an FGF receptor inhibitor.
pitfalls: PDGFRa alone does not identify presomitic cells here: it also marked about 75% of Msgn1-negative cells, and a quarter of Msgn1+ cells were Flk-1+.
Serum lots differ; the Wnt/BMP balance may need re-titration with a new FBS batch (general caution, not from the paper).
unverified: Day numbering assumes the optional 2-day NK1 step is counted as days 0-2 so that the PdL step starts at day 6, as the text states ('4-6 days in RDL', 'day 6 cultures'). The exact schedule is in supplementary Table S1, which was not opened. Without NK1, RDL would run from day 0 to day 6.
Base of the 'DMEM-based' and 2% horse serum media (other supplements) is in the supplementary Methods, not read.
Whether DMSO and Rspo3 are both kept in the reduced-serum phase is stated only as 'supplemented as indicated above'.
Feeding interval before day 8: not stated in the main text.

protocols.name: Doxycycline-inducible Pax3 in embryoid bodies, sorted PDGFRa+ Flk-1- progenitors
protocols.principle: Embryoid bodies make very little paraxial mesoderm on their own. Switching on a Pax3 transgene with doxycycline during embryoid body differentiation boosts paraxial mesoderm and its myogenic potential; sorting PDGFRa+ Flk-1- cells then removes residual undifferentiated cells and gives expandable myogenic progenitors that engraft in dystrophic muscle.
protocols.start_requirements: A mouse ES cell line carrying a doxycycline-inducible Pax3 transgene (iPax3). Embryoid bodies are made by the hanging-drop method.
tips: Later papers from the lab used doxycycline at 0.75-1 µg/ml from day 2 for the related iPax7 line, and 0.8 µg/ml from day 3 for iPax3 iPS cells.
FACS staining in the lab's later papers: antibodies at 1 µg per 10^6 cells in 100 µl PBS + 2% FBS for 30 min at 4 C, after Fc block at 0.25 µg per 10^6 cells.
See the Filareto 2013 protocol for a fully specified version of the same approach applied to mouse iPS cells.
pitfalls: Unsorted Pax3-induced cells form teratomas on transplantation; the PDGFRa+ Flk-1- sort is what removes residual undifferentiated cells.
The method needs a genetically modified line and a cell sorter.
unverified: The full text of Darabi 2008 (Nat Med) could not be opened. Hanging-drop embryoid bodies, doxycycline from day 2 to day 5, the day 5 PDGFRa+ Flk-1- sort and 7-10 days of expansion with doxycycline are taken from Darabi 2009 Exp Neurol (PMID 19682990), which restates the method.
Doxycycline concentration in the original paper: not confirmed (left blank).
Embryoid body medium composition, cells per hanging drop and whether embryoid bodies were transferred to suspension: not confirmed.
Expansion medium composition in the original paper: not confirmed.
The terminal differentiation step (low-glucose DMEM + 2% horse serum for about 1 week) is from Darabi 2011 Stem Cell Rev Rep (PMID 21461712) on iPax7 iPS cells, not from the 2008 paper.
Yield and percentage of PDGFRa+ Flk-1- cells: not confirmed.
Stage 3 and 4 days (5-13, 13-20) are nominal, built from the restated '7-10 days' and 'about 1 week'.

stages.base_medium: Same medium with doxycycline (later papers from the lab add bFGF, horse serum and chick embryo extract)

factors.name: Doxycycline
factors.role: Keeps Pax3 on so progenitors proliferate without differentiating

actions: Plate the sorted cells as a monolayer and expand for 7-10 days with doxycycline
Use at this point for transplantation or for in vitro differentiation
stages.checkpoint: Proliferating mononucleated cells positive for Pax3 and Myf5, with little MyHC

stages.name: Terminal differentiation

factors.name: Horse serum
factors.role: Low-mitogen medium; with doxycycline withdrawn, cells fuse into myotubes

Assess by immunofluorescence after about 1 week

protocols.name: Inducible Pax3 in mouse iPS cells: rotating embryoid bodies, PDGFRa+ Flk-1- sort, bFGF expansion
protocols.principle: The Pax3-induction approach applied to mouse iPS cells and written out in full: suspension embryoid bodies on a rotator, doxycycline for 2 days, a sort for PDGFRa+ Flk-1- paraxial mesoderm, expansion with doxycycline and bFGF, and differentiation in horse serum.
protocols.efficiency: Fusion index 82% ± 8% when the sorted, expanded progenitors were differentiated into myotubes.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse iPS (or ES) cells carrying doxycycline-inducible Pax3. Trypsinise and plate at 50,000 cells/cm2 on mouse embryonic fibroblast feeders; 3 days later, remove feeders by pre-plating on gelatin for 1 h in embryoid body medium.
materials: iPax3 mouse iPS or ES cells
Table rotator (70 rpm) in the incubator
tips: The expanded progenitors are M-cadherin+ by flow in this paper.
The same lab's earlier ES cell papers start doxycycline on day 2 rather than day 3.
pitfalls: Skipping the feeder-depletion step puts fibroblasts into the embryoid bodies.
Transgene induction is required: the lab's work shows that uninduced embryoid bodies yield very few myogenic cells.
unverified: Embryoid body medium composition: not given in the section read.

Length of the expansion and differentiation phases is not stated in this paper's methods; days 5-13 and 13-20 follow the '7-10 days' expansion and 'about 1 week' differentiation quoted in the lab's other papers (Darabi 2009, Darabi 2011).
Passaging schedule during expansion: not stated.

cell_types.notes: There are two families of method. The transgene-free monolayer route (Chal) needs careful control of Wnt and BMP signalling and gives mixed cultures of fibres, Pax7+ cells and non-muscle cells. The Pax3-induction route (Darabi/Perlingeiro) needs an engineered line and a cell sorter but gives a nearly pure, expandable progenitor population suited to transplantation. Chal 2015 was read as the authors' submitted manuscript and Darabi 2008 only through restating papers; see each protocol's unverified list. Do not use numbers from the human protocol (Chal 2016 Nat Protoc) for mouse cells.

cell_types.name: Osteoblasts (bone)
cell_types.summary: RUNX2- and SP7-positive bone-forming cells that deposit a collagen type I matrix and mineralise it into alizarin-red-positive nodules. iPSC-derived osteoblasts are used to model skeletal disease (for example fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and other heritable bone disorders), to screen bone-augmentation compounds, and as a cell source for bone tissue engineering.
cell_types.maturation_note: Osteoblast transcripts (RUNX2, SP7) rise within the first week, but mineralisation takes longer: alizarin red and von Kossa staining become clear at days 19-23 in the Kanke/Zujur small-molecule routes, and the StemPro osteogenesis route in Xi 2017 runs for 28 days after the somite stage. Nodules keep mineralising if the culture is held longer.

morphology.endpoint: A dense layer of cuboidal to polygonal cells overlaid by refractile matrix, with dark, three-dimensional mineral nodules visible by phase contrast and strongly alizarin-red positive.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies on vitronectin in a defined medium, taken to about 70% confluence before induction.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Colonies break up under high-dose CHIR99021; cells form clusters and the sheet looks uneven. Substantial cell death at this step is expected.

stages.label: Osteoblast induction
stages.look: Replated cells form a dense proliferating monolayer that begins to look granular.

stages.label: Early mineralisation
stages.look: Small dark nodules appear within cell clusters; alizarin red staining is clearly positive.

stages.label: Mineralised osteoblast layer
stages.look: Confluent layer with multiple dense mineral nodules, RUNX2 throughout the clusters and SP7 concentrated at their periphery.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Downregulated throughout; Zujur 2020 also track ZFP42/REX1 as a second exit-from-pluripotency marker.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Transiently up at day 3-5 of the CHIR/cyclopamine mesoderm step; 20 uM CHIR gave the best T and MIXL1 induction in Zujur 2020.

markers.name: MIXL1
markers.note: Second mesoderm readout, significantly higher at 20 uM than 15 uM CHIR99021.

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Loh 2016 used PDGFRA to purify sclerotome (85.2 +/- 8.4% of day 5-6 cultures), which is the osteogenic precursor in the paraxial route.

markers.name: RUNX2
markers.note: Master osteogenic transcription factor; Kanke 2014 found it evenly expressed across day-23 hiPSC-derived cell clusters.

markers.name: SP7
markers.note: Downstream of RUNX2 and more specific for committed osteoblasts; concentrated at the periphery of clusters at day 23.

markers.name: COL1A1
markers.note: Main bone matrix protein; the 2.3 kb Col1a1-GFP reporter is the classic osteoblast reporter in these protocols.

markers.name: ALPL
markers.note: Enzymatic activity stain is the quickest functional osteoblast readout, though it is also high in hPSCs, so use it after pluripotency is lost.

markers.name: IBSP
markers.note: Significantly upregulated at days 19-23 in hiPSCs in Kanke 2014.

markers.name: BGLAP
markers.note: Late mineralisation marker; clearly induced in the mouse arm of Kanke 2014.

markers.name: SPP1
markers.note: Commonly reported alongside IBSP and BGLAP in osteogenic panels.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Should stay low; SOX1/SOX2 induction indicates ectodermal drift, which Zujur 2020 monitored across CHIR doses.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Checked in Zujur 2020 and not significantly altered at any CHIR concentration tested.

markers.name: ACAN
markers.note: Cartilage drift is the usual off-target in sclerotome-derived osteogenic cultures.

functional_assays: Alizarin red staining and quantification
Von Kossa staining
Alkaline phosphatase activity assay
Col1a1-GFP (2.3 kb) reporter expression
Micro-CT or mechanical testing of engineered bone constructs
Ectopic bone formation after subcutaneous implantation in immunodeficient mice
qc: TBXT and MIXL1 transiently up at the end of mesoderm induction, with SOX1 and SOX17 not induced (Zujur 2020)
RUNX2 and SP7 protein detectable by immunofluorescence at day 21-23
Alizarin red staining significantly above the day-5 baseline (Kanke 2014, Zujur 2020)
NANOG and REX1 downregulated relative to day 0 before any transplantation

protocols.name: Xeno-free small-molecule osteoblasts: CHIR/cyclopamine, then SAG and a helioxanthin derivative
protocols.principle: Three phases with defined small molecules only: activate Wnt and block hedgehog to make mesoderm, then switch hedgehog on with SAG together with the helioxanthin derivative TH to induce osteoblasts, and finally mature the cells in osteogenic medium alone. The whole protocol runs on Essential 8/vitronectin with no Matrigel and no serum.
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs adapted over 6-10 passages to Essential 8 medium on recombinant human vitronectin-coated dishes (5 ug/ml), grown in 6-well plates to 70% confluence (day 0).
materials: TH (helioxanthin derivative, e.g. Tokyo Chemical Industry M3085)
tips: Dropping CHIR99021 from 30 uM (the original mouse-derived protocol) and shortening treatment to 3 days was what allowed the switch from Matrigel to vitronectin without losing cells.
FGF2 in the osteoblast induction medium measurably improves COL1A1 and RUNX2 induction.
The same group also ran the protocol on Cellnest recombinant collagen peptide scaffolds for 3D bone constructs.
pitfalls: High-dose CHIR99021 kills cells on vitronectin; this is the main reason the xeno-free version uses 15-20 uM for only 3 days.
TH is not a catalogue-standard reagent in every country and its target is unknown.
Concentrations in the dose titration (20 uM CHIR) differ slightly from the final xeno-free protocol (15 uM); follow the protocol section, not the titration.
unverified: No purity or percentage efficiency is reported for the osteoblast population.

source.authors: Zujur D, Kanke K, Onodera S, Tani S, et al.

factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt on, drives mesoderm

Apply CHIR99021 with 5 uM cyclopamine in xeno-free basal medium for 3 days
Change medium every day
stages.checkpoint: TBXT and MIXL1 up at day 3, NANOG and REX1 down, SOX1 and SOX17 not induced

stages.name: Osteoblast induction
stages.base_medium: Xeno-free osteogenic (OG) medium: the xeno-free basal medium plus 50 ug/ml ascorbic acid phosphate, 10 mM beta-glycerophosphate, 0.1 uM dexamethasone and 100 ng/ml FGF2

factors.name: SAG
factors.role: smoothened agonist; hedgehog on for osteoblast induction

factors.name: TH (helioxanthin derivative)
factors.role: osteoblast-promoting small molecule; molecular target not established

On day 4 dissociate with Accutase and replate onto vitronectin-coated 12-well plates at 2.5-3 x 10^5 cells per well
Continue SAG plus TH to day 10, changing medium daily
stages.checkpoint: COL1A1 and RUNX2 up at day 10; FGF2 in the medium significantly improved this step

stages.name: Osteoblast differentiation (CHIR/TH)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: Wnt reactivation to push osteoblast differentiation

stages.feeding: Daily medium change for 2 days
actions: From day 10, treat for 2 days with 4.5 uM CHIR99021 plus 1 uM TH in xeno-free OG medium
stages.checkpoint: Osteoblast marker expression at day 14 higher with TH plus CHIR than with TH plus SAG

stages.base_medium: Xeno-free osteogenic medium with no inducers

Stain with alizarin red to confirm mineralisation
stages.checkpoint: Mineralised, alizarin-red-positive culture by day 21

protocols.name: Four small molecules (CHIR99021, cyclopamine, SAG, TH) in serum-free feeder-free culture
protocols.principle: The original three-phase small-molecule strategy: Wnt activation with hedgehog blockade for mesoderm, then hedgehog agonism with the helioxanthin derivative TH for osteoblast induction, then maturation in osteogenic medium. Published with full concentrations for mouse ESCs/iPSCs and applied to hiPSCs with modifications.
protocols.efficiency: Reported as marker induction and alizarin-red quantification rather than a purity percentage; mineralisation at days 19 and 23 significantly above day 5 in hiPSCs
protocols.start_requirements: For hiPSCs, Matrigel-coated plates (the authors note substantial hiPSC death on Matrigel during the first 5 days and flag this as a limitation). For mESCs, 100,000 cells/cm2 on gelatin-coated 6-well plates with 24 h in 2i medium first.
materials: TH (available on request from the authors)
Von Kossa and alizarin red reagents
tips: Running Runx2-knockout mESCs through the protocol recapitulated the Runx2-null bone phenotype, which makes this a good platform for genetic studies.
The 2.3 kb Col1a1-GFP reporter can be used to sort the osteoblasts out of the culture.
For human cells, prefer the later xeno-free version (Zujur 2020) which fixes the Matrigel and cell-death problems.
pitfalls: The authors report substantial hiPSC death on Matrigel during the first 5 days of induction.
TH's molecular target was unknown at publication.
Human gene expression kinetics differ from mouse (the authors attribute this to hedgehog signalling differences), so do not expect the mouse timeline to transfer exactly.
unverified: The exact hiPSC-specific modifications (basal medium, CHIR99021 and cyclopamine concentrations, stage lengths) are in the Supplemental Experimental Procedures, which could not be read in this session; the concentrations listed here are those given for the mouse arm in the main text.
No osteoblast purity percentage is reported.

factors.name: Cyclopamine
factors.role: hedgehog antagonist; required for efficient mesoderm induction

actions: Culture for 5 days in basal medium with CHIR99021 and cyclopamine
Expect colonies to break up and re-form clusters
Replace medium daily
stages.checkpoint: T (TBXT) and MIXL1 transiently up at day 5; NANOG down; RUNX2 and SP7 already rising in hiPSCs at this point

stages.base_medium: Basal medium with 50 ug/ml ascorbic acid phosphate, 10 mM beta-glycerophosphate and 0.1 uM dexamethasone
stages.feeding: Media replaced daily for 14 days

Replace medium daily

protocols.name: Somite induction, SAG plus FGF2, then commercial osteogenesis medium
protocols.principle: Make a defined somite stage in four days, ventralise it towards sclerotome with a smoothened agonist and FGF2, then hand the cells to a standard osteogenesis differentiation medium for a month. Useful when you want one somite induction to feed muscle, bone and cartilage arms in parallel.
protocols.start_requirements: On day -1 seed single hPSCs on Matrigel-coated plates at 25,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 with 10 uM Y-27632.
tips: Days 0-6 are shared with this paper's chondrogenic arm, which splits off into a StemPro Chondrogenesis pellet at day 6, and days 0-4 are shared with the myogenic arm.
The replating at day 4 at a defined 35,000 cells/cm2 is part of the osteogenic branch and is easy to overlook.
Use the commercial osteogenesis medium as supplied; this protocol deliberately does not define its own osteogenic cocktail.
pitfalls: Relies on a proprietary differentiation medium, so the late phase is not chemically defined.
No purity percentage or mineralisation quantification is reported for the osteogenic arm.
unverified: Osteogenic efficiency/purity and mineralisation quantification are not reported in this paper.

stages.checkpoint: TBX6-positive paraxial mesoderm

stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Replace with BDM plus LDN193189 and SB431542 for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: Somite stage at day 4, PDGFRA+/KDR- by flow

stages.name: Sclerotome/osteogenic priming

factors.name: FGF2
factors.role: survival and proliferation of the replated culture

factors.role: hedgehog on; ventralises somite towards sclerotome

Replate on Matrigel at 35,000 cells/cm2 in BDM with FGF2 and SAG
Culture 2 days

cell_types.notes: Decide first whether you want osteoblasts through paraxial mesoderm/sclerotome (the route for axial and appendicular bone; Loh 2016, Xi 2017) or through the small-molecule mesoderm route (Kanke 2014, Zujur 2020), since disease-relevant cell identity may depend on the developmental origin. Reported outputs are almost always marker expression plus alizarin red quantification, not percentage purity, so decide your acceptance criterion in advance. For patient-specific bone phenotypes the most sophisticated system is Kawai et al. 2019 (Nat Biomed Eng, PMID 31182836), which generates self-organising in vitro bone-like nodules from patient iPSCs that reproduce pathological bone phenotypes; it is not open access and its protocol parameters could not be verified in this session. Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva lines are a well-characterised model in this area: Matsumoto et al. 2013 (Orphanet J Rare Dis, PMID 24321451) showed increased mineralisation and cartilage formation in patient iPSCs, and Hino et al. 2015 (PNAS, PMID 26621707) traced it to a neofunction of mutant ACVR1.

cell_types.name: Skeletal muscle (myotubes and satellite-like cells)
cell_types.summary: Multinucleated skeletal myotubes and the PAX7-positive progenitors that sit alongside them, made by walking a pluripotent culture through presomitic mesoderm, somite and dermomyotome. People use them to model Duchenne and other dystrophies, to screen drugs on contractile human fibres, and as a source of transplantable myogenic progenitors.
cell_types.maturation_note: Transgene-free monolayer routes are slow: MYOG-positive myocytes appear around day 10-12 and PAX7-positive progenitors after about two weeks (Al Tanoury 2020), while the Shelton CHIR route needs 40-50 days for MYH-positive myotubes. Replating the day-21 culture into SkGM-2 and then a low-CHIR fusion medium gives millimetre-long striated fibres within about a week. Inducible PAX7 or MYOD1 lines reach myotubes far faster but need a transgene.

morphology.endpoint: Long, aligned, multinucleated fibres with visible cross-striations lying over a bed of smaller mononucleated cells. In good cultures the fibres reach a millimetre or more and twitch spontaneously; unfused reserve cells with small bright nuclei sit between them.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat, tightly packed colonies with sharp edges on Matrigel, Geltrex or vitronectin, typically 40-70% confluent at the start of differentiation.

stages.label: Paraxial/presomitic mesoderm
stages.look: Colony borders break down into a dense, fairly uniform sheet of small cells; proliferation slows noticeably compared with untreated wells.

stages.label: Somite and dermomyotome
stages.look: A packed sheet with three-dimensional clusters and ridges rising out of the monolayer; cells are small and refractile.

stages.label: Myocytes appearing
stages.look: Bipolar, elongated cells become obvious among the flatter background cells and begin to align with each other in patches.

stages.label: Myotubes
stages.look: Broad aligned bundles of multinucleated fibres, often with faint striations, that occasionally contract; mononucleated progenitors persist between the fibres.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be gone within the first few days; Shelton 2014 report a sharp drop in SOX2/NANOG/OCT4 by day 2 of CHIR99021.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Peaks at day 2 in the CHIR route; Shelton 2014 counted 91 +/- 6% T-positive nuclei at this point.

markers.name: MSGN1
markers.note: Paraxial-specific; distinguishes a true presomitic response from the lateral/cardiac mesoderm you get with BMP4 plus activin A.

markers.name: TBX6
markers.note: Up with MSGN1 at day 2 and down again by day 8.

markers.name: PAX3
markers.note: Shelton 2014 report 58 +/- 10% PAX3-positive cells at day 8 versus 1 +/- 1% in untreated wells.

markers.name: PAX7
markers.note: The satellite-like readout. Shelton 2014: 43 +/- 4% at day 50. Al Tanoury 2020 report roughly 20-25% PAX7-Venus-positive mononucleated cells between days 20 and 30.

markers.name: MYF5
markers.note: One of the myogenic regulatory factors; rises from about day 25 in the Shelton route.

markers.name: MYOD1
markers.note: Commitment marker. Also the transgene used in the Maffioletti/Tedesco inducible route.

markers.name: MYOG
markers.note: Al Tanoury 2020 see MYOG-Venus myocytes from day 10, peaking at 12-15% of mononucleated cells at three weeks.

markers.name: MYH3
markers.note: Embryonic isoform dominates in vitro; mature adult isoforms stay low without extra stimulation.

markers.name: MYH1
markers.alias: fast skeletal myosin heavy chain (MY-32 antigen)
markers.note: MF20 and MY-32 pan/fast myosin antibodies are the usual fibre stain; Shelton 2014 report 47 +/- 3% MYH-positive cells at day 50.

markers.name: DES
markers.note: Broad muscle cytoskeletal marker; useful when myosin staining is still weak.

markers.name: NKX2-5
markers.note: Should be low. BMP4 plus activin A instead of CHIR drives cardiac rather than skeletal muscle (Shelton 2014).

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Low levels of neural crest transcripts appear early in the CHIR monolayer route; worth checking if yields are poor.

functional_assays: Spontaneous twitch contraction by phase-contrast or video microscopy
Electrical or optical pacing of myotube contraction
Calcium transients on stimulation
Fusion index from multinucleated MYH-positive fibres
Engraftment and DYSTROPHIN restoration in dystrophic mouse muscle
qc: TBXT-positive nuclei > 85% at day 2 in the CHIR route (Shelton 2014 report 91 +/- 6%)
PAX3-positive cells well above background at day 8 (58 +/- 10% in Shelton 2014)
PAX7-positive plus MYH-positive cells together around 90% of the day-50 culture in the Shelton route
Myotubes multinucleated and striated by immunofluorescence, not just elongated

protocols.name: Chal/Pourquie serum-free route via presomitic mesoderm, with replating for long fibres
protocols.principle: Mimic the embryo: switch Wnt on and BMP off to hold cells in a presomitic state, then let them run forward through somite and dermomyotome to myogenic cells without any transgene or cell sorting. Replating the primary culture into a myoblast growth medium and then a low-CHIR fusion medium produces long striated fibres.
protocols.efficiency: About 20-25% PAX7-Venus+ and 12-15% MYOG-Venus+ mononucleated cells at 3 weeks; roughly 30% of the culture myogenic (PAX7+ or MYOG+) at 3-4 weeks
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs on Matrigel or Geltrex in a defined maintenance medium, passaged as small clumps and differentiated as a subconfluent monolayer. Al Tanoury 2020 used NCRM1 and PAX7-Venus/MYOG-Venus reporter iPSC lines.
tips: The primary three-week phase is where most failures happen; check for PAX7 and MYOG by immunofluorescence before committing to replating.
Replating is what produces long fibres: primary cultures alone give short, poorly aligned myotubes.
Reporter lines (PAX7-Venus, MYOG-Venus) make the protocol far easier to troubleshoot, though they are not required.
pitfalls: The PAX7-positive fraction declines after three weeks, so time the replating rather than letting primary cultures run on.
Myogenic yield is only around 30% of the culture even in a good run; the rest is non-myogenic mesoderm.
DAPT shifts the balance towards differentiation and will deplete the satellite-like pool.
unverified: Concentrations and exact day boundaries of CHIR99021, LDN193189, FGF2, HGF and IGF1 in the primary phase: these live in Chal et al. 2016 Nat Protoc (PMID 27583644), which is not open access and could not be read in this session.
Basal medium formulation for the primary phase (Chal 2016) not verified.
