protocols.name: Two-day CHIR99021 pulse, then FGF2 and N2 (serum-free, transgene-free)
protocols.principle: A short, strong GSK3-inhibitor pulse pushes almost the whole monolayer into paraxial mesoderm; FGF2 then expands the PAX3/PAX7 progenitor pool while holding back the myogenic regulatory factors, and an N2 medium finally lets the cells commit and fuse.
protocols.efficiency: 91 +/- 6% TBXT+ at day 2; 58 +/- 10% PAX3+ at day 8; at day 50, 43 +/- 4% PAX7+ and 47 +/- 3% MYH+ (about 90% myogenic)
protocols.start_requirements: H9 hESCs maintained feeder-free on Matrigel in E8. Plate 1.5 x 10^5 cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 12-well plate in E8 with 10 uM Y-27632 overnight before starting. Seeding density is critical: below 1 x 10^5 cells/ml survival drops even with ROCK inhibitor.
materials: Antibodies to TBXT, PAX3, PAX7, MF20
tips: Ten micromolar CHIR99021 for exactly two days beat both 2.5 uM and longer exposures in the authors' titration.
Total cell number grows about 20-fold from day 0 to day 50, and about 42% of day-50 PAX7-positive cells still incorporate EdU, so the progenitor pool is genuinely proliferative.
Forskolin, which helps in aggregate-based protocols, gave no extra benefit in this monolayer system.
pitfalls: Seeding density is the single most important variable; sparse wells die or differentiate off-target.
BMP4 plus activin A instead of CHIR gives cardiac, not skeletal, muscle.
Low levels of neural crest transcripts are present early and about 10% of the day-50 culture is neither PAX7+ nor MYH+.

source.authors: Shelton M, Metz J, Liu J, Carpenedo RL, et al.
source.title: Derivation and expansion of PAX7-positive muscle progenitors from human and mouse embryonic stem cells

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
stages.feeding: Daily medium change; 0.1% DMSO is the vehicle control
actions: Replace overnight E8 with E6 plus 10 uM CHIR99021
Keep for exactly 2 days: longer or weaker (2.5 uM) treatment gave less paraxial mesoderm
Change medium daily
stages.checkpoint: TBXT-positive nuclei around 90% at day 2; cells look visibly different from vehicle controls

stages.name: Spontaneous somite/dermomyotome progression
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Wash out CHIR99021 at day 2
Culture in plain E6 and watch for three-dimensional cell clusters by day 8
stages.checkpoint: PAX3-positive cells around 58% at day 8 and visible 3D clusters

stages.name: Progenitor expansion
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Switch to StemPro-34 for days 12-20 to expand the PAX3/PAX7 progenitor pool while suppressing early myogenic regulatory factors
stages.checkpoint: Dense culture with a growing mononucleated progenitor population

stages.name: Return to basal medium
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Return to E6 from day 20 to day 35
stages.checkpoint: PAX7, MYF5, MYOD1 and MYOG transcripts clearly up by day 25

stages.name: Terminal differentiation
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Switch to N2 medium at day 35
Expect the first myocytes about 5 days later (day 40)
Hold to day 50 for large aligned myocyte/myotube fields
stages.checkpoint: 47 +/- 3% MYH-positive cells and 43 +/- 4% PAX7-positive cells at day 50; spontaneous contractions visible

protocols.name: Four-day somite induction, then CHIR/FGF2 and an HGF/IGF1 fusion medium
protocols.principle: Build a somite stage first with a CHIR pulse followed by dual BMP and TGF-beta inhibition, then take the somite cells towards myogenic fate with CHIR plus FGF2 and finish in a KSR medium with HGF and IGF1. Day-29 cells can be dissociated, expanded in SkGM-2 and refused in N2 medium.
protocols.start_requirements: On day -1 dissociate hPSC colonies to single cells with TrypLE Express and seed on Matrigel-coated plates at 25,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 with 10 uM Y-27632.
tips: The same first four days feed the authors' osteogenic and chondrogenic routes, so one somite induction can be split three ways.
FGF2 at the day 4-6 step is there for survival of a very dense culture, not for patterning.
The N2 fusion step is taken from Shelton 2014 and works on replated, expanded progenitors.
pitfalls: Seeding at day -1 must give an even monolayer; patchy wells differentiate unevenly.
The paper reports marker dynamics rather than a single purity figure, so set your own acceptance threshold on TBX6 and PDGFRA.
unverified: No overall myogenic purity percentage is given for the day-27 or replated cultures in this paper.

source.authors: Xi H, Fujiwara W, Gonzalez K, Jan M, et al.
source.title: In Vivo Human Somitogenesis Guides Somite Development from hPSCs

stages.name: Paraxial mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: BDM: DMEM/F12 with 1% ITS-G and 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin
stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Switch mTeSR1 to BDM plus 3 uM CHIR99021 on day 0
Feed daily for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: TBX6-positive paraxial mesoderm by immunofluorescence/flow

stages.name: Somite specification
stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Replace the CHIR medium with BDM plus LDN193189 and SB431542 for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: Somite-stage culture at day 4, PDGFRA+/KDR- by flow

stages.name: Myogenic commitment

factors.name: FGF2
factors.role: supports survival of the dense culture

stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: On day 4 switch to BDM with 3 uM CHIR99021 and 20 ng/ml FGF2 for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: Dense culture surviving the transition without large gaps

stages.name: Myotube differentiation
stages.base_medium: DMEM with 15% knockout serum replacement and 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin
stages.feeding: Every other day after day 6
actions: Switch to the KSR/HGF/IGF1 medium on day 6
Keep for 14-21 days, feeding every other day
stages.checkpoint: Myogenic markers by immunofluorescence at day 27

stages.name: Optional replating and fusion
stages.base_medium: SkGM-2 then N2 medium (BDM with 1% N2 supplement)
stages.feeding: SkGM-2 plus FGF2 for 7-10 days, then N2 medium for 5 days
actions: At day 29 dissociate with collagenase IV then TrypLE, filter through 100 um and 40 um strainers
Replate at 15,000-20,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in SkGM-2 plus 20 ng/ml FGF2
Grow 7-10 days to over 70% confluence, then switch to N2 medium for 5 days to trigger fusion
stages.checkpoint: Fused multinucleated myotubes after 5 days in N2 medium

protocols.name: STEMdiff Myogenic Progenitor Supplement Kit (Media A-D for 30 days, then MyoCult)
protocols.principle: Four serum-free supplements, each diluted in DMEM/F-12, are applied in sequence with daily feeding (A days 0-1, B days 2-3, C days 4-5, D days 6-29) to turn a sparse hPSC monolayer into a dense multilayered culture of CD56+ CD82+ myogenic progenitors. On day 30 the cells are dissociated, expanded in MyoCult-SF Expansion Medium and can be fused into MyHC+ myotubes with MyoCult Differentiation Medium.
protocols.start_requirements: High-quality hPSCs (strong OCT4 and TRA-1-60) kept as clumps in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8 on Corning Matrigel-coated 6-well plates. On day -1 dissociate to single cells with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent and plate 30,000-40,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in 2 mL maintenance medium + 10 µM Y-27632. Colonies must contain about 10-30 cells on day 0.
materials: STEMdiff Myogenic Progenitor Supplement Kit (100-0151): Supplement A (100X) 240 µL, Supplement B (100X) 240 µL, Supplement C (100X) 240 µL, Supplement D (5X) 60 mL
tips: The seeding range (30,000-40,000 cells/cm2) exists because lines grow at different rates; optimise it per line using the day 0 and day 2 checkpoints.
Media A-D keep 4 weeks at 2-8°C once made; warm to room temperature before use.
Expand the day 30 cells for at least one passage in MyoCult-SF Expansion Medium before differentiating them to myotubes.
pitfalls: Continuing when the culture is under 80% confluent on day 2; the PIS says to stop and reseed.
Starting from hPSCs with poor pluripotency marker expression.
The dense day 30 culture needs the full TrypLE plus collagenase and trituration sequence to come apart.
unverified: Efficiency: no percentage of CD56+/CD82+ progenitors or MyHC+ myotubes is stated.
Expansion stage: no day count is given (cells are passaged whenever 60-80% confluent), so the expansion step is folded into the day-30 stage as an action.

Myotube stage: its start depends on how long expansion takes, so it is folded into the day-30 stage as an action; the PIS gives 5 days in MyoCult Differentiation Medium plus up to 5 more after a half-change, preceded by an unspecified time to reach 95-100% confluence.
Composition and preparation of MyoCult-SF Expansion Medium and MyoCult Differentiation Medium are in their own sheets, not in this PIS.
The protocol diagram is an image and was not available.

stages.name: Day -1: single-cell plating
stages.base_medium: mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-E8 + 10 µM Y-27632
stages.feeding: No feeding for 24 h; do not disturb
actions: Coat a 6-well tissue culture-treated plate with Matrigel (at room temperature for at least 1 h before use)
Rinse with D-PBS, treat with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent 8-10 min at 37°C, pipette 3-4 times, spin 300 x g for 5 min
Resuspend in medium + Y-27632, count and plate 30,000-40,000 cells/cm2
Shake the plate back-and-forth and side-to-side to spread the cells
stages.checkpoint: Day 0: small colonies of about 10-30 cells; if not, reseed at a corrected density

stages.name: Days 0-1: Medium A
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff Myogenic Progenitor Medium A (DMEM/F-12 without HEPES + Supplement A)
stages.feeding: Daily full change, 2 mL per 6-well
actions: Replace the plating medium with Medium A on day 0
Change again on day 1
stages.checkpoint: Day 2: culture should be more than about 80% confluent; if not, stop and restart at a higher density

stages.name: Days 2-3: Medium B
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff Myogenic Progenitor Medium B (DMEM/F-12 without HEPES + Supplement B)
stages.feeding: Daily full change, 2 mL per 6-well
actions: Change to Medium B on day 2 and day 3

stages.name: Days 4-5: Medium C
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff Myogenic Progenitor Medium C (DMEM/F-12 without HEPES + Supplement C)
stages.feeding: Daily full change, 2 mL per 6-well
actions: Change to Medium C on day 4 and day 5
stages.checkpoint: Day 6: 3D structures should be forming

stages.name: Days 6-29: Medium D
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff Myogenic Progenitor Medium D (DMEM/F-12 without HEPES + Supplement D)
stages.feeding: Daily full change, 2 mL per 6-well, every day to day 29
actions: Feed daily with Medium D
Watch the morphology; lines differ in appearance
stages.checkpoint: Dense, multilayered, tightly packed culture; the medium yellows from about day 10

stages.name: Day 30 onward: replate, expand, then myotube differentiation (undated in the PIS)
stages.base_medium: MyoCult-SF Expansion Medium + 10 µM Y-27632 (MyoCult-SF Expansion Supplement Kit (Human), 05980; not in kit)

factors.name: Y-27632 (Dihydrochloride) (not in kit)
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor, first 24 h after replating

stages.feeding: Plate for 24 h, then change to medium without Y-27632
actions: Rinse with 2 mL D-PBS, add 0.5 mL TrypLE Express per well for 6 min at 37°C
Add 200 µL Collagenase Type IV, triturate 2 min with a cut 1 mL tip, incubate 4 min more
Add 3 mL DMEM/F-12, triturate 1-2 min, pass through a 70 µm strainer and spin 300 x g for 5 min
Count and plate 15,000-20,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel

Expansion (no day count given): At 60-80% confluence harvest with the Animal Component-Free Cell Dissociation Kit Replate at 5,000-10,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel to expand (5 or more passages), or freeze in CryoStor CS10 Give at least one passage in expansion medium before starting myotube differentiation Feeding: Full change every other day

Myotube differentiation (timing depends on expansion): Seed progenitors at 80,000 cells per 12-well (20,000 cells/cm2) on Matrigel in MyoCult-SF Expansion Medium and feed every other day At 95-100% confluence wash with D-PBS and add 1.5 mL MyoCult Differentiation Medium After 5 days replace half the medium and continue for up to 5 days Feeding: 1.5 mL per 12-well left for 5 days, then one half-change (0.75 mL) and up to 5 more days
stages.checkpoint: Expected yield about 1-4 x 10^6 cells per 6-well; progenitors are CD56+ and CD82+ Later: Multinucleated MyHC+ myotubes; use once myotubes have formed

protocols.name: Quick-Muscle Skeletal - SeV Kit
protocols.principle: Sendai virus carrying myogenic transcription factors is dropped straight onto freshly plated hPSCs at 33 C, boosted the next day by a transfected mesendoderm mRNA, then selected with puromycin and shifted to 37 C, giving myosin-heavy-chain-positive skeletal muscle cells in 7 days.
protocols.efficiency: The release specification for the matching ready-made cell product (CW50065) is over 70% MHC-positive cells at day 7 post-differentiation; no separate figure is published for user runs with the kit
protocols.start_requirements: Source hPSCs must have been maintained by single-cell passaging (StemFit Basic04, StemFit AK02N or StemFlex) and be at least 14 days post-thaw. Wells of a 6-well plate are precoated on day -3 with iMatrix-511 silk at 0.25 ug/cm2 in 2 mL chilled PBS and held at 4 C (or coated on day 0 and warmed 2 h at 37 C). Starting cultures must be 50-70% confluent and never above 90%. ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 is used at 10 uM stock diluted 1:1000 (final 10 uM) in the pre-harvest and plating media. A puromycin kill curve must be run in advance; the vendor's internal range is 0.5-2 ug/mL. About 4 x 10^6 viable hPSCs are needed (3 wells of a 6-well plate at 50-70% confluency) and a stable 33 C, 5% CO2 incubator. Cells are plated across six wells at a range of densities (the virus dose is scaled per well from 4 x 10^5 to 9 x 10^5 cells) in Medium M, a KnockOut Serum Replacement-based MEM-alpha medium made up by the user. One kit covers 6 wells of a 6-well plate.
materials: Quick-Muscle Skeletal - SeV Kit (SM-SeV): QMS-SeV, Mesendoderm RNA-P, Component P

MEM-alpha without nucleosides (Thermo 12561056), KnockOut Serum Replacement (10828010), sodium pyruvate (11360070), MEM non-essential amino acids (11140050), beta-mercaptoethanol (21985023), GlutaMAX (35050061), penicillin-streptomycin (15140122)
StemFit Basic04 Complete Type (AMSBio SF041-001), StemFit AK02N or StemFlex (Thermo A3349401)
TrypLE Select Enzyme 1X (Thermo 12563011) and 0.02% EDTA in DPBS (Sigma E8008) for Solution D1
ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 (Selleckchem S1049) and DMSO (Sigma D2650)
Optional STEM-CELLBANKER (AMSBIO 11890) for cryopreserving at the day-3 passage
tips: The virus is added to the well after plating, as surface drops, not pre-incubated with the cells as in the Quick-Neuron kits
Plating a spread of densities on day 0 lets you pick the best well, since the virus dose is tabulated per density
The day-1 incubation length is set by what you see down the microscope, not by the clock
pitfalls: BSL-2 containment is required for the Sendai virus
Wells over 70% confluent at the day-1 boost give lower differentiation efficiency
Medium M is made by the user from seven components; a mistake there affects the whole run
unverified: No purity figure published for user differentiations with the kit itself
No fusion index or myotube-formation metric is given; the guide only shows MHC staining at day 7

stages.name: Day -3: plate preparation
stages.feeding: None; hold the plate at 4 C
actions: Dilute 43.2 uL iMatrix-511 silk in 13 mL chilled PBS and add 2 mL per well of 6 wells

Prepare Medium M (MEM-alpha without nucleosides, 5% KnockOut Serum Replacement, sodium pyruvate, non-essential amino acids, GlutaMAX, penicillin-streptomycin, 0.1 mM beta-mercaptoethanol) and Medium M(P)

stages.name: Day 0: plate, then add Sendai virus per well
stages.base_medium: Medium iM (Medium M with 10 uM Y-27632)

factors.name: QMS-SeV (Sendai virus particles)
factors.role: myogenic transcription factors; dose scaled to the cells plated per well (for example 7.8 uL for 5 x 10^5 cells)

factors.name: Y-27632 (user-supplied)
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor for harvest and plating

stages.feeding: 1 mL Medium iM per well; densities spread from 4 x 10^5 to 9 x 10^5 cells per well
actions: Pre-treat the source hPSCs 1 h at 37 C in maintenance medium with Y-27632
Harvest with 300 uL Solution D1 per well and resuspend in Medium iM
Plate 1 mL per coated well at the chosen densities and rock to distribute evenly
Add the per-well QMS-SeV volume as small drops touching the medium surface at several points; never vortex or pipette the virus
Incubate overnight at 33 C

stages.name: Day 1: medium change, mesendoderm mRNA boost, medium change
stages.base_medium: Medium M; the boost is delivered in Medium M

factors.name: Mesendoderm RNA-P (synthetic mRNA)
factors.role: mesendoderm booster transfected once on day 1 (composition proprietary)

stages.feeding: 1 mL Medium M, 1-4 h at 33 C depending on confluency; then 1.2 mL booster mix per well for 2.5 h; then 2 mL Medium M overnight at 33 C
actions: Change to 1 mL Medium M and incubate 1-4 h: immediately to 1 h if wells are 50-70% confluent, up to 4 h if under 50%, within 1 h if over 70%
Make Mix 1 (800 uL Opti-MEM + 33 uL MessengerMAX, 10 min) and Mix 2 (800 uL Opti-MEM + 36 uL Mesendoderm RNA-P, tapped not vortexed)
Combine, hold 5 min, add 6 mL Medium M and apply 1.2 mL per well for 2.5 h at 33 C
Replace with 2 mL Medium M and keep at 33 C overnight
stages.checkpoint: Confluency decides the pre-boost incubation; over 70% confluent wells are expected to differentiate less well

stages.name: Day 2: puromycin selection

factors.name: Puromycin (user-supplied)
factors.role: selection at the kill-curve concentration, 0.5-2 ug/mL

stages.feeding: 2 mL per well, overnight at 33 C
actions: Replace most of the medium with Medium M plus puromycin and keep at 33 C
stages.checkpoint: Untransduced puromycin control should be dying out by about 60 h

stages.name: Day 3: medium change and shift to 37 C

factors.name: Medium M (user-made KSR-based medium)
factors.role: carrier medium during the temperature shift

stages.feeding: 2 mL per well, late in the day, then overnight at 37 C
actions: Change to fresh Medium M in the late afternoon
Move the plate to 37 C, which inactivates the Sendai virus

stages.name: Day 4: Medium M(P) maintenance
stages.base_medium: Medium M(P) (Medium M with Component P)
stages.feeding: 2 mL per well, then 3 days at 37 C
actions: Change to Medium M(P) and leave the cultures undisturbed for 3 days
stages.checkpoint: Elongated spindle-shaped muscle cells are visible from day 4

stages.name: Day 7: assay or continued maturation
stages.base_medium: Quick-Muscle Skeletal Maintenance Medium (SM-MM) or user's choice

factors.name: Quick-Muscle Skeletal Maintenance Medium (SM-MM, sold separately)

stages.feeding: Switch to maintenance medium from day 7
actions: Assay or carry the culture on in SM-MM
Confirm with an anti-myosin heavy chain antibody
stages.checkpoint: Elongated MHC-positive muscle cells by day 7

cell_types.notes: Three families of protocol exist and they are not interchangeable. Transgene-free monolayer routes (Chal/Pourquie, Shelton, Xi) need 4-7 weeks and top out around 30-90% myogenic depending on how you count, but need no genetic modification. Inducible-transgene routes are much faster and cleaner: Darabi et al. 2012 (Cell Stem Cell, PMID 22560081) differentiate doxycycline-inducible PAX7 hES/hiPSC lines for 7 days as embryoid bodies, replate for 3 days, induce PAX7 with doxycycline on day 10, sort GFP+ cells after 4 days of induction and expand them in bFGF plus doxycycline; Maffioletti et al. 2015 (Nat Protoc, PMID 26042384; corrigendum PMID 26313482) derive mesoangioblast-like cells in four density/medium/coating stages and then induce MYOD1 transiently. Both require a vector and a sort. Lines differ substantially in how they respond to the CHIR dose and in how long they take to reach myotubes, so titrate CHIR and re-time the stages for each new line.

cell_types.name: Chondrocytes (cartilage)
cell_types.summary: SOX9-positive cells that deposit a proteoglycan-rich, collagen type II matrix, grown as three-dimensional pellets or micromasses after a staged monolayer induction through paraxial mesoderm and sclerotome. They are used to model osteoarthritis and skeletal dysplasias, to test cartilage-protective drugs, and as a renewable source for cartilage repair.
cell_types.maturation_note: The monolayer induction takes 12-21 days, then pellets or micromasses need 28-42 days more before the matrix is convincing. Safranin-O staining and GAG/DNA ratios keep rising to about day 42. Keeping TGF-beta3 gives articular-like cartilage, while switching to BMP4 pushes the tissue towards hypertrophy and endochondral ossification.

morphology.endpoint: A dense, glossy, cartilage-like pellet or micromass a millimetre or so across, firm enough to handle with forceps, with rounded cells sitting in lacunae in a matrix that stains strongly with safranin-O. Off-target cells, when present, appear as a looser perichondral rim.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat compact colonies on vitronectin or Matrigel; the Adkar/Wu route starts at only 40-70% confluence.

stages.label: Paraxial mesoderm and early somite
stages.look: Dense, uniform monolayer with no visible colony boundaries after the daily medium swaps.

stages.label: Sclerotome
stages.look: Confluent sheet that becomes more refractile; cells are smaller and tightly apposed.

stages.label: Chondroprogenitors
stages.look: A mixed monolayer of flattened and spindle-shaped cells ready to be dissociated and pelleted.

stages.label: Chondrogenic pellet
stages.look: Opaque, rounded pellet that holds its shape; cut sections show rounded cells in a safranin-O-positive matrix.

stages.label: Mature cartilage
stages.look: Larger, firmer, whiter tissue with an even matrix; perichondral off-target layers are reduced when WNT is inhibited.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be gone within the first few days of the staged induction.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Peaks after the 24 h activin A/CHIR99021/FGF2 step.

markers.name: TBX6
markers.note: Day-2 paraxial marker; falls when FGF and WNT are inhibited.

markers.name: PAX1
markers.note: Sclerotome identity after purmorphamine/Wnt-C59; with PAX9 and FOXC2 the standard sclerotome trio.

markers.name: PAX9
markers.note: Confirms the sclerotome rather than dermomyotome branch.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Master chondrogenic transcription factor; Adkar 2019 built a COL2A1-GFP reporter precisely because SOX9 alone does not let you purify the population.

markers.name: COL2A1
markers.note: The defining hyaline cartilage matrix protein; the GFP knock-in reporter in Adkar 2019 enables sorting.

markers.name: ACAN
markers.note: Main proteoglycan; underlies the safranin-O and GAG/DNA readouts.

markers.name: PRG4
markers.note: Articular surface marker; the reason TGF-beta rather than BMP4 is used for articular fate.

markers.name: COL6A1
markers.note: Pericellular matrix; enriched in sorted COL2A1-GFP-high pellets in Adkar 2019.

markers.name: COL10A1
markers.note: Hypertrophy. Adkar 2019 saw no type X immunostaining in their pellets; BMP4-driven protocols deliberately induce it.

markers.name: COL1A1
markers.note: Fibrocartilage contamination; appears at the pellet periphery and increases with chondroprogenitor passage number.

markers.name: MITF
markers.note: Wu 2021 identified MITF-high melanocyte-like cells in day-7 and day-14 pellets as a major off-target population.

markers.name: NES
markers.note: The other off-target branch found by Wu 2021; both are reduced by WNT inhibition with C59.

functional_assays: Safranin-O/haematoxylin histology of sections
GAG/DNA ratio biochemistry
Type II, VI and X collagen immunohistochemistry
Mechanical testing of engineered cartilage
Ectopic or osteochondral defect implantation in immunodeficient mice
qc: Sclerotome stage PAX1/PAX9/FOXC2 positive before pelleting; PDGFRA can be used to purify sclerotome (Loh 2016 report 85.2 +/- 8.4% PDGFRA+ in day 5-6 sclerotome)
Day-28 pellets safranin-O positive with type II/VI collagen and no detectable type X collagen (Adkar 2019)
GAG/DNA ratio increased relative to unsorted or untreated controls
Melanocytic (MITF) and neural (NES) off-target cells scored on sections, not just assumed absent

protocols.name: Daily-stepped sclerotome induction, then TGF-beta3 pellet chondrogenesis (COL2A1-GFP sortable)
protocols.principle: Follow the embryonic sequence one day at a time (anterior primitive streak, paraxial mesoderm, early somite, sclerotome, chondroprogenitor), each stage defined by a specific set of agonists and antagonists, then pellet the chondroprogenitors in TGF-beta3. A CRISPR COL2A1-GFP reporter lets you sort the chondrogenic cells.
protocols.efficiency: Sorting COL2A1-GFP-high cells enriched type II/VI collagen in day-28 pellets relative to unsorted cells; no overall percentage purity is given for the unsorted culture
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs (BJFF, ATCC ACS-1019 or RVR) maintained on vitronectin in Essential 8 Flex (or CellMatrix/ATCC SFM, or mTeSR1), fed daily and passaged at 80-90% confluency. Start induction when cells reach 70% confluency.
tips: Chondroprogenitors can be expanded on 0.1% gelatin at 10,000 cells/cm2 in DMEM/F12 with 10% FBS, ITS+, 2-mercaptoethanol, NEAA, bFGF and ascorbate-2-phosphate, and passaged at 70-80% confluence.
Pellets made from passage-0 progenitors have the best matrix; type I collagen creeps in with passage.
The COL2A1-GFP reporter is the most reliable way to compare runs, since SOX9 immunostaining does not track matrix quality.
pitfalls: Pellets from late-passage (P3-P5) progenitors show more type I collagen and less type II.
Starting the induction at the wrong confluence (not around 70%) is a common cause of failure.
Each stage is only 24 h for the first three days: miss a medium change and the sequence derails.

source.authors: Adkar SS, Wu CL, Willard VP, Dicks A, et al.
source.title: Step-wise chondrogenesis of human induced pluripotent stem cells and purification via a reporter allele generated by CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing

Feed with the day-0 factor cocktail for 24 h

stages.feeding: Daily medium change for 12-21 days total
actions: Wash briefly with DMEM/F12
Feed 20 ng/ml BMP4 daily until day 12-21
Optionally sort COL2A1-GFP-high cells at this point
stages.checkpoint: COL2A1-GFP expression detectable; progenitors ready to pellet

stages.name: Pellet chondrogenesis
stages.base_medium: Chondrogenic medium: DMEM/F-12 GlutaMAX with 1% FBS, 1% ITS+, 55 uM 2-mercaptoethanol, 1% MEM non-essential amino acids, 1% penicillin-streptomycin

factors.name: TGF-beta3
factors.role: chondrogenic driver; favours articular over hypertrophic fate

stages.feeding: Chondrogenic medium changed every 3 days for 28 days
actions: Dissociate chondroprogenitors with 0.02% EDTA at 37 C and neutralise with an equal volume of DMEM/F12 plus 10% FBS
Centrifuge 5 min at 300 x g, resuspend in chondrogenic medium
Pellet 300,000-500,000 cells per tube
Culture 28 days, changing medium every 3 days
stages.checkpoint: Safranin-O-positive pellet with type II and VI collagen and no type X collagen at day 28

protocols.name: Same staged induction with WNT (and optionally MITF) inhibition through pellet culture
protocols.principle: Single-cell transcriptomics showed that the cells that spoil hiPSC chondrogenesis are neural and melanocytic, with WNT and MITF as the hub pathways. Adding the porcupine inhibitor Wnt-C59 (and optionally the MITF inhibitor ML329) throughout pellet culture suppresses those off-target populations and gives a more homogeneous cartilage.
protocols.efficiency: Reported as improved homogeneity and stronger safranin-O staining with fewer off-target cells rather than as a purity percentage
protocols.start_requirements: STAN (WiCell STAN061i-164-1), ATCC ACS-1019 or BJFF hiPSCs below passage 30, on vitronectin in Essential 8 Flex (or CellMatrix/ATCC SFM), passaged with ReLeSR. Start mesodermal induction at 40% confluency.
tips: WNT inhibition during pellet culture (not during the somite step, where WNT is required) is the key change relative to the parent protocol.
RNA-FISH showed WNT ligands concentrated in the perichondral layer, which explains why the off-target cells sit at the pellet rim.
The published scRNA-seq atlas across hiPSC, sclerotome, Cp and six pellet time points is a useful reference dataset for benchmarking your own cultures.
pitfalls: Timing matters: inhibiting WNT during somite specification blocks the protocol, so apply C59 only in pellet culture.
MITF inhibition alone is less effective than WNT inhibition; the two were tested in combination.
The paper reports qualitative improvement rather than a purity number, so define your own histology score before you start.
unverified: No single purity percentage for chondrocytes in the final pellets is reported.

source.authors: Wu CL, Dicks A, Steward N, Tang R, et al.

stages.name: Anterior primitive streak

stages.feeding: 24 h; wash daily with 50:50 IMDM/F12 before each feed
actions: Start at 40% confluency
Rinse with wash medium then feed the day-0 cocktail for 24 h

stages.name: Early somite

actions: Rinse and feed the quadruple-inhibition cocktail for 24 h
stages.checkpoint: Early somite stage reached on day 3

stages.checkpoint: Sclerotome signature at day 6 (confirmed by scRNA-seq in this paper)

stages.name: Chondroprogenitor
stages.feeding: Daily for 6 days
actions: Feed 20 ng/ml BMP4 daily for 6 days
Dissociate with TrypLE for 3 min at 37 C and neutralise with DMEM/F12 plus 10% FBS
stages.checkpoint: Chondroprogenitor (Cp) stage confirmed before pelleting

stages.name: Pellet chondrogenesis with WNT inhibition
stages.base_medium: Chondrogenic medium: DMEM/F-12 with 1% FBS, 1% ITS+, 55 uM 2-mercaptoethanol, 100 nM dexamethasone, 1% NEAA, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 50 ug/ml L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate, 40 ug/ml L-proline

factors.name: Wnt-C59
factors.role: porcupine inhibitor; suppresses neural and melanocytic off-target cells, applied day 0 to day 42 of pellet culture

factors.name: ML329
factors.role: MITF inhibitor; optional, used alone or with C59 to suppress melanocyte-like cells

stages.feeding: Chondrogenic medium with the stated additions, over 42 days of pellet culture
actions: Resuspend Cp cells at 5 x 10^5 cells/ml in chondrogenic medium
Centrifuge 5 min at 300 x g to form pellets
Add TGF-beta3 with 1 uM C59 (and 1 uM ML329 if desired) from pellet day 0 through day 42
Score safranin-O staining and off-target cells on sections
stages.checkpoint: Stronger safranin-O staining and fewer off-target cells than TGF-beta3 alone; most residual WNT signal sits in the perichondral layer

protocols.name: Craft/Keller embryoid-body route to articular chondrocytes in high-density micromass
protocols.principle: Form small embryoid bodies, specify mesoderm with low-dose BMP4, activin A and bFGF, then dual-inhibit activin and BMP receptors to generate chondrogenic progenitors; a high-density micromass in TGF-beta3 gives articular-like cartilage, while swapping to BMP4 switches the tissue to the growth-plate (hypertrophic) lineage.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated with 1 mg/ml collagenase B (20 min) then TrypLE (3-5 min), scraped off and broken up by pipetting through a 2 ml serological pipette into embryoid bodies of 3-10 cells.
tips: TGF-beta3 versus BMP4 at the micromass stage is the switch between articular and growth-plate cartilage; this is the central finding of Craft et al. 2015 (Nat Biotechnol, PMID 25961409).
High-density micromass droplets (250,000 cells in 20 ul) give better matrix than sparse pellets in this system.
The small 3-10 cell EB size matters: large EBs differentiate unevenly.
pitfalls: The brief 2% FBS window is only for adherence; leaving serum in longer compromises the serum-free design.
BMP4-specified chondrocytes initiate endochondral ossification in vivo, so do not use them where stable articular cartilage is the goal.
No purity percentage is reported, so judge success on histology and matrix biochemistry.
unverified: Efficiency/purity of chondrocytes in the micromass is not stated in this paper.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation

actions: Culture the 3-10 cell EBs in suspension for 24 h
stages.checkpoint: Small, even embryoid bodies in suspension

actions: Collect the EBs and resuspend in induction medium
Culture until day 3
stages.checkpoint: Mesodermal EBs ready for dissociation at day 3

stages.name: Chondrogenic progenitor specification (monolayer)
stages.base_medium: StemPro-34 SFM with 2 mM glutamine, 50 ug/ml ascorbic acid, 400 uM MTG
stages.feeding: Plate and culture to day 5

stages.feeding: Medium changed every second day

stages.checkpoint: Expanded chondrogenic progenitors at day 14

stages.name: Micromass chondrogenesis
stages.base_medium: Chondrogenic medium: high-glucose DMEM with 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 1% ITS-A, 40 ug/ml L-proline, 0.1 uM dexamethasone (plus 2% FBS for the first 3 days only)

factors.name: TGF-beta3
factors.role: articular chondrocyte fate; added from day 3 of micromass culture

factors.name: BMP4
factors.role: alternative: replaces TGF-beta3 after two weeks of micromass culture to drive growth-plate cartilage

stages.feeding: Serum-containing medium for 3 days, then serum-free chondrogenic medium with TGF-beta3
actions: Dissociate and plate at 250,000 cells per 20 ul droplet (high-density micromass) at day 14

stages.checkpoint: Cartilage matrix in the micromass by histology; PRG4-positive articular phenotype with TGF-beta3 versus COL10A1-positive hypertrophy with BMP4

cell_types.notes: Two protocol families dominate: monolayer sclerotome routes (Loh-derived; Adkar 2019, Wu 2021) and embryoid-body routes (Oldershaw/Kimber and Craft/Keller). The landmark Oldershaw et al. 2010 paper (Nat Biotechnol, PMID 20967028) reported a chemically defined 3-stage protocol giving 74% SOX9-positive cells in HUES1 and up to 95-97% in HUES7/HUES8, but it is not open access and its growth factor concentrations and day boundaries could not be verified here; the same group's later open-access work (Cheng et al. 2014, PMID 25273540; Wang et al. 2019, PMID 31326745) builds on it. The articular/hypertrophic distinction is real and matters for any repair application: TGF-beta signalling gives stable articular-like cartilage, BMP4 gives hypertrophic cartilage that ossifies. Off-target neural and melanocytic cells are the main contaminant and are best controlled by WNT inhibition during pellet culture (Wu 2021) or by sorting a COL2A1 reporter (Adkar 2019). Chondroprogenitors can be expanded, but matrix quality falls with passage number.

cell_types.name: Podocytes
cell_types.summary: Large, arborised glomerular epithelial cells with interdigitating foot processes that express nephrin, podocin and synaptopodin and form the filtration barrier with glomerular endothelium. iPSC-derived podocytes are used to model nephrotic syndrome and APOL1-associated kidney disease, to study filtration on glomerulus-on-a-chip devices, and for nephrotoxicity testing.
cell_types.maturation_note: Musah's route takes 2 days to mesoderm, a minimum of 14 days to intermediate mesoderm and 4-5 days of podocyte induction, so about three weeks in total, and reaches over 90% efficiency. The one-step Rauch protocol gives podocyte-like cells in 10 days of differentiation medium followed by 10 days of maintenance medium. Foot processes and interdigitations are the slowest feature to appear and depend strongly on cell density and on being on laminin.

morphology.endpoint: Very large, flat, polygonal to stellate cells with long arborised processes that interdigitate with their neighbours; nuclei are large and the cells cover far more area than the progenitors they came from.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Round colonies with defined boundaries on Matrigel in mTeSR, 3-4 days post-passage and about 70% confluent.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: An even monolayer on laminin-511-E8 after two days of activin A, CHIR99021 and ROCK inhibitor.

stages.label: Intermediate mesoderm
stages.look: A confluent, fairly uniform epithelial-looking sheet that can be passaged for up to a month or cryopreserved.

stages.label: Podocytes
stages.look: Cells enlarge dramatically and develop branched processes that contact neighbouring cells; nephrin and podocin staining outlines the cell borders.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent; Rauch 2018 track OCT4 and SOX2 transcripts falling across the 17-day differentiation.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Second exit-from-pluripotency marker in the Rauch time course.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Induced over the first two days of activin A plus CHIR99021 on laminin in the Musah route.

markers.name: PAX2
markers.note: Intermediate mesoderm and renal progenitor marker during the 14-day BMP7/CHIR99021 phase.

markers.name: WT1
markers.note: Podocyte transcription factor; Musah 2018 stain for nephrin, WT1 and podocin together as the podocyte panel.

markers.name: NPHS1
markers.note: Slit diaphragm protein and the key specificity marker; Musah 2018 report over 90% efficiency using this panel.

markers.name: NPHS2
markers.note: Slit diaphragm protein; co-stained with nephrin and WT1.

markers.name: SYNPO
markers.note: Foot process cytoskeletal marker; Rauch 2018 follow SYNPO transcript across days 1, 3, 6, 9, 13 and 17.

markers.name: PODXL
markers.note: Apical surface sialoprotein of podocytes; widely used for flow quantification.

markers.name: MAFB
markers.note: Podocyte transcription factor commonly included alongside WT1.

markers.name: SYNPO2
markers.note: Secondary cytoskeletal readout of maturity.

markers.name: CDH1
markers.note: Podocytes are not E-cadherin-high epithelium; strong CDH1 suggests tubular drift.

markers.name: LTL
markers.note: Proximal tubule contamination, the usual off-target when the protocol slips towards general nephron fate.

markers.name: TUBB3
markers.note: Neural drift is worth excluding in any long monolayer differentiation.

functional_assays: Albumin retention versus inulin clearance on a glomerulus chip
Foot process and interdigitation imaging (immunofluorescence or SEM)
Permeability response to injury (for example puromycin aminonucleoside)
Cyclic mechanical strain response on a chip
Co-culture with glomerular endothelium to reconstitute the filtration barrier
qc: Nephrin, WT1 and podocin triple-positive by immunofluorescence, with flow cytometry for the efficiency number (over 90% in Musah 2018)
Large arborised cells with visible interdigitating processes, not just marker-positive flat cells
OCT4 and SOX2 transcripts down relative to the starting iPSCs (Rauch 2018)
Proximal tubule (LTL) and neural (TUBB3) markers low

protocols.name: Laminin-511-E8 with activin A/CHIR, BMP7/CHIR, then BMP7/activin A/VEGF/retinoic acid/CHIR
protocols.principle: Culture on a laminin-511-E8 fragment (the podocyte's own basement membrane ligand) and step the cells through mesoderm and intermediate mesoderm, then apply a five-component podocyte induction medium. The matrix is as important as the soluble factors, and the result is mature podocytes at over 90% efficiency, suitable for a glomerulus-on-a-chip.
protocols.efficiency: Over 90% efficiency for mature podocytes
protocols.start_requirements: Human iPS or ES cells adapted to feeder-free culture in mTeSR on Matrigel-coated plates, used 3-4 days after passaging at about 70% confluency and in the mitotic phase, with any spontaneously differentiated cells scraped away first. All 2D differentiation is done in 12-well plates on laminin-511-E8 coated at 5 ug/ml (700 ul per well).
materials: iMatrix-511 laminin-E8 fragment (Iwai N-892012) at 5 ug/ml
Recombinant human laminin-511 (BioLamina LN511-02) at 50 ug/ml for chips
Microfluidic chip with side vacuum chambers (optional)
tips: Laminin-511-E8 is not interchangeable with Matrigel here; the matrix is part of the specification.
Lot-test CHIR99021: the authors explicitly report quality differences between suppliers and lots.
Protect the retinoic acid medium from light, and refresh daily because the cells deplete the factors quickly.
Intermediate mesoderm cells can be banked, so one differentiation can supply many podocyte experiments.
On the chip, cyclic mechanical strain applied through the side vacuum chambers mimics glomerular pulsation and improves the barrier.
pitfalls: Start from mitotic, roughly 70%-confluent iPSCs; over-confluent or partly differentiated starting cultures fail.
Clumps larger than 200 um at the podocyte replating step do not spread and will not form interdigitations.
The PDMS chip can absorb small hydrophobic molecules, which limits some drug studies (a limitation the authors state).
This protocol makes only podocytes; it is not a route to other kidney cell types.

source.authors: Musah S, Dimitrakakis N, Camacho DM, Church GM, Ingber DE
source.title: Directed differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells into mature kidney podocytes and establishment of a glomerulus chip

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with GlutaMAX and 1x B27 serum-free supplement

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor; survival of the replated single cells

stages.feeding: Refresh the medium the next day; 2 days total

Scrape gently, pipette to individualise the cells and pellet
Resuspend in mesoderm induction medium and plate 1 ml per well of a laminin-511-E8-coated 12-well plate
Refresh the medium the next day and culture 2 days in total
stages.checkpoint: Even mesoderm monolayer at day 2

stages.name: Intermediate mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with GlutaMAX and 1x B27 serum-free supplement
stages.feeding: 1 ml per well of a 12-well plate, refreshed daily for at least 14 days
actions: Replace the mesoderm medium with intermediate mesoderm medium
Refresh daily; if the medium turns yellow, increase the volume
Culture 14 days; the cells can be passaged for up to a month or cryopreserved at this stage
stages.checkpoint: Confluent intermediate mesoderm culture after 14 days (about 100% confluent before passaging)

stages.name: Podocyte induction
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with GlutaMAX and 1x B27 serum-free supplement

factors.name: All-trans retinoic acid
factors.role: podocyte specification; the medium must be protected from light

Refresh daily for 4-5 days, keeping the retinoic acid-containing medium in the dark

protocols.name: One-step podocyte differentiation: activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid in low serum
protocols.principle: A single differentiation medium containing activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid applied directly to seeded iPSCs for ten days, followed by ten days in factor-free maintenance medium, yields podocyte-like cells. Initial and seeding cell densities, and how the plate is handled when seeding, determine whether foot processes and interdigitations form.
protocols.start_requirements: Pre-cultures of undifferentiated iPSCs plated at 50,000-100,000, 200,000 or 400,000 cells/cm2 and grown 4 days, then passaged with Accutase to single cells and seeded on Geltrex-coated plates at 9,000, 15,000 or 40,000 cells/cm2 for differentiation. Seed in half the recommended medium volume, rock the plate gently back-and-forth and left-right rather than swirling, and add the rest of the medium after 5 h once cells have attached.
tips: The authors single out seeding and handling technique: half-volume seeding, gentle back-and-forth and left-right rocking rather than swirling, and adding the remaining medium after 5 h, all to avoid an uneven concentric cell distribution.
It is a one-step protocol with no passaging, which makes it quick and cheap when you only need podocyte-like cells.
The 20-day time course with qPCR at days 1, 3, 6, 9, 13 and 17 published in the paper is a useful benchmark.
pitfalls: Both the density of the undifferentiated pre-culture and the seeding density of the differentiation culture must be controlled; the paper devotes a section to this.
Uneven concentric distribution in multiwell plates prevents proper foot process and interdigitation formation.
No purity percentage is reported, so this route is harder to benchmark than the Musah protocol.
unverified: No differentiation efficiency or purity percentage is reported.

Maintain in M1, feeding every 2-3 days, for 10 days

protocols.name: Embryoid-body route with activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid
protocols.principle: The earliest hiPSC podocyte protocol: suspend colony fragments as embryoid bodies in a low-serum medium containing activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid for three days, then plate them on gelatin in the same medium for a further week, giving podocytes at about day 10 that can be maintained without the factors.
protocols.start_requirements: iPSC colonies (in this paper reprogrammed from normal human kidney mesangial cells) cut mechanically into similarly sized pieces.
materials: Glutaraldehyde and cacodylate buffer for SEM
tips: The activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid combination established here is the basis of the later Rauch and Musah media, which is why the three protocols look related.
Podocytes keep their morphology and function after the factors are withdrawn, so you do not need to maintain them on expensive medium.
The paper compares the iPSC podocytes directly with primary human podocytes isolated by glomerular sieving, a good benchmark design.
pitfalls: Embryoid-body routes are inherently heterogeneous: Musah 2018 cite exactly this as the reason EB-based podocyte differentiation is inefficient.
No purity figure is given, so quantification needs to be added by the user.
Mechanical cutting of colonies is operator-dependent and hard to standardise.
unverified: No differentiation efficiency or purity percentage is reported.

stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with 2.5% FBS, 100 uM non-essential amino acids and 100 uM beta-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: 3 days in ultra-low-cluster 6-well plates
actions: Cut iPSC colonies mechanically into similarly sized pieces
Culture in ultra-low-cluster 6-well plates in the differentiation medium for 3 days
stages.checkpoint: Embryoid bodies formed and ready to plate

stages.name: Adherent podocyte differentiation
stages.base_medium: Same differentiation medium (DMEM/F12 with 2.5% FBS, NEAA, beta-mercaptoethanol)
stages.feeding: 7-8 days in the same medium before sub-passaging
actions: Transfer the embryoid bodies to 0.1% gelatin pre-coated 10 cm dishes

cell_types.notes: Efficiency differs enormously between routes and most of the difference comes from the matrix and from heterogeneity. Musah et al. report over 90% mature podocytes on laminin-511-E8 and explicitly attribute part of that to the matrix, contrasting it with embryoid-body routes (Song 2012) and with organoids, where podocytes are only one component. The one-step Rauch protocol is quick but gives no purity number and is highly sensitive to seeding density and even to how the plate is rocked. Whichever route you use, judge success on arborised morphology and interdigitating processes as well as on nephrin/podocin/WT1 staining: marker-positive flat cells are not functional podocytes. Note also that CHIR99021 lots vary enough to change the outcome (a caution the Musah protocol makes explicitly).

cell_types.name: Ureteric bud / collecting duct organoids
cell_types.summary: The branching epithelium that forms the collecting duct system and ureter, derived through anterior (not posterior) intermediate mesoderm and nephric duct rather than through nephron progenitors. hPSC-derived ureteric bud organoids branch in culture, can be expanded, differentiate to principal and intercalated collecting duct cells, and can be recombined with nephron progenitors to build higher-order kidney tissue; they also model ADPKD cystogenesis and lower urinary tract disorders.
cell_types.maturation_note: The Osafune-lab route reaches nephric duct in about 6 days (16-28 h anterior primitive streak, 3 days anterior intermediate mesoderm, 2 days nephric duct elongation), epithelialises the aggregate in 2 days and gives a branching ureteric bud organoid by day 6 of 3D culture, so under two weeks to a branching organoid. Tips can be separated and reconstituted repeatedly (3-4 times), and collecting duct progenitors take a further 7 days in 2D or 14 days in 3D. Zeng 2021 organoids expand for months, with human collecting duct differentiation taking 14 days.

morphology.endpoint: A translucent epithelial organoid with a hollow trunk and multiple rounded buds or tips at its periphery, visibly branching over days; sections show a single-layered CK8/RET-positive epithelium around a lumen.

stages.label: Anterior primitive streak
stages.look: After 16-28 h in activin A plus CHIR99021 the monolayer is BRACHYURY-positive; residual SOX2-positive hPSCs mean the induction was too short.

stages.label: Anterior intermediate mesoderm
stages.look: Dense monolayer co-expressing GATA3, LHX1 and PAX2; the cells are replated at 1 x 10^5 cells/cm2 partway through.

stages.label: Nephric duct
stages.look: Epithelial-looking sheet positive for RET and GATA3; when induction is patchy the positive cells form islands rather than a continuous sheet.

stages.label: Nephric duct aggregate
stages.look: One aggregate per well of a 96-well M-bottom plate, with a bright duct core and a looser halo of unwanted cells that is pipetted away.

stages.label: Branching ureteric bud organoid
stages.look: Floating organoid with distinct budding tips; laminin and ezrin outline the epithelium, with RET concentrated in the tips.

stages.label: Collecting duct
stages.look: Tip-derived colonies or reconstituted organoids expressing collecting duct markers after further differentiation.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Ryosaka 2022 co-stain day-0 anterior primitive streak cells for BRACHYURY and SOX2; remaining SOX2-positive cells mark incomplete induction.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: The 16-28 h readout; Zeng 2021 see mesendodermal T expression in most cells by day 3 of their schedule.

markers.name: GATA3
markers.stage_label: Anterior intermediate mesoderm and nephric duct
markers.note: The anterior intermediate mesoderm marker that distinguishes this lineage from the posterior (nephron) lineage; co-expressed with LHX1 and PAX2 at day 3.

markers.name: LHX1
markers.note: Part of the GATA3/LHX1/PAX2 triple stain at 72 h of anterior intermediate mesoderm induction.

markers.name: PAX2
markers.note: Zeng 2021 used a PAX2-mCherry knock-in reporter to purify precursors, and showed KIT-positive sorting enriches the same PAX2-positive population.

markers.name: RET
markers.note: The tip progenitor marker and the GDNF receptor; Zeng 2021 showed RET knockout blocks branching, and used an anti-RET extracellular-domain antibody to isolate human tip cells.

markers.name: WNT11
markers.note: Tip-restricted; Zeng 2021 built a WNT11-GFP reporter alongside PAX2-mCherry.

markers.name: KRT8
markers.note: Epithelial identity of the bud; Ryosaka 2022 stain cryosections for CK8 with RET.

markers.name: KIT
markers.note: The reporter-free sorting handle in Zeng 2021: 36.1% KIT-positive cells in a hESC line, 55.4% in H1 and 43.9% in SOX9-GFP hiPSCs after 7 days of differentiation.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Zeng 2021 purified SOX9-GFP-positive precursors on day 7 from a reporter hiPSC line.

markers.name: CDH1
markers.note: Used with RET in whole-mount staining of reconstituted organoids.

markers.name: AQP2
markers.note: Principal cell marker and one of the two screening endpoints Zeng 2021 used to find their collecting duct differentiation medium.

markers.name: FOXI1
markers.note: Intercalated cell marker; the second screening endpoint in Zeng 2021.

markers.name: SIX2
markers.note: Should be absent: nephron progenitors come from posterior intermediate mesoderm and their presence means the anterior patterning drifted.

functional_assays: Branching morphogenesis quantified over days of live imaging
Serial tip separation and organoid reconstitution (3-4 rounds)
Recombination with nephron progenitor aggregates to build higher-order kidney tissue

protocols.name: Osafune-lab iUB organoids: anterior primitive streak, anterior intermediate mesoderm, nephric duct, then 3D budding
protocols.principle: The ureteric bud arises from anterior rather than posterior intermediate mesoderm, so the first step is an anterior primitive streak induction with activin A and low CHIR99021 followed by retinoid, BMP and TGF-beta manipulation with FGF8. Nephric duct cells are then aggregated, epithelialised and cultured in a Matrigel-containing medium with GDNF, where they bud and branch; tips can be separated and reconstituted indefinitely.
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs (for example 1231A3, 1383D2) with 1 day of pre-differentiation in StemFit AK02N before the anterior primitive streak step; two wells of a 4-well plate per standard experiment.
tips: Use M-bottom (spindle-shaped) 96-well plates, not U-bottom: the authors state U-bottom plates make it hard to form and observe the aggregates.
Nephric duct cells can be cryopreserved at up to 2 x 10^6 cells/ml in STEMCELL BANKER, which breaks the protocol into manageable sessions.
The LDN193189 concentration increases tenfold (0.1 uM to 1 uM) when you move from nephric duct to organoid medium; this is easy to miss.
Pipette the aggregate 10-20 times to remove unwanted cells, and never more than 30, or budding is reduced.
pitfalls: Accutase exposure beyond 3 min reduces viability at every dissociation step.
If the GATA3/PAX2-positive cells form islands rather than a sheet, the nephric duct induction rate is too low and the anterior primitive streak step must be re-optimised.
Reduced or thickened budding regions in day-6 organoids indicate a low induction rate (the paper's troubleshooting item 3).
Every medium must be made fresh for each use.
unverified: No numeric induction efficiency or purity percentage is given in this protocol paper.

protocols.name: Expandable iUB organoids from KIT-sorted precursors, with a collecting duct differentiation medium
protocols.principle: A 7-day directed differentiation generates ureteric bud precursors that can be purified on the surface marker KIT (CD117) without any reporter, then expanded for months as branching organoids in a ureteric bud culture medium; a separately screened differentiation medium converts them to a patterned collecting duct organoid containing principal and intercalated cells.
protocols.efficiency: KIT-positive cells at day 7: 36.1% (WNT11-GFP/PAX2-mCherry hESC), 55.4% (H1 hESC) and 43.9% (SOX9-GFP hiPSC); about 30% of single mouse ureteric bud cells self-organised at clonal density
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs pre-treated with 10 uM Y-27632 in mTeSR1 for 1 h, dissociated to single cells with Accumax, and 60,000-80,000 cells seeded per Matrigel-coated 12-well plate in 1 ml mTeSR1 with either 10 uM Y-27632 (original protocol) or 1x CloneR (refined protocol). Seeding number needs optimising per line.
materials: Lentiviral CRISPR reagents (for RET knockout experiments)
tips: KIT (CD117) sorting is the practical breakthrough here: it removes the need for a reporter line and works across hESC and hiPSC lines.
Wait for expansion to stabilise (at least 25 days post-FACS, organoids at least 900 um) before starting collecting duct differentiation.
Gene expression stayed stable at 33, 49 and 66 days of culture, so these organoids genuinely expand rather than drift.
The same system supports recombination with nephron progenitor aggregates to build an engineered kidney precursor at an air-liquid interface.
pitfalls: The exact media formulations are in the supplementary methods, so you cannot run this protocol from the main text alone.
Seeding number must be optimised per line (60,000-80,000 cells per 12-well is only a starting point).
GDNF/RET signalling is essential: RET knockout abolishes branching, so check RET expression if organoids stop branching.
unverified: Compositions and component concentrations of the ME, UB-I, UB-II, hUBCM, hUBCM-v2 and hCDDM media, and of the hBI14 base medium, are in the paper's supplementary methods and could not be read in this session (set to null).

The precise day on which collecting duct differentiation starts depends on when expansion stabilises; the day numbers in the expansion and differentiation stages here are representative, based on the stated minimum of 25 days post-FACS.

protocols.name: Separate ureteric bud and nephron progenitor induction, then reassembly into higher-order kidney
protocols.principle: Ureteric bud and nephron progenitors have distinct developmental origins, so induce each lineage separately from PSCs and then reassemble them. The reconstructed organoid develops the architecture of the embryonic kidney: a peripheral progenitor niche and internally differentiated nephrons connected to a branching ureteric epithelium.
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse and human pluripotent stem cells; the specific starting densities and maintenance conditions could not be verified in this session.
materials: Reagents not verified in this session
tips: The conceptual point, that ureteric bud and nephron progenitors must be induced separately and then recombined, underpins the later expandable-organoid work (Mae 2018, Zeng 2021).
If you need connected nephrons and collecting duct with a progenitor niche rather than a nephron-only organoid, this reassembly strategy is the published route.
Zeng et al. 2021 implement an equivalent recombination at an air-liquid interface using expandable progenitors, which is more practical if you need many replicates.
pitfalls: Protocol parameters could not be verified here, so treat this entry as the strategy rather than a bench recipe.
Reassembly protocols are technically demanding and low-throughput compared with single-lineage organoids.
unverified: All media, factor concentrations, stage durations and day boundaries: the Cell Stem Cell paper is not open access and only the abstract could be read in this session (day_end values set to null).
Induction efficiencies for either lineage not confirmed.

cell_types.notes: The crucial distinction is anterior versus posterior intermediate mesoderm: ureteric bud and collecting duct come from the anterior lineage (GATA3/LHX1/PAX2, then RET), whereas nephron progenitors (SIX2) come from the posterior lineage, which is why most nephron organoid protocols contain little or no collecting duct. In the Takasato protocol the length of the CHIR99021 phase shifts the balance between the two. Two practical routes exist for a dedicated ureteric bud: the Osafune-lab iUB organoid (Mae et al. 2018, Biochem Biophys Res Commun, PMID 29158085, with the step-by-step version in Ryosaka et al. 2022, and an ADPKD collecting duct application in Mae et al. 2023, Cell Rep, PMID 38039961), and the expandable KIT-sorted organoid of Zeng et al. 2021, which can be grown for months and then differentiated to a patterned collecting duct. Both depend on GDNF/RET signalling, and RET loss abolishes branching. Taguchi and Nishinakamura 2017 established the reassembly strategy that makes higher-order kidney tissue possible, but its protocol parameters are behind a paywall.

cell_types.name: Kidney organoids
cell_types.summary: Three-dimensional tissues containing segmented nephrons (podocytes, proximal tubule, loop of Henle and distal tubule) and, depending on the protocol, collecting duct, stroma and endothelium, made by inducing posterior intermediate mesoderm and nephron progenitors then letting them self-organise. They are used to model polycystic kidney disease and congenital nephropathies, to test nephrotoxicity, and to study human nephrogenesis.
cell_types.maturation_note: Nephron progenitors appear by day 9 in the Morizane protocol (80-90% SIX2+) and renal vesicles around day 14, with segmented nephrons by day 21; organoids remain stable for at least three months. In the Takasato route the intermediate mesoderm takes 7 days, then aggregates develop for 11-18 days (day 7 to 25). Proximal tubule maturation remains the weak point in all protocols, and organoids stay fetal in character with no vasculature unless grafted or vascularised.

morphology.endpoint: A domed, 0.5 mm or larger aggregate on a transwell filter or in a round-bottom well, shot through with translucent convoluted tubules and lighter, denser glomerulus-like bodies; under higher power the tubules have clear lumens and the whole mass is surrounded by looser stroma.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Feeder-free hPSCs at the confluence the protocol specifies (40-50% for Takasato; carefully titrated for Morizane, where confluence at initiation is the single most important variable).

stages.label: Late primitive streak
stages.look: Loosely formed dense clusters of cells over a confluent sheet: in the Morizane protocol this is the cue to switch to activin A, and judging it correctly is the critical step.

stages.label: Nephron progenitors
stages.look: Dense monolayer with 80-90% SIX2-positive nuclei; ready to aggregate or continue in 2D.

stages.label: Renal vesicles
stages.look: Round polarised structures with clear lumens appear within the aggregate or monolayer; this is the point to withdraw CHIR99021.

stages.label: Segmented nephrons
stages.look: Convoluted tubules with distinguishable segments and glomerulus-like bodies; in Takasato organoids, collecting duct, renal interstitium and endothelium as well.

stages.label: Mature organoid
stages.look: Around 0.5 mm or larger, each organoid holding multiple nephron structures; tubules can be imaged live and take up labelled dextran.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Takasato 2016 note hPSCs should still be OCT4/NANOG positive on day 0 before CHIR99021 is added; it must be gone later.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Induced by the CHIR99021 phase; the balance of anterior versus posterior streak sets the collecting duct to nephron ratio.

markers.name: HOXD11
markers.note: The key posterior intermediate mesoderm check. Takasato 2016 stain day-7 cells for HOXD11 (posterior) alongside GATA3 (anterior) and treat HOXD11-negative cultures as a failed differentiation.

markers.name: WT1
markers.note: Positive with HOXD11 after the 3-day activin A step in Morizane 2017; later marks podocytes.

markers.name: SIX2
markers.note: The nephron progenitor readout: Morizane 2017 report 80-90% SIX2+SALL1+WT1+PAX2+EYA1+ cells at day 9.

markers.name: SALL1
markers.note: Co-expressed with SIX2 in true nephron progenitors.

markers.name: LHX1
markers.note: Morizane 2017 use LHX1 as the troubleshooting marker when renal vesicle structures fail to appear.

markers.name: NPHS1
markers.note: Marks the podocyte compartment of the organoid; with WT1 and PODXL the glomerular readout.

markers.name: PODXL
markers.note: Freedman 2015 report about 80% of LTL-positive organoids also containing PODXL-positive podocyte-like cells.

markers.name: LTL
markers.note: Proximal tubule brush-border lectin; Freedman 2015 report LTL-positive cells as about 25% of the total culture.

markers.name: CDH1
markers.note: Distal epithelium; Morizane 2017 list the exact antibody. CDH1+GATA3+ cells indicate a collecting-duct-like population, which the Morizane protocol largely lacks and the Takasato protocol contains.

markers.name: GATA3
markers.note: Anterior intermediate mesoderm at day 7 in Takasato 2016 and the collecting duct lineage later; the CHIR99021 duration sets how much of this you get.

markers.name: HAVCR1
markers.note: Injury rather than identity marker: Freedman 2015 detected luminal KIM-1 in about 80% of organoids after cisplatin or gentamicin.

markers.name: TUBB3
markers.note: Off-target neural cells are a known contaminant of kidney organoids; Freedman 2015 screened for TUJ1 and intestinal markers.

protocols.name: CHIR99021 then FGF9, aggregate on a transwell with a CHIR pulse (multi-lineage organoid)
protocols.principle: A CHIR99021 phase of adjustable length sets the anterior/posterior balance of the intermediate mesoderm, FGF9 with heparin then expands it; aggregating the day-7 cells on a transwell filter with a brief CHIR99021 pulse lets ureteric epithelium and metanephric mesenchyme interact, so nephrons, collecting duct, interstitium and endothelium all form in one organoid.
protocols.efficiency: High success rate, defined by the authors as organoids containing segmented nephrons with collecting duct, renal interstitium and endothelium; demonstrated for HES-3 hESCs and hiPSC lines
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs grown on MEF feeders then transferred to Matrigel for 2 days. Dissociate with TrypLE Select (3 min), pipetting no more than twice, and seed 375,000 cells into a Matrigel-coated 25 cm2 flask in MEF-conditioned hESC medium with 10 ng/ml bFGF, i.e. 15 x 10^3 cells/cm2, overnight. Cells should be 40-50% confluent on day 0.
materials: MEF feeders and MEF-conditioned hESC medium
Antibodies for whole-mount staining (GATA3, HOXD11, nephron segment markers)
tips: The CHIR99021 duration (2-5 days) is the main dial: use it to tune how much collecting duct versus nephron you get.
Use freshly thawed FGF9 and do not skimp on medium volume; both are listed as causes of failed intermediate mesoderm induction.
Check HOXD11 at day 7 before committing to aggregation; it is much cheaper than discovering the failure at day 25.
pitfalls: Cells coming off the plastic during the CHIR99021 phase means the seeding density was too low.
Inadequate FGF9 concentration or medium volume is the stated cause of inefficient intermediate mesoderm induction.
Carrying too much medium over when transferring pellets to the transwell disrupts the air-liquid interface.

protocols.name: High-efficiency nephron progenitors (80-90% SIX2+) then 2D or 3D nephron organoids
protocols.principle: Induce late primitive streak with a line-specific CHIR99021 dose (with or without a BMP inhibitor), then posterior intermediate mesoderm with activin A, then nephron progenitors with FGF9. A transient CHIR99021 plus FGF9 treatment converts the progenitors to renal vesicles, which self-organise into segmented nephrons in either 2D or 3D.
protocols.efficiency: 80-90% SIX2+SALL1+WT1+PAX2+EYA1+ nephron progenitors within 9 days, with no sorting; 3D organoids about 0.5 mm in diameter containing multiple nephron structures
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs in ReproFF2 or StemFit Basic on 6-well plates coated with 1% LDEV-free hESC-qualified Geltrex, passaged with Accutase and plated with 10 uM Y-27632. Plating density at differentiation initiation strongly affects efficiency, so prepare several densities in parallel.
materials: Anti-SIX2, anti-LHX1, anti-CDH1 (Abcam ab11512) and nephron segment antibodies
tips: The CHIR99021 dose and whether you need a BMP inhibitor are line- and medium-dependent: 8 uM for H9 in ReproFF2, 10 uM plus 5 ng/ml noggin for the HDF iPSC line.
Judging the day-4 morphology (loosely formed dense clusters) is the single most important decision in the protocol; feed again rather than advancing early.
If the induction rate of nephron progenitors is around 80%, 3D organoid formation is highly reproducible well to well.
The authors specify the exact CHIR99021 product because substitutes need re-titration.
pitfalls: Unlike the Takasato protocol, this route yields few CD31-positive endothelial or CDH1+GATA3+ collecting-duct-like cells, which matters if you need those lineages.
Interstitial cells in the organoid were not well characterised in the original study.
Some lines differentiate faster than expected and form renal vesicles spontaneously; shorten the CHIR step if so.
unverified: The activin A working concentration for the day 4-7 step is not stated in the portion of the protocol read here (the stock is prepared at 50 ug/ml); confirm against the paper's reagent setup before use.

factors.role: transient Wnt activation; converts progenitors to renal vesicles

stages.feeding: 2 days; for 3D, seed 100,000 cells/well in 200 ul into 96-well round-bottom ultra-low-attachment plates
actions: For 2D: replace the medium with 500 ul-1 ml of CHIR 3 uM plus FGF9 10 ng/ml for 2 days

For 3D: dissociate with Accutase (10-15 min), resuspend at 500,000 cells/ml in medium with CHIR 3 uM and FGF9 10 ng/ml and plate 100,000 cells per well of a 96-well round-bottom ultra-low-attachment plate
If round polarised structures with lumens already appear, shorten this step from 2 days to 1
stages.checkpoint: Round polarised structures with lumens (renal vesicles); LHX1 positive

stages.name: Nephron formation

factors.name: FGF9
factors.role: supports nephron formation after CHIR withdrawal

stages.feeding: 750 ul-1 ml for 2-3 days
actions: Withdraw CHIR99021 and continue with FGF9 alone for 2-3 days
If renal vesicles do not appear within 3 days, check LHX1; if LHX1 is positive, feed daily with FGF9 medium for 3 more days
stages.checkpoint: Renal vesicle structures clearly established before growth factors are withdrawn

stages.name: Growth-factor-free maturation
stages.base_medium: Basic differentiation medium with no growth factors
stages.feeding: 500-750 ul every 2-3 days
actions: Switch to basic differentiation medium with no growth factors
Feed every 2-3 days; organoids are stable for at least 3 months
Analyse nephron segments by immunocytochemistry (2D) or immunohistochemistry (3D) around day 21
stages.checkpoint: Segmented nephron structures at day 21; 3D organoids about 0.5 mm with multiple nephrons per well

protocols.name: Epiblast spheroids sandwiched in dilute Matrigel, then a high-dose CHIR99021 pulse
protocols.principle: Sandwiching hPSCs under dilute Matrigel produces isolated, lumen-containing epiblast spheroids; a 36 h high-dose CHIR99021 pulse then takes them through an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and back, so by about day 10 they fold and re-epithelialise into tubular kidney organoids. Simple enough to make CRISPR disease modelling (for example PKD1/PKD2 cystogenesis) practical.
protocols.efficiency: LTL-positive cells about 25% of the total culture; about 80% of LTL-positive organoids also contained CD31-positive endothelial and PODXL-positive podocyte-like cells
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained feeder-free on 3% reduced-growth-factor Geltrex for at least one passage in mTeSR1. Plate 60,000-120,000 H9 hPSCs per 1.9 cm2, enough to give scattered isolated spheroid colonies, then sandwich under dilute Matrigel.
tips: The sandwich step is what makes the organoids reproducible: plate sparsely enough to get isolated spheroids rather than a confluent sheet.
Cysts form in PKD1/PKD2 knockout organoids, which is the main published application; they appear over weeks (a representative cyst is shown at day 58).
Rhodamine dextran localises to tubular lumens within 2-4 h and persists through a 24 h washout, which is a quick functional check.
pitfalls: LTL-positive cells are only about a quarter of the culture, so this protocol trades purity for simplicity and genetic tractability.
Two induction schedules are published (36 h CHIR alone, or the staged CHIR/IWP2 version); do not mix them.
Organoid tubules are fetal and non-vascularised in vitro, as in all of these protocols.

source.authors: Freedman BS, Brooks CR, Lam AQ, Fu H, et al.
source.title: Modelling kidney disease with CRISPR-mutant kidney organoids derived from human pluripotent epiblast spheroids

stages.name: Epiblast spheroid formation (sandwiching)

factors.name: GelTrex overlay
factors.role: dilute matrix overlay that drives spheroid formation with a central lumen

stages.feeding: Overlay the day after plating, change medium after 24 h
actions: Plate 60,000-120,000 hPSCs per 1.9 cm2 on 3% Geltrex in mTeSR1
The following day replace the medium with 500 ul of 1.5% GelTrex in mTeSR1
Change the medium after 24 h and wait 48 h from sandwiching before inducing
stages.checkpoint: Scattered, isolated spheroid colonies with lumens

stages.name: CHIR99021 pulse
stages.base_medium: mTeSR1 (or RB minus insulin for the alternative schedule)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: high-dose GSK3 inhibition for 36 h (or 24 h in the alternative schedule)

factors.name: IWP2
factors.role: alternative schedule only: Wnt inhibition for 48 h after the CHIR pulse and a 48 h gap, mirroring 2D cardiomyocyte differentiation

stages.feeding: 36 h single treatment, or the staged alternative
actions: 48 h after sandwiching, treat the spheroids with 12 uM CHIR99021 for 36 h
Alternatively: 12 uM CHIR99021 in RB minus insulin for 24 h, RBNI for 48 h, 5 uM IWP2 for 48 h, RBNI for 48 h
stages.checkpoint: Spheroid cells undergoing epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition

stages.name: Tubular organoid formation and maturation
stages.base_medium: RB: Advanced RPMI with 1x GlutaMAX and 1x B27 supplement
stages.feeding: RB replaced every 3 days
actions: Change to RB medium after the CHIR pulse and replace every 3 days
Expect the monolayer to aggregate into folds by about day 10 and undergo mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition into convoluted translucent tubular organoids
