stages.checkpoint: Tubular organoids with LTL-positive proximal tubule; about 80% also containing CD31-positive endothelium and PODXL-positive podocyte-like cells

protocols.name: STEMdiff Kidney Organoid Kit (cavitated spheroids, two-stage, 96-well)
protocols.principle: Based on Freedman et al. 2015: sparsely seeded single hPSCs are overlaid with Matrigel so they form cavitated spheroids, then Stage 1 medium (Supplement SG, about 36 h) induces late primitive streak and Stage 2 medium (Supplement DM) is fed until day 18, when tubular organoids with podocyte, proximal and distal tubule segments stand up from the adherent layer.
protocols.start_requirements: High-quality hPSCs (under 5% differentiation) kept in mTeSR1; lines kept in mTeSR Plus must be in mTeSR1 from day -3 to day 0. On day -3 dissociate with ACCUTASE, filter through a 37 µm strainer and seed 750-3,000 single cells per well of a 96-well plate coated with Matrigel GFR (0.5 mg/mL, 50 µL = 25 µg protein per well) in up to 200 µL mTeSR1 + CloneR2 (1 in 10). No Y-27632 is used.
materials: STEMdiff Kidney Organoid Kit (05160): Kidney Basal Medium 100 mL, Kidney Supplement SG (100X) 200 µL, Kidney Supplement DM (50X) 1.6 mL
Corning Matrigel GFR Basement Membrane Matrix, Phenol Red-Free (Corning 356231)
96-well flat-bottom tissue culture-treated plate (e.g. 38022); for imaging Corning 96-Well Half-Area High-Content Imaging Microplate (100-0367) or Ibidi µ-Plate 96-well, black (Ibidi 89626)
tips: The optimal single-cell number per well is line-dependent; titrate it once for each line.
Stage 2 Medium keeps 2 weeks at 2-8°C; thawed basal medium keeps 2 months.
Matrigel-coated plates can be sealed and stored up to 7 days at 2-8°C.
Use mTeSR1 for days -3 to 0 even if the line is maintained in mTeSR Plus.
pitfalls: Cells detaching completely after Stage 1: seeding too sparse, or too little Matrigel in the coat or overlay.
No tubular structures by day 8-10 means the run has failed and should be restarted.
Over-confluent wells turn yellow, and organoids darken and lose their tubular shape.
unverified: Efficiency: no percentage or organoid count per well is stated.
Feeding between day 1.5 and day 4: the manual says to incubate 2 days after the day 1.5 change but the next change is listed on day 4 (2.5 days later).
Seeding range: the protocol says 750-3,000 cells per well, while the troubleshooting table suggests testing 1,000-7,000 and a figure legend reports 5,000 cells per well for one line.
CloneR2 is given as a 1 in 10 dilution in the protocol but as '10 µM' in the troubleshooting table.
The protocol diagram is an image and was not available.

stages.name: Day -3: single-cell seeding
stages.feeding: No feeding overnight
actions: Coat 96-well plates with Matrigel diluted to 0.5 mg/mL in cold DMEM/F-12 with 15 mM HEPES (50 µL per well) for at least 1 h at room temperature
Remove differentiated areas, rinse with D-PBS, treat with 0.5 mL ACCUTASE per 6-well for 10 min at 37°C
Collect in DMEM/F-12, pipette 3-4 times, spin 300 x g for 5 min, resuspend in mTeSR1 + CloneR2 and pass through a 37 µm strainer
Count and seed 750-3,000 cells per well with a multichannel pipette (top up to 200 µL); test 750, 1,000, 2,000 and 3,000 for a new line
Let the plate sit 5-10 min in the cabinet before moving it to the incubator

stages.name: Day -2: Matrigel overlay

factors.name: Corning Matrigel GFR (not in kit)
factors.role: overlay that makes the colonies cavitate

stages.feeding: Single full change, 100 µL per well, for 24 h
actions: Dilute Matrigel into cold mTeSR1 without CloneR2
Remove the medium and immediately add 100 µL of the cold mix per well
Do not touch the well bottom with the tips

stages.name: Day -1: mTeSR1
stages.feeding: Single full change, 100 µL per well, for 1 day
actions: Change to room-temperature mTeSR1
stages.checkpoint: Round, cavitated PSC spheroids (visible from day -1) by day 0

stages.name: Stage 1: late primitive streak
stages.base_medium: Stage 1 Medium (STEMdiff Kidney Basal Medium + STEMdiff Kidney Supplement SG)
stages.feeding: Single 200 µL dose left for 36 h (up to 40 h is acceptable)
actions: Start late on day 0 so that the 36-40 h point falls at a convenient time
Remove mTeSR1 carefully and add 200 µL room-temperature Stage 1 Medium
stages.checkpoint: Day 1.5: heavy cell death, partial detachment and smaller colonies are expected

stages.name: Stage 2: nephron induction and organoid formation
stages.base_medium: Stage 2 Medium (STEMdiff Kidney Basal Medium + STEMdiff Kidney Supplement DM)
stages.feeding: Day 1.5: 200 µL per well; day 4: 100 µL; then 100 µL every 2-3 days (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) to day 18
actions: Day 1.5: remove Stage 1 Medium and add Stage 2 Medium dropwise down the wall of a tilted plate; cells lift easily here
Day 4 and afterwards: full changes of 100 µL
If the medium yellows quickly, feed every 2 days from day 10, double the volume or feed daily
Day 18: use for assays, flow cytometry or fix for staining; cultures can be held about one more week without further development
stages.checkpoint: Day 4: recovering, near-confluent monolayer. Day 8-10: early tubular structures must be visible, otherwise restart. Day 15: dense multi-tubular organoids. Stain PODXL (podocytes), LTL (proximal tubule), ECAD (distal tubule), CD31

cell_types.notes: The three protocols are genuinely different products. Takasato organoids contain nephrons plus collecting duct, interstitium and endothelium and let you tune the collecting duct to nephron ratio with the length of the CHIR99021 phase; Morizane organoids are nephron-focused with 80-90% SIX2-positive progenitors but few collecting-duct or endothelial cells; Freedman organoids are the simplest and most genetically tractable but only about 25% of the culture is proximal tubule. Starting cell density and confluence at induction dominate reproducibility in all three, and the CHIR99021 dose is line-dependent (8 uM for H9 versus 10 uM plus noggin for an HDF iPSC line in Morizane 2017). All three give fetal, non-vascularised tissue; proximal tubule maturity and off-target neural cells remain the main limitations.

cell_types.name: Definitive endoderm
cell_types.summary: Definitive endoderm is the germ layer that gives rise to liver, pancreas, gut, lung, thyroid and thymus. hPSC-derived endoderm is the mandatory first step of every protocol in this group and is also used on its own to test a line's endoderm competence.
cell_types.maturation_note: Usable at day 3 (short small-molecule/Activin protocols) to day 5 (Activin-only protocols); it is a transient population and should be patterned onwards immediately.

morphology.endpoint: A flat, confluent sheet of fairly uniform cells that are larger and less tightly packed than the starting hPSC, with no sharp colony borders left.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies with sharp edges and small cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio.

stages.label: Streak-like cells leaving the colonies
stages.look: Colony borders dissolve as cells undergo an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and spread outward; some floating dead cells are normal.

stages.label: Definitive endoderm sheet
stages.look: Original colonies are no longer recognisable; a continuous sheet of larger, slightly cobbled cells covers the well.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be lost within the first days of endoderm induction.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Residual NANOG+ patches mean induction was incomplete, often because the starting culture was too dense.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Transient at about 24 h; should be down again by the endoderm stage.

markers.name: MIXL1
markers.note: Transient streak marker; Loh 2014 report >99% MIXL1-GFP+ cells after 24 h.

markers.name: EOMES
markers.note: Early streak/endoderm transcription factor.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Core definitive endoderm transcription factor; check together with FOXA2.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Co-expressed with SOX17 in definitive endoderm and retained in most endoderm derivatives.

markers.name: CXCR4
markers.note: Live-cell surface readout of endoderm induction; usually combined with KIT (CD117) or EPCAM.

markers.name: KIT
markers.note: CXCR4+/KIT+ double positivity is the usual flow gate for endoderm.

markers.name: GATA4
markers.note: Expressed in endoderm in the Si-Tayeb and Vallier protocols.

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Mesoderm marker; Loh 2014 score endoderm as CXCR4+ PDGFRA-.

markers.name: HNF4A
markers.note: Absent from day-5 definitive endoderm; presence at this stage suggests visceral endoderm (Si-Tayeb 2010).

functional_assays: Competence test: ability to give HNF4A+ hepatic, PDX1+ pancreatic or CDX2+ hindgut cells on further patterning
qc: CXCR4+ (with KIT or SOX17) >= 60% by flow before continuing; the Vallier protocols expect 60-90% and others >= 80-90%
SOX17+/FOXA2+ double-positive nuclei >= 85% by immunostaining (McCracken 2011)
FOXA2+/SOX17+ > 90% at the end of stage 1 for beta-cell differentiations (Hogrebe 2021)

protocols.name: Three-day serum-free induction: streak (Activin/CHIR/PI-103) then BMP block
protocols.principle: Anterior primitive streak is induced for 24 h with high Activin plus Wnt activation and PI3K inhibition, then BMP is inhibited while Activin continues so that streak cells become endoderm rather than mesoderm.
protocols.efficiency: 94.0 ± 3.1% CXCR4+PDGFRA- definitive endoderm by day 3 across 9 hESC and hiPSC lines
protocols.start_requirements: mTeSR1-grown hPSC passaged about 1:3 as small clumps (collagenase IV) onto fibronectin- or Matrigel-coated plates; start 1-2 days later.
materials: CDM2 basal medium (recipe in the paper's supplement)
tips: Timing is strict: the Wnt/PI3K-inhibitor pulse is 24 h, then BMP inhibition for 48 h.
The same paper continues to foregut (A-83-01 + DM3189), posterior foregut (RA + DM3189) or mid/hindgut (BMP4 10 ng/mL, CHIR 3 µM, FGF2 100 ng/mL) for 4 more days.
pitfalls: BMP present during days 1-3 diverts streak cells to mesoderm.
CDM2 composition must be taken from the supplement; substituting another basal medium changes efficiency.
unverified: Exact CDM2 recipe and seeding density are in the supplemental procedures, which were not read.

source.authors: Loh KM, Ang LT, Zhang J, et al.
source.title: Efficient endoderm induction from human pluripotent stem cells by logically directing signals controlling lineage bifurcations

stages.name: Anterior primitive streak
stages.base_medium: CDM2 (serum-free chemically defined basal medium of the paper)

factors.name: Activin A
factors.role: Nodal/TGF-beta signal; drives primitive streak and endoderm

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt activation for streak induction (first 24 h only)

stages.feeding: Single 24 h treatment
actions: Wash the cells before adding induction medium
Treat for exactly 24 h
stages.checkpoint: MIXL1/BRACHYURY+ streak-like cells; colonies loosen and cells spread

stages.name: Definitive endoderm

factors.name: DM3189 (LDN-193189)
factors.role: BMP inhibitor; blocks the mesoderm alternative

actions: Remove CHIR and PI-103
Keep BMP inhibited for the full 48 h
stages.checkpoint: CXCR4+ PDGFRA- cells with SOX17 and FOXA2 in most nuclei (94 ± 3% CXCR4+PDGFRA- reported across nine lines)

protocols.name: Chemically defined Activin/FGF2/BMP4/LY294002/CHIR induction (Vallier lab)
protocols.principle: Activin with FGF2, BMP4 and PI3K inhibition drives hPSC through a streak-like state; a one-day CHIR pulse boosts mesendoderm, and a final day in RPMI/B-27 with Activin and FGF2 commits the cells to endoderm.
protocols.efficiency: 60-90% CXCR4+ and/or SOX17+ by flow after 3 days
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC maintained in chemically defined medium with Activin A (10 ng/mL) and FGF2 (12 ng/mL); passaged as small clumps with collagenase/dispase onto gelatin plates pre-coated with serum-containing medium and grown for about 2 days before induction (the paper calls plating 'day 0' and the first induction day 'day 2').
tips: Add growth factors fresh each day rather than making bulk medium.
Optimise the FGF2 and CHIR99021 doses for each new line; the authors name this as the main lever for poor lines.
The later protocol from the same lab (Sampaziotis 2017) uses the same recipe with FGF2 at 80 ng/mL and reports >90% SOX17+.
pitfalls: About 20% of hiPSC lines were resistant to endoderm induction in the authors' hands.
Cell death on days 1-2 is expected; if it is excessive, lower the LY294002 dose.

source.authors: Hannan NR, Segeritz CP, Touboul T, Vallier L
source.title: Production of hepatocyte-like cells from human pluripotent stem cells

stages.name: Endoderm induction, day 1
stages.feeding: 24 h only
actions: Add all factors fresh to the medium on the day
Never carry CHIR99021 beyond the first day
stages.checkpoint: Cells migrate out of the colonies (EMT); T, MIXL1 and EOMES are induced

stages.name: Endoderm induction, day 2
stages.feeding: 24 h only
actions: Replace with the same medium without CHIR99021
stages.checkpoint: Original colony outlines are gone; SOX17 and CXCR4 switch on as T and MIXL1 fall

stages.name: Endoderm commitment, day 3
actions: Switch basal medium to RPMI/B-27
stages.checkpoint: 60-90% CXCR4+ and/or SOX17+ by flow at the end of this day

protocols.name: Activin A with stepped serum (D'Amour-style, as written out by the Wells lab)
protocols.principle: High Activin A in RPMI with serum raised stepwise from 0 to 2% mimics Nodal signalling while keeping PI3K/insulin signalling low; this is the low-serum Activin approach introduced by D'Amour et al. 2005 (Nat Biotechnol, PMID 16258519), in the form used for gut organoid work.
protocols.efficiency: 85-90% SOX17+/FOXA2+ double-positive cells
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC on hESC-qualified Matrigel in mTeSR1, passaged with dispase into 24-well plates and grown to about 85-90% confluence with minimal spontaneous differentiation.
tips: Make the Activin media fresh each day if possible.
The updated Wells-lab protocol (Broda 2019) plates single cells with Y-27632 the day before, adds NEAA, and includes BMP4 50 ng/mL on the first day only.
pitfalls: Starting density is the main failure point: too dense leaves undifferentiated patches, too sparse never reaches a usable sheet.
Serum lot matters; the authors specify defined FBS.
unverified: The original D'Amour 2005 methods text could not be opened (paywalled); only its abstract (Activin A plus low serum, up to 80% endoderm, CXCR4 enrichment) was confirmed. The day-by-day recipe here is from McCracken 2011.

source.title: Generating human intestinal tissue from pluripotent stem cells in vitro

protocols.name: STEMdiff Definitive Endoderm Kit (Supplement MR + CJ, 5 days)
protocols.principle: A near-confluent single-cell hPSC monolayer gets one day of basal medium with both Supplement MR and Supplement CJ, then three days with Supplement CJ alone, giving CXCR4+/SOX17+/FOXA2+/c-KIT+ definitive endoderm on day 5. The TeSR-E8 Optimized kit (05115) adds a 20X supplement used to pre-condition TeSR-E8 cultures before plating.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs about 70% confluent, maintained in eTeSR, mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-AOF (kit 05110) or in TeSR-E8 (kit 05115, after at least 24 h in TeSR-E8 Pre-Differentiation Medium). Single-cell passage with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent onto CellAdhere Laminin-521, Corning Matrigel hESC-qualified matrix or Vitronectin XF (Matrigel or Vitronectin XF only for TeSR-E8 cultures) at 2.1 x 10^5 cells/cm2 (2 x 10^6 cells per well of a 6-well plate) in maintenance medium + 10 µM Y-27632. STEMdiff Definitive Endoderm Kit (TeSR-E8 Optimized) (05115): the same plus Definitive Endoderm TeSR-E8 Supplement (20X) 7 mL
CellAdhere Laminin-521 (200-0117), Corning Matrigel hESC-qualified matrix (Corning 354277) or Vitronectin XF (07180; needs CellAdhere Dilution Buffer 07183)

Tune the seeding number so the well is 90-100% confluent on day 1.
TeSR-E8 Pre-Differentiation Medium keeps 2 weeks at 2-8°C.

TeSR-E8 cultures need at least 24 h in Pre-Differentiation Medium before day 0.

unverified: Efficiency: no percentage is given in the PIS.
The TeSR-E8 pre-conditioning stage is drawn as day -1 to 0; the PIS only says 'at least 24 hours' and until about 70% confluent, so it can be longer.
The protocol diagram is an image and was not available.

protocols.name: Gibco PSC Definitive Endoderm Induction Kit (2-day, two media)
protocols.principle: Two ready-to-use 1X media are applied for 24 hours each to a sparse hPSC culture on vitronectin, giving definitive endoderm in two days instead of the usual five or more.
protocols.efficiency: ≥90% CXCR4+/PDGFRα− definitive endoderm cells across multiple PSC lines (vendor product page)
protocols.start_requirements: Karyotypically normal, undifferentiated hPSCs grown feeder-free in Essential 8 or Essential 8 Flex on vitronectin (VTN-N), passaged routinely at about 70% surface coverage. On day 0 lift with StemPro Accutase as fine clumps and reseed on VTN-N at roughly a 1:10 split from a 70% confluent culture (1:15-1:30 if over 90% confluent; optimum 0.01-0.04 × 10^6 cells/cm²) so the culture is 15-30% confluent the next day. A ROCK inhibitor overnight is optional (1X RevitaCell, 10 µM Y-27632 or 0.5 µM thiazovivin).
materials: PSC Definitive Endoderm Induction Kit (Medium A 50 mL, Medium B 50 mL; stored at -20 to -5°C)
Essential 8 Medium (A15170 / A1517001) or Essential 8 Flex Medium Kit (A2858501)
tips: Schedule from Thermo user guide MAN0016100 Rev. 1.0; day 0 is plating, kit media are used on days 1 and 2.
Thaw each medium at 4°C overnight (or about 2 h at room temperature / 20 min at 37°C), mix well and use warm; thawed medium keeps 2 weeks at 2-8°C or can be aliquoted and frozen once.
The product page states that each incubation can be 24 ± 3 hours if needed.
Scrape off differentiated colonies daily before the experiment; they persist through induction.
pitfalls: Cold medium visibly disturbs the morphology of the differentiating cells.
Starting above 15-30% confluence makes the layer lift during induction.
Leaving spent medium behind at each switch reduces efficiency; aspirate completely.
unverified: The user guide's volume table lists 0.5 mM EDTA although the plating steps use Accutase; EDTA appears to be for routine passaging only.

protocols.name: Two-step serum-free EBs with high activin A (Kubo 2004)
protocols.principle: EBs are started in serum-free medium, then moved after two days to serum-replacement medium with a high dose of activin A, which drives a Brachyury+ primitive-streak-like population towards definitive endoderm instead of mesoderm.
protocols.start_requirements: Undifferentiated mouse ES cells, dissociated to single cells and seeded at 4 × 10³ cells/ml in 60-mm bacterial-grade Petri dishes.
tips: A Brachyury-GFP reporter line was used in the paper to show that endoderm comes from Brachyury+ cells that also have mesoderm potential; without a reporter, follow T, Foxa2 and Sox17 by qPCR.

Activin dose decides the outcome in these serum-free EB systems: later Keller-lab work used activin A at 25-50 ng/ml (with Wnt3a 3-5 ng/ml) for endoderm and 2 ng/ml (with Wnt3a and BMP4 0.3-1 ng/ml) for mesoderm (Gadue 2009).
The paper also reports endoderm induction by a limited exposure to serum as an alternative to activin A (abstract).
In a later use of this protocol by the same first author (Kubo 2011), EBs were kept to day 10 and then plated on Matrigel-coated dishes in IMDM + 15% FCS for further maturation.
pitfalls: Too little activin, or added BMP4, shifts the Brachyury+ population towards mesoderm (see the dose ranges in the tips).

Afp is also made by visceral (extra-embryonic) endoderm that forms on the outside of EBs, so Afp alone does not prove definitive endoderm; use Foxa2/Sox17 together with c-Kit/Cxcr4 and absence of extra-embryonic markers.
Seeding density is very low (4 × 10³ cells/ml); count carefully.
unverified: The full text of Kubo 2004 was not accessible (publisher page showed abstract only). Cell density, media, Kit ligand and activin A 100 ng/ml for days 2-6 are taken from Kubo et al. 2011 (PLoS One 6:e24058, PMID 21931641), where the same first author restates this method as 'Protocol #1 … as previously described' citing Kubo 2004.
Activin A concentrations other than 100 ng/ml tested in the original paper were not confirmed.
Percentage of Foxa2+ or c-Kit+ cells in the original paper not confirmed, so efficiency is left empty.
The hepatocyte maturation conditions of the original paper were not confirmed and are not given as a stage.

materials: Low-attachment Petri dishes and 24-well low-cluster plates
Antibodies to c-Kit and Cxcr4 for flow
tips: BMP4 is the key addition: without it the activin-induced endoderm is not efficiently specified to the hepatic lineage.

c-Kit/Cxcr4 flow at the end of the activin step is the in-process control; Keller-lab reporter lines (Brachyury-GFP, Foxa2-hCD4) or the ENDM1 antibody have been used for sorting the endoderm fraction.
Later papers from the same groups use 75 ng/ml activin A from day 2 to day 5 for the endoderm step (Han 2011; Bardot 2017), so the activin dose and length of the step vary between versions.

Versions of this protocol differ on timing: one restating paper re-aggregates with BMP4/bFGF/activin at day 4 and plates at day 6, another plates on gelatin at day 5. Decide on one schedule and keep it.

protocols.name: Low-serum monolayer with small molecules IDE1 or IDE2 (Borowiak 2009)
protocols.principle: Two cell-permeable small molecules found in a 4000-compound screen, IDE1 and IDE2, induce Sox17+/Foxa2+ definitive endoderm from feeder-depleted ES cells plated as a sparse monolayer in low-serum medium, replacing activin A or Nodal.
protocols.efficiency: At day 6 of treatment 81 ± 14% (IDE1) and 76 ± 14% (IDE2) of mouse ES-derived cells were Sox17+, and over 95% of the Sox17+ cells co-expressed Foxa2; activin A gave fewer Sox17+ cells at early time points (13% at day 2, 28% at day 4)
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ES cells grown on irradiated MEF feeders in DMEM + 15% FBS + LIF to 80-90% confluence. Deplete feeders by plating the suspension on gelatin for 30 min, then seed the ES cells at 2,500 cells/cm² on gelatinised plates and culture overnight before induction.
materials: Irradiated MEF feeders and ES medium with LIF for maintenance
Optional: Wnt3a, activin A or Nodal for a growth-factor control
tips: Growth-factor control arm from the same paper: Wnt3a 25 ng/ml + activin A 50 ng/ml (or Nodal 500 ng/ml) in DMEM + L-glutamine + 0.2% FBS for 1 day, then activin A or Nodal alone in the same medium for 4-6 days.
Adding Nodal to IDE2 raised Sox17+ cells at day 4 (55.8% versus 42% with compound alone); Wnt3a added nothing, and combining IDE1 with IDE2 gave no synergy.
For pancreatic progenitors the paper then switches to DMEM + B27 with FGF10 50 ng/ml, KAAD-cyclopamine 0.75 µM and retinoic acid 2 µM (or indolactam V 330 nM) for 4 days.
A Sox17 reporter line (Sox17-dsRed in the paper) makes dose-finding quick; titrate the compound on your own line.
pitfalls: The paper is internally inconsistent on dose: the Results give 250-800 nM as the most effective non-toxic range, while the Experimental Procedures say compounds were added at 5 µM (the screening concentration). Titrate rather than assume.

Sox17 is also expressed by extra-embryonic endoderm; dispersed Sox17+ cells that co-express Gata4, Sparc, Afp or Dab2 are extra-embryonic, whereas compound-induced definitive endoderm forms clustered epithelial patches lacking those markers.
Starting density is low (2,500 cells/cm²); residual feeders or higher density change the response.

protocols.name: Planar stages 1-4 of the Millman-lab beta-cell protocol
protocols.principle: Activin/CHIR endoderm, KGF gut tube, a high-retinoid PDX1 induction step and a low-retinoid step with KGF, PKC activation, hedgehog inhibition and BMP inhibition give PDX1+/NKX6-1+ progenitors on plastic in 12 days.
protocols.efficiency: >40% PDX1+/NKX6-1+ required at the end of stage 4; >80% PDX1+ at the end of stage 3
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in mTeSR1 on Matrigel, passaged as single cells with TrypLE and 10 µM Y-27632. Seed differentiation plates near confluence at 0.32-0.74 x 10^6 cells/cm2 (line-dependent; 0.53 x 10^6 cells/cm2, i.e. 5 x 10^6 per well of a 6-well plate, is the suggested starting point) and begin 24 h later on a confluent monolayer.
tips: Stage 4 flow for PDX1/NKX6-1 is the authors' routine quality-control check.
Keeping the cells attached to stiff plastic helps NKX6-1 induction and prevents premature NEUROG3 expression.
pitfalls: Seeding density is line-dependent and is the first thing to optimise.

source.authors: Hogrebe NJ, Maxwell KG, Augsornworawat P, Millman JR
source.title: Generation of insulin-producing pancreatic β cells from multiple human stem cell lines

stages.name: Stage 1: definitive endoderm
stages.base_medium: BE1 (MCDB131 + glucose 0.8 g, NaHCO3 0.587 g, BSA 0.5 g and GlutaMAX 5 mL per 500 mL)
stages.feeding: Daily

Days 1-3: Activin A only

stages.name: Stage 2: primitive gut tube
stages.base_medium: BE2 (MCDB131 + glucose 0.4 g, NaHCO3 0.587 g, BSA 0.5 g, GlutaMAX 5 mL and vitamin C 22 mg per 500 mL)
stages.feeding: Daily

stages.feeding: Daily
actions: Protect retinoic acid from light
stages.checkpoint: >80% PDX1+ by flow; a 'hill and valley' texture is common

stages.name: Stage 4: pancreatic progenitor 2
stages.feeding: Daily

stages.checkpoint: >40% PDX1+/NKX6-1+ by flow (the routine go/no-go check)

protocols.name: STEMdiff Pancreatic Progenitor Kit (four stages, six media)
protocols.principle: A serum-free four-stage monolayer protocol with daily feeding: definitive endoderm (2 days), primitive gut tube (3 days), posterior foregut endoderm (3 days) and pancreatic progenitors, giving PDX1+ NKX6.1+ SOX9+ cells that can be transplanted or matured further towards insulin-producing cells with published protocols.
protocols.efficiency: typically in the range of 66.5 - 74.5% PDX1+NKX6.1+ cells
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in mTeSR1 (or mTeSR Plus), about 70% confluent. Single-cell passage with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent onto tissue culture-treated 6-well plates coated with Corning Matrigel hESC-Qualified Matrix for at least 2 h at 37°C, at 2.6 x 10^5 cells/cm2 (2.5 x 10^6 cells per well) in mTeSR1 + 10 µM Y-27632. Must be about 90-100% confluent on day 1. For mTeSR Plus cultures, halve the seeding density and seed in mTeSR1 on day 0 (24 h transition).
materials: STEMdiff Pancreatic Progenitor Kit (05120): Endoderm Basal Medium 100 mL, Pancreatic Stage 2 - 4 Basal Medium 265 mL, Definitive Endoderm Supplement MR (100X) 350 µL and CJ (100X) 1.1 mL, Pancreatic Supplement 2A 240 µL, 2B 720 µL, 3 720 µL, 4 1200 µL
tips: Seeding density is the main variable; the best number depends on how fast the line grows.
Add and remove medium slowly at the well wall; a little medium left behind does no harm.
Stage 2-4 Basal Medium is stored at 2-8°C; supplements are thawed on ice, and leftover supplement can be frozen once in aliquots.
Lines kept in mTeSR Plus: halve the seeding density and plate in mTeSR1 on day 0.
pitfalls: If the well is not 90-100% confluent on day 1, do not extend the culture; restart.
Monolayer detachment: coat with Matrigel for at least 2 h at 37°C and avoid scratching or aspirating the sheet.
Supplements 2B, 3 and 4 contain human plasma-derived material.
unverified: Stage 4 length: the heading says '6 days', but feeds are given on Stage 4 days 1-5 and cells are ready 'on Day 6 of Stage 4'. Continuous day numbers here assume day 0 = seeding and Stage 1 day 1 = day 1, which puts the endpoint on day 14; the PIS itself numbers days within each stage only.
Supplement concentrations (X) for the Pancreatic Supplements are not printed; only volumes are given.
The schematic is an image and was not available.

factors.name: Y-27632 (Dihydrochloride) (not in kit)

Plate 2.6 x 10^5 viable cells/cm2 straight after aspirating the Matrigel

stages.feeding: Single 2 mL dose for 24 h
actions: Prepare Medium 2A (use at once) and Medium 2B (store at 2-8°C)
Change to warm Medium 2A

stages.base_medium: Medium 2B (STEMdiff Pancreatic Stage 2 - 4 Basal Medium + Supplement 2B)
stages.feeding: Daily full change, 2 mL per 6-well

Change the medium gently down the wall of the well

cell_types.name: Hepatocyte-like cells
cell_types.summary: Hepatocytes are the parenchymal cells of the liver responsible for plasma protein secretion, drug metabolism, and lipid and glycogen handling. hPSC-derived hepatocyte-like cells are used for metabolic disease modelling, hepatotoxicity testing and as a prospective cell-therapy source, although they remain fetal-like.
cell_types.maturation_note: Polygonal morphology from about day 15; albumin and A1AT secretion from about day 15 and inducible P450 activity from about day 20 (Hannan 2013). Cells keep AFP and CYP3A7 and survive only a few weeks.

morphology.endpoint: A tight sheet of polygonal cells with dark granular cytoplasm, round pale nuclei (some cells binucleate) and bright refractile borders resembling bile canaliculi; lipid droplets appear with time.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact, sharp-edged colonies of small cells.

stages.label: Definitive endoderm
stages.look: Colonies have dispersed into a continuous sheet of larger, flatter cells.

stages.label: Hepatic endoderm
stages.look: A cobblestone epithelium of polygonal cells forms as the sheet re-epithelialises.

stages.label: Hepatoblasts
stages.look: Cells darken, nuclei look pale and round, and bright cell borders begin to appear.

stages.label: Hepatocyte-like cells
stages.look: Polygonal, sometimes binucleate cells with canaliculi-like bright borders and lipid vesicles.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be lost within the first days of endoderm induction.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Core definitive endoderm transcription factor; check together with FOXA2.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Co-expressed with SOX17 in definitive endoderm and retained in most endoderm derivatives.

markers.name: HNF4A
markers.note: Switches on at hepatic specification; >80-90% of cells expected.

markers.name: AFP
markers.note: Fetal marker; stays high in hPSC-derived cells and falls only partially with maturation.

markers.name: TBX3
markers.note: Hepatoblast transcription factor used to monitor specification.

markers.name: ALB
markers.note: Main readout; about 80% ALB+ by flow in Si-Tayeb 2010; secreted albumin measurable by ELISA.

markers.name: SERPINA1
markers.note: Co-stained with albumin; also the disease readout in A1AT-deficiency models.

markers.name: KRT18
markers.note: Hepatocyte cytokeratin, co-stained with albumin.

markers.name: TTR
markers.note: Hepatic secreted protein.

markers.name: CYP3A4
markers.note: Adult P450; activity is well below primary hepatocytes.

markers.name: CYP3A7
markers.note: Fetal P450; persistent expression shows the fetal-like state of the cells.

functional_assays: Albumin and A1AT secretion (ELISA)
CYP3A4 activity and induction
Glycogen storage (PAS stain)
LDL uptake (DiI-LDL)
Indocyanine green uptake and release
Oil Red O lipid staining
qc: Endoderm: >= 60% CXCR4+/SOX17+ before hepatic specification (Hannan 2013)
HNF4A+ in about 90% of cells at the hepatic endoderm stage (Hannan 2013)
Albumin+ about 80% by flow at the end of the Si-Tayeb protocol
AFP+/HNF4A+ 86-89% at the end of the DMSO stage (Siller 2015)

protocols.name: Four 5-day stages: Activin, BMP4/FGF2, HGF, oncostatin M (Duncan lab)
protocols.principle: Mimics liver development in four growth-factor steps of five days each, with the middle stages run at 4% oxygen: Activin for endoderm, BMP4 plus FGF2 for hepatic specification, HGF for hepatoblast expansion and oncostatin M for maturation.
protocols.efficiency: About 80-85% albumin-positive cells by flow cytometry (hESC and hiPSC)
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free monolayer on Matrigel in MEF-conditioned hESC medium, maintained at 4% O2 / 5% CO2; >95% OCT4+ at the start.
tips: Needs a tri-gas incubator for the 4% oxygen steps.
Works as a true monolayer without embryoid bodies or serum.
pitfalls: Cells remain fetal-like (AFP stays high).
Small timing differences in marker onset between hESC and hiPSC lines were noted by the authors.
unverified: Feeding frequency, B-27 type and seeding density are in the supplementary methods, which were not read.

source.authors: Si-Tayeb K, Noto FK, Nagaoka M, et al.
source.title: Highly efficient generation of human hepatocyte-like cells from induced pluripotent stem cells

stages.name: Definitive endoderm
stages.feeding: Not stated in the main text
actions: Move the cultures to ambient oxygen / 5% CO2 for this stage
stages.checkpoint: >80% FOXA2+, GATA4+, SOX17+; OCT4 lost in >90% of cells; HNF4A still negative

stages.name: Hepatic specification
stages.feeding: Not stated in the main text
actions: Move the cultures to 4% O2 / 5% CO2
stages.checkpoint: >80% HNF4A+; GATA4 and SOX17 fall while FOXA2 persists

stages.name: Hepatoblast expansion
stages.feeding: Not stated in the main text
actions: Keep at 4% O2 / 5% CO2
stages.checkpoint: Strong AFP in nearly all FOXA2+ cells

stages.name: Hepatocyte maturation
stages.feeding: Not stated in the main text
actions: Return the cultures to ambient oxygen / 5% CO2
stages.checkpoint: Polygonal, partly binucleate albumin+ cells; albumin detectable in medium

protocols.name: Chemically defined route via anterior endoderm (Vallier lab)
protocols.principle: Endoderm made with Activin/FGF2/BMP4/LY294002/CHIR is anteriorised with Activin alone, specified to hepatic endoderm with BMP4 and FGF10, and matured with oncostatin M and HGF.
protocols.efficiency: Under optimal conditions >85% ALB+/A1AT+ cells; about 15 million immature hepatocytes from 600,000 hPSC plated on a 10 cm dish
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC maintained in chemically defined medium with Activin A (10 ng/mL) and FGF2 (12 ng/mL); passaged as small clumps with collagenase/dispase onto gelatin plates pre-coated with serum-containing medium and grown for about 2 days before induction (the paper calls plating 'day 0' and the first induction day 'day 2').
tips: The paper counts days from plating, so its 'day 25' endpoint is day 23 here.
If BMP4 harms hepatoblast specification in a given line, the authors replace that stage with 3 extra days of Activin in RPMI/B-27.
pitfalls: About 20% of hiPSC lines failed at the endoderm step.
Survival beyond the assay window varies by line; the troubleshooting table notes HepatoZYME can replace the Lonza basal medium if a line responds poorly.

source.authors: Hannan NR, Segeritz CP, Touboul T, Vallier L
source.title: Production of hepatocyte-like cells from human pluripotent stem cells

stages.name: Endoderm induction, day 1
stages.feeding: 24 h only
actions: Add all factors fresh to the medium on the day
Never carry CHIR99021 beyond the first day
stages.checkpoint: Cells migrate out of the colonies (EMT); T, MIXL1 and EOMES are induced

stages.name: Endoderm induction, day 2
stages.feeding: 24 h only
actions: Replace with the same medium without CHIR99021
stages.checkpoint: Original colony outlines are gone; SOX17 and CXCR4 switch on as T and MIXL1 fall

stages.name: Endoderm commitment, day 3
actions: Switch basal medium to RPMI/B-27
stages.checkpoint: 60-90% CXCR4+ and/or SOX17+ by flow at the end of this day

stages.name: Anterior definitive endoderm
stages.feeding: Daily for 3 days
actions: Feed every 24 h
stages.checkpoint: Cells re-epithelialise into a monolayer expressing FOXA2 and HHEX

stages.name: Hepatic specification
stages.feeding: Daily for 3 days, then leave a further 24 h
actions: Monitor HNF4A, PROX1, HHEX, AFP and TBX3 by qPCR
stages.checkpoint: About 90% HNF4A+ cells; dark cytoplasm and pale nuclei

stages.name: Hepatocyte maturation
stages.base_medium: Hepatocyte Basal Medium (Lonza CC-3199) prepared with its supplement kit
stages.feeding: Every 2 days
actions: Assay protein secretion, P450 activity, LDL uptake and glycogen between about days 18 and 28 of differentiation
stages.checkpoint: Polygonal, multinucleated cells with canaliculi-like borders from about day 13; albumin and A1AT in the medium

protocols.name: Growth-factor-free: CHIR99021, DMSO, then dexamethasone + dihexa
protocols.principle: A 24 h GSK3-inhibitor pulse is enough to make endoderm, DMSO specifies hepatic progenitors, and dexamethasone with the HGF-receptor agonist dihexa replaces HGF/oncostatin M for maturation.
protocols.efficiency: 86-89% AFP+/HNF4A+ hepatic progenitors after the DMSO stage
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in Essential 8 on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel, passaged with 0.5 mM EDTA; seeded at a 1:3-1:4 split into Matrigel-coated 12-well plates and started 24 h later. Optimal density must be set per line.
tips: Cheap: no recombinant growth factors.
Titrate CHIR99021 (the authors tested 1-10 µM) and the insulin content of B-27 on each new line.
pitfalls: Dihexa was a gift from its inventor in the paper and is not a standard catalogue reagent everywhere; check supply before starting.
The maturation medium contains FBS, so the method is growth-factor-free but not serum-free.
unverified: Final percentage of albumin-positive cells is given in a figure and was not captured.

source.authors: Siller R, Greenhough S, Naumovska E, Sullivan GJ
source.title: Small-molecule-driven hepatocyte differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells

stages.name: Phase I: CHIR pulse
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 GlutaMAX + B-27 (with or without insulin)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; drives cells through primitive streak to endoderm

actions: Wash with PBS, then add CHIR medium
Use 3 µM for H1; 4 µM in B-27 minus insulin was best for the other lines tested

stages.name: Phase I: rest
stages.feeding: 24 h without factors
actions: Remove CHIR99021
stages.checkpoint: FOXA2+/SOX17+ endoderm with raised HHEX, CER1 and GSC

stages.name: Phase II: hepatic specification
stages.base_medium: KnockOut DMEM + 20% KnockOut Serum Replacement + 2 mM GlutaMAX + 100 µM 2-mercaptoethanol + 1x NEAA
stages.feeding: Every 48 h
actions: Expect a burst of proliferation and a rapid change in morphology
stages.checkpoint: 86-89% AFP+/HNF4A+ cells

stages.name: Phase III: maturation
stages.base_medium: Leibovitz L-15 + 8.3% tryptose phosphate broth + 8.3% FBS + 10 µM hydrocortisone 21-hemisuccinate + 50 µg/mL sodium L-ascorbate + 0.58% ITS + 2 mM GlutaMAX
stages.feeding: Every 48 h
actions: Culture for 10 days
stages.checkpoint: Polygonal albumin+/HNF4A+ cells with A1AT, glycogen storage and ICG uptake

protocols.name: STEMdiff Hepatocyte Kit (three stages, 21 days)
protocols.principle: A serum-free, three-stage 2D protocol on Laminin-521: definitive endoderm with the Supplement MR/CJ system (days 1-5), hepatic progenitors in Hepatic Progenitor Medium (days 5-10), then hepatocyte-like cells in Hepatocyte Medium (days 10-21) that express albumin and alpha-1 antitrypsin.
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained in eTeSR, mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-AOF on CellAdhere Laminin-521 (cells kept on Matrigel should be adapted to Laminin-521 for at least one passage); seed 6-8 days after their last passage, after removing differentiated areas. Plate single cells in maintenance medium + 10 µM Y-27632 on Laminin-521-coated (8 µg/mL, overnight at 2-8°C) 24- or 96-well tissue culture-treated plates. Seeding by maintenance medium: eTeSR 4.21 x 10^4, mTeSR1 2.11 x 10^5, mTeSR Plus 1.05 x 10^5, TeSR-AOF 2.11 x 10^5 cells/cm2. Monolayer must be at least 80% (80-100%) confluent on day 1.
materials: STEMdiff Hepatocyte Kit (100-0520): Endoderm Basal Medium (Hepatic) 100 mL, Definitive Endoderm 100X Supplement MR 0.35 mL, Supplement CJ 1.1 mL, Hepatic Progenitor Medium 100 mL, Hepatocyte Medium 150 mL
D-PBS with calcium and magnesium (Thermo Fisher 14040133)
eTeSR (100-1215), mTeSR1 (85850), mTeSR Plus (100-0276) or TeSR-AOF (100-0401)
tips: Run a seeding-density titration for first experiments and for each new line; the recommended density differs five-fold between eTeSR and mTeSR1 cultures.
Medium 1 keeps 1 day and Medium 2 keeps 3 days at 2-8°C; thawed Hepatic Progenitor Medium keeps 3 weeks and Hepatocyte Medium 2 weeks.
Laminin-521-coated plates can be stored up to 4 weeks at 2-8°C if sealed and never allowed to dry.
Warm media to room temperature before use.
pitfalls: Starting below 80% confluence on day 1.
Leaving differentiated colonies in the starting culture lowers efficiency.
Letting the Laminin-521 coat dry out inactivates it.
unverified: Efficiency: the PIS gives no percentage of ALB+ or A1AT+ cells.
Day 8: the PIS lists feeds on days 5, 6, 7 and 9 of the hepatic progenitor stage and does not mention day 8; whether day 8 is deliberately skipped is not stated.
The protocol diagram is an image and was not available.

stages.name: Day 0: seed hPSCs on Laminin-521
stages.base_medium: Single-cell passaging medium (maintenance medium + 10 µM Y-27632)

factors.name: Y-27632 (Dihydrochloride) (not in kit)
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor in the single-cell plating medium, day 0 only

stages.feeding: No feeding for 24 h
actions: The day before: dilute CellAdhere Laminin-521 to 8 µg/mL in ice-cold D-PBS with Ca/Mg, add 0.25 mL per 24-well (50 µL per 96-well), seal and coat overnight at 2-8°C
Swap the coating solution directly for passaging medium (0.5 mL per 24-well, 0.1 mL per 96-well) without letting the surface dry
Scrape off differentiated areas, rinse with D-PBS, treat with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent 8-10 min at 37°C and pipette to single cells
Count, spin 300 x g for 5 min and seed at the density for your maintenance medium
96-well plates: seed with a multichannel pipette and leave 1 h in the cabinet to settle
Seed spare wells if you want to check endoderm on day 5 and hepatic progenitors on day 10

stages.base_medium: Medium 1 (STEMdiff Endoderm Basal Medium (Hepatic) + Supplement MR + Supplement CJ)
stages.feeding: Single full change, 0.5 mL per 24-well (0.1 mL per 96-well), for 24 h
actions: Prepare Medium 1 and Medium 2 on day 1
Start only when wells are 80-100% confluent
Change to Medium 1

stages.name: Days 2-4: Medium 2 (definitive endoderm)
stages.base_medium: Medium 2 (STEMdiff Endoderm Basal Medium (Hepatic) + Supplement CJ)
stages.feeding: Full change on days 2, 3 and 4, 0.5 mL per 24-well
actions: Change to Medium 2 daily
Day 4: start thawing Hepatic Progenitor Medium overnight at 2-8°C
stages.checkpoint: Day 5: definitive endoderm by flow cytometry (CXCR4, c-Kit or SOX17) or qPCR (FOXA2, SOX17, CXCR4)

stages.name: Days 5-10: hepatic progenitors
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff Hepatic Progenitor Medium (ready to use)
stages.feeding: Full change of 0.5 mL per 24-well on days 5, 6, 7 and 9, as listed in the PIS
actions: Change to Hepatic Progenitor Medium on day 5 and feed on the listed days
Day 9: start thawing Hepatocyte Medium overnight at 2-8°C
Antibiotics (1%) may be added if wanted
stages.checkpoint: Day 10: hepatic progenitors by morphology, qPCR (AFP, HNF1B, CK19, HNF6, TBX3) or flow cytometry (% AFP+, HNF1B+, CK19+)

stages.name: Days 10-21: hepatocyte-like cells
stages.feeding: Full change of 0.5 mL per 24-well on day 10, day 12 and then every 2 days
actions: Change to Hepatocyte Medium on day 10
Feed every 2 days
Day 21: analyse
stages.checkpoint: Day 21: functional assays (CYP3A4 activity, albumin ELISA), qPCR (ALB, A1AT, HNF4A, CYP3A4, ASGR1, CPS1) and flow cytometry (% ALB+ and % A1AT+)

protocols.name: StemXVivo Hepatocyte Differentiation Kit
protocols.principle: Four pre-mixed factor cocktails used over two RPMI-based media take hPSCs stepwise through definitive endoderm, hepatic specification, hepatoblast expansion and hepatocyte maturation across 19 days, ending in albumin-positive hepatocyte-like cells for toxicology work.
protocols.efficiency: Vendor states a highly enriched population, greater than 70% purity, of hepatocyte-like cells
protocols.start_requirements: Wells coated with Cultrex Stem Cell Qualified RGF BME PathClear (3434-001-02) diluted 1:40 in ice-cold medium, 1-2 h at room temperature (0.5 mL per well of a 24-well plate; coverslips optional for ICC). The datasheet uses BG01V hESCs in MEF conditioned medium: Accutase dissociation and plating at 1.1-1.25 x 10^5 cells/cm2 in MEF conditioned medium with 4 ng/mL FGF basic, with daily feeding until the monolayer is 80-90% confluent. Differentiation works best started the day after plating. No ROCK inhibitor is specified.
materials: Cultrex Stem Cell Qualified RGF BME PathClear (3434-001-02)
MEF Conditioned Media (AR005) and Recombinant Human FGF basic (233-FB)
RPMI 1640; DMEM/F-12; GlutaMAX; optional penicillin-streptomycin; PBS; very low endotoxin BSA
Fixation and staining reagents, NorthernLights secondary (NL007), mounting medium (CTS011)
tips: Reconstituted cocktails are 500X; dilute each 1:500 into the matching base medium just before use
Note that the base medium changes from Supplement I to Supplement II at stage 3 - the cocktails are not interchangeable between base media
Plate with coverslips in some wells if albumin ICC is planned
pitfalls: Starting below about 80% confluency or from feeder-grown cells without depletion costs yield; feeder depletion may be needed
Different vessel formats need volume re-optimisation; the protocol is written for 24-well plates
19 days of daily to alternate-day feeding - a missed stage boundary cannot be made up later
unverified: No seeding guidance for feeder-free maintenance media or ROCK inhibitor use
The >70% purity figure is a vendor claim with no stated assay or marker threshold
No CYP activity or urea/albumin secretion numbers given

stages.base_medium: MEF conditioned medium with 4 ng/mL FGF basic

factors.name: Cultrex Stem Cell Qualified RGF BME (user-supplied)

factors.name: Hepatocyte Differentiation Base Media Supplement I (50X)

actions: Reconstitute Cocktail I in 250 uL 0.1% BSA/PBS and dilute 1:500 into warm Base Media I
Replace the stem cell medium with Stage 1 medium

cell_types.name: Liver organoids / liver buds
cell_types.summary: Liver organoids are three-dimensional hepatic tissues grown from hPSC-derived foregut cells; depending on the method they contain hepatocyte-like cells alone or together with stellate-like, Kupffer-like and biliary cells, or are built by mixing hepatic endoderm with endothelial and mesenchymal cells (liver buds). They are used to model steatohepatitis and fibrosis, to screen for drug-induced liver injury, and as transplantable tissue.
cell_types.maturation_note: Organoids are analysed between about day 20 and day 30; bile-acid transport and CYP3A4 induction are measurable at that point.

morphology.endpoint: Translucent epithelial cysts and denser spheres, roughly 100-300 µm across, embedded in a Matrigel drop; lumens are visible in many organoids.

stages.label: Pluripotent cells

stages.label: Liver organoids
stages.look: Cystic and dense epithelial organoids with visible lumens fill the Matrigel drop.

protocols.name: Multicellular human liver organoids from foregut spheroids (Takebe lab)
protocols.principle: Endoderm is posteriorised with FGF4 and CHIR until it buds into foregut spheroids; these are embedded in Matrigel, pulsed with retinoic acid, and matured in hepatocyte medium, which yields hepatocyte-like cells together with stellate-like and Kupffer-like cells.
protocols.efficiency: EpCAM+ epithelial cells 78.9 ± 7.4% of organoid cells; EpCAM-CD166+ stellate-like cells about 7%
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC dissociated with Accutase; 200,000 cells seeded on Matrigel- or iMatrix-coated plates (day 0). The paper numbers the first Activin day as day 1.
tips: For steatohepatitis modelling the organoids are freed from Matrigel and exposed to oleic acid (up to 800 µM) on ultra-low-attachment plates for 3-7 days.
Spheroid yield at day 6 is the practical go/no-go point.
pitfalls: The wording 'day 4-6' for the FGF4/CHIR step can be read as 2 or 3 days; spheroids are collected on day 6.
Organoid composition (parenchymal versus stellate-like and Kupffer-like cells) varies between lines.
unverified: Plate format for the 200,000-cell seeding and feeding interval during the retinoic acid step are not stated in the main methods.

cell_types.name: Intestinal organoids
cell_types.summary: Intestinal organoids are three-dimensional fetal-like gut tissues containing a CDX2+ epithelium with absorptive and secretory cells surrounded by mesenchyme. They are used to study intestinal development, host-microbe interaction, epithelial transport and inherited gut disease; small-intestinal and colonic versions exist.
cell_types.maturation_note: Spheroids form by day 5-7; organoids need 14 days in Matrigel to form pseudostratified epithelium and about 28 days for columnar epithelium with villus-like folds. Tissue stays fetal unless transplanted.

morphology.endpoint: Organoids of 0.5-2 mm in Matrigel with a folded, columnar epithelium around a central lumen that fills with shed cells and mucus, wrapped in a layer of mesenchyme.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies

stages.label: Intestinal organoids

protocols.name: Small-intestinal organoids: Activin, FGF4 + WNT3A, then R-spondin/Noggin/EGF (Spence/Wells)
protocols.principle: Endoderm is posteriorised with high FGF4 and WNT until the monolayer buds off CDX2+ mid/hindgut spheroids, which are embedded in Matrigel and grown in adult intestinal stem-cell medium. This is the step-by-step version of Spence et al. 2011 (Nature, PMID 21151107).
protocols.efficiency: Endoderm 85-90% SOX17+/FOXA2+; more than 90% of the organoid epithelium CDX2+
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC on hESC-qualified Matrigel in mTeSR1, split with dispase into 24-well plates and grown 2-4 days to about 85-90% confluence with minimal spontaneous differentiation.
tips: The authors kept organoids growing for 140 days by repeated splitting.
Pre-loading the Matrigel with growth factors is optional but improves spheroid outgrowth.
pitfalls: Wrong hPSC density at the start is the commonest failure: discard plates that are too dense or too sparse.
Whether spheroids form from endoderm of lower purity than 85-90% was not tested by the authors.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in mTeSR1 on Matrigel, passaged with Accutase and plated at 100,000 cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 24-well plate with 10 µM Y-27632 for the first day, then one more day in mTeSR1 before induction.
tips: Regional identity is fixed by the first 3 days in Matrigel and stays stable afterwards.

protocols.name: STEMdiff Intestinal Organoid Kit (endoderm, mid-/hindgut spheroids, Matrigel domes)
protocols.principle: Based on Spence et al. 2011: a clump-seeded hPSC monolayer is taken to definitive endoderm (3 days), then to mid-/hindgut, where spheroids bud off into the medium; these are collected, embedded in Matrigel domes and grown in Intestinal Organoid Growth Medium into organoids with epithelium and mesenchyme that can be passaged every 7-10 days or frozen.
protocols.start_requirements: High-quality hPSCs (under 5% differentiation) in mTeSR1, mTeSR Plus or TeSR-AOF, about 70% confluent. Clump-passage with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (8 min at room temperature, then scrape) and seed 6,000 clumps of 50-200 µm per well of a 24-well plate coated with Corning Matrigel hESC-Qualified Matrix, in 0.5 mL maintenance medium; no ROCK inhibitor is used. Start when 85-90% confluent, 24 h later.
materials: STEMdiff Intestinal Organoid Kit (05140): Endoderm Basal Medium 100 mL, Definitive Endoderm Supplement CJ (100X) 1.1 mL, Gastrointestinal Supplement PK 0.64 mL, Gastrointestinal Supplement UB 0.64 mL, Intestinal Organoid Basal Medium 100 mL, Intestinal Organoid Supplement 2 mL
STEMdiff Intestinal Organoid Growth Medium (05145) for continued passaging: Intestinal Organoid Basal Medium + Intestinal Organoid Supplement
Corning Matrigel hESC-Qualified Matrix (Corning 354277) for the monolayer
Corning Matrigel GFR Basement Membrane Matrix, Phenol Red-Free (Corning 356231) for domes
tips: For a new line seed 4,000, 5,000 and 6,000 clumps per well and start all on the same day; too low a density on day 3 gives no spheroids.
Complete growth medium keeps 2 weeks at 2-8°C; thawed basal medium 2 months; supplement aliquots are single-use.
Use a Matrigel lot with at least 8 mg/mL protein and remove all residual medium before embedding, otherwise domes collapse or spheroids sink and attach.
For more differentiated intestinal cell types keep organoids 2 weeks without passaging, feeding every 3-4 days.
pitfalls: Cells lifting during endoderm induction: day 0 density too high or more than 24 h between changes.
Over-pipetting organoids to single cells at passage; fragments should stay 100-500 µm.
Changing the spheroid harvest day between experiments changes regional identity.
unverified: Efficiency: no percentage or organoid yield is stated.

The spheroid harvest day is the user's choice within days 5-9; the stage boundaries here use day 8 (the day the manual says budding is often greatest), so the embedding day and duration_days (day 8 + 7 days to first passage) are illustrative, not fixed by the manual.
The manual calls the seeding day only '24 hours before day 0'; it is labelled day -1 here.
Supplement concentrations (X) for Supplements PK, UB and the Intestinal Organoid Supplement are not printed.
The protocol diagram is an image and was not available.
protocols.product: STEMdiff Intestinal Organoid Kit; STEMdiff Intestinal Organoid Growth Medium

stages.name: Day -1: clump seeding
stages.feeding: No feeding for 24 h; if under 85-90% confluent, give fresh medium and wait another 24 h
actions: Coat a 24-well tissue culture-treated plate with Matrigel for at least 1 h at room temperature
Remove differentiated areas, treat with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent 8 min at room temperature, scrape in maintenance medium
Pipette to 50-200 µm clumps (not single cells) and count clumps in a 5 µL sample
Seed 6,000 clumps per well; for a new line compare 4,000, 5,000 and 6,000
Rock the plate to spread the clumps and leave it undisturbed
stages.checkpoint: 85-90% confluent with under 5% differentiation before day 0

stages.name: Days 0-3: definitive endoderm
stages.base_medium: DE Medium (STEMdiff Endoderm Basal Medium + STEMdiff Definitive Endoderm Supplement CJ)
stages.feeding: Full change every 24 h or less: 0.7 mL per 24-well on day 0, 0.5 mL on days 1 and 2, warmed to 37°C
actions: Make DE Medium for all three days on day 0 and keep it at 2-8°C
Add medium dropwise down the side of a tilted plate
Keep the plate out of the incubator as briefly as possible; the cells are fragile after the first 24 h
stages.checkpoint: Heavy cell death is normal; by 72 h a confluent sheet of tightly packed endoderm. Day 3: FOXA2, SOX17, CXCR4 and c-KIT by flow cytometry or FOXA2/SOX17 staining

stages.name: Days 3-8: mid-/hindgut and spheroid release
stages.base_medium: MH Medium (STEMdiff Endoderm Basal Medium + STEMdiff Gastrointestinal Supplement PK + Supplement UB)
stages.feeding: Full change of 0.5 mL every 24 h (days 3 to 9 at the latest), medium at room temperature
actions: Day 3: switch to MH Medium
From day 4, move each day's spent medium to a spare 24-well plate to count the spheroids that have lifted, then add fresh MH Medium
Return plates to the incubator within 30 min
On the chosen day (spheroids float free on days 5-9; day 8 often shows most budding) collect about 50 free-floating spheroids per dome into a 15 mL tube
Harvest on the same day in every experiment: time in MH Medium sets regional identity (shorter towards duodenum, longer towards ileum)
stages.checkpoint: 3D structures may appear from day 4; free-floating spheroids of 75 µm or more on days 5-9. Mid-/hindgut cells are CDX2+

stages.name: Embed spheroids and grow organoids
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff Intestinal Organoid Growth Medium (Intestinal Organoid Basal Medium + Intestinal Organoid Supplement + L-Glutamine)
stages.feeding: 0.5 mL per well; full change every 3-4 days
actions: Let spheroids settle, wash with 1 mL DMEM/F-12 with 15 mM HEPES, spin 300 x g for 5 min and remove as much liquid as possible
With a cold 100 µL tip mix the pellet into 50 µL cold Matrigel GFR (Corning 356231) and place one dome in the centre of a 24-well
Let the dome set 20 min at room temperature, then add 0.5 mL room-temperature growth medium at the side of the well

After 7-10 days passage: break the dome in cold DMEM/F-12, pipette organoids to 100-500 µm fragments in tubes pre-rinsed with Anti-Adherence Rinsing Solution, let fragments settle on ice, wash, spin 200 x g for 5 min and re-embed in 50 µL Matrigel
Keep passaging every 7-10 days, or freeze fragments in CryoStor CS10
stages.checkpoint: Organoids with epithelium and mesenchyme; 40-80 organoids per dome is the target density. Markers listed: CDX2, E-cadherin, EpCAM, MUC2, KRT20, villin, KLF5, SOX9, CHGA, vimentin, desmin

cell_types.notes: hPSC-derived intestinal organoids contain mesenchyme, unlike adult-stem-cell enteroids, and are fetal in maturity. Spheroid yield varies between lines and between FGF4 lots.

cell_types.name: Cholangiocytes (bile duct)
cell_types.summary: Cholangiocytes line the bile ducts, modify bile through secretion and absorption, and carry a primary cilium. hPSC-derived cholangiocytes are used to model cystic fibrosis liver disease, polycystic liver disease and other cholangiopathies, and to test CFTR modulators.
cell_types.maturation_note: Organoids form 2-4 days after transfer to 3D and are used at about day 26 (Sampaziotis 2017); ciliated, CFTR-functional monolayers take until about day 49 (Ogawa 2021).

morphology.endpoint: In 3D: thin-walled, clear cystic organoids and branching tubular structures in Matrigel. In 2D on feeders: a tight cobblestone epithelial sheet.

stages.label: Definitive endoderm

stages.label: Cholangiocyte progenitors

stages.label: Cholangiocyte organoids

protocols.principle: Chemically defined endoderm is taken through foregut and hepatoblast stages, steered to biliary progenitors with FGF10, Activin and retinoic acid, then matured as organoids in Matrigel with EGF.
protocols.efficiency: CK7+ in >75% of cells at the end; stage checkpoints of >90% SOX17, >90% GATA4, >95% AFP and >75% SOX9
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC maintained in CDM-PVA with Activin (10 ng/mL) and FGF2 (12 ng/mL), passaged as 50-100-cell clumps with collagenase/dispase onto gelatin-coated plates; 500,000-1,000,000 cells per 10 cm dish for differentiation, grown until ready. The paper numbers the first induction day as day 1.
tips: Clump size at the 3D transfer is critical: single cells die and large clumps sink and fail to form organoids.
Keep the Matrigel mix on ice and plate onto a warmed plate so that domes set quickly.
pitfalls: Poor hepatoblast or progenitor stages cannot be rescued later; check AFP and SOX9 before embedding.
Replating density after an optional split must give a near-confluent layer; overlapping layers reduce efficiency.
unverified: Full recipe of the supplemented William's E medium was only partly captured.

stages.checkpoint: 60-90% CXCR4+ and/or SOX17+ by flow at the end of this day

stages.name: Foregut progenitors
stages.feeding: Daily
actions: After 3 days judge morphology: continue in place, or split with cell dissociation buffer and replate at 150,000 cells/cm2 with 10 µM Y-27632

stages.feeding: Daily
actions: Monitor HNF4A, AFP and TBX3

stages.checkpoint: >75% SOX9+ cells

stages.feeding: Every 2 days
actions: Lift cells with cell dissociation buffer as clumps of 10-50 cells
Resuspend in 50% Matrigel with EGF and Y-27632
Plate 50 µL domes on a pre-warmed 24-well plate, invert, and set 30 min
Overlay with medium
stages.checkpoint: Organoids appear within 2-4 days; CK7+ >75%, ALP and GGT activity at the end

protocols.name: Hepatoblast co-culture on OP9-Jagged1, then RA and Noggin/forskolin/ROCK inhibitor for ciliated cells (Keller/Ogawa)
protocols.principle: Hepatoblasts are pushed to the biliary lineage by Notch ligand presented on OP9-Jagged1 feeder cells with HGF and EGF; retinoic acid then induces CFTR, and Noggin, forskolin and Y-27632 drive ciliogenesis. This is the open-access refinement of Ogawa 2015 (Nat Biotechnol, PMID 26167630).
protocols.efficiency: 87.2 ± 2.5% of cells ciliated after the RA then Noggin/forskolin/Y-27632 sequence
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC maintained on irradiated MEFs, then plated on 2.5% Matrigel at 100,000-175,000 cells per well of a 12-well plate one day before induction (density set per line). Days 0-21 are run at 5% O2.
tips: Check albumin by flow before the co-culture step; slow iPSC lines need extra days as hepatoblasts.
The cells can be moved to 3D gels to form cysts for CFTR swelling assays.
pitfalls: Requires the OP9-Jagged1 feeder line and an irradiator.
Long protocol (7 weeks) with a low-oxygen phase; feeder and hepatoblast quality both affect the outcome.
unverified: The original Ogawa 2015 Nat Biotechnol methods (paywalled) were not read; all values are from the 2021 paper.

cell_types.name: Pancreatic beta cells / islets
cell_types.summary: Beta cells are the insulin-secreting endocrine cells of the pancreatic islets. hPSC-derived beta cells and islet-like clusters are used for diabetes modelling, drug and toxicity studies, and cell-replacement therapy.
cell_types.maturation_note: Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion appears 10-14 days into the final stage and peaks around day 14 of that stage; function declines after extended culture.

morphology.endpoint: Planar: rounded, enlarged, slightly golden endocrine cells in a monolayer with some holes. After aggregation or in suspension: smooth, compact islet-like clusters of roughly 150-250 µm.

stages.label: Confluent pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Single-cell-seeded hPSC forming a fully confluent sheet of small cells.

stages.label: Definitive endoderm
stages.look: Confluent sheet after some cell death; cells look larger and flatter.

stages.label: Pancreatic progenitors
stages.look: Dense monolayer, often with a ridged 'hill and valley' texture.

stages.label: Endocrine cells
stages.look: Monolayer with some holes after latrunculin treatment; cells start to round up.

stages.label: Islet-like clusters
stages.look: Rounded, golden endocrine cells; after orbital shaking they form smooth clusters of about 200-250 µm.

markers.name: SOX9

functional_assays: Static glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (2 mM versus 20 mM glucose)
Dynamic perifusion GSIS (first and second phase)
Insulin content and proinsulin/insulin ratio
Dithizone staining
Transplantation into diabetic mice
qc: FOXA2+/SOX17+ >90% at the end of stage 1
PDX1+ >80% at the end of stage 3
PDX1+/NKX6-1+ >40% at the end of stage 4 (all Hogrebe 2021)

protocols.name: Six-stage planar protocol with latrunculin A (Millman lab)
protocols.principle: The whole differentiation is run as a monolayer; because stiff plastic keeps actin polymerised and blocks NEUROG3, a 24 h latrunculin A pulse at the start of endocrine induction releases endocrine commitment. Cells mature in an enriched serum-free medium and can be aggregated into clusters.
protocols.efficiency: Quality gates: >90% FOXA2+/SOX17+ (stage 1), >80% PDX1+ (stage 3), >40% PDX1+/NKX6-1+ (stage 4); final C-peptide+/NKX6-1+ fraction is line-dependent
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in mTeSR1 on Matrigel, passaged as single cells with TrypLE and 10 µM Y-27632. Seed differentiation plates near confluence at 0.32-0.74 x 10^6 cells/cm2 (line-dependent; 0.53 x 10^6 cells/cm2, i.e. 5 x 10^6 per well of a 6-well plate, is the suggested starting point) and begin 24 h later on a confluent monolayer.
tips: Optimise seeding density per line first, using stage 1 and stage 4 flow as readouts.
If stage 5 death is excessive lower latrunculin A to 0.5-0.75 µM; if off-target areas dominate raise it to 1.5-2 µM.
Aggregation loses up to 50% of cells but enriches endocrine cells.
pitfalls: Starting below confluence changes proliferation and derails stage 1.
Function declines after prolonged stage 6 culture; plan assays for about day 14 of stage 6.

factors.name: ALK5 inhibitor II
factors.role: TGF-beta inhibition; favours the beta-cell fate

stages.feeding: Daily to day 4 of the stage, then every other day
actions: Add latrunculin A for the first 24 h only
Continue the same medium without latrunculin for 6 more days

stages.feeding: Every other day

Assess function around day 14 of this stage

protocols.name: Suspension (spinner flask) SC-beta protocol (Melton lab)
protocols.principle: Clusters grown in spinner flasks are stepped through endoderm, gut tube and two pancreatic progenitor stages, then given Notch and TGF-beta inhibition with thyroid hormone and betacellulin to make monohormonal, glucose-responsive beta cells at scale.
protocols.efficiency: 33 ± 2% NKX6-1+/C-peptide+ cells on average; >55% NKX6-1+/PDX1+ at the PP2 stage
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC adapted to suspension culture in mTeSR1 in 500 mL spinner flasks at 70 rpm; seeded at 6 x 10^5 cells/mL in mTeSR1 + 10 µM Y-27632 and started 48 h later (HUES8) or 72 h later (the two hiPSC lines).
materials: S1, S2, S3, S5 and S6 base media (recipes in the paper's supplement)
tips: The paper numbers days from 1; stage boundaries here are converted to a day-0 start.

The Millman-lab refinement (Velazco-Cruz 2019, Stem Cell Reports, PMID 30661993) shortens PP1 to 1 day, resizes clusters, removes ALK5 inhibitor and T3 from the last stage and uses serum-free ESFM, which gave dynamic first- and second-phase secretion.
pitfalls: Needs hPSC already adapted to suspension culture and spinner equipment.
Without the later refinements insulin secretion lacks clear first- and second-phase dynamics; some polyhormonal cells remain.
unverified: Compositions of the S1-S6 base media are in the supplemental procedures and were not read.

cell_types.name: Gastric (stomach) organoids
cell_types.summary: Gastric organoids are three-dimensional stomach tissues with a glandular epithelium of mucous, endocrine and, in the fundic type, chief and parietal cells. They are used to study stomach development, Helicobacter pylori infection and gastric disease.
cell_types.maturation_note: Both types are analysed at about day 34; fundic organoids get a 2-day BMP4 + MEK-inhibitor pulse at day 30 to induce parietal cells.

morphology.endpoint: Translucent epithelial organoids in Matrigel that grow from small cysts into larger structures with a complex, budded glandular epithelium.

protocols.name: Antral gastric organoids (Wells lab)
protocols.principle: Endoderm is turned into posterior foregut spheroids by combining Wnt and FGF4 with BMP inhibition and a late retinoic acid pulse; in Matrigel, three more days of EGF, Noggin and retinoic acid followed by EGF alone give antral-type stomach epithelium. Protocol paper for McCracken et al. 2014 (Nature, PMID 25363776).
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in mTeSR1 on hESC-qualified Matrigel; single-cell passaged on day -1 into Matrigel-coated 24-well plates at a line-specific ratio so that the monolayer is at the target confluence on day 0.
tips: The first 6 days are identical for antral and fundic organoids, so both can be run from one plate.
Change medium at least every 4 days whatever its colour.
pitfalls: Confluence outside the target range on day 0 is the main cause of failed spheroid formation; restart rather than proceed.
The authors did not test media or supplements from other vendors.
unverified: No numerical efficiency was captured.

Support of host T-cell development after transplantation into mice (Parent 2013)

protocols.name: Five-medium monolayer protocol in X-VIVO 10 (Russ lab)
protocols.principle: High-density hPSC are taken to endoderm with Activin A (plus Wnt3a on the first day), anteriorised with a retinoid, pushed to pharyngeal endoderm with BMP4, TGF-beta inhibition, retinoid and hedgehog activation, and then held in a multi-factor medium (FGF8, Wnt3a, BMP and hedgehog inhibition, EGF, low Activin) that promotes thymic epithelial progenitors. Bio-protocol version of Ramos et al. 2022 (J Allergy Clin Immunol, PMID 34331993).
protocols.efficiency: Ramos 2022 report about 90% EPCAM+ and about 45% EPCAM+CD205+ cells at day 14; one 24-well yields about 6 x 10^6 progenitors
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in mTeSR Plus; on day -1 plate 600,000 single cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 24-well plate (3.15 x 10^5 cells/cm2) in mTeSR Plus + 10 µM Y-27632.
tips: For thymus organoids the authors combine the progenitors with hPSC-derived splanchnic mesoderm and haematopoietic progenitors (mesenchyme : haematopoietic : thymic = 1:1:20) on an air-liquid-interface insert; one well gives three organoids.
Medium-change timing matters: the authors stress a strict 24 h rhythm.
pitfalls: Thymic epithelial progenitors made in vitro are immature and need organoid culture with haematopoietic and mesenchymal cells, or transplantation, to become functional.
The very high seeding density is required; do not scale it down.
unverified: Stage names (endoderm, anteriorisation, pharyngeal endoderm) are my reading of the factor logic; the protocol itself labels the media only TCD-1 to TCD-5.
The day-14 efficiency figures come from Ramos 2022, not from the 2026 protocol.

cell_types.name: Lung alveolar epithelial type 2 cells
cell_types.summary: Alveolar type 2 cells produce and recycle pulmonary surfactant and act as the stem cells of the alveolus. hPSC-derived AT2 cells, grown as self-renewing alveolospheres, are used to model surfactant disorders, lung fibrosis and respiratory virus infection.
cell_types.maturation_note: SFTPC+ cells appear 3-5 days after replating sorted progenitors in alveolar medium (day 15 onwards); spheres are passaged around day 30 and a CHIR withdrawal/add-back cycle from about day 30-42 increases SFTPC expression. Purified cells self-renew for months.

morphology.endpoint: Monolayered epithelial spheres ('alveolospheres') with a clear lumen suspended in Matrigel; cells are cuboidal and contain lamellar bodies visible by electron microscopy.

Score NKX2-1+ on day 14-15 and abandon runs with very low induction

protocols.name: Self-renewing alveolospheres (Kotton lab)
protocols.principle: Endoderm is anteriorised by dual BMP/TGF-beta inhibition and specified to NKX2-1+ lung progenitors with CHIR99021, BMP4 and retinoic acid; progenitors are sorted and grown in Matrigel with CHIR99021, KGF, dexamethasone, cAMP and IBMX, which drives distal (alveolar) fate. Protocol version of Jacob et al. 2017 (Cell Stem Cell, PMID 28965766).
protocols.efficiency: SFTPC-reporter+ about 30-50% after CHIR withdrawal/add-back (about day 42); 90-100% maintained after sorting and a few passages
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC kept feeder-free for 3-4 passages; colonies 70-80% confluent; plated as single cells in mTeSR1 + Y-27632 24 h before induction.
tips: Test several endoderm split ratios at day 3 and pick the one giving the most NKX2-1+ cells at day 14.
Sorting is not strictly required but unsorted cultures give lower and more variable AT2 yield.
Purified SFTPC+ cells can be cryopreserved and maintained for up to a year.
pitfalls: NKX2-1 induction efficiency is strongly line-dependent.
SFTPC antibodies are unreliable; lack of a reporter makes purity hard to judge.
Overgrown spheres lose SFTPC expression; passage on time.
unverified: Composition of cSFDM is summarised from the same lab's 2025 thyroid protocol; check the reagent table of Jacob 2019 for exact amounts.

protocols.name: Embryoid-body endoderm to 2D lung and airway epithelium (Snoeck lab)
protocols.principle: Endoderm made in embryoid bodies is anteriorised by sequential BMP/TGF-beta inhibition and Wnt/TGF-beta inhibition, ventralised to lung progenitors with CHIR99021, FGF10, KGF, BMP4 and retinoic acid, and matured with dexamethasone, cAMP and IBMX into a mixed distal and proximal epithelium rich in surfactant-producing cells. Protocol version of Huang et al. 2014 (Nat Biotechnol, PMID 24291815).
protocols.efficiency: FOXA2+/NKX2-1+ lung progenitors about 80% or more for RUES2 and about 30-60% or higher for other lines at day 15
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC maintained on MEFs, depleted of feeders on Matrigel, then dissociated with Accutase and aggregated as embryoid bodies in low-attachment plates. Differentiation is run at 5% O2 until day 8-12.
tips: Timing of the switch from endoderm to foregut (day 4, 4.5 or 5) must be set per line from the CXCR4/KIT peak.
Cultures can be kept for many months in maturation medium.
pitfalls: Produces a mixed epithelium, not purified AT2 cells; there is no sorting step.
Dorsomorphin/Noggin and retinoic acid doses are line-dependent.
unverified: Fractional day boundaries follow the protocol's 'day 4/4.5/5' convention; 4.5 is used here.

cell_types.name: Thyroid follicular cells
cell_types.summary: Thyroid follicular cells form hormone-producing follicles that take up iodide and synthesise thyroglobulin-bound T4 and T3. hPSC-derived thyroid cells are used to model congenital hypothyroidism and to explore cell therapy.
cell_types.maturation_note: NKX2-1+/PAX8+ progenitors are scored at day 14; follicle-like organoids mature over 14 or more further days in TSH-containing medium.

morphology.endpoint: Small epithelial organoids in Matrigel domes; thyroid clusters are compact and bright and develop follicle-like lumens, alongside morphologically distinct non-thyroid structures.

protocols.name: BMP4 + FGF2 thyroid specification in 3D Matrigel (Hollenberg/Kotton labs)
protocols.principle: Kit-derived endoderm is embedded in Matrigel and anteriorised by dual BMP/TGF-beta inhibition; BMP4 together with FGF2 then specifies NKX2-1+/PAX8+ thyroid progenitors, which mature into follicular cells with FGF2, FGF10, EGF, IGF-1 and TSH. It builds on Kurmann et al. 2015 (Cell Stem Cell, PMID 26593959) and Serra et al. 2017 (Development, PMID 28947536).
protocols.efficiency: Mean 36 ± 20% NKX2-1/PAX8 reporter double-positive cells at day 14 (n = 12)
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in mTeSR on Matrigel at about 80% confluence; on day -1 seed 1.5-2 x 10^6 live single cells per well of a 6-well plate in mTeSR + 10 µM Y-27632; wells must be fully confluent by the end of day 0.
tips: The endoderm step here is 2 days, shorter than in the same labs' lung protocols.
Seeding density on day -1 is critical and should be adjusted per line.
A NKX2-1/PAX8 dual reporter line makes the day-14 check simple; otherwise use intracellular staining.
pitfalls: Day-14 efficiency varies widely between runs (SD of 20 percentage points).
Non-thyroid structures grow alongside thyroid clusters; purification by sorting may be needed.
unverified: Presence of supplement MR in the day-0 medium was inferred from the kit workflow and the same labs' other protocols; the day-0 table was only partly read.

cell_types.name: Airway epithelium (basal, ciliated, secretory)

cell_types.maturation_note: Airway basal cells are sorted at about day 40-45; a differentiated mucociliary epithelium needs about 3 further weeks at air-liquid interface.

morphology.endpoint: 3D stage: epithelial spheres with lumens in Matrigel. Final air-liquid-interface stage: a tight cobblestone pseudostratified sheet on a Transwell membrane with beating cilia and patches of mucus.

protocols.name: Airway basal cells and air-liquid-interface epithelium (Hawkins/Kotton labs)
protocols.principle: Sorted NKX2-1+ lung progenitors are grown in 3D without Wnt activation, in FGF2 and FGF10, to give airway organoids containing TP63+ cells; dual SMAD inhibition in a commercial basal-cell medium then matures them into NGFR+ basal stem cells that can be expanded, frozen, and differentiated at air-liquid interface. STAR Protocols version of Hawkins et al. 2021 (Cell Stem Cell, PMID 33098807).
protocols.efficiency: Day 14-16: 10-60% NKX2-1+ in non-reporter lines, >90% after sorting; day 40+: about 70% basal cells from reporter-sorted cells, or 10-60% NGFR+ cells in non-reporter lines
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in feeder-free culture, plated as single cells with Y-27632 the day before endoderm induction with the STEMdiff Definitive Endoderm kit.
tips: Optimise the day-3 endoderm passaging ratio per line (1:5-1:6 for the authors' reporter line) to maximise NKX2-1+ cells at day 14-16.
Sorted basal cells can be expanded and cryopreserved; post-thaw survival varies from 10 to 70%, so plate densely.
A high proportion of NGFR+ cells is needed for good air-liquid-interface cultures; re-sort if secretory cells accumulate.
pitfalls: Without an NKX2-1/TP63 reporter the yield of basal cells is lower and depends on the NKX2-1 efficiency of the line.
Dense cultures acidify the CBRa medium quickly and need more frequent feeding.
unverified: Dorsomorphin (2 µM) and SB431542 (10 µM) concentrations for the foregut step are from the same lab's Jacob 2019 protocol; the Suzuki 2021 media table for that step was not read.
The switch-to-ALI timing after seeding follows the PneumaCult instructions and was not captured in detail.

stages.name: Anterior foregut
stages.base_medium: cSFDM (IMDM/Ham's F12 3:1 + B-27 and N-2 supplements, BSA, monothioglycerol, ascorbic acid, GlutaMAX)
stages.feeding: Re-feed once after 24 h
